# AxVigil

> Every inference, a line of defense.

AxVigil points Web3's AI compute at smart-contract exploits instead of puzzles that exist only to mint an NFT. An agent patches a fresh rewrite inside a vulnerability sandbox, a deterministic grader checks the patch and the proof of concept, and three validators (currently permissioned, run by the team) re-grade it. At least two signatures let the Agent ID owner mint a collectible and a non-transferable skill record: a verifiable on-chain capability record.

**Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon · BSC testnet · sandbox/whitehat demo**

**Pages.** The project website is in [`web/index.html`](web/index.html), a one-page submission pitch in [`web/pitch.html`](web/pitch.html), and the interactive pipeline demo in [`web/demo.html`](web/demo.html) (`demo/index.html`) — all self-contained static pages (no build step; open directly or serve the folder).

**Docs.** [`docs/hackathon-pitch.md`](docs/hackathon-pitch.md) is the concise submission pitch (the built Crucible is the star); [`docs/whitepaper.md`](docs/whitepaper.md) is the full vision — the Crucible that exists today plus the defense network it is the trust root for. Traditional Chinese versions: [`docs/hackathon-pitch.zh-TW.md`](docs/hackathon-pitch.zh-TW.md), [`docs/whitepaper.zh-TW.md`](docs/whitepaper.zh-TW.md).

## Why AxVigil

AI coding agents can generate patches, but it is difficult to distinguish a plausible answer from a fix that actually removes an exploit without breaking the contract. AxVigil connects four pieces:

```text
challenge → AI-generated patch + PoC → deterministic verifier → signed on-chain capability record
```

Tenet is a benefits navigator that helps a North Carolinian apply for **Medicaid** (the state's DHB-5200 application) and **SNAP** food assistance (the state's DSS-8207 application). Your answers stay on your device, and nothing is sent anywhere without your explicit consent. Every number that lands on a form is computed by deterministic rules, never an AI guess. And the output stays honest by construction: a prepared application is never a submitted one, Tenet never promises an outcome, and eligibility is decided solely by the agency.

Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Oct 26 – Nov 4, 2026) — see [Status](#status).

1. **Choose how to start.** Voice the whole way, voice with the option to switch to typing at any point, or the step-by-step wizard — all first-class paths through the same journey.
2. **Answer the quick questions.** Tenet computes the questions the applications actually still need, from the field registries of the two real forms — when the computed list is shorter than the full intake, the stage shows an honest "N of M" counter. Questions arrive in small grouped cards; sensitive ones (health, disability, pregnancy, and similar) come last, marked optional, each with a "why we ask" note and a skip affordance. Skipping never blocks the journey.
3. **Talk it through.** One continuous conversation captures the rest — no per-question record/stop ritual; you may answer several questions in one breath, and replies acknowledge what you said before asking the next thing. The step-by-step wizard stays reachable at every point as the typed path.

5. **See what may be worth pursuing.** After a few answers, a ranked match (read-only over your stored answers) shows programs that may be worth pursuing — never a determination. # Malleable

Our goal: an ambulance gets a clear road ahead of it because cars share a live road record, with robotaxi fleets as the first buyers. In simulation, a road edit merges only after [a second car confirms it](docs/gates/phase-15a-scores.jsonl#L10), and a spoofed edit never merged in any of the [10 scored seeds of the Phase 15a gate](docs/gates/phase-15a-scores.jsonl). We have not shown that any vehicle arrives faster; see Limits.

AVs read and write the road record the way coding agents commit to a codebase. Edits are commits, a second car's confirmation is review, and conflicting claims are merge conflicts. This is the protocol analogy; fleet deployment and general conflict resolution are not built. See the [implemented protocol](docs/SPEC.md).

## What the evidence shows

- **Propose, confirm, merge with a set reach.** [PR #50](https://github.com/jerrydjin/malleable/pull/50) plays the original [seed 1 RECORD gate row](docs/gates/phase-15a-scores.jsonl#L10): a car proposes, a second car confirms from its simulated sensor, then the edit merges. The cached model reply sets [route reach, radius 1500 m](docs/gates/phase-15-model-replies.json). Play the [committed replay](recordings/phase15a-seed1.json); do not regenerate it.
- **A spoofed edit does not merge in the scored matrix.** [`spoof_merged: false` and `spoof_caused_reroutes: 0` hold for seeds 1–10 in the original Phase 15a gate](docs/gates/phase-15a-scores.jsonl). This does not establish trust for real fleets or independent cameras.
- **The Meta LLM picks label, reach and who gets priority; it never touches physics.** [Recorded label/reach](docs/gates/phase-15-model-replies.json), [live grant/deny evidence](docs/gates/phase-c-reasons.jsonl), and the [policy adapter](src/reason.rs) show that boundary. [`RoadEdit::review`](src/record.rs) is the hazard merge authority; the [host](src/record_host.rs) and [physical executor](src/make_way.rs) retain movement control. The scored Phase 15 priority grants use Mock, not live LLM decisions.

## Where Meta models sit

**SAM 2.1 is the eyes:** its committed masks provide visual evidence. **The Meta LLM (Muse, via Baseten) writes label and reach and decides grant/deny.** Muse is Meta's LLM; the project is Malleable. The [Phase 16b gate](docs/gates/phase-16b-summary.md) records live SAM and a live Baseten label/reach reply from a numerical SAM summary, not from images. Reach is reply metadata; the model cannot merge an edit or move a car.

In Phase 16b, **B is same source, different viewpoint**. It is not independent corroboration. The label sits on the white trailer, not the crash; the trust rule was not tested because A failed detection and B review was never applied. See [bars and caveats](docs/gates/phase-16b-summary.md), [merge check](experiments/phase16b/output/merge-check.json), and [retained overlay](experiments/phase16b/overlays/B.mp4).

# Physics Twin

Film one second of a ball rolling down a ramp. Physics Twin turns the clip into a 2D physics simulation, tunes the simulation's friction and bounce until it matches the footage, then freezes the clip and predicts where the ball goes next, as a band, with a hash of the prediction shown before the rest of the clip plays. Then it reports how far off it was, in cm, px and ms. You can also ask "what if the ramp were steeper, or the block gone?" and the same frozen frame plays the new future.

Narrow on purpose: a 2D, side-on, rigid-body tabletop scene, with an error number every time.

## Demo video

**Video: link to come** (3:00). Every scene in it is **synthetic**: drawn from the simulation with known parameters, not filmed, and labelled that way on screen. The SAM 3.1 and Muse Spark calls in it are live calls, made on Nov 3 on those synthetic scenes ([docs/live-calls.md](docs/live-calls.md)).

## Built during the event

Everything in this repository was built during the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, **Oct 27 – Nov 4, 2026**: the first commit is Oct 27, 22:05 JST, and each day's work is one pull request (Day 1 to Day 6). Nothing was forked or copied from another repository; the libraries used are the npm packages in `package.json`.

## Try it

`npm ci && npm run dev`, then open the page and press a preset (**A** baseline, **B** steeper ramp, **C** block removed). Presets need no API key. Then **Fit on the first 1.0 s**, **Freeze and predict**, **Reveal**, and under the result, the **What if** panel.

The three presets are **synthetic for now**: no real takes were on the build machine when they were made, so they are drawn from the simulation with known parameters, and the page says so on each one. [docs/presets.md](docs/presets.md) has their results and how to swap in real takes.

## What each model does

| Model | Role here | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **SAM 3.1** (`sam-3.1`, Meta Model API) | Tracks the ball and the blocks through the whole clip, prompted with boxes on frame 0 so the object IDs are ours. Its boxes, per frame, are the measurement: the fit's loss and the reveal's ground truth. Parsed with `@meta-sam/parser`. | `/api/track`, `src/tracks/` |

# Gözüm

**A Turkish-language find-and-guide agent for blind and low-vision people**, built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Indie track, theme: *Build for Your World*).

**Live demo:** https://gozum-delta.vercel.app (open on a phone; camera and microphone permission required)

> Gözüm is a wayfinding aid. It does **not** replace a white cane, a guide dog or a person, and it never tells you a path is safe.

## What it does

You tap the big button and say a goal, e.g. *"Çıkış kapısını bul"* (find the exit door) or *"Otobüsün numarasını oku"* (read the bus number). Gözüm then runs a multi-step agent loop over camera frames:

1. **Plan** – Muse Spark looks at the frame and picks the next action as JSON: `locate`, `read_text`, `ask_user`, `whats_ahead` or `done`.
2. **Act** – the server executes it:
   - `locate` → converts the model's box into clock-face directions and coarse distance (*"Kapı saat 1 yönünde, orta mesafede"*)
   - `read_text` → crops the region at full resolution and asks Muse Spark to read it
   - `ask_user` → asks a clarifying question (*"İki kapı görüyorum, sağdaki mi soldaki mi?"*) and waits for a spoken answer
3. **Repeat** every ~2.5 s until the target is reached, then stop.

Design choices:
- **Stop–scan–move, not continuous hazard radar.** Model latency is seconds, so Gözüm guides you step by step instead of claiming real-time collision warnings.
- **Clock-face directions** (the convention used in orientation & mobility training) and coarse distance (near / medium / far), never metres.
- **Safety guards:** refuses street-crossing decisions and medicine/dose reading; strips any "safe / you can cross" claim from model output.
- **Accessibility:** output goes to an `aria-live` region (read by TalkBack/VoiceOver) and to Turkish speech synthesis; one large button; wake lock.

## Meta models used

| Model | Role |
|---|---|
| Muse Spark (`muse-spark-1.3`) | planner, perception grounding, text reading |
| Muse Voice Transcribe | spoken goals and answers (16 kHz WAV recorded in the browser) |
| SAM 3.1 | *planned:* target segmentation overlay |

## Measured latency

Single calls from a home connection in Turkey (Nov 4, 2026), Muse Spark with `reasoning.effort = minimal`:

| Step | Latency |
|---|---|
| Planner (frame → JSON action) | ~3.1 s (18.5 s at default effort) |
| Full agent step incl. upload and direction math | ~4.5 s |
| Crop-and-read step | ~5.1 s |
| Speech-to-text (short clip) | ~2.7 s |

This is why Gözüm uses a stop–scan–move loop rather than real-time warnings.

```bash
uv sync
cp .env.example .env    # leave MODEL_API_KEY empty for mock mode
uv run uvicorn server.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

# Office of Otherwise

**One question. One alternate history. Scrub through it by date.**

Office of Otherwise is a worldbuilding workbench for writers and worldbuilders. Ask a “what if?” question, then build one alternate history by weaving possibilities into its timeline. Muse Wonder checks each suggestion against the full timeline: it either **fits**, or **conflicts** with a named event and an explanation. Fitting suggestions are woven in by date with links to their causes; conflicts fork through **What if instead…**.

Swipe right in the suggestion deck to weave an event. Wonder checks the selected set together before insertion, with review for conflicts or proposed merges. Muse Spark 1.3 runs ripple checks after weaves to flag later events that may no longer fit. The **Chronicle** rail organizes events by era, while the globe shows scenario geography as of the selected date. Muse Image supplies scenes and SAM 3.1 supplies subject cutouts. Geography is illustrative, not a scientific simulation or historical claim.

Built for the **Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon** (October 26–November 4, 2026), **Startups Track**, theme **Build for Your World**. Divakar Dev is the solo founder and sole contributor. The project is **pre-launch, with no users**.

# Drawing Lazarus

An agent that turns a scanned legacy engineering drawing (a P&ID) into a **verified, simulatable
connectivity graph**: which symbols exist, what they are, what joins to what, and which parts a
person still has to look at. Then you can close a valve on the drawing and see what gets cut off.

Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Cerebral Valley): Indie Developer track, "Push the
Frontier". Team AxeCap.

## Why it matters

Plants run on drawings that only exist as scans. Nobody can query a scan, so "what is isolated if
valve V-104 is shut?" is answered by a person reading paper. Reading a drawing is easy to get
*mostly* right and dangerous to get quietly wrong, so Lazarus does not stop at detection: a
deterministic verifier checks the result, a re-inspection loop re-looks at what it flags, and
whatever is still doubtful is handed to a human instead of being guessed.

## What it does

1. **Find symbols.** Meta SAM 3.1, prompted with "symbol", over overlapping tiles of the whole sheet.
   Small scans are upscaled first so symbols land at a size SAM handles.
2. **Find what SAM cannot.** Muse Spark (Meta API) looks at the whole sheet for large outlines SAM
   never returns (vessels, exchangers), for non-drawing areas (title block, notes), and for the
   legend, which it then reads into `{item, meaning}` entries.
3. **Classify.** Muse Spark Open (via Baseten) types each symbol and reads its tag. On the
   benchmark it matches against the drawing's legend; on real scans it uses a fixed taxonomy plus the
   vocabulary the legend defines (instrument codes, valve names).
4. **Trace pipes.** Classical vision: erase symbols, skeletonise the line work, flood from each
   symbol, find junctions. Output is a graph of symbols, junctions and pipe edges.
   A second trace closes gaps along the horizontal and vertical axes, which turns a dashed line into
   one component; symbol pairs only this trace joins are kept as **dashed links**, separate from the
   pipe edges (a signal line is not a process line, so isolation analysis never crosses one). Each is
   then checked against the pixels by a deterministic checker (drafted by Muse Code); the ones it
   confirms are marked pixel-verified, the rest stay "inferred".
5. **Verify.** No model in the loop. Dangling pipe ends, isolated symbols, valves with the wrong
   number of connections, tags that are not codes the legend defines, tags that disagree with their
   type, low-confidence classifications.
6. **Re-inspect.** Actionable flags get a closer look: SAM re-runs zoomed in around a dangling end,
   Spark re-reads a bad tag. A found symbol is kept only if it is confidently typed, wired into the
   graph, and removes the flag that prompted the search.
7. **Hand off.** What is still flagged is reported as needing a human. Pipes that just stop are
   reported separately as open ends.
8. **Simulate.** Connectivity and isolation: close valves, pick a source, see what stays reachable.

# Drafty

Drafty is an engineering workstation that turns a described or typed part into a real solid, meshes it, and solves it with finite element analysis. You can start from a conversation or work manually — both paths meet on the same parametric part, the same solver, and the same results.

Engineering design usually splits into two disconnected steps: figuring out *what* to build (loads, dimensions, materials, assumptions) and *running the numbers* (CAD, mesh, solver). Drafty connects them in one loop:

1. **Start with meta AI** — describe the problem in the scenario assistant. Drafty asks for what is missing, keeps assumptions and sources visible, and proposes a part.
2. **Approve and open Studio** — nothing is solved from the chat alone. You approve the proposed part, then edit and run it in the manual Studio.
3. **Edit and solve** — change dimensions, material, support, and load, or sketch extra pieces. Run the solve and read the displacements and stresses.
4. **Return to the scenario** — send the part back, edited or not. The scenario updates its inputs and context, so the conversation continues about the part as it actually is now.

You can also skip the conversation entirely: **Open Studio** works on its own, with no AI key required.

## How Meta AI is used in this field

Meta AI (Muse Spark 1.3 by default, Muse Wonder 1.0 for harder turns) acts as the *front door*, never as the calculator:

- It interprets your description, classifies which supported part you mean, and asks for the missing physical inputs.
- It can search published references for loads and material data. Checked references, retrieved pages, and model citations are kept in separate source classes.
- With a photo or drawing attached, SAM 3.1 segmentation can outline what is visible. An image is evidence, never a measurement.
- The server — not the model — computes every number, builds the geometry, and chooses the solver. The model never invents stresses, displacements, or safety factors, and a part reaches the solver only after your approval.

Without `MODEL_API_KEY`, Drafty still works: the assistant becomes a labeled guided template with built-in demos, and Studio is fully usable.

## Run it

You need Python 3.12 with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), Node, and Docker (for the CalculiX solver image).

From the repository root:

```powershell
uv sync --extra dev
docker build -t drafty-ccx -f infra/docker/Dockerfile.ccx infra/docker
Copy-Item .env.example .env
uv run drafty-api
```

In other terminal:

```powershell
cd apps/web
npm install
npm run dev
```

Or with Docker Compose (web on port 15173, API on port 18080):

```powershell
docker compose up --build
```

## Main features

- **Scenario assistant** — chat that collects inputs, shows assumptions, sources, and missing data, and proposes a part for your approval.
- **AI ↔ Studio round trip** — approve a part into Studio, edit it there, and return it; the scenario context follows the edited part.

# Hazina — a tax agent for small and micro businesses

**Helping small and micro businesses keep up with the digitizing tax systems.**

KRA has gone digital: invoicing is electronic under eTIMS, and KRA now validates
returns against that digital record — an expense without an eTIMS invoice behind
it is disallowed. But a small business's records still live in M-Pesa messages,
till statements and paper receipts in a drawer. Hazina is the bridge: hand it the
pile you already have, and it returns books that can stand in the digital system.
The agent who does the work — who reads, matches, asks and computes — is **Hazi**.

## What the agent does

One month-end run:

1. **Gather** — M-Pesa statement, bank statement, photos of paper receipts,
   voice notes for cash spent.
2. **Read** — Muse Spark vision turns documents into structured records.
3. **Match** — deterministic code matches every shilling in the statements to a
   record, or lists it as unmatched. Nothing is silently filled in.
4. **Ask** — the agent takes the unmatched list back to the merchant, one
   question at a time. The answers become records.
5. **Compute** — tax rules live in versioned config (`config/rules.ke.yaml`),
   never in the model: Turnover Tax on gross sales, a rolling VAT-registration
   threshold watch, and the eTIMS-backed vs paper-only expense split.
6. **Record** — every match, classification and merchant answer is written
   into the run's audited record, hash-stamped and tied to the documents it
   rests on, so every figure can later answer "why is this number what it is?"
7. **Hand over** — a filing pack: the TOT figures, threshold status, flagged
   items, and the evidence index. **A human files on iTax. The agent never
   submits anything itself, and never invents a record for a gap.**

## Pre-existing vs built during the event (26 Oct – 4 Nov, 2026)

- **Pre-existing:** the Hazina product concept and the pilot relationship
  with Beautify by Angel. No pre-existing code is used anywhere in the build.
- **Built during the event:** everything in this repository — the agent, its
  tools, the rules engine, the merchant web app, and the evaluation harness —
  written from scratch during the event window.
- **Post-hackathon roadmap:** sealing each run's decisions to Attest, Ansai's
  attestation infrastructure, so a finished pack also carries a remotely
  verifiable, signed seal.

## Pilot

The use case is **Beautify by Angel**, a real Nairobi beauty business: its real
month of M-Pesa records, statements and receipts is the fixture set the agent is
graded against. Raw business records are never committed to this repo (see
`fixtures/README.md`); the public samples are synthetic.

## Setup

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and add your Meta Model API key. Keys live in
`.env` only — never in code, never in git.

**Find where a loose part belonged, using the history you recorded.**

A new, standalone visual-memory module for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon indie track. It grows out of the ReverseSteps product idea: preserve the evidence of taking something apart so another person can understand how it goes back together.

## The experience we are building

1. Photograph a simple object as its parts are removed.
2. Photograph a loose part during reassembly.
3. Suggest its possible appearances in the recorded steps, with source photographs and highlighted regions.
4. Ask for another view when the recorded evidence does not distinguish similar parts.

# Ask the Control Tower — build scaffold

Scaffold stood up Mon Oct 26, 2026 (event Day 1), after the official-rules
read in `../event-requirements-verified-2026-10-26.md`.

## Files
- `index.html` — standalone assistant page (integrates into the live Control
  Tower page at the Oct 29 step).
- `app.js` — Q&A engine + Meta Model API phrasing layer (stubbed, see below).
- `fact-store.json` — the SETTLED fact store (copy of
  `../fact-store-settled-2026-10-26.json`). The only numbers the assistant
  may state.
- `questions.json` — the 10-question bank + trustee summary. Templates are
  filled exclusively from `fact-store.json` via the audited placeholder map
  in `app.js` (`buildView`).

## Architecture (accuracy by construction)
1. Question → matched to the bank (exact or keyword match).
2. Answer assembled from fact-store values only; an unresolvable placeholder
   withholds the answer instead of guessing.
3. Citation line appended to every answer.
4. Unmatched questions get an explicit "outside the verified fact set"
   response — never an improvised figure.

## Engine v1 (Mon Oct 26, 2026 — the Oct 28 milestone, pulled forward)
`app.js` matching was hardened beyond the scaffold's keyword counter:
- **Normalization + variants:** case/punctuation/hyphen variants collapse;
  institution variants fold to canonical tokens ("UNC Wilmington",
  "UNC-Wilmington", "University of North Carolina Wilmington" → `uncw`).
- **Weighted intent scoring with synonyms** (gap/difference/disparity/
  divide; drives/factors/predicts; trust/error; …), exact bank questions
  keep a fast path.
- **Multi-part questions** are split into clauses; each strongly matched
  clause is answered separately, each part with its own Source + Scope.
- **Near-miss questions** answer the closest supported fact with a
  closest-fact preface that names the scope — including three derived
  intents with no bank question: spotlight institutions (Harvard, Trine),
  sector-specific Pell gaps, and the year-4 horizon gap.
- **Citation discipline:** every answer carries a Source line AND a Scope
  line (panel vs analysis set, cohort, years).
- **Clean refusals:** unsupported metrics (tuition, salary, debt,
  enrollment size, acceptance-rate values), future values, unknown
  institutions, and institutional trivia are refused before scoring.

# LinguaCheck

**Benchmarks ask *"is the AI right?"* LinguaCheck asks *"does the AI say the same thing in every language?"***

LinguaCheck is a **cross-lingual factual consistency evaluator** for Meta's AI models. It asks the same medical, legal or finance question in **English** and **Brazilian Portuguese**, compares the two answers, and flags **cross-lingual drift**: places where the model gives different facts, warnings, numbers, deadlines or rights depending on the language it is asked in. A professional interpreter then reviews the flags.

> Model output shown in LinguaCheck is **output under audit — not medical, legal or financial advice.** All test cases are fictional; no real patient or client data is used anywhere.

## Built during the hackathon
The code, the app, the test set and the review were created **Oct 26 – Nov 4, 2026** for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Indie Developer track, "Build for Your World"). The code was written with an AI coding assistant (Claude); the test design, interpreter traps and review decisions are by Maria Myers, a professional medical & legal interpreter (EN / PT-BR / ES, about 20 years).

## How it works
1. **Ask** — the same question goes to **Muse Spark Open** in English and in Brazilian Portuguese (temperature 0).
2. **Check, layer 1 (code)** — numbers, units and dates are compared exactly, aware of the Brazilian decimal comma (2,5 = 2.5), thousands dot and date order.
3. **Check, layer 2 (AI judge)** — the same Muse Spark Open model, in a second evaluation step and guided by an interpreter trap file (`data/traps.csv`), lists each meaningful difference, quotes the evidence from both answers and assigns a severity.
4. **Human review** — the interpreter confirms or rejects each flag, can add errors the judge missed, and writes a corrected version. Review decisions are saved separately from the model's answers, which are never edited.

No answer key is needed to *flag* drift: the model is compared with itself. Human review decides which flags are real and which language is wrong.

## Meta model used
- **Muse Spark Open** (Meta open weights) served by **Baseten** — `meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026`, OpenAI-compatible endpoint `https://inference.baseten.co/v1`. Both the answers and the judge use this model.

# Suite Fleet

I run a personal agent fleet that handles my real daily work on one small server. For the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Indie Developer track, October 26 to November 4, 2026), I am rebuilding its model layer on Meta models.

Demo site: https://demo.kaziprince.com

## The story

Suite Fleet is not a demo I assembled for this event. It is a working fleet of agents on one small server, and it already handles the ordinary work of my life: triaging my mail, scoring job leads, evaluating deals, and checking my notes, alongside a personal suite I use for mail, notes, files, and chat. I direct the fleet, and it works under hard approval gates that stay with me: spending money, sending messages to other people, and making submissions always wait for my approval.

With this hackathon build I am answering a practical question using real workloads instead of benchmarks: when I plug Meta's newest models into jobs my fleet already runs every day, what do they cost, how fast are they, and how good are the results, measured head to head against the models doing those jobs today?

## The hackathon layer

During the event window, I am wiring Meta models into four real jobs my fleet already runs:

1. Mail triage: sorting and summarizing incoming mail the way my fleet already does it daily.
2. Job lead scoring: rating job postings against my standing criteria.
3. Deal evaluation: judging whether a found deal is real, relevant, and worth acting on.
4. Notes QA: checking my notes for errors, gaps, and stale facts.

I measure every run on the same three axes and publish the results on a public dashboard:

1. Cost: what the run actually cost.
2. Latency: how long the run actually took.
3. Quality: whether the output was accepted, edited, or rejected when reviewed against the result my fleet already produces for the same job.

I am publishing the measurements, including the runs where the new models lose, because I will keep whichever model wins each job. The dashboard is my record of that decision being made in the open.

## What is in this repo

This repo is a curated public staging of my hackathon layer only. I am not publishing the production fleet itself, its data, or its configuration here.

- `README.md`: this file: the project story, architecture, and disclosure
- `LICENSE`: proprietary license: viewing and evaluation only
- `demo/`: the demo site source (index.html, styles.css), live at the demo link above

These pieces landed here as I built them during the event:

- `routing/`: the model routing layer that sends each fleet job to a chosen model lane and logs cost and latency
- `lanes/`: the Meta model lanes for mail triage and job lead scoring, with their ledgers and measured results
- `dashboard/`: the public results dashboard source that renders the measured runs

# AwasScan Agent

A Telegram bot that investigates suspicious Malaysian messages, screenshots, payment QRs and voice notes with real
tools (QR decoding, link checks, transcription) and replies with an evidence-backed verdict. Built on Meta's Muse
models for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Indie track).

Built during the hackathon, 27 Oct to 4 Nov 2026. Work in progress; see [PLAN.md](PLAN.md).

## Run it

Needs Node 24 (runs TypeScript directly, no build step).

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env   # then fill in the keys
npm test               # unit tests, no network or API calls
npm run smoke          # one live investigation (costs a few cents)
```

`AGENT_PROVIDER=baseten npm run smoke` runs the same agent on Muse Spark Open via Baseten.
`npm run eval` runs the synthetic test set ([eval/cases.json](eval/cases.json)) on both models and writes
[eval/results.md](eval/results.md).

## Eval (33 synthetic cases: 25 scam, 8 legitimate)

| Model | Scams caught | Of those, high risk | False alarms | Median time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Muse Spark 1.3 (Meta Model API) | 25/25 | 22/25 | 1/8 | 7.9s |
| Muse Spark Open (Baseten) | 25/25 | 22/25 | 1/8 | 5.0s |

Cases are written from public scam advisories (bank and courier impersonation, APK "wedding invitations",
police threats, fake fund recovery, tampered DuitNow QR stickers, APK files forwarded as invitations or receipts,
ZIP "statements" named like PDFs, and screenshots of such chats). All names, numbers and sites are made up.
The one false alarm: a friend sharing a ZIP of photos is rated "suspicious" by both models. We left the case
labelled legitimate rather than tune it away; unexpected ZIPs from hacked contacts are a real pattern.

## How an investigation works

Code first scans the message text for known scam tactics (`src/tools/tactics.ts`: asking for a TAC/OTP,
"safe account" transfers, arrest threats, guaranteed returns...) and forwarded files for Android apps and
disguised ZIPs (`src/tools/attachments.ts`, by name and type only: the file is never downloaded). For screenshots,
the model passes the text and file names it reads to the same code checks.

`src/agent.ts` sends the message (and any images) to the model with six tools from `src/tools/`:
`decode_qr`, `parse_duitnow`, `inspect_link` (behind an SSRF guard), `official_contact`, `check_text` and
`check_file_name`.
Each tool result becomes numbered evidence (E1, E2...). The model's final findings must cite that evidence;
`src/verdict.ts` drops uncited findings and decides the verdict in code. The model can raise the risk, never
lower it, and can only reach "high risk" by citing evidence that itself carries a warning. There is no "safe" verdict.

# SUZARCHI (சுழற்சி) — Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026

**One Material. Multiple Possibilities.**
*Named after the Tamil word **சுழற்சி** (pronounced **Suzharchi**), meaning **"Cyclical Rotation"**.*

## Project Overview

SUZARCHI explores how AI can help businesses discover practical, compliant reuse opportunities for industrial surplus materials, grounded in the textile manufacturing hub of **Tiruppur, Tamil Nadu**—the global pioneer in 100% Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) water recycling and pre-consumer textile waste valorisation.

Textile manufacturers often have leftover fabric, yarn, garment offcuts, trims, and other materials that may still have commercial value. Identifying suitable next uses requires understanding the material, its properties, the requirements of potential applications, and the checks needed before reuse.

This hackathon project will explore an AI-assisted material opportunity workflow using Meta models and transparent, rule-based compatibility checks.

## Hackathon Track

**Proposed track:** Push the Frontier

**Focus:** Textile surplus reuse and material opportunity discovery.

## Planned Demonstration

The initial prototype aims to demonstrate a focused workflow:

1. **Material input:** Enter textile surplus details and optionally provide a photograph.
2. **Material Passport:** Organise available information into a structured material record.
3. **AI-assisted analysis:** Use a Meta model to help interpret the supplied information and propose potential reuse destinations.
4. **Compatibility checks:** Apply explicit rules to assess suitability and flag missing information.
5. **Opportunity results:** Present potential destinations, supporting reasons, uncertainties, and recommended verification steps.

These are planned capabilities, not claims about features already implemented.

## Responsible AI Principles

- Distinguish confirmed information from estimated and unverified information.
- Do not infer exact fibre composition, GSM, contamination status, or chemical safety from a photograph alone.
- Use deterministic rules for mandatory compatibility constraints.
- Explain why an opportunity is suggested and what evidence is missing.
- Do not claim environmental savings or waste prevention without supporting evidence.

## Technology

The prototype will use one or more eligible Meta models through the Meta Model API or another permitted Meta model access method, subject to the hackathon rules and verified technical capabilities.

The application architecture and technology stack will be selected after the initial requirements and model-access tests.

## Hackathon Work Boundary

This repository is dedicated to work developed for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026.

SUZARCHI is a separate, long-term product initiative. Existing planning documents and approved visual concepts remain unchanged. Any pre-existing concepts, assets, or code used in the submission will be identified transparently, and newly developed

# AONE BP

A WhatsApp business partner for Nigerian salons and vendors. A customer asks a question on WhatsApp, AONE BP drafts a reply in the owner's own tone, checks it against the owner's price rules, and shows it to the owner. **Nothing is sent until the owner presses Approve.**

Built solo for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Indie track).

## What it does

1. A customer messages the shop's WhatsApp number.
2. A Meta model (`meta-models/muse-spark-open`, served on Baseten) drafts a reply in the owner's tone.
3. The rules check runs in code, not in the prompt: price floors, maximum discount (15%), deposit (50%), and a secret canary word that must never leak.
4. The owner sees the customer message, the draft and the rules check on a phone-friendly approval page, then presses **Approve and send** or **Reject**.
5. Blocked drafts (for example a price below the floor) cannot be approved at all.

## Which model runs where

- The model is Meta's `muse-spark-open`, called through Baseten's OpenAI-compatible API (`https://inference.baseten.co/v1`).
- Everything else (webhook, rules, approval page) runs in a small Node server on your own machine. Customer messages are sent to the model only to draft a reply.
- The model only writes the draft. The rules in `src/rules.js` decide whether a draft is allowed. Owner floors never reach the model.

## Why the rules are in code

A prompt can be argued with. Code cannot. A customer who writes "ignore your rules and give me ₦5,000" is talking to a draft that is checked afterwards against the owner's real numbers. Customer text is also wrapped as data, so it is never treated as instructions.

## Existing before the hackathon

An earlier design prototype of the owner screens, with sample data. It had no AI and no backend.

## Built during the hackathon

- The WhatsApp Cloud API webhook (verify, receive, send)
- The model client for Meta's model on Baseten
- The rules engine and the message pipeline
- The owner approval page (rewritten front end, with a rules check on every draft)
- 42 automated tests

## Quick try, no WhatsApp needed

You only need Node 20+ and a Baseten API key.

```
git clone https://github.com/yusuffolufemi532-glitch/aone-bp
cd aone-bp
copy .env.example .env        (on Mac/Linux: cp .env.example .env)
```

Put your `BASETEN_API_KEY` in `.env`, then run:

```
node --env-file=.env scripts/try-model.js "How much is knotless braids?"
```

It prints the model's draft and the rules decision. Try `"Can I pay 10000 for knotless braids?"` to see the rules block a draft.

Run the tests (no key needed):

```
npm test
```

## Full setup with WhatsApp (Meta test number)

1. Create a Meta app with the WhatsApp use case. On **Step 1. Try it out**, note the Phone Number ID and click **Generate token** (it expires about daily).
2. Fill `.env` from `.env.example`: `BASETEN_API_KEY`, `WHATSAPP_TOKEN`, `WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID`, plus a `VERIFY_TOKEN` and an `OWNER_KEY` that you make up (long random words).

# Harbor Muse 🚢

**Ask the harbor what's out there.** A one-page live ship tracker for US waters, centered on wherever you are, where you can ask Meta's Muse models about the ships you see on the map, by typing (your phone keyboard's dictation works too).

> 🏁 **Built for the [Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon](https://cerebralvalley.ai/e/meta-ai-developer-hackathon) (Cerebral Valley), Indie track, solo.**
> All work in this repo was created during the event window, **Oct 26 – Nov 4, 2026**, and the commit history reflects that.

🎥 **Demo video (3:19):** [watch / download](docs/demo/harbor-muse-demo.mp4) · YouTube: [watch on YouTube](https://youtu.be/JKQHclwB5n0)

---

## What it does (planned)

- 🗺️ **Live map near you.** Your phone's location centers the map and tells the server which waters to watch (a ~25 nm box around you, anywhere in the US). Real-time positions come from the free [aisstream.io](https://aisstream.io/) AIS feed, on a [MapLibre GL](https://maplibre.org/) map with the keyless [OpenFreeMap](https://openfreemap.org/) Positron style (Leaflet + OpenStreetMap as fallback).
- 💬 **Ask Muse.** Ask questions like *"What's that big ship heading into the port?"* Muse answers from a snapshot of the live ship data: name, type, speed, heading, and destination. If a ship card is open, follow-ups like *"tell me about it"* refer to that ship. **Tell me more** on a named ship card asks Muse Spark (with web search) and posts into the same side chat with sources.
- 📇 **Tap a ship** for name, type, speed, heading and destination ("unknown" when AIS doesn't say; AIS has no origin, so none is shown).
- ⏪ **Replay demo.** If location is denied or unavailable, the map opens on Corpus Christi Bay (our beach demo home) and plays recorded real traffic when the live feed is quiet or no key is set. If you're located elsewhere and nothing live is near you yet, the badge says **WAITING** instead of jumping you to Texas.

## Run it

Needs Node 20.6+ (uses Node's built-in `--env-file`, no dotenv). One server file, one HTML page, no build step.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Cole-Z/harbor-muse.git
cd harbor-muse
npm install
cp .env.example .env   # then fill in AISSTREAM_API_KEY (free at aisstream.io) and MUSE_API_KEY (Ask, coming soon)
npm start              # runs node --env-file=.env server.js; without a .env it just runs node server.js
```

Hosted (Render, Fly, …): set `AISSTREAM_API_KEY` / `MUSE_API_KEY` as host env vars and run `node server.js`.

A hackathon entry for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Indie
Developer track): an agent that builds a persistent wardrobe from the
photos you share, then styles validated full looks from it — conversing
through an Instagram-DM-style chat thread.

Three Meta models do the heavy lifting, all called through one

# NIGHTRIDE

**Built for the worst hour. Works at every hour.**

**Demo video:** https://youtu.be/ZW6jwK26yeE  ·  **Receipts (every claim, its test, its code):** [RECEIPTS.md](RECEIPTS.md)

**Live:** https://nightride.nohumannearby.com (open it on a phone; Add to Home Screen installs it, and it keeps working with no signal)

A voice-first night dispatcher for people who are not in a car: cyclists, e-bike riders, walkers, skaters.
When something goes wrong after dark (a flat, a snapped chain, an e-bike that cuts out miles from home,
a driver who won't leave you alone), you hold one button and say what happened. NIGHTRIDE sorts it,
tells you the one next thing to do out loud, and shows you where that advice came from.

Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Indie track) by a rider who commutes 20 miles a shift
on an e-bike through California's High Desert, often home after dark. Every line in this repo was
written during the hackathon building period, starting Oct 27 2026 12:00 AM ET. The commit history is the record.

## Why

- 76% of US pedestrian deaths and 52% of cyclist deaths happen in the dark (NHTSA, 2024 data).
- Pedestrian deaths at night rose 84% from 2010 to 2023; daytime deaths rose 28% (GHSA, 2025).
- 1 in 4 pedestrians and 1 in 5 cyclists killed were hit by a driver who left the scene (NHTSA, 2024).
- 11.3 million US households have no vehicle (Census ACS 2024).

## What it does

| Feature | How | Meta model |
|---|---|---|
| **Talk** | Hold to talk; audio is converted to WAV and transcribed in about two seconds. A model's refusal is never shown as the rider's words; silence gets a mic hint. | Muse Voice Transcribe (Meta Model API), Muse Spark Open as backup |
| **Dispatch** | One card: FIX IT, RIDE, SAFE PLACE, or EMERGENCY, spoken aloud. | Muse Spark Open |
| **Fix it** | Camera frame of the problem; the model names it and picks a verified playbook card. | Muse Spark Open (vision) |
| **Part outline** | The part Muse Spark named ("rear tire") is outlined in amber in every frame of the rider's clip, then replayed on screen. No made-up outline: if SAM finds nothing, none is drawn. | SAM 3.1 (Meta Model API) |
| **Get me somewhere** | Real places open right now, ranked for the situation, one tap to bike directions. | none (OpenStreetMap) |
| **Tell my people** | Message with battery and a live map link, sent from the rider's own phone. | none |
| **Close call** | One tap logs where a driver came too close. Reports stack into hotspots on a night map; the city can download them as CSV. | none |

Sorting and seeing (and backup hearing) use **Muse Spark Open** (open weights, `meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026`) served on Baseten.
Hearing uses **Muse Voice Transcribe** (muse-voice-transcribe-1.0, Meta Model API). The part outline uses **SAM 3.1** (`sam-3.1`) on the Meta Model API: the clip is converted to H.264 MP4, sent with the
part name as the concept prompt, and the streamed masks are decoded with Meta's `@meta-sam/parser`.

# Handoff Studio

Handoff Studio is a prototype for checking whether a proposed agent handoff fits an explicitly declared permission scope. Its core idea is simple: a model can suggest what to do, but it cannot grant authority.

## Current verified state (2026-11-02)

- Light-theme browser prototype with synthetic invoice scenarios, deterministic scope checks, and an optional Meta Llama proposal endpoint using a server-side Cloudflare Workers AI binding.
- Worker code and local mock tests cover email-code sign-in, server-side hashed sessions, HttpOnly cookies, and per-user synthetic scenario storage. These are not enabled in the public fallback.
- Local tests: 33/33 passing, including mock-D1 isolation checks. This is not a live sign-up, deployment, or user-validation claim.
- Wrangler dry-run succeeds with a free D1 database and account-defined rate-limit namespace. Deployment is not configured or verified.
- The public fallback has no sign-up controls. Arbitrary-recipient transactional email is not available through Cloudflare Workers Free. A free email provider would still need an owner-authorized account and verified sender-domain DNS setup.

## Run locally

Install dependencies with `npm ci`, then `npm test`. `npm run dev` starts the Cloudflare Worker preview. The static UI also opens from `index.html`, but account and model APIs require the Worker bindings.

## Public fallback limits

The current fallback deliberately has no email/sign-in inputs or save button. It demonstrates synthetic scope checking only. The Worker still contains local-tested auth and D1 storage code, but auth is inactive because no email binding or session secret is configured. D1-backed account isolation has only been tested against mock bindings locally.

## Truthful demo limits

The grant and incoming text are synthetic fixtures; their source is not authenticated. The policy gate only compares supplied values, and its verdict never sends a message or performs a handoff. The optional model endpoint proposes a tuple that must still be checked. The session ledger shown in the demo is local to the browser and not a durable audit log. Email sign-up, D1 persistence, and live deployment are not yet available.

See `DEMO.md` for the current three-minute narration and `EVAL.md` for the limited synthetic test scope.

**Speak a sale. Nawa keeps the books.**

Nawa is a voice powered bookkeeping app for small shop owners and market vendors. The owner says or types a sale or a payment, reviews what the AI understood, confirms, and Nawa keeps track of who owes what, what is left in stock, and which customers to remind.

Live demo: https://nawa-9y6c.onrender.com

Hackathon: Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, theme **Build for Your World**.

---

## The problem

Many small vendors in Namibia sell on credit and write debts in a notebook, or keep them in their heads. Debts are forgotten, stock is guessed, and reminders are never sent. Typing into a typical accounting app is slow and hard for someone who is serving customers all day.

Nawa lets the vendor simply speak: "Sold one power bank to Anna, paid 150." Nawa turns that into a proper record.

## What Nawa can do

**Record sales by voice or by typing**
- Record with the microphone, with a live timer and Clear and Cancel buttons.
- A typed box is always available as a fallback.
- Meta AI turns the sentence into a structured sale: customer, product, quantity, total and amount paid.
- If something is missing, the AI asks a short clarifying question instead of guessing.

**Review before saving**
- Nothing is saved until the owner confirms an editable review card.
- Saving is blocked for an empty or unknown customer name.
- Walk in (cash) sales are always fully paid.
- A duplicate sale warning helps avoid recording the same sale twice.

**Payments and debts**
- Say "Anna paid 30", "Anna paid half" or "Anna paid everything". Half and everything are calculated from the customer's real balance, not guessed by the AI.
- Customer names are matched to real customers, so a small mishearing such as "Jon" for "John" still finds the right person.
- Unknown names are refused. A customer who owes nothing cannot be paid.
- An overpayment records only the balance owed and shows a change message.
- One field in the database (`customers.balance_owed`) is the single source of truth for debts.

**Stock**
- A Stock page with products, unit, selling price, cost price, quantity and a low stock alert.
- On the sale review card, the spoken product is matched to the stock list. The price for one is shown and the total is filled in automatically, and recalculated when the quantity changes.
- A warning (not a block) appears when the quantity sold is more than what is in stock.
- When a sale is saved, the stock quantity goes down and never below zero.

---

## 🌟 Overview

**SightGuide** is a phone-first assistive web application designed to help blind and visually impaired individuals perceive and navigate their physical surroundings. 

By capturing continuous rear-camera video samples, SightGuide leverages **Meta AI's Muse Spark** and **Segment Anything Model (SAM 3.1)** to detect immediate path obstacles, compute coarse monocular distance bands, prioritize safety hazards, and deliver concise, natural-voice audio instructions straight into the user's ears.

```
       [ Mobile Camera ]
              │ (Sampled every 1.5s)
              ▼
    [ SightGuide Web App ]
              │
              ├───► [ Meta AI Cloud Vision (Muse Spark + SAM 3.1) ]
              │       └─ Multi-concept obstacle detection & segmentation
              │
              ├───► [ Local Risk & Direction-Lock Engine ]
              │       └─ Coarse distance estimation (Very Close, 1-3m, >3m)
              │       └─ Anti-flapping direction consistency
              │
              └───► [ Synthesized Spoken Audio Output ]
                      └─ e.g. "Monitor 0.5 meters ahead. Stop."
```

---

## ⚠️ Important Safety Notice

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **ASSISTIVE PROTOTYPE ONLY — NOT A CERTIFIED MOBILITY DEVICE**  
> SightGuide is an experimental assistive tool designed to supplement, **never replace**, traditional mobility aids such as white canes, guide dogs, sighted companions, or formal O&M (Orientation and Mobility) training. 
> 
> Because cloud visual processing has inherent sampling and network latency (typically 1–3 seconds), guidance is **not** an instantaneous collision warning system. Users should always test in safe, controlled environments with a sighted companion present. SightGuide will never claim a pathway is completely safe merely because an obstacle was undetected.

---

## ✨ Key Features

1. **Real-Time Camera Guidance (Rear-Lens Priority):**
   - Direct browser access to the high-resolution rear camera with environment constraints.
   - Intelligent sampling (every 1.5 seconds) to minimize bandwidth and compute load while maintaining timely situational awareness.

2. **Meta AI Vision Integration:**
   - Powered by **Muse Spark** (`muse-spark-1.3`) for rapid scene understand

# Plomba

**A digital seal on a shipping container's condition at every handover.**

[![CI](https://github.com/Lisovate/plomba/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Lisovate/plomba/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

> **For judges** · Built during the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, Oct 26 – Nov 4, 2026 ([build log](docs/build-log.md)).
> - **Live app:** https://app.plomba.lisovate.com (access code in the submission). Start with [Try](https://app.plomba.lisovate.com/try): sample footage with the AR a checker sees, no container needed. Then container **PLBU 400004 3**: rust recorded at Gdynia, drawn on a new photo at Łódź.
> - **Meta models at run time:** SAM 3.1 tracks and outlines the container and blurs people; Muse Spark reads the number, names faces, finds and codes damage, and drafts claims as an agent; Muse Voice Transcribe takes spoken damage notes; Muse Spark Open runs the vision on open weights.
> - **Website:** https://plomba.lisovate.com · **Integrations:** [docs/integrations.md](docs/integrations.md) and [examples/](examples)

![Plomba on a phone: Home with "Start here" for a first visit; sample footage where SAM 3.1 tracks a container and its tag shows the number, type, last sealed handover and the rust recorded at Gdynia; the open gate-out at Łódź with that rust drawn on the new photo; the damage passport placing a dent between two handovers](docs/images/screens.jpg)

*Plomba* is Polish for the seal on a container's doors, the tag that proves the box wasn't opened. Plomba does the same for the container's condition.

On its way from a seaport to the customer, a container changes hands several times: ship, port terminal, train, inland terminal, truck, depot. Each handover moves liability for damage. Yet at most inland and rail terminals, the container's condition is still recorded on paper or in loose phone photos. When a dent turns up later, nobody can prove where it happened.

Plomba is an app for the checker doing the walk-around at a handover. It installs from the browser onto an iPhone or an Android phone. It uses Meta's models to see, read, listen and reason, and it keeps every mark on the container's own coordinates, so the next handover, in another city, sees the same damage on the same spot.

It's open source (Apache-2.0) and built to be self-hosted: a terminal, depot or rail operator runs one container on its own machine and keeps its data ([self-hosting](docs/self-hosting.md)).

**Try it:** a demo installation runs at https://app.plomba.lisovate.com (the access code is in the hackathon submission). It looks like an inland terminal three weeks in: a fleet of containers with sealed histories, walk-around videos and damage placed between two handovers, and a train due at Łódź. **No container nearby?** Its [Try page](https://app.plomba.lisovate.com/try) plays sample footage with the AR a checker sees: the tracked outline, the faces, the container's information and its recorded damage on the same spot. Two, pick a theme.

A parent picks a character (8 Bellefly Kids characters), a theme (6: kindness, courage, sharing, patience, gratitude, friendship), and an age band (2–3, 4–5, 6–7), and an optional first name that is never stored or sent anywhere. https://belleflykids.github.io/bellefly-kids-story-builder/

Demo video (Unlisted, 2:57): https://youtu.be/nzNGtM1hfis

This demo was built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, October 26 to November 4, 2026, for the pre-existing Bellefly Kids world. The Bellefly Kids characters and world existed before the hackathon and are not claimed as hackathon inventions.

Built during the hackathon:

No draft reaches a child without both checks. A simple parent quick-check unlocks the AI draft button for that page visit, the draft is checked first, and only a parent tapping Approve makes it a story to read aloud. It never goes straight to a child.

There are no child accounts, no child typing, no ads, no trackers, and no personal data collected by the demo itself; standard host logs only.

# Ground Truth

**What the label says, and what the soil does.**

Constellia Group · Montevideo, Uruguay
Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026 · Startup Track · Push the Frontier

---

## The problem

Companies print "biodegradable" on packaging. Nobody can check whether it is true.

Not because they are lying. Because the tests that exist were run somewhere
else, on pieces that are not shaped like the actual package. Someone measured a
thin film in a lab at 25 °C. That says nothing about a thick cap buried in a
field in Montevideo.

The information needed to answer that question does exist. It is scattered
across hundreds of studies from the last thirty years, each measuring something
slightly different.

A 2026 PRISMA review of 202 soil studies (Govil et al., *Frontiers in
Microbiology*) reaches the same conclusion this project started from: wall
thickness is a control on degradation rate, and it is reported inconsistently
or not at all. That review is the strongest external support for the premise
here — and it also marks the boundary of what exists. It covers soil, in prose
and static tables, read by a human over months. It cannot be queried by
geometry, and it cannot be extended to a new corpus.

Ground Truth produces the queryable artifact, across seven environments.

## Why thickness is the variable nobody crossed

After the environment, the single strongest driver of degradation time is **wall
thickness**. Degradation is a surface process: microorganisms work from the
outside in. A film and a bottle of the same resin, in the same soil, are not the
same experiment — but they are quoted as if they were.

Published work clusters heavily at film thicknesses. Real containers are an
order of magnitude thicker. That gap is the project.

### What the literature already shows, where anyone bothered to measure it

One study in the corpus varies thickness and holds everything else fixed.
PHBV with almond-shell filler, same formulation, same two Mediterranean sites,
same 18 months of seawater exposure:

| Nominal thickness | Disintegration at 18 months |
|---|---|
| 150 µm | 88 % |
| 500 µm | 33 % |

A 3.3× change in thickness moved the outcome by a factor of 2.7. Nothing else
differed.

Thickness also sets the scale of the whole question. The thinnest specimens in
the corpus are 10–15 µm PHB and PHBV films, gone completely in saturated
potting soil in **14 days**. The thickest are 4 mm injection-moulded PHBV bars,
which lost **8 wt% in 365 days** of real harbour seawater.

Those two are not a controlled comparison — the environments differ — and this
project does not present them as one. What they establish is the span: the
published record on one polymer family runs from total loss in two weeks to
92 % of the mass still present after a year, and the variable that spans it is
almost never tabulated.

Containers are moulded in the second regime. Claims are made from the first.

A paper goes in as a PDF. A structured, cited row come

## 현재 상태

프로젝트 폴더와 공개 Git 저장소를 준비하는 단계다. 실행 가능한 앱과 API 연결은 아직 없다. Meta Model API 지원 크레딧 지급 후 본격적인 구현을 시작한다.

## 학습 경험

첫 과목은 수학이다. 7~8세 아이가 숫자를 누르면 책 위의 도토리 같은 사물이 늘어나거나 줄어드는 모션으로 수량 변화를 이해하게 한다. 사칙연산을 후보로 두고 첫 시연에서 다룰 연산과 페이지 수는 착수 때 정한다.

핵심은 아이가 직접 만지는 3D 책과 계산에 맞춰 움직이는 사물이다. 단순 문제 풀이 챗봇으로 만들지 않는다.

수학 시연을 예상보다 빨리 완성하고 검증까지 마친 경우에만 영어·한글·과학 중 한 과목의 학습 장면 하나를 추가한다. 추가 과목은 아직 정하지 않았다.

## 기술 방향

- Three.js로 책과 사물, 조작 및 모션을 구현한다. 구체적인 웹 프레임워크와 배포 서비스는 미정이다.
- 계산과 사물 개수는 일반 코드로 정확하게 처리한다.
- 앱 안에서 Meta AI 모델을 실제로 활용한다. 아이의 요청 해석이나 활동 구성은 후보이며, 구체적인 역할은 착수 때 결정한다.
- Meta Model API와 Muse Spark를 우선 검토한다. 실제 모델 이용 가능 여부와 요금은 연결 시점에 다시 확인한다.
- 개발 도구는 사용자가 익숙한 OpenCode를 사용할 예정이다. Muse Code 설치를 필수로 보지 않는다.
- 사용자는 OpenRouter의 Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor를 예비 수단으로 제안했다. 연결 가능 여부, 데이터 이용 조건, 별도 요금과 대회 적합성은 사용 전에 확인한다.
- API 비밀키는 공개 코드나 브라우저에 넣지 않는다. 중계용 서버리스 함수 등을 검토한다.

## 해커톤 준비

2026-10-26에 확인한 참가자 안내 기준이다. 재개할 때 최신 안내와 정식 규칙을 다시 확인한다.

- 공개 코드 저장소와 접근 가능한 3분 시연 영상이 필요하다.
- 심사는 코드, 시연 영상 및 실제 제품을 대상으로 한다.
- 행사 중 새로 만든 기능과 기여를 명확히 구분한다.
- 프로젝트에 Meta Model API 또는 Meta 공개 모델을 적절히 활용해야 한다.
- 제출 마감은 미국 동부 시간 2026-11-04 21:00이며, 한국 시간으로 2026-11-05 11:00이다.
- 개발과 검증, 시연을 우선하고 과목 추가는 남는 시간에 판단한다.

## 다음 작업

다음 세션의 진행 순서와 미결 질문은 [인계 메모](docs/HANDOFF.md)를 참고한다.

# PartForge

**Two photos of a broken part → measured, editable, printable CAD.**

Built for the [Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026](https://dev.meta.ai/events/global-hackathon)
(Oct 26 – Nov 4, 2026).

| | |
|---|---|
| Track | Indie developer (individual / student) |
| Theme | Push the Frontier — manufacturing & physical systems |
| Status | Day 1 working slice — photo → measured plate → live-edited CAD → STL/STEP |

## The idea

Reverse-engineering a replacement part usually starts with calipers and a lot of
guesswork. Photo-CAD aims to take one or more photos of a physical part and return a
parametric CAD model you can actually edit — dimensions, features, and sketch
geometry — rather than a dead triangle mesh.

Pipeline (measured, never hallucinated):

1. **Capture** — top + side + front photos, each on the printed calibration card.
2. **Segment** — click-select the broken instance with SAM 3.1 (OpenCV card fallback runs now).
3. **Measure** — deterministic OpenCV per view: top gives outline/holes/slots;
   side/front vote on thickness; an L-profile proposes a bracket bend.
4. **Fuse** — thickness votes average (disagreement asks you, caliper wins);
   mismatched poses are reported, never silently merged.
5. **Ask** — PartForge asks only the ambiguous dimensions (confirm thickness,
   uncertain holes, bend angle), via Muse Spark reasoning; typed/voice
   correction loop ("hole 2 is 5, not 4", "bend 90").
6. **Build** — spec → parametric build123d model (plate, or folded single-bend
   bracket), regenerated live on every edit.
7. **Verify** — CAD overlay on the rectified photo + caliper error table (coming).
8. **Print** — export STL (print) or STEP (edit in Fusion/Onshape).

Scope: flat plates + single-bend brackets with holes/slots. No gears, threads,
or freeform shapes.

## Tech

- **Meta Model APIs** — SAM 3.1 (instance selection), Muse Spark (interpretation,
  the one ambiguous question), Muse Voice Transcribe (hands-dirty correction loop).
  Thin wrappers in `partforge/meta_api.py`; app runs fully offline without keys.
- **Geometry** — OpenCV + ArUco calibration, build123d CAD, Streamlit + Three.js viewer
- **Output** — `PartSpec` JSON (single source of truth), STL, STEP

## Getting started

```bat
py -3.11 -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv\Scripts\streamlit run app.py
```

Then: hit **▶ Demo part** in the sidebar, or print the card
(sidebar → ⬇ Print card, at exactly 210×148 mm), lay the part on it, and upload a photo.

## Repo layout

```
.
├── app.py                  # Streamlit UI: upload 3 views -> 3D viewer -> edit -> export
├── partforge/
│   ├── spec.py             # PartSpec: outline/holes/slots/bend + thickness votes + questions
│   ├── card.py             # printable calibration card + ArUco rectification
│   ├── measure.py          # deterministic mm measurement from a photo
│   ├── fusion.py           # multi-view fusion: thickness votes + bend proposals
│   ├── synthetic.py

# Agentimo

![An independent agent in Lisbon updates their forecast by voice](docs/assets/agentimo-banner.jpg)
<sub>Banner generated with Meta's Muse Image.</sub>

**See how much of your commission is really yours, and keep it up to date by just talking.**

Agentimo is a cash-flow forecast for independent real-estate agents in Portugal, built by PropWare (CrmWare) for the [Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon](https://cerebralvalley.ai/e/meta-ai-developer-hackathon/). Startups track, theme "Build for Your World".

- **Live:** https://app.agentimo.propware.pt
- **Demo video (3 min):** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0M3KLqLW5Tk

## The problem

In Portugal, an independent agent is paid a share of the agency's commission. That money arrives months after the deal, with IVA (VAT) collected on top and income tax withheld. Before any of it is really theirs, the agent still has to set aside IRS and Social Security and pay their own fuel, lunches and phone. The director of a Portuguese real-estate association told us agents routinely treat the commission as profit and find out at year end that they earned far less. Most keep track in a spreadsheet, if at all.

## What Agentimo does

For every month, it answers three questions: what will reach my account, what must I protect, and what is really mine?

- **Forecast dashboard.** It shows the last three closed months and the next three expected ones. The expected months are split into confirmed, likely and potential deals, and a chart of what is really yours per month marks any month that goes negative.
- **Expenses with honest rules.**
  - A past month subtracts the expenses actually recorded.
  - A future month subtracts the agent's own estimate plus any planned expenses, so the agent never counts on money they will spend.
  - The current month subtracts the larger of what is recorded so far and the estimate.
- **One Speak button.** "New deal, a T4 in Infantado, December, 10,000 euros, 3%, potential." Agentimo asks only for what is missing, reads the deal back in one line and saves it when the agent says "yes". Changes ("the Alvalade deal moved to March") and expenses ("120 euros of lunch with client Alberto for the Infantado deal") work the same way.
- **Per-deal view.** Each deal shows what it leaves and its linked expenses. "Comissão" always means the agency's commission; the agent's part is "A tua parte" (your share).

## How it works: Meta's models interpret, deterministic code decides

```
voice (browser, 16 kHz WAV)
  → Muse Voice Transcribe 1.0   page language + domain keywords
  → Muse Spark 1.3              one JSON object: intent, kind, stated facts only
  → application code            missing fields, deal matching, one-line read-back
  → engine.calc                 every euro, in integer cents
  → agent says "sim"/"yes"      only then is anything saved
```

- **The model never touches money.** Amounts are computed by `engine/calc.py` from exact decimal rates, in integer cents, rounding half-up pe

# Petey Plant 🌱

A Duolingo-style gamified indoor plant pet app — built for the **Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon**.

Petey turns each plant into a reactive, expressive cartoon pet with HP bars, XP levels,
streaks, Mulch Shields (streak protection), a Duolingo-style "guilt engine", and a
deterministic ReAct agent that explains its reasoning step by step. Underneath the pet
is real plant-care math: Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD), Penman-Monteith-inspired soil
moisture decay, a camera EXIF light meter, leaf-lesion analysis, and a time-series
forecasting engine with uncertainty bands and anomaly detection.

> **Demo plants ship with synthetic history.** The 30-day histories are deterministic
> synthetic data for demo purposes — not real user watering data.

## Honest provider disclosure (read this first)

**No live Muse model call happens in this build.** The backend exposes a configurable
provider layer (`backend/config.py`):

| Env var | Default | Allowed values |
|---|---|---|
| `MUSE_MODEL_ID` | `muse-glimmer-30b` | `muse-glimmer-30b`, `muse-spark-open` |
| `MUSE_CREATIVE_MODEL` | `muse-image` | `muse-image`, `muse-wonder` |
| `MUSE_API_BASE` | `""` (empty) | Reserved for future wiring — **currently unused; no Muse HTTP call exists yet** |

With the defaults, every agent/creative result is produced by a **deterministic local
fallback** that returns the same response shapes a real model call would (triage
reasoning, avatar prompts, rig parameters). This is disclosed, not hidden:

- Every API response carries `X-Model-Provider: Meta-Muse-Open-Weights`,
  `X-Muse-Model-ID`, `X-Muse-Creative-Model`, **and `X-Muse-Fallback: true`**.
- `/health` and triage telemetry report `"fallback": true`.
- The Agent Brain drawer labels the run as a deterministic local fallback, and each
  trace step records measured per-step latency (not a fabricated constant).

Muse Spark Open and Muse Wonder are named only as allowed-but-not-wired values; this
build does not claim to call them. When real Muse endpoint credentials exist, the
provider layer is the single place to wire them in.

- **79 starter species records** across all 12 avatar archetypes and 25+ families —
  **not 10,000**. The file is named `seed_10k_species.py` for a future 10,000-record
  ingest target that is **not shipped**. `ingest_json_dump` is implemented but is not

- **31 of the 79 records carry source-verified qualitative data** (light, watering,
  soil moisture, humidity, temperature, pests/diseases, toxicity) cited to Missouri
  Botanical Garden, ASPCA, NC State Extension, RHS, UF/IFAS, and other extension
  sources, with per-field evidence

# ECHKILI Evidence Lab — Meta Hackathon 2026

An **offline-first, intentionally limited fictional vehicle-cabin diagnostics demo** for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026.

> All observations, case identities, labels, and outcomes in this demo are fictional. This is **not** a validated diagnostic service. It does **not** suggest repairs, provide safety clearance, or diagnose real equipment.

## What it demonstrates

- Selecting simulated observations from distinct sources.
- Traceability: each proposed explanation links to the evidence that supports it.
- Explicit contradiction detection and cautious human review.
- A server-audited **before/after evidence trace** that explicitly names new evidence, newly surfaced conflicts, and withdrawn hypotheses.
- A **three-step judge demo** (initial observations → corroboration → conflicting report and human review), with no Meta requests.
- A visual, source-cited **evidence graph and analysis-result panel** sharing one language switch for **English, French, and Arabic**; Arabic copy uses RTL while technical IDs and changing numeric tokens stay LTR.
- An always-visible uncertainty indicator (illustrative, **not** calibrated).
- A separate, optional Meta Model API enrichment path that is **disabled by default**.

The demo contains no ECHKILI production algorithms, real customer information, unreleased commercial datasets, or private monorepo code. **The commercial ECHKILI platform remains separate and private.**

## Run locally

Requires Python 3.10+; no third-party packages.

```bash
python -m demo.server
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:8765** on the same machine. The server refuses non-loopback addresses.

Try:

1. Click **Start guided demonstration** to run an auditable, three-step fictional story. Use **Next evidence step** twice, then **Replay** to restart.
2. Observe a tentative `h-flow` hypothesis; later add a new report that conflicts with `e1`. The previously surfaced `h-flow` explanation is **withdrawn**, uncertainty rises, and the system requires qualified review.
3. To explore manually, use **Try supporting evidence** or **Try a contradiction**, then click **Analyze selected evidence**.
4. Deselect everything to see the demo decline to infer a diagnosis.
5. After an analysis, scroll to the evidence graph and switch **Language · Langue · اللغة** to review the same fictional relations in three languages without another model call.

In production agentic and robotics pipelines, this produces two pervasive failure modes: 1. **Recursive Attractor Traps (Infinite Retry Loops):** When an external tool, API, or physical actuator stalls against an obstacle, static context windows trigger working-memory latching ($T-2, T-1$). # ClauseTrace

When a law changes, ClauseTrace finds which legal conclusions depended on it, re-checks only those, and shows exactly why each follows — or why it can't be established.

A version-aware legal verification engine, started at the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon. Demo domain: India's DPDP Act 2023 / DPDP Rules 2025 applied to a fictional data-processing agreement (Acme Retail / Nimbus Analytics).

ClauseTrace shows what follows from accepted premises and stated source versions. It does not assert that the law or premises are true, and it is not legal advice.

**3-minute demo video:** https://youtu.be/dTUU6wS-3lI
**Live demo:** https://meta-global-ai-developer-hackathon.vercel.app (sign in, then Review a clause — ask about clause 9.2)

## Why it's different

- **A dependency graph says what to re-check.** When a source version changes, reverse traversal marks only the findings that actually depended on the changed provision. An unrelated decoy source flags none.
- **An independent checker validates proofs.** The checker is a separate Python package with no model and no network. It never imports the agent. Muse Spark drafts; it cannot set a finding's status.
- **Validity is decided by propositional logic, deterministically.** Each proof is also checked as propositions (premises + inference rule ⊢ conclusion), which powers the what-if preview and the conflicting-interpretations state.
- **History is never overwritten.** Findings, source versions, provisions, and the audit log are append-only. A stale finding is replaced by a new row; the old one stays.

## What it does

- **Review a clause** — ask a question, get a checked answer with numbered reasoning, exact clause and section quotes, and the facts relied on (each labelled: confirmed by you / taken from the document / proposed, not yet approved).
- **Law changes** — preview a law change without saving anything (what-if), apply it, see only the affected answers move to a re-check queue, re-check them, and compare before/after answers.
- **Conflicting readings** — when two legal tests cited in one proof contradict each other, the answer is stored as "Two readings of the law conflict — your call", never silently resolved.
- **Your control room** — approve or challenge facts (approval mints a new confirmed copy; nothing is edited), correct fact wording, dictate a fact by voice or add a scanned page — both arrive as *proposed* facts that cannot support any answer until a lawyer approves them.
- **Evidence page** — every answer has a page with its reasoning, citations, facts, and earlier versions.
- Uploads run as tracked background jobs, including PDF files (text layer read directly; image-only pages transcribed, with a per-page confidence flag for spot-checking).
- **Contract understanding** — parties, obligations grouped by who owes them, defined terms and key dates extracted from the uploaded document, all as proposed items until a lawyer confirms them.

**Lunes** ("Monday" in Spanish) is an AI assistant for the electronics bench. Tony Stark had FRIDAY; a repair
technician in Cochabamba gets Lunes, the one who shows up to work on Monday.

You put a broken board on the bench and say "it doesn't work". Lunes looks at the board through a USB microscope,
tells you exactly where to probe, reads your instruments, compares every measurement against a simulation of the
circuit, picks the next most informative measurement, and finds the faulty component. The hands are yours; the
reasoning and the eyes are Lunes's.

microscope, a 2010 Kinect), speaks Spanish, and keeps working without internet on open weights (Muse Glimmer on one
consumer GPU). A student builds a circuit and the machine looks at it, points at the pin and measures it: learning
electronics by controlled physical debugging instead of guessing. And every session leaves a record of what was planned,
simulated, seen and measured on a real board. That is grounded data from the physical world that future AI models can
learn from, to understand real circuits and not only text about them.

# MolDeNovo

**An evidence-grounded medicinal chemistry copilot built on Meta's Muse models.**

### Try it now: https://moldenovo-ai.vercel.app/

No install needed. Hackathon track: *Push the Frontier* (accelerating a scientific experiment).
Demo video: *(https://youtu.be/mp_2YTwgDoI?si=xcV2IKFWnWxaPL89)*

> The first request after a quiet period can take up to a minute while the server wakes up. A campaign takes about a minute to run.

Early drug discovery needs tools that small labs can't afford, and AI that invents chemistry is dangerous in this field. MolDeNovo uses Meta's models to **see and plan**, and uses RDKit to **apply and verify**. No AI writes a molecule.

## How Meta's models are used

| Model | Job | Built-in check |
|---|---|---|
| **SAM 3.1** | Finds every structure in a figure from a paper | Each crop is shown to the user beside the result |
| **Muse Wonder** | Reads each structure as a SMILES string, twice at different reasoning effort | Two agreeing reads earn a green badge. A single read or a disagreement turns amber. RDKit rejects invalid molecules. The user confirms against an RDKit redraw |
| **Muse Spark 1.3** | Chooses the next edit from an approved menu, using your goals and matched-pair statistics | Cannot write SMILES. Its edit is applied by RDKit and checked by guardrails. If a call fails, a rule-based planner takes over |
| **Muse Image** | Made the hero artwork and the PDF cover | Decoration only. It draws no chemistry |

Everything chemical (properties, edits, validity, drawings, statistics) is computed by RDKit.

## What you can do

1. **Read figures.** Upload a figure with many structures. SAM finds them, Wonder reads them, RDKit checks them, and each result shows a badge as it arrives.
2. **Set the goal.** Choose a profile (oral, brain-penetrant, gut-restricted or custom), lock the groups to protect, and decide how close to stay to your molecule. A live preview shows your molecule and its properties against your limits.
3. **Run a campaign.** Spark proposes an edit, RDKit applies it, and the guardrails accept or reject it. Every rejection is logged with its reason.
4. **See the evidence.** Each step shows matched-pair statistics beside Spark's rationale. The numbers come from code, not from the model.
5. **Save and share.** Download the campaign as a project file, reopen it later with no model calls, or export a PDF report.

## Guardrails (enforced in code)

- Protected groups cannot be removed.
- The ring skeleton must be kept, and at most one ring C-to-N swap is allowed.
- A minimum similarity to the starting molecule.
- No new Lipinski, Veber or structural-alert violations.
- Each edit must move the molecule toward your target profile.
- The campaign stops when the goals are met.

## Results

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| SAM 3.1 on a 5-structure alkaloid figure | 5 of 5 structures found |
| Muse Wonder on 6 computer-drawn molecules, no names shown | 6 of 6 read correctly (checked by RDKit) |

> v0.20.78, the last commit before the 2026-11-04 9 PM ET deadline. Please judge that version. Development has
> continued on `main` since the deadline, so the default branch includes post-submission work.

MemriPal is a place-based recall coach for speeches, not a study chatbot. It turns any place you know into a memory
palace for a talk you must deliver (or exam facts, vocabulary). The demo palace starts from one photo of a familiar
space; SAM 3.1 segments distinct objects
into an ordered walking route of loci; Muse Spark splits your study list into items and writes a validated multisensory
association tying each item to its locus; Muse Image renders each scene onto the photo. You then walk the route
eyes closed and recall aloud; a deterministic matcher (no LLM) checks the Muse Voice Transcribe transcript, marks
each locus you recall and lists the ones you miss, with per-locus hit rates and chronic misses across rehearsals, so
you re-recite only those. The full encode-and-recall loop runs live against the Meta Model API or offline from
recorded fixtures.

On the page, Load demo builds the demo palace, renders its scenes and opens the walk view; the recall panel then
takes spoken recall (mic), typed answers (no mic, or the speech relay failed), or a replay of a recorded session.
While you speak, a board badged "LIVE" lights each point as you recall it (5 s slices through the same relay); the
replay lights the same board badged "recorded replay".
Each run is saved in the browser with a said-vs-palace view; deleting one asks to confirm and offers Undo. On the
end screen, "Mark got it" overrides a missed point (counts and hit rates update, kept across reloads). Stored runs
and hit rates show on page load in a history section; each row's "View" opens that run's said-vs-palace.
Runs saved in localStorage before IndexedDB was available are copied into IndexedDB once on page load.

Benchmarking language models as **drone navigators** and
**reconnaissance advisors** in simulated 3D disaster environments.

frontier + Modal-hosted HuggingFace. All runs tracked.

  perception (segmentation maps → routes + severity).
