nmuller17/Meta-Globlal-AI-Developer-Hack.readme_excerpt: # Doubloon **We monetize the web for agentic traffic.** *Any website. Any AI agent. Any piece of information. One payment.* Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026 · Startup track · Theme: Build for Your World · Maximilien Rambaud, Cosme de Ranieri, Aristote Pellissier, Nathanaël Muller AI agents are the web's fastest-growing audience: about 1.7% of web activity in 2026, a quarter of web traffic expected by 2035 (DataDome, June 2026; Cisco, 2026). They read pages without seeing ads or paying, so websites earn almost nothing from them, and blocking agents is their only safe default. On the other side, an agent that needs one precise figure can only scrape public pages, or buy a whole report built for humans, which it cannot do on its own. **We know both sides firsthand.** Before MIT, we worked in strategy consulting and M&A / private equity (BCG). We often needed one number the same day, a market share, a growth rate, a competitor figure, and the only way to get it was a €3,000 report or a yearly subscription. That research is now done more and more by AI agents, and agents cannot pay for a single fact: no credit card, no checkout page, no account. We saw the other side with one of our own websites: traffic and ad revenue kept falling as people asked AI assistants instead. The content was still read, by machines, but nobody paid for it. Doubloon makes every website **payable for all AI agent readers**. A content owner pastes its URL, and in about 60 seconds its content becomes data that any AI agent can discover, negotiate for and buy, with no code. For publishers, it is a **new revenue stream** from an audience that never sees an ad. For buyers, it is **access to information without buying the whole report**: one figure for 0.10 USDC, a small table for 0.50, a full section for 2.00, while the rest of the report stays protected. **Meta's Muse Spark does the language work.** It writes the catalog that agents browse, turns prices written in plain words into a price table, negotiates with buyer agents as the publisher's sales agent, and decides for our buyer agent whether an offer fits its mission. Code then checks every one of its answers: **a language model may propose, but only code decides price, permission and money.** Every sale runs on **x402**, the open protocol that finally puts HTTP's `402 Payment Required` to work. The agent receives an invoice, signs a payment and gets the data in seconds, settled in **USDC on the Base blockchain**. Every transaction is public and verifiable, and the publisher is paid before any data leaves. | At a glance | | | --- | --- | | Demo video | [3-minute demo on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=svdWuwi0hfs) | | Meta model | Muse Spark (`muse-spark-1.3`) on the Meta Model API, in four roles: [how Doubloon uses it](#how-doubloon-uses-muse-spark) | | Proof | 64 payments settled on-chain, 2 of them on Base mainnet with real USD

# BlueprintTo3D

Turn a residential floor-plan image into an interactive 3D reconstruction. Muse Spark 1.3 extracts strict-JSON
structure (walls, doors, windows, rooms, stairs, roof) with an optional deep verification pass; Three.js rebuilds
it locally in the browser. Remodel everything in the Build tab (move/add/delete with undo), walk inside in first
person, click any element to customize it (with Muse recommendations), verify symbols with SAM 3.1, restyle with
Muse Image, view in mobile AR, walk in VR, and export to GLB, DXF and CSV.

## Run locally

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local   # then add your META_API_KEY
npm run dev                  # http://localhost:3000
```

Without a key the app still runs: the three labeled samples work fully offline, and plan Q&A falls back to a
clearly labeled on-device geometry summary. Live uploads without a key return 503 and never substitute sample data.

## Checks

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm run build
```

## Pipeline

- `POST /api/analyze` — live Spark 1.3 vision extraction plus optional deep verification pass, or a labeled
  prebuilt archetype when `isDemo` is set.
- `POST /api/ask` — plan Q&A via Muse Wonder with Spark fallback, else a labeled local heuristic.
- `POST /api/recommend` — door/window product recommendation for one opening (style, material, color + reason).
- `POST /api/texture` — Muse Image finishes (facade, floor, roof) applied as tiling textures.
- `POST /api/sam` — SAM 3.1 symbol grounding, one concept per request, overlaid on the source image.
- `GET /api/health` — key status and model IDs.

## Editor

- Build tab: select / move / add-wall / add-door / add-window / add-decor / measure tools, undo + redo
  (Ctrl+Z/Y), element lists with delete. New walls snap to grid, 15° angles and existing endpoints.
- Furniture catalog (31 pieces incl. fireplace, vase, table lamp): sofas (2/3-seat), beds, dining sets,
  bath, office and decor. Click to place with a live ghost preview (R rotates) — on floors or on top of
  tables; then drag, lift, recolor, resize or swap variants.
- Everything is editable: wall geometry, height and thickness, all opening styles and dimensions, roof shape
  and finishes, room floors, working light switches, duplicate-anything (Ctrl+D).
- Start from a blank canvas to design from scratch, or from AI extraction.
- Projects autosave to the browser, with named slots and JSON export/import in the Export tab.

## Current limits

Single-floor 3D view. Dimensions, roof shape, furniture and heights may be inferred; confidence is the model's

# ReActSim

**A robot that imagines before it acts, and recovers when the world fights back.**

ReActSim is a closed-loop robot agent in a physics simulator. You give it an instruction in plain language. **SAM 3.1** finds the objects. **Muse Spark** plans with a fixed set of skills. A Franka Panda carries out the plan in ManiSkill 3, on a table of everyday YCB objects (a banana, a mug, a soup can, a plate). Then we interfere on purpose: knock the banana away, make the gripper drop it, move the target. The agent detects what went wrong from the physics state, explains the cause, and replans until the task is done.

> *From following instructions to understanding failures.*

Built for the **Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon**, *Push the Frontier* track.

**Results** (real ManiSkill runs, real Muse Spark, two-sided Fisher exact tests):

| | Muse Spark + Imagination | Rule-based retry | Muse Spark alone |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 objects × 2 disturbances, 20 seeds each | **116/120** | 105/120 (p=0.015) | – |
| From SAM 3.1 perception only (banana) | **40/40** | 34/40 (p=0.026) | 28/40 (p=0.0002) |
| Three goals, two containers | **28/30** | 18/30 (p=0.005) | – |

---

## What makes it different

| | Typical language-to-robot demo | ReActSim |
|---|---|---|
| Plan | One shot | Closed loop: perceive → plan → act → diagnose → replan |
| Choosing an action | The LLM's first guess | 🧠 **Imagination**: forks the physics, tries each candidate, keeps the best |
| Disturbances | Avoided | 😈 **Chaos Mode**: the audience types perturbations live |
| Success check | The LLM says "done" | The simulator's physical state (pose, contact, velocity) |
| Failure handling | Retry, or nothing | A typed diagnosis (grasp slip, object moved, drop, missed placement) plus a recovery aimed at that cause |

### 🧠 Imagination: real physics lookahead
Before a pick, the agent snapshots the simulator state (`get_state_dict`). It tries 9 grasp candidates: `top`, plus `angled` and `side` from the robot's side, its left, its right and the far side of the object. Each candidate runs together with the placement that follows it, because a grasp that holds can still make the object tip over when set down. Each result is scored with the same diagnoser used at runtime, and the state is restored. The planner's proposal stands when it works in physics and is overruled only when it fails. The real run then replays the exact joint commands of the winning rollout: motion planning is random, and replaying makes what was imagined what happens, to within 0.3 mm. Unreachable candidates fail in planning almost instantly, so trying nine takes about 3-4 s.

When no grasp works, the agent does not act. A candidate that only moves the object is imagined one step further, and the agent nudges only if a grasp then works. Otherwise Muse Spark hears which grasps were tried and why each failed, and changes strategy (pushes a neighbour aside, or gives up and says why).

# English

Afet Destek (Disaster Relief) is a Flutter application intended to connect
people affected by disasters with relief locations, logistics teams, and
crisis coordinators. It brings citizen reports, aid-location information,
and shipment tracking into role-based workflows.

> **Important:** This project is a prototype. Map locations and sample reports
> may contain demo data, and AI output can be inaccurate or incomplete. The
> app is not a replacement for official emergency services, AFAD, or the
> 112 Emergency Call Center. Call **112** in an urgent or life-threatening
> situation.

## Features

- **Citizens:** Create an account and sign in; submit a needs/disaster report
  with location; review AI-assisted category, urgency, and resource
  suggestions; find assembly areas, tent cities, relief and medical points on
  the map; request walking directions; share safety status and location with
  a safety circle; prepare SMS drafts; and use the SOS siren, vibration, and
  optional camera flashlight.
- **Carriers and logistics:** Create truck or van shipments for water, tents,
  medicine, infant formula, food, or blankets; select a destination; advance
  shipment status; and track destination stock. Stock is updated when a
  delivery is completed.
- **Crisis management:** Review live incoming reports and urgency filters,
  view report locations on the map, track response status, manage relief
  locations and stock, and monitor shipments.
- **Shared experience:** Turkish and English interface, light/dark themes, a
  role-based home screen, disaster map, AI triage, and a Llama-powered
  disaster assistant.
- **Connectivity:** Firestore streams synchronize report, area, and shipment
  data when Firebase is configured. Some reports can be saved as SMS drafts
  while offline; drafts are not sent automatically.

## Stack

Flutter and Dart; Firebase Authentication and Cloud Firestore; `flutter_map`,
`latlong2`, and `geolocator`; OpenRouteService for walking directions; and a
Meta AI/LLM API for the assistant and report classification, with local
fallback behavior in some flows.

## Setup

Install Flutter and Dart (the project specifies Dart `^3.9.2`), then run:

```sh
flutter pub get
```

Copy `secret.example.json` to `secret.json` and configure `META_API_KEY`,
`FIREBASE_API_KEY`, and `OPENROUTESERVICE_API_KEY`. If using your own Firebase
project, update the platform configuration in
[`lib/firebase_options.dart`](lib/firebase_options.dart) as well.

Run the app with:

```sh
flutter run --dart-define-from-file=secret.json
```

In VS Code, choose an `Afet Destek` launch configuration and press **F5**.
Never commit or share `secret.json`. Client-side API keys can be extracted
from published builds; use server-side proxies and restrict keys for
production. See [`DEVELOPMENT.md`](DEVELOPMENT.md) for local setup notes.

## Validation

```sh
flutter analyze
flutter test
```

# LYLO Mechanic

**LYLO Mechanic is an Android phone app that tells you what's wrong with your car, in plain English, using Meta AI.** You don't need any special tools. Tell it what's happening, type a code, or take a photo of your dashboard lights. If you have a small plug-in car reader (an "OBD adapter"), LYLO can also read your car's computer directly.

It answers the question most people actually have: **is it safe to drive?** **Fixed safety rules set the floor. The AI can only make the answer more cautious, never less.** Then it explains what is probably wrong, what to do next, and roughly what it might cost, and it shows the evidence behind every answer.

**LYLO stands for Love Your Loved Ones.** Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Oct 26 – Nov 4, 2026).

## Watch, try, download
- **Demo video:** https://youtu.be/4lrNDRI9mP0
- **Try it in your web browser (no install):** https://lylo-api.thegoodneighborguard.com/try (describe the problem, type a code, add a dash photo; rate-limited)
- **Android app, v0.7.8:** [lylo-078-8a54f0a.apk](https://zion.thegoodneighborguard.com/lylo-078-8a54f0a.apk), sha256 `29a98f958e4ef19709b04a49a251503509fc0879e87cf429688f6bc1342db2c4`. It's a debug-signed test build, so allow "install unknown apps". There is no iPhone version.
- **Website:** https://thegoodneighborguard.com
- **Scanner (optional):** works with OBDLink Bluetooth adapters. They plug into the port under the dashboard, near the steering wheel. See what one looks like: https://www.obdlink.com/products/obdlink-mxp/
- **No scanner? It still works.** Use a photo and a description of the problem.

## Why Chris built it
Chris (the builder) borrowed $2,000 for a used car. It looked and drove fine. Two weeks later the check-engine light came on (P0300, misfire). He replaced the coil pack and cleared the code, and two days later it was back. Three weeks after that the transmission failed, stuck in reverse, and the car was a total loss. The seller had a shop and most likely cleared the codes just before the sale. Chris had no proof. **LYLO shows when codes were recently cleared**, so buyers and drivers get that proof.

## What you can do with it
**No adapter needed:**
- **Tell LYLO what's wrong**, by typing or talking. It asks up to 3 follow-up questions and gives you likely causes and a fix-it card.
- **Type a trouble code** (like P0302) and get its meaning in plain words. Works offline for 9,415 standard codes.
- **Snap your dashboard lights** and LYLO reads them from the photo.
- **Photo Helper:** take a photo under the hood and LYLO circles the part you're looking for (for example the air filter).
- **Your car's ID number (VIN):** type it or photograph it, and see recalls for your model.
- **Price help:** rough repair cost ranges, plus buttons that search parts stores and how-to videos.

# QuickAisle

Snap a store map (or use a saved store), type / photograph / say your
shopping list, and get the shortest walking route through the store.

Who it helps: shoppers in big unfamiliar stores, people with limited
mobility or time, and store staff picking orders.

## Try it

- Web: https://quickaisle.pages.dev — the sample stores work fully
  offline in the browser (bundled store, on-device matching and routing).
- Android APK: GitHub Releases (link added at release).
- Demo video: https://youtu.be/wQ-Z9OLb3tE

The demo is rate-limited: 40 AI units per hour per visitor, 400 units
per day total across everyone. A map read costs 3–6 units, a list photo
2, resolving terms or transcription 1 each. When the limit is hit the
server answers 429 ("Demo limit reached — try again later or use the
sample store") and the app shows that message; the sample store and
offline matching keep working.

## Core idea

AI drafts, a human reviews, an exact solver routes.

The AI never decides the route. Once items are matched to stops, an
exact Held–Karp solver (up to 15 stops, greedy heuristic above that)
finds the shortest path over the store's walkway graph — computed on
the phone, not by the model.

## How it works

```
map photo ──> /ingest ──> AI draft ──> YOU review ──> walkway graph
typed / photo / spoken list ──> matching ──┐
                                            ├─> exact solver ──> route
store walkway graph ────────────────────────┘
```

Server (Hono Worker, keys only server-side):

- `/read-list` — list/recipe photo → items. Meta `muse-spark-1.3`
  primary, Baseten hedge if it hasn't answered in 8 s.
- `/resolve` — messy terms → catalog matches. Baseten primary
  (`meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026`, Meta open weights — it won the
  T3 eval), Meta hedge after 12 s.
- `/ingest` — store map → layout draft. Meta only, no fallback:
  3 parallel reads + majority merge. Two-view: the map is also read
  rotated 90° so sideways aisle labels read upright; each aisle takes
  items from the view where its labels are upright, geometry always
  from the original. 6 Meta calls, ~30–35 s per map.
- `/voice-list` — spoken list → transcript → text box → normal
  matching. Meta speech-to-text (`muse-voice-transcribe-1.0`);
  16/24 kHz mono 16-bit WAV only, 30 s cap.

On the phone, offline: matching (fuzzy + learned aliases +
staple→department fallback, e.g. eggs → Dairy), routing, map drawing.
API keys live only in the Worker — never in the app, repo, or
`EXPO_PUBLIC_*`.

## Add a store

Photo of the store map → AI draft → review screen → saved on device.
The review screen is required: you fix aisle numbers, orientations,
and items before anything is saved. Then code (not the model) builds
the walkway graph from the draft (`build-from-draft`) and the store is
saved on the device.

Tip: for wide maps, hold your phone sideways so the whole map fills
the photo.

## Results

T1–T4 numbers come from the eval runner (`eval/`, summaries in `eval/results/*-summary.md`

# Expert judge: stop rules learned from an expert

Our solution to the Plata challenge below. It is for teams who need an LLM judge that agrees with their domain expert and can show why.

**What it does.** The expert labels conversations like a credit policy with stop factors: one violated rule makes a conversation `bad`. `adapt` recovers that policy from the labeled training conversations as an explicit rulebook. A strong model induces rules per topic from each `bad` conversation next to its most similar `good` one and merges the requirements shared by all topics into global rules. A checker model audits the rules blind on the training set. Refinement then revises a topic's rules, or adds an exception to a global rule that holds in that topic only, and is kept only if training accuracy rises and does not fall on a held-out half. Rules that flag as many `good` as `bad` conversations, and topic rules backed by fewer than two `bad` ones, are disabled. Students often receive course material as static files. Meet Mita tests a focused design idea: a familiar, character-led presentation may make those materials easier to begin and easier to stay with. These figures describe the intended audience's digital and media context; they do not measure Meet Mita's impact.

## How Mita supports a learner

Mita is designed to be a warm, curious guide who explains unfamiliar terms in everyday language before using the formal vocabulary. Her playful side serves the explanation, and she treats a mistake as something to work through. When a correction matters, her guidance stays direct and respectful.

# meta-ai-hackathon
Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon repository

대회링크: https://cerebralvalley.ai/e/meta-ai-developer-hackathon

## SIGNAL WAR

자연어 전략으로 지휘하는 1:1 멀티 에이전트 절차 생성 3D 전장의 게임. Spark 사령관 → 역할별 Glimmer 수행자 → 엔진의 동시 판정 → Muse Image 결과 일러스트 → 경기 아카이브.

[제품·기술 설계](SIGNAL_WAR_DESIGN.md)

### 로컬 실행

Node.js 20.9+ 및 Python 3.12+가 필요합니다. 저장소 루트에서:

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r backend/requirements.txt
npm install --prefix web
```

한 번에 실행하려면 `./dev.sh`를 사용합니다. 또는 두 터미널에서 각각 실행합니다.

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m uvicorn backend.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
```

```sh
npm run dev --prefix web
```

http://127.0.0.1:3000 에서 확인합니다. 메인(경기 설정) → 에이전트 선택 → 전장 순서로 진행합니다. 규칙·도구·성격·페르소나 선택은 아직 목업이며 경기에 반영되지 않습니다. 최초 실행은 **엔진 테스트 / AI 미사용** 모드입니다. 5000×5000 자유 지형(비대칭 랜덤: 양 기지·강·다리·숲·바위·호수)이 생성되고, 세 거점 ALPHA/BRAVO/CHARLIE는 양 기지에서 걸어서 가는 거리가 거의 같은 곳에 놓입니다. 사령관 또는 개별 캐릭터를 선택해 전략을 입력하고 전달한 뒤 `EXECUTE`(자동 진행) 또는 `1 TURN`(한 턴)을 누릅니다. 새 전장 생성에서 바이옴과 시드를 바꿀 수 있습니다. 같은 시드는 같은 전장이 됩니다. 종료 후 아카이브에서 경기 기록과 리플레이를 다시 열 수 있습니다. 현재는 동일 브라우저에서 양쪽을 입력하는 hot-seat 방식이며 원격 두 사용자 매칭은 아직 없습니다.

조작: `1–4` 캐릭터 선택·포커스, `WASD`/방향키/화면 가장자리 카메라 이동, 드래그 회전, 우클릭 드래그 이동, 스크롤 확대, `F` 선택 대상 포커스, `R` 전체 맵, `V` 전장의 안개, `SPACE` 자동 진행/정지, `N` 한 턴. 미니맵을 클릭하면 카메라가 이동합니다. 유닛은 `move(x, y)`로 임의 지점을 목표로 받고 엔진이 장애물을 피해 턴당 최대 500u 이동합니다. 숲·바위는 통행과 시야를 막고, 강은 다리에서 건널 수 있습니다. 지도·에이전트·거점·판정은 같은 서버 지형 데이터를 사용합니다. 규칙 수치는 [설계 문서](SIGNAL_WAR_DESIGN.md#경기-규칙-v03--5000u-자유-필드)에 있습니다.

21×21 격자 시절 경기 기록은 새 지형 형식과 호환되지 않아 아카이브에 표시되지 않습니다(DB에는 남아 있습니다).

### 실제 모델 연결

루트 `.env`는 백엔드만 읽습니다. 기존 `.env`를 덮어쓰지 말고 `.env.example`에서 필요한 값을 추가하세요.

```dotenv
MODEL_API_KEY=your_meta_key
WORKER_PROVIDER=glimmer
GLIMMER_BASE_URL=https://your-glimmer-server.example/v1
GLIMMER_MODEL=your-provider-model-id
GLIMMER_API_KEY=your_provider_key_if_required
```

Glimmer는 Meta API에서 자동 제공되지 않습니다. 별도 추론 서버가 필요합니다. 설정한 주소는 OpenAI 호환 `/chat/completions`를 지원해야 합니다.

받은 Baseten 키로 수행자를 실행하려면 아래처럼 **명시적으로 모델을 교체**할 수 있습니다. UI와 경기 기록에도 Glimmer가 아닌 Spark Open으로 표시합니다.

```dotenv
WORKER_PROVIDER=baseten
BASETEN_API_KEY=your_hackathon_key
```

이 경우 모델 ID는 코드에서 `meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026`으로 고정합니다. 설정 변경 후 백엔드를 재시작하고 화면을 새로고침하세요. 우측 상단 설정에서 연결 상태를 확인하고 새 대결의 실행 모드를 선택합니다. `설정됨`은 실제 호출 성공을 보장하지 않습니다.

사령관 연결만 1회 유료 검증하는 선택 명령:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m backend.smoke
```

경기 종료 후 `Muse Image 결과 생성`을 누르면 Meta 크레딧을 사용하는 실제 생성 요청이 발생합니다. 이미지는 `.data/images/`, 경기·이벤트·프레임은 `.data/battles.sqlite3`에 저장합니다. 생성하지 않은 이미지를 생성 완료로 표시하지 않습니다.

### 배포

- Next.js: Vercel의 프로젝트 Root Directory를 `web`으로 설정합니다.
- Python: `backend/modal_app.py`에 Modal 배포 설정을 제공합니다. Glimmer 모델 자체의 GPU 배포와는 별개입니다.
- Modal secret `signal-war`: `MODEL_API_KEY`, 수행자 설정, 강한 `BACKEND_TOKEN`을 저장합니다. 키를 Git에 넣지 않습니다.
- Vercel 서버 환경 변수: `BACKEND_URL`과 같은 `BACKEND_TOKEN`을 설정합니다. 로컬에서 토큰을 사용하려면 `web/.env.local`에도 설정합니다.

# Proof-Carrying Code

Turn Python functions into formally verified Dafny code, together with its proof.

Built for the [Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026](https://dev.meta.ai/events/global-hackathon).

## Built during the hackathon

Everything in this repository was created after the official hackathon kickoff on October 26, 2026, 12:00 PM ET.
No code, data or assets were prepared before the event.

## What it does

Every Python function gets one of two things: a proof certificate, a Dafny file with spec and proof that anyone can
re-check with `dafny verify`, or a counterexample, a concrete input on which the code breaks its spec, delivered as a
ready-to-run Python test. The pipeline collects context, writes the intent in plain text and the spec as an executable
Python predicate without ever seeing the function body, translates the function to Dafny with a rule-based transpiler
(or a model fallback where the transpiler cannot reach), proves it with escalating prover stages, searches for a
counterexample only after a failed proof, and reports one result per function (`proven`, `counterexample`, `open` or
`not_checkable`) with its certificate and assumptions. Certificates live with the code under `proofs/` and stay
re-checkable without this package.

One example pull request comment:

```markdown
<!-- pcc-check -->
## Proof-carrying code

12 proven, 1 counterexample, 3 open.

### ❌ `strings/palindrome.py::is_palindrome_recursive` — counterexample (transpiler)

Intent: return whether the string reads the same forward and backward (docstring).

```python
def test_palindrome_counterexample():
    assert is_palindrome_recursive("abcdba") is True
```

`pre` accepted 100% of the generated inputs. Assumptions: none.

<details><summary>Dafny spec</summary>

```dafny
predicate spec(s: string, result: bool) {
  result == (s == Reverse(s))
}
```

</details>
```

## Quick start

Add the action to a repository that holds the Python code to check. Store a Meta Model API key as an Actions secret
named `META_API_KEY`; the action sets `PCC_META_ALLOWED=1` for its own run and never bakes a key in.

```yaml
name: proof-carrying-code
on:
  pull_request:
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: hosbe1/Proof-Carrying-Code-Meta-AI-Hackathon-2026@main
        with:
          meta-api-key: ${{ secrets.META_API_KEY }}
```

`fetch-depth: 0` provides the Git history needed to compare against the pull request's base branch.

On each pull request the action checks the changed functions plus affected callers with `pcc-check run`, uploads the
`proofs/` certificates as a workflow artifact, and updates one comment on the pull request. The check turns red only on
a real finding: a `counterexample`, or a stale certificate whose function is no longer proven.

# BenchTruth

**A hardware build verifier that refuses impossible builds — with the physics, the cost,
and the fix.**

Anyone can prompt a chatbot for a wiring diagram. BenchTruth is the one that tells you
your build **cannot work**: it names the violated rule, explains the physics in physical
terms, prices each way out, and then proves the corrected build.

```
user prompt
   → Muse Spark 1.3  → project_spec.json      (intent only: no pins, no code, no geometry)
   → SOLVER          → plan.json              (pins, I2C, power, mechanical, violations)
   → renderers       → artifacts              (BOM, wiring table, .ino, diagram.json, plate, drill template)
   → compile gate → simulation → teaching panel
```

**The models do what models are good at; the deterministic engine decides what is true.**

---

## The refusal card, verbatim

```
❌ CANNOT BUILD AS SPECIFIED
esp32-devkitc-v4 · 5 signals

R17: MQ-2 gas/smoke sensor (LPG, methane, smoke) analog output can exceed the 3.3 V ADC range
  Why it matters: The ADC saturates at 3.3 V. Anything above that reads as full-scale
  forever -- a silent, wrong measurement.
  A. Add a resistor divider (measure the output first) · Rp 3,000–10,000 · 2 resistors
  B. Power the sensor from 3.3 V if it allows · - · move one jumper

R12: 250 mA of loads must run off the board itself
  Why it matters: Servos, motors and LED strips draw stall current far beyond the 3V3
  regulator. The board will brown out and reset.
  A. Add a separate 5 V supply with a common ground · Rp 40,000–120,000 · 2 extra wires
  B. Use a PCA9685 driver on its own supply · Rp 18,000–45,000 · +3 solder points
  C. Allow an external supply · - · free

R11: 3V3 rail needs 540 mA but the board is rated 300 mA
  Why it matters: Breakdown on the 3V3 rail: SG90 micro servo 250 mA, 0.96in SSD1306
  OLED 20 mA, Piezo buzzer 30 mA, WiFi TX reserve 240 mA. Over budget by 240 mA.
  A. Move the load to VIN (5 V) with a common ground · - · 2 extra wires
  B. Add an external supply · Rp 40,000–120,000 · 1 supply
  C. Drop the heaviest peripheral · - · edit the request

Pick one and I will rebuild, recompile and re-simulate.
```

Every pin that survives to the plan is justified: `MQ-2 → GPIO 33 (ADC1)`,
`SSD1306 → 21/22 (shared I²C bus)`, `SG90 → GPIO 32 (PWM/LEDC capable)`.

---

## The verification corpus

`eval/cases.json` holds 20 mutually conflicting specs; `eval/golden_specs.json` holds a
hand-written spec for each. The harness never calls a model, so the number measures the
solver and nothing else.

| Case | Conflict | Rule | Verdict |

# HEARSAY

A 2D space exploration game where the galaxy is built from rumors, and the people telling them might be lying.

The game engine decides what is true. A local Llama model decides how each character *says* it: charming, nervous, lonely, or scheming. Lies spread between NPCs and mutate as they travel, growing more confident, more rewarding, and more dangerous with every retelling.

## Run it (scripted dialogue, no AI needed)

You need Python 3.10 or newer.

```
pip install -r requirements.txt
python main.py
```

On Mac, use `pip3` and `python3` if `pip`/`python` don't work.

## Turn on the AI dialogue (Llama)

1. Install Ollama from https://ollama.com
2. Download Meta's small Llama model (about 1.3 GB):
   ```
   ollama pull llama3.2:1b
   ```
3. Start the game as usual. The top-right corner says `AI: llama3.2:1b` when it's connected.

Want a bigger model? `ollama pull llama3.2:3b`, then run with
`HEARSAY_MODEL=llama3.2:3b python main.py` (Mac/Linux) or
`set HEARSAY_MODEL=llama3.2:3b` then `python main.py` (Windows).

If the model isn't running, the game uses handwritten lines, so it never breaks during a demo.

## Controls

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| W / ↑ | Thrust |
| A D / ← → | Turn |
| Space | Fire |
| E | Dock and talk / leave |
| 1 | "Where did you hear that?" |
| F1 | Truth debug view (shows the real cache and whether the NPC lied) |
| P | Save a screenshot |
| Esc | Quit |

## How it works

- `main.py` — the game: flying, combat, NPC minds, and the rumor system.
- `llm.py` — sends each NPC's personality, mood, and the engine's decision (truth, lie, or mistaken) to Llama, and gets back one or two lines. Runs in the background so the game never freezes. Lines that point the wrong direction are rejected, so the AI can't break the world's logic.

Built to run later on a Raspberry Pi 5 (8 GB) handheld.

# Chef in Your Ear

**A voice-first WhatsApp sous-chef that saves family recipes before they disappear — then calls you back and cooks alongside you, step by step, hands-free.**

Every family has a recipe that only lives in one person's memory. The problem is never that people don't want to preserve it; it's that archiving tools ask them to sit down and type into a form. They won't. But they will happily send a voice note to WhatsApp.

So that's the entire entry point. A grandmother records herself explaining how she makes rendang, in her own language and her own words — *"sejemput"*, *"sampai minyak naik"*. The **AI sous-chef** transcribes it with Whisper, then uses Meta Llama to structure it into a real recipe: name, ingredients, steps, region, even the family or clan name she mentions. Where she speaks in folk measurements, we keep her exact phrasing and add metric estimates beside it, because the original wording *is* the heritage. Within seconds she gets a voice reply back in WhatsApp confirming the recipe is saved — and the original recording is archived alongside it, so the sound of her voice is preserved too.

The second half is where the archive comes alive. On a recipe page there's a button: **Cook via Call**. Tap it and WhatsApp actually rings. The call is terminated over SIP into Asterisk, which hands the audio to your **chef on the line**. It greets you — *"Ready when you are, chef"* — reads step one, and waits. Say *"next"* and it moves on. Say *"repeat"* and it goes back. Ask *"how much coconut milk?"* and it answers from that specific recipe's context, in two sentences, out loud. Your hands stay in the dough the whole time. At the end of the last step: *"That's the whole recipe, chef. Selamat makan."*

Under the hood it's three services working together: a Node/TypeScript gateway that verifies Meta's webhook signature and acknowledges in under 200 milliseconds, a Redis-backed reliable queue, and a Python worker running the transcription, structuring, storage, and speech synthesis pipeline. A web vault lets family members manage recipes, control privacy, and share publicly if they choose. The build is genuinely production-shaped — duplicate messages are deduplicated, forged webhooks are rejected, failed jobs return errors so Meta retries, and in-flight jobs are requeued if the worker crashes.

We built this because cultural knowledge doesn't get lost in one dramatic moment. It gets lost quietly, one unwritten recipe at a time. **Chef in Your Ear makes preservation as easy as talking — then turns every saved recipe into a chef who's always available, always patient, and always in your ear.**

# Кейс хакатона: расчет массы шлака и металла по ИК-видео разливки стали

## 1. Краткое описание

В металлургическом производстве при разливке жидкой стали важно контролировать попадание шлака в конечный расплав. Шлак ухудшает качество металла, повышает риск неметаллических включений и может приводить к отклонениям в дальнейшей обработке плавки.

Участникам хакатона предоставляется набор видеозаписей разливки жидкой стали, снятых в длинноволновом инфракрасном диапазоне. В таком спектре шлак обычно выглядит более ярким по сравнению с металлом из-за различий в тепловом излучении и свойствах поверхности. Известно, что содержание шлака часто резко увеличивается ближе к концу разливки и обычно составляет не более нескольких процентов от общей массы расплава.

Задача участников — разработать метод, который по ИК-видео, известному диаметру струи и частоте кадров оценивает:

1. массу шлака, попавшего в конечный расплав;
2. массу металла, прошедшего через струю;
3. при необходимости — временную динамику доли шлака и момент начала интенсивного шлакоуноса.

В датасете нет готовых значений массы. Команды должны самостоятельно предложить модель перехода от видеоданных к массовым характеристикам процесса.

Диаметр струи: 180 мм.
Допустимая конечная масса шлака: от 500 до 2000 кг.
Датасет: https://storage.yandexcloud.net/geryon-shared-bucket/DM-CV-Dataset/Digital%20metallurgy.v1i.yolov8.zip

---

## 2. Производственная легенда

На металлургическом предприятии выполняется разливка жидкой стали. На большей части процесса через выпускное отверстие проходит преимущественно металл. Однако ближе к завершению разливки уровень металла в агрегате снижается, поток становится менее стабильным, и в струю может начать попадать шлак.

Даже если суммарная доля шлака невелика, его попадание в конечный расплав критично для качества стали. Визуальный контроль оператором не всегда надежен: процесс происходит при высокой температуре, присутствуют дым, пар, засветки, вибрации, нестабильная форма струи и ограниченная видимость.

Предприятие хочет получить прототип интеллектуальной системы, которая по ИК-видео сможет оценивать, сколько металла и сколько шлака прошло через струю во время разливки. Такая система может использоваться для постанализа плавок, контроля качества, формирования технологических рекомендаций и дальнейшего перехода к онлайн-поддержке оператора.

---

## 3. Данные

Участникам предоставляются видеозаписи или последовательности кадров процесса разливки жидкой стали в длинноволновом ИК-диапазоне.

В датасете отсутствуют:

- фактическая масса всей плавки;
- фактическая масса металла;
- фактическая масса шлака;
- данные весов;
- датчики расхода;
- покадровые физические измерения скорости потока;
- готовые значения целевой переменной.

./tools/mongodb/mongo.sh start    # start (fork) the instance
./tools/mongodb/mongo.sh status   # check it reported ready
./tools/mongodb/mongo.sh stop     # shut it down
```

Point the app at it with `MONGODB_URI=mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017` in `.env`

OAuth2 password flow with JWT (HS256 access tokens, 30 min) plus rotating
refresh tokens (7 days). Passwords are bcrypt-hashed (12 rounds); the app
refuses to start with a `JWT_SECRET_KEY` shorter than 32 bytes.

```bash
# register (role defaults to resident; admin is never self-granted)
curl -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/auth/register \

`GET /api/v1/auth/users` is visible to

# Trace

**Understand any Python codebase visually. Ask a question, watch an AI agent trace the answer through the code, and learn the codebase one node at a time.**


## The problem

Developers constantly land in code they did not write: a new job, an open-source repo, or code generated by an AI. The usual way to understand it is to grep across dozens of files and hold the call chain in your head. That is slow, and it is easy to get wrong.

## What Trace does

Trace turns a Python repo into an interactive graph, then lets an AI agent answer questions by walking that graph. Every claim the agent makes is checked against the real code before you see it, and the claims that fail are sent back to the model once to fix.

## Main features

- **Any public Python repo:** the Repositories page takes a GitHub URL, clones it, finds where its imports start and builds the graph in seconds. Switch between repos from the breadcrumb.
- **Codebase view:** modules and files as a map of the repo.
- **Click to code:** click any node to open the exact file and line in a code panel.
- **Ask the codebase:** ask "How does a user log in?" and watch the agent trace the answer node by node across the map. Every claim shows whether it was verified, and links to the line that proves it. Edges the parser could not resolve are dashed.
- **Repair:** claims the validator rejects, and gaps in the path, go back to the model for one round of fixes. The answer shows its first draft's tally next to the final one.
- **Agent trace:** a tab in the answer panel with every tool call the agent made, its arguments and results, and the timing of each step, then the answer, the validation and the repair.
- **Graphify:** from the code panel, take one file apart. Its functions become blocks of real code, and arrows run from each calling line to what it calls.
- **Ask about a file or a block:** a question typed on a file's page is about that file. Select a block first and it shows in the ask box, and the agent starts from that function.
- **Recorded questions:** ten answers recorded on the demo repo replay instantly. Anything else runs live.
- **Developer-tool shell:** a ⌘K search, a collapsible sidebar (⌘B), and Auto or Manual playback that steps through an answer one node at a time.

# Shrimp size check

Entry for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026, Indie Developer track (solo). Build period 27 Oct to 4 Nov 2026; all project code in this repository was written in that period.

## What it does
A small shrimp farmer decides every few days whether the shrimp are still growing. Today the only way is a cast net sample: catch about 1 kg, weigh it, count by hand. It takes about 15 minutes and two people, hurts the shrimp, and the result depends on luck.

Here the farmer lays about 10 shrimp flat next to a ruler and sends one photo to a Messenger bot. The bot answers with:
- the photo with every shrimp outlined, a line along its body, its number and its length;
- the number of shrimp measured, the average length and the size in shrimp per kg;
- a short Vietnamese text written by Muse Spark.

The farmer can reply "có" to save the sample, or type the numbers of the shrimp to count (for example `1 3 5`). A web dashboard shows the trend over samples, a hint when growth looks slow, and what a day without growth costs in feed. The app never tells the farmer to harvest or sell; the farmer decides.

## How the Meta models are used
- **SAM 3.1** finds each shrimp and the ruler (one noun phrase per request: "shrimp", "ruler", "credit card"). Code turns the masks into millimetres: the scale comes from the ruler, and each length follows the curved body (longest path of the skeleton), not the bounding box.
- **Muse Spark 1.3** writes the reply text from the structured result. Every number in its text must appear in the result, words that tell the farmer to harvest or sell are refused, and any failure falls back to a fixed Vietnamese template.
- Rules live in code, never in a language model: the length table, thresholds, the slow-growth hint and the cost of a day without growth are plain Python with tests.

## Honest limits
- One pond only: samples, feed entries and all settings are shared. Several ponds (each with its own name, stocking date, feed and thresholds, picked in the bot with a command such as "ao 2") is the next step and is not built.
- Evidence is one farmer's call and market shrimp laid flat; the farmer was not farming during the build, so there are no pond photos.
- The size table is a temporary public length-weight formula (Chow and Sandifer 1991), labelled "temporary table, not the CP table" on screen; it can be off by 20% or more.
- The dashboard history in the demo is demo data and is labelled as such. Measured error against hand measurements is in `docs/results/error-table.md` when present (n stated there).
- The slow-growth hint is noisy: the spread of one tray's mean length can exceed 0.33 mm a day over 3 days. It is information only.

## Run it
Python 3.8 and Node 22.

# 🌾 Krishi Mitra: a voice-first farming agent in Telugu, Hindi and English

Built for the **Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon** (Indie track, "Build for Your World").
**Everything in this repository was built during the hackathon window (Oct 27 – Nov 4, 2026).**

## The problem
Small farmers in India often cannot type long questions, read English websites, or find out which
government schemes they qualify for. Prices, weather and expert advice live in different places.
Krishi Mitra lets a farmer **speak** (or type, or send a **photo** of the crop) in their own language and get a
short, practical answer, read aloud if they want.

## What it does
- **Voice in, in any of 3 languages:** Telugu, Hindi, English (auto-detected, or pick one).
- **Photo to action plan:** one crop photo goes through the *same agent* (vision + tool calling): it names the likely problem and how sure it is, checks the weather to time spraying, mentions crop insurance if there is real loss, and sends the farmer to a human expert when unsure.
- **Multi-turn:** follow-up questions work ("and groundnut?"). Quick-ask buttons for common questions.
- **A real agent, not a chatbot:** the model decides which tools to call, in several steps:
  `get_mandi_price`, `best_markets` (where to sell for the highest price) and `get_price_trend` (rising or falling? sell now or wait?), all from Agmarknet via data.gov.in, `get_weather` (Open-Meteo),
  `check_schemes` (PM-KISAN, PMFBY, KCC, state support, with the documents needed), `calculate_revenue` (exact income maths, never done by the model), `get_expert_help` (Kisan Call Centre 1800-180-1551), plus the advisor tools below (`get_msp`, `net_market_value`, `spray_window`, `lookup_problem`, `hold_or_sell`).
- **Live agent steps:** the answer streams its progress ("checking mandi prices… checking weather… re-checking figures") so the farmer, and the judge, can see the agent working. Endpoints: `/api/agent/stream` and `/api/diagnose/stream` (newline-delimited JSON).
- **Sell now or wait:** the agent combines the price trend, best markets and the weather forecast into one clear recommendation (guidance, not a guarantee).
- **The agent can always talk:** browser voice when the device has one for the language, otherwise a server-generated voice (`/api/tts`, gTTS), so Telugu and Hindi are audible even on laptops without those voices.
- **Works on weak networks:** installable PWA with an offline shell; saved answers stay readable and playable offline; large-text mode for older farmers.
- **Verification layer (idea from Meta's Agents 102 workshop):** every figure in the final answer must come from a tool result.
  Otherwise the answer is sent back for a rewrite, and if it still fails the farmer sees an explicit "could not verify" warning, never a confident made-up number.
- **Honest about limits:** no pesticide doses, escalates to a human expert when unsure, says when price data is sample data.
- **New chat UI:** WhatsApp-style conversation, hands-free

﻿# fasal doctor

A crop doctor that tells Indian vegetable farmers whether to spray again, by re-measuring the damage on the same leaves and checking the bottle label's dose before they spray.

Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Cerebral Valley, Oct 26 - Nov 4, 2026).

## The problem

Crop diagnosis apps name a disease from a photo, but the farmer still has to guess how much to spray. Surveys of Indian vegetable growers report widespread overdosing and pesticide labels farmers can't read. The diagnosis apps we checked don't re-measure the same leaves to tell the farmer whether to spray again.

## What it does

1. The farmer sends a leaf photo next to a printed scale card and a voice note in their own language (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu or Marathi).
2. SAM 3.1 masks every lesion and measures the affected leaf area.
3. Muse Spark reads the pesticide label photo for its dose and spray interval and flags any mix above it. It never computes a dose of its own.
4. On day 3 to 5 the farmer re-photographs the same leaves. The masks are compared, and the answer is spreading, stable or shrinking, so the farmer knows whether a second spray is needed.

## Meta models

- SAM 3.1 for lesion segmentation and area measurement
- Muse Spark for label reading and the spray-or-wait comparison
- Meta voice transcription for the farmer's spoken question

## Inference

Muse Spark Open runs on Baseten or Fireworks, with hosted Spark 1.3 as the fallback. SAM 3.1 open weights run on a Modal GPU endpoint, with the Meta Model API as the fallback.

## Status

Hackathon build starts Oct 26, 2026.

# GuardPet

## What it is

GuardPet is an Android security-guardian pet: a floating cat that watches
over the phone, automatically detects scams and risky apps, and warns the
user in plain language. It is built for people who do not read security
jargon — the warning tells you what happened, why it is risky, and what to
do next.

Track: **Build for Your World** — Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026,
indie (solo) entry. Building period: October 27 – November 4, 2026.

## What it does

- Floating pet cat: walking, idle, sleeping, alerting, tap-to-chat,
  Chinese/English switching, pin / walk toggle
- App permission scan (logistic-regression model)
- Scam SMS detection
- Suspicious call screening
- Suspicious link check (offline lexical scoring)
- Open Wi-Fi warning (fully offline)
- AI explanations (opt-in, OFF by default, with a privacy notice in the
  app): tap the cat on an alert to get a plain-language explanation. The
  bubble switches to "thinking…" immediately (up to 2 minutes), shows the
  explanation for 15 seconds, calls the API only once per alert, and never
  lets an old explanation overwrite a newer alert
- Link explanations: when a shared link is judged dangerous, an "AI
  explanation" button lists only the rules that actually scored
- Companion chat: tap the cat to chat, last 6 turns kept, voice input
  included
- API key storage encrypted with Android Keystore (AES/GCM); an old
  plaintext key is migrated automatically on first open, and a decryption
  failure is shown honestly instead of pretending the key is active

## How it works

**Detection layer (on-device, deterministic).** Two on-device models plus a
rule engine decide every verdict. Nothing about detection leaves the phone,
and no detection decision needs the cloud.

**Explanation layer (Meta Model API, opt-in).** Only after a verdict is
made, and only if the user opted in and provided a key, the app asks a Meta
model to explain it. The model can never overturn a verdict. With no key, no
network, or an API error, the app silently falls back to scripted text.

## Meta products used

| Product | Model / endpoint | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Meta Model API — chat completions | `muse-spark-1.3` via `api.meta.ai/v1/chat/completions` | Alert explanations, link explanations, companion chat |

not stored (the temporary file is deleted after use). Alert explanations send

# Safe House Vision & Response

## What it is

Safe House Vision & Response — existing cameras → detection → graded alert → evidence with custody → human decides.

Local detection discards almost everything for free; only candidates go up to the verifier (Muse Spark Open via Baseten); only verified becomes an alert. The detector proposes; the verifier and a human decide.

tirthpatel002/reflex.readme_excerpt:
# Reflex

Reflex sits in an agent's action path. Before an agent's proposed action
(a **step**) runs, Reflex:

1. **Gates** it with cheap, deterministic rules.
2. **Escalates** flagged steps to a judge (the SDK's `judge` option; contract only, no model judge built yet).
3. **Learns lessons** from flagged cases that can become new rules (contract only; not built yet).

A learned rule can block, ask or flag, never allow: only a rule with a `human:` origin may allow.

Every package is small and has a README that says what it does and why.

Schema version: **0** (`SCHEMA_VERSION = "0"` in `@reflex/schema`).

## Layers

```
            apps/  demo
                         │
            packages/sdk                                    (Reflex.wrap: gate and record tool calls)
                         │
   ┌─────────── engine ───────────┐   judge · compiler · learner
   │  (gate: rules → Decision)    │   (interfaces / stubs)
   └──┬───────┬────────┬──────────┘
      │       │        │
   registry  expr    store        render      trials   pricing   caller-openai
      │       │        │            │            └─────────┼─────────┘
      └───────┴──── schema ─────────┘                    caller
```

`caller` (model invocation, metering, observability) and `trials` (evaluation harness)
stand beside the core: `trials` depends on `caller`, and `caller` depends on nothing internal.
`caller` holds the provider and cost-resolution contracts only; `caller-openai` (in `packages/adapters/caller/openai`) implements a provider
and `pricing` implements price catalogs, both configured by the app.

### Bench packages

Three self-contained packages sit beside the core with no dependency on it, so they can be extracted and reused:

- `sandbox` (no deps): deterministic mock tools (`shop`, `git`, `mail`) with previewable, measurable effects.
- `scenarios` (zod only): the labelled mistake dataset, its format, seeded dev / held-out split, leakage check,
  validator and a fixed-policy human. See its datasheet.
- `bench` (`scenarios`, `trials`): plays scenarios through arms and reports catch, false block, ask, judge share,
  tokens, cost and gate vs judge latency.

`apps/demo` is the thin Reflex adapter that wires them to the SDK; the facts report (`apps/demo/FACTS.md`) lives there too.

## Dependency rule

Dependencies point **down** only.

- `schema` depends on nothing internal.
- `registry`, `store`, `render` depend only on `schema`; `expr` depends on nothing internal.

# HargaTetangga

An Android app for households that buy staple groceries. It reads shopping receipts from a photo, remembers what each item cost at each store, and answers two questions before a trip: **how much cash to bring**, and **which store is cheapest for this list**. After the trip it compares the plan with the receipt.

Built solo for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026 (Indie track, theme "Build for Your World") on the Meta Model API. Planning documents are in Indonesian: [PRD.md](PRD.md), [BACKLOG.md](BACKLOG.md), [META-API.md](META-API.md).

## Why

In our house in Kudus, Indonesia, the same item costs different amounts at different shops, and nobody remembers the last price. So we guess how much cash to bring. Bring too little and the trip stalls; bring too much and it goes on things that were never on the list. HargaTetangga turns receipts we already get into a price memory, and turns that memory into a cash estimate and a store plan.

## What it does

| **Harga** (prices) | Latest confirmed price of every product at every store, with its age. |

# Oren

AI assistants for small businesses in French-speaking Africa. First market: Lomé, Togo.

## The problem

A small restaurant in Lomé cannot afford a full-time person to answer customer messages. Customers ask the same questions all day — the menu, prices, opening hours, delivery — and orders get lost between phone calls, notebooks and chat threads. Generic chatbots do not help: they invent prices, cannot take a real order, and do not know when to hand over to a human.

## The solution

Oren gives a business its own assistant, live in under an hour. The assistant answers customers in French from the business's real information — and **acts**: it composes an order, shows a code-computed summary, waits for the customer's explicit confirmation, then sends the order to the owner's live dashboard. Setup is multimodal: a photo of the paper menu and a voice message become a verified catalog. No app to install for customers: a link or a QR code is enough.

## Platform architecture

Oren is a multi-business platform, not a single restaurant bot. The restaurant is the first vertical slice, built on the full platform architecture:

- **Multi-tenancy first.** Every business row carries a `business_id`; PostgreSQL Row Level Security is enabled on every table, and automated tests prove one business can neither read nor write another's data. Businesses declare a `business_type` and activate **capabilities**.
- **Capability tool registry.** Each capability (today: `catalog_orders`; later: `bookings`, `appointments`) declares its tools with Zod schemas, read/write flags and confirmation requirements. The assistant only ever receives the tools of the capabilities enabled for that business. Adding a trade means adding configuration, not rewriting the core.
- **Channel-independent core.** `core/handleMessage` knows nothing about channels. A channel is an adapter (in: normalize the message; out: format the reply). Only the `web` adapter is built today; Telegram and WhatsApp adapters will plug in without touching the core.
- **Replaceable modules** behind small interfaces: `LlmProvider` (Meta Model API: Muse Spark for chat/vision, Muse Voice Transcribe for voice), `PaymentProvider` (cash on delivery / on pickup, plus a fake test provider), `NotificationProvider` (realtime dashboard, Web Push, e-mail), `SmsProvider` (interface only).

Stack: Next.js (App Router, TypeScript), Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Supabase (PostgreSQL, RLS, Realtime, email-link auth, Storage), Zod validation, Vitest. Prices are integer FCFA — never decimals, never negative. No vector database: a restaurant catalog fits in the model context.

## What makes it different

- **Code decides, the model proposes.** Prices, totals, quantities, delivery fees and statuses are always computed or validated by code. Model output is never a source of truth for money.
- **Verified confirmation.** No write happens without a code-computed summary and the customer's explicit agreement bound to that exact summary

# MIRAIWERK AI

**The intelligence engine for projects that move forward.**

MIRAIWERK AI is an AI-native project delivery platform built around one question: *if this ticket or decision moves, what else moves with it?*

It combines a multi-tenant delivery workspace (organizations, workspaces, teams, tasks, roadmaps, documentation, meetings and discussions) with **RippleMap** — a deterministic change-impact engine — and evidence-labelled AI analysis. A model may propose; only an authorized human can approve a plan change.

> Precise German engineering × Japanese forward thinking × modern English technology.

---

## The core loop

```text
Brief ──► Generated plan ──► Ticket intake ──► AI analysis
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                              Human approval ◄── RippleMap impact simulation
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                      Versioned plan + audit trail
```

1. **Brief** — describe the project, goal, dates and stated constraints.
2. **Draft plan** — generate requirements, milestones, tasks, dependencies, assumptions and missing information.
3. **Ticket intake** — capture an incident, bug, feature request, debt item or vague report.
4. **Analysis** — classify the ticket, separate observed evidence from inferred links, list unknowns and propose accept/split/defer/clarify/duplicate options.
5. **RippleMap** — apply the proposed change to the dependency graph and compute schedule, effort, milestone and critical-path impact in deterministic code.
6. **Decision** — an owner, admin or manager approves, rejects, defers, links a duplicate or requests clarification.
7. **Versioning** — accept/split create a new plan version and decision audit. Defer/duplicate/clarify record the outcome without silently changing the plan.

## What ships

### Decision intelligence
- Plan generator with review-before-commit, explicit assumptions and missing information.
- Ticket intake and analysis with three evidence states (`observed`, `inferred`, `unknown`), unknowns, clarifying questions, duplicate candidates and proposed tasks.
- Deterministic RippleMap simulation for every decision option, including before/after milestone dates, critical path and plan diffs.
- Transactional approvals with stale-proposal detection, stored-scenario revalidation, optimistic plan versioning and append-only audit history.
- Role-based project permissions: `owner`/`pm` approve, `member` creates and analyses, `viewer` is read-only.

### Delivery platform
- Multi-tenant organizations and workspaces with role-based access (`owner`, `admin`, `manager`, `member`, `viewer`).
- Email/password authentication using Argon2id, short-lived JWT access tokens and rotating refresh tokens in an httpOnly cookie.
- Optional Meta OAuth sign-in, session listing/revocation, password reset, and a seeded demo-login pat

Property acquisition across Cameroon and the Central African sub-region faces deep structural challenges rooted in paper-based archives, fragmented records, and manual survey workflows. Land buyers, banks, diaspora investors, and conveyancing notaries frequently confront three critical failure modes:

1. **"Superficie Fictive" (Fraudulent Surface Inflation):** Paper boundary plans (*Plans de Bornage*) frequently state an inflated parcel area (for example, declaring 1,500 m² for a plot whose physical boundary beacons enclose only 980 m²). This gap is exploited to overvalue collateral, inflate compensation during expropriation, or defraud buyers who cannot independently calculate coordinates.
2. **Topological Defects & Coordinate Inconsistencies:** Boundary polygons with unclosed perimeters (where beacon $B_n$ does not return to $B_1$), self-intersecting boundary lines (figure-eight or bow-tie anomalies), or inverted Easting/Northing coordinates that place the parcel in an entirely different administrative zone.
3. **UTM Projection & Ellipsoid Confusion:** Cameroon spans two Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) zones: **Zone 32N** (`EPSG:32632`, Western, Littoral, and Central regions) and **Zone 33N** (`EPSG:32633`, Northern and Eastern regions). Coordinates computed in one zone but plotted in another produce massive positional shifts and distorted area figures.

Without specialized surveying software or access to a licensed surveyor before placing a purchase deposit, buyers face substantial financial loss and years of litigation.

---

## 3. The Solution: Independent Mathematical & AI-Assisted Audit

**Cadastra-Cameroon** is an independent, automated cadastral screening instrument. It bridges the gap between raw surveying data and everyday legal due diligence:

- **Instant Plan Ingestion:** Ingests boundary survey plans via document drop (PDF / JPG), manual coordinate entry, or mobile submission.
- **Deterministic Mathematical Verification:** Reconstructs the true boundary polygon in projected metric space (UTM 32N / 33N), evaluates perimeter closure, and compares declared vs. computed surface area.
- **AI Forensic Analyst:** Translates complex geodetic discrepancies into plain-language legal assessments in English and French, identifying specific statutory risks before funds are transferred.

# Genebark

![Genebark](public/brand/genebark-lockup-white.png)

**An agent harness for evidence-grounded genetics research.**

[Live demo](https://evidence-workbench-xi.vercel.app) · [Architecture](docs/architecture/00-overview.md) · [Evaluation evidence](evals/genetics/) · [Security](SECURITY.md)

Genebark turns an open-ended genetics question into a concise, traceable answer and an appropriate scientific visualization. It retrieves literature, reads the relevant sections, extracts atomic findings, checks those findings against verbatim source text, compares experimental context and progressively renders the result while research continues.

It is designed for researchers, laboratory teams and technically trained students who need to understand what the evidence actually supports without manually reconciling dozens of papers. Genebark is a research tool—not a clinical decision system and not medical advice.

## Why it is different

A conventional chatbot usually retrieves passages and writes an answer. Genebark provides a controlled execution environment around the model:

- **Progressive research:** an immediate contextual acknowledgement is followed by an explicitly provisional abstract-grounded overview, then an immutable synthesis grounded in verified findings.
- **Evidence verification:** claims retain their source, locator and verbatim quote; deterministic checks validate existence, quotation, numbers, retraction signals and scope before verification.
- **Context-aware comparison:** agreement or contradiction is assessed only after considering organism, model, intervention, assay and experimental conditions.
- **Intent-driven visuals:** the same evidence can become an evidence map, comparison matrix, mechanism diagram or decision algorithm instead of a wall of text.
- **Transparent ranking:** every source receives an explainable score based on deterministic relevance, evidence level, explicit quality signals, currency and applicability.
- **Temporary conversational memory:** follow-up questions can refer to earlier genes, studies and findings inside the active anonymous chat without permanent conversation storage.

## How Meta powers Genebark

Genebark uses **Muse Spark 1.3 through the Meta Model API** for the semantic work that deterministic code cannot reliably perform:

- structuring complex genetics questions;
- reformulating thin or ambiguous literature searches;
- extracting atomic findings from scientific passages;
- judging semantic support and experimental scope;
- synthesizing provisional and verified overviews;
- labelling cross-study concordance and contradiction;
- transforming verified evidence into mechanism and algorithm structures.

Every call is bounded by a Zod output schema, timeout, token/cost budget and tool allow-list. The model proposes structured interpretations; code controls execution and verifies the evidence. Removing the model would remove the semantic bridge between heterogeneous scientific language. Removin

# Neural Lab

An Android app running an on-device "failure-learning" AI — the **Trinity** lifecycle
(**Ghost → Molecule → Black Hole**) — inside a live 3D terrarium.

Built by Ahkeem Barros (**Team Annihilus**) for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon
(Indie Dev track, theme: Push the Frontier).

## What it does

- A small neural brain (24 → 16 → 16 → 8, 808 parameters) lives in a 3D terrarium,
  sensing gravity, objectives, and its own prediction error.
- When it fails at an objective, the failure is **sealed as a Ghost**: a deterministic
  FNV-1a hash of the objective and the action trace. Inside the seal step, a Meta AI
  model (`muse-spark-1.3`, via the Meta Model API) **judges the sealed failure**; the
  short verdict is stored with the ghost and shown in the app's thought log. The seal
  itself is local and authoritative — the judge call is fire-and-forget and never
  blocks the loop. The verdict also carries a machine-readable tail naming the
  blamed action and a severity; when it parses, the brain mints **one bounded
  molecule fragment from the verdict** — same caps, mass ladder and black-hole
  overflow as ghost fragments — so the judge's words steer future decisions. A
  **Judge's Review** card (Instruments) bundles the recent ghost history into one
  further call and renders the judge's paragraph review of the brain's habits.
- A later run at the same objective is the ghost's **appeal**. Success redeems it.
  Failure breaks it into **Molecules** — steering fragments (mass + bias) that bias
  future decisions away from the failed run's action pattern.
- Overflow collapses into **Black Hole** gravity wells instead of being discarded.
- Capacities are not hand-set: they derive from a **substrate probe** of the host
  device (ceiling = 26000 × core × memory × benchmark factors), and the network grows
  by function-preserving Net2Net widening up to that ceiling.
- **Dish instruments** (Events / Seals / Molecules / Gravity) expose the live brain
  state, and a fullscreen demo view presents it. The trained brain can also be
  exported to C (`neural_lab_infer.h` / `.c`) and runs bit-exact in a virtual MCU
  simulator in the app.

## Layout

- `www/` — the entire app UI and brain in plain JavaScript: `terrarium-core.js`
  (Trinity lifecycle), `terrarium.js` (3D dish), `meta-judge.js` (Meta Model API
  judge), `app.js` plus feature modules, `index.html`.
- `src/` — the Android host: `MainActivity` and the native bridges (HTTP bridge used

- `terrarium_tests.js` — the brain-core test suite (111 tests, run with Node).
- `build.sh` — the APK build used for the current build (aapt2 + javac + d8 +
  apksigner; Android SDK build-tools 36.1.0, JDK 21).

**Pre-existing base:** the Trinity lifecycle, the terrarium brain, training/gym

# MatchPic — one creative → every placement size

Our studio adapts every approved creative to 6–8 placement sizes by hand,
every day, for 100+ brands. Generic AI resizers redraw the product, break
Hebrew lettering and ignore the brand's own layout rules for each size.
MatchPic adapts with Meta's models and is trustworthy: brand templates per size,
protected product/logo pixels with proof, and a model QA check on every
output.

**Live demo: https://app.mashrokit.co.il/matchpic/**

Upload a finished creative, pick a brand and sizes, get every placement back —
in **Protected** mode (AI paints only the background; product, logo and text
go back as original pixels, with a pixel proof) or **Fast** mode (AI
recomposes the whole creative in one pass). A brand teaches its layout per
size through **templates**: past finished creatives that Spark reads into a
stored layout spec. Every output is QA-checked by a fresh Spark call; on FAIL
it retries once, then marks the output "needs review".

Everything is bilingual (English default, Hebrew toggle, RTL). All demo
brands are synthetic and fictional; nothing is ever published.

## How it works

1. **Spark** (`muse-spark-1.3`) reads the source creative: products, logo,
   verbatim headline/sub-text, offer/CTA panel, background style,
   language/direction.
2. **SAM** (`sam-3.1`) cuts exact product and logo masks (phrase + box-prompt
   union); contrast completion finishes the logo lockup when Spark's box ends
   mid-word. Code plans the layout from the brand template for that size, or

# Camtoshop

**The AI community manager that lives in WhatsApp.** A merchant sends a product photo to one WhatsApp line. Minutes later the Reel comes back with **Publish / Change / Discard** buttons, and one tap posts it to *their own* Instagram. Every morning the agent suggests what to promote next, and it learns from the results of the merchant's real Reels.

No app to learn, no filming, no editor: the merchant already knows how to use WhatsApp.

## How a merchant uses it

1. **Sign up** at the portal, connect Instagram + Facebook Page (and Shopify, if they have it) and link the phones they'll use: the portal gives a one-time code and the merchant sends it to the line, which proves the number is theirs.
2. **Send a product**: 1–8 photos with what it is and the price, or a voice note. Camtoshop recognizes the merchant by phone number and asks only for what's missing.
3. **Approve**: the Reel arrives in the chat. *Publish* is tied to that exact version; *Change* takes a plain-language request ("calmer", "another hook") and invalidates the old approval.
4. **Every morning** the agent proposes the product that has gone longest without promotion. With enough data it compares hook styles on real Instagram results and applies the winner, and it says why. With too little data it draws no conclusion.

**Trust is the product.** Nothing is published without the merchant's tap. Prices come only from the merchant or the store, never from the model. Unsupported promises are removed. AI scenes start from the real product cutout and are labeled as AI. Each merchant's tokens are encrypted, and webhooks without a valid Meta signature are rejected.

## Beyond WhatsApp

**From camera to shop.** A small merchant talks about a product on their phone, mistakes included. Camtoshop turns that one video into everything needed to sell it:

- **An edited Reel**, directed by an AI agent. It removes failed takes and self-corrections, puts word-by-word captions where they never cover the product, adds giant text behind the speaker, product-in-use cutaways and an end card with the price. Then it **watches its own render and fixes it**.
- **Studio catalog photos** made from the real product, not a lookalike.
- **A bilingual store listing** (English first, plus the video's language) with title, description, key points, SEO and price.
- **Three Meta ad variants** (benefit, story, offer), with copy and a designed creative.
- **One-click publishing** to a **Shopify** store, the **Meta catalog** (Instagram & Facebook Shops, WhatsApp catalog) and **Instagram Reels**.

**No video? No problem.** Camtoshop also builds the Reel from **a few photos** (plus a short message and, optionally, a voice note) or **straight from the products already in a Shopify store**: SAM 3.1 cuts out the real product, Muse Spark writes the script, Muse Image places the *same* product in a lifestyle scene, and the product moves in layers over its own photo with giant text behind it. # LocalDub

LocalDub takes a Hindi or Urdu video and gives it back dubbed in English, with each character speaking in a voice cloned from their own original lines and the original music and sound effects kept underneath.

I'm Muhammad Asim, a student developer from Pakistan. I built this for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026 (Indie Developer track, "Build for Your World"), with no budget, on free Kaggle CPU machines.

**Built by Muhammad Asim, a student developer, with AI coding assistance; the pipeline runs on Meta's open-weight models.** The code was written with the help of an AI coding assistant; the Meta models (Muse Glimmer, Omnilingual ASR, Demucs) are what the pipeline itself runs on, they did not write the code.

- Demo video (2:55): https://github.com/TurabDevs/localdub/releases/download/demo-v2/localdub_demo_v5.mp4
- Full 5-minute English dub (latest, v6): https://github.com/TurabDevs/localdub/releases/download/demo-v2/aib_depression_en_v6.webm
- Frame-by-frame AV-QA report of that dub: [`results/avqa_v6/report.html`](results/avqa_v6/report.html) (v5 for comparison: [`results/avqa_v5/report.html`](results/avqa_v5/report.html))
- All releases: https://github.com/TurabDevs/localdub/releases

## Why I built this

Where I live, almost everything people watch and make is in Urdu, Punjabi, Saraiki or Hindi. There are thousands of creators here making comedy, cooking videos, tutorials and lectures, and their work almost never travels past people who already speak the language. Big channels pay dubbing studios. A kid with a phone and a good sketch can't.

The other direction hurts too. Most good teaching material online is in English, and a lot of students around me (I'm one of them) follow it slower than they should because they are translating in their head the whole time.

Automatic dubbing tools exist, but the ones I tried had the same three problems with our content:

1. Jokes get translated word for word, so they stop being jokes. Hinglish (Hindi and English mixed in one sentence) confuses them badly.
2. Everyone gets the same stock voice, or the wrong voice for the person on screen.
3. Lines don't fit. The dub keeps talking after the actor's mouth has stopped.

LocalDub is my attempt to fix those three things, using models I can actually run.

## Why open-weight models

This part is not a style choice. Pakistan is one of the countries where Meta's hosted Model API is not available. I asked Meta support during the hackathon; they confirmed the restriction and couldn't give an exception or API credits. I also don't have a card or a budget for paid inference.

So every Meta model in LocalDub is an open-weight model that I downloaded and ran myself, offline, inside free Kaggle notebooks. No hosted Meta API, no VPN. That turned out to be the point of the project: if it runs on a free CPU box, it can run for creators who have nothing else either.

The cost of doing it this way is speed. My Kaggle account could only use CPU machines

# ClearDesk AI

**AI-assisted invoice review with human oversight.**

ClearDesk AI is a hackathon prototype designed to help small businesses review invoice information, identify missing details and potential inconsistencies, and organize review work before a person makes a decision.

## Features

- AI-assisted invoice analysis from submitted text.
- Detection of missing invoice information and potential inconsistencies.
- Document queue for organizing review work.
- Exact duplicate-text warnings.
- Review tracking with a Mark as Reviewed action.
- Browser local storage for document and review state.
- Human-in-the-loop workflow: AI findings support review but do not automatically approve or pay invoices.

## Technology

- React
- TypeScript
- Vite
- Node.js and Express
- Meta Model API integration through the backend

## Requirements

- Node.js and npm.
- A valid Meta Model API key with access to the configured model.

## Getting started

### 1. Install dependencies

```bash
npm install
```

### 2. Configure the API key

Create a `.env` file in the project root and add:

```env
MODEL_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
```

Replace the placeholder with your own API key. Never commit `.env` or share its contents publicly. The backend reads the key so it does not need to be placed in frontend code.

### 3. Start the backend

Open a terminal in the project folder and run:

```bash
node ./server/index.js
```

The backend runs at `http://localhost:3001` by default.

Health check: `http://localhost:3001/api/health`

### 4. Start the frontend

Open a second terminal in the project folder and run:

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open the local URL printed by Vite, typically `http://localhost:5173`.

### 5. Build and lint

```bash
npm run build
npm run lint
```

## API endpoints

| Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/health` | Reports backend health and whether the API key is configured |
| POST | `/api/analyze` | Accepts document text and returns AI-assisted analysis |

## Current limitations

- Automatic text analysis supports `.txt` and `.csv` inputs.
- PDF and image files are not automatically extracted or analyzed in the current prototype.
- AI findings may be incomplete or incorrect and must be checked by a person.
- Browser local storage is specific to the browser and is not a centralized database.
- This prototype does not replace accounting controls, professional judgment, or independent payment verification.

## Security

- Keep API keys in the backend environment, never in frontend source code.
- Do not commit `.env`, credentials, private keys, or sensitive invoice records.
- Use fictional or sanitized examples in public demonstrations.
- Never treat AI-generated findings as proof of fraud or as authorization to make a payment.

## Project status

ClearDesk AI is a hackathon prototype demonstrating an AI-assisted invoice-review workflow with human oversight. It is not presented as a production-grade financial verification system.

# EchoVoiice Assistant

A voice app for people who speak **Ewe**. It has three parts:

- **Talk**: have a spoken conversation in Ewe with an assistant that can talk about anything. A hospital mode turns it into a reception guide that also writes a French summary for staff.
- **Translate**: a face-to-face interpreter between someone who speaks only Ewe and someone who speaks English or French.
- **Learn**: type a word in English, French or Ewe and see it in Ewe, hear how it sounds, and use it in a sentence.

```
Someone speaks Ewe

  -> Muse Spark (Meta Model API)                   understands, answers or translates, in Ewe
  -> EchoVoiice TTS (Meta MMS-TTS as fallback)     Ewe text to speech
They hear the reply in Ewe
```

Muse Spark, through the Meta Model API, does all the language work: conversation, translation, word lessons and, on the Translate page, deciding which language was spoken. It reads and writes Ewe directly, with an everyday Ewe reference sheet in its prompt (see below), so there is no separate translation model. English and French speech is transcribed by Muse Voice Transcribe on the same API. Only Ewe speech recognition and the fallback voice run locally.

### Hearing everyday Ewe

Ewe speech is transcribed by [`waxal-benchmarking/mms-300m-waxal-ewe`](https://huggingface.co/waxal-benchmarking/mms-300m-waxal-ewe), Meta MMS fine-tuned on everyday conversational Ewe from Google's WAXAL corpus (model licence CC BY-NC 4.0).

We chose it by measuring. On 30 real conversational recordings from the WAXAL Ewe test set (about 10 minutes of speech), the share of words each setup got wrong was:

| Setup | Word error rate | Character error rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`mms-300m-waxal-ewe` alone (used)** | **33.6%** | **13.5%** |
| Muse Spark combining it with `facebook/mms-1b-all` (the previous setup) | 39.8% | 16.6% |
| Same, but told to trust the everyday model first | 32.9% | 13.4% |
| `facebook/mms-1b-all` alone (trained mostly on Bible readings) | 48.3% | 16.9% |
| Muse Spark 1.2 hearing the audio, with the MMS versions as hints | 36.7% | 14.9% |
| Muse Spark 1.2 hearing the audio alone | 78.8% | 37.6% |

Adding `facebook/mms-1b-all` barely helps at best, while costing about 1.5 seconds per turn and 4 GB of memory, so the everyday model runs alone. Muse Spark still reads every transcript knowing it may contain recognition errors, and works out what the person meant. To add models, list them in `ASR_MODELS`.

English and French speech (Translate page) is transcribed by Muse Voice Transcribe, and English and French replies are spoken by the browser's own voices.

# Acan

Acan is a scope-first behavior gate for coding agents. The developer approves what an agent may change, a scope with obligations, before any code exists. Acan then runs the old app twice and the new app once, side by side, on each probe. The old runs start from the protected head, and the new run uses the exact merged commit that would land. Differences outside the scope bounce back to the agent with a reproducer. The developer rules only on what is left. Each ruling is recorded, and every later receipt must report it or label it not enforced.

The plant view shows where each agent went, what bounced, and any clash held before either worker writes. The developer decides on the anchored card.

Work in progress for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon.

## Why Meta models matter here

Muse Spark is the foreman: it splits each order into tasks and drafts the scope contract a human then confirms. Muse Spark Open is every worker: it reads back the task, claims it and writes the code. Acan checks the result itself, so no model's word decides whether a change lands.

- The routing in `crates/acan-llm/llm.example.toml` sends the foreman to Muse Spark and the workers to Muse Spark Open.
- Foreman: Muse Spark drafted a scope from a real order, and Acan's decoder accepted it. See `receipts/m01-scope-draft.md`.
- Workers: Muse Spark Open answered live through Baseten and Fireworks. See `receipts/p00-provider-smoke.md`.
