A local video evidence workstation. Trace a published edit to a provided source, reconstruct the sequence,

## Architecture

Deterministic first. The aligner (4 Hz spatial color sequence matching via `spatial-color-sequence-v2` and normalized acoustic cross-correlation) finds and timestamps the omissions it can align. # Nara Agent

An Arabic-first AI agent that turns a student's answers and photos of their certificates into a
university application pack. A school counsellor then checks the pack field by field. It runs on
Meta's models and was made for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026 (startup track) by Nara
Abroad.

- **Live product:** https://nara-application-agent.vercel.app (class mode: `/class`)
- **Code:** https://github.com/KhalidBakroun/nara-application-agent

> **Sample data for the demo.** The universities, programmes and admission rules in this app are
> fictional. The sample certificate images are synthetic and carry the watermark "SAMPLE: DEMO DATA".
> No real student data is used anywhere.

## The problem

Arab students and their school counsellors lose days on study-abroad applications. They copy grades
from photos of certificates, work out whether a Tawjihi score is enough, pick courses, fill in forms
and chase missing documents. Many families pay an agent USD 300–500 just for advice.

Nara works with schools, and a person checks every application. Nara Agent does the counsellor's
paperwork, and the counsellor approves every field.

## What it does

1. **Interview in Arabic.** The student answers by voice or by typing. The agent builds a profile:
   grades, stream, goals, budget, preferred countries and English level.
2. **Photos of documents.** The student photographs their Tawjihi certificate and English test report.
   The app finds the document in the photo, crops it, and reads every field together with where it
   sits on the page.
3. **The agent works on its own.** A tool-calling loop of at most 12 steps:
   - converts the Tawjihi grade;
   - searches the sample programmes;
   - checks the entry requirements;
   - fills the application form for the best match;
   - lists what is missing.

   Every step shows in a live trace.
4. **Counsellor review.** Every field shows:
   - its value;
   - its source: a zoomed crop of the document with the value highlighted, or a quote from the
     interview;
   - a confidence level.

   A field with no source is marked "needs counsellor". The counsellor approves or edits each field,
   then the whole pack.
5. **Class mode.** A counsellor runs the agent for a whole class: up to 30 students, 3 at a time. The
   result is one table showing each student's best programme, entry route and number of missing
   items, with a link to each pack.
6. **Arabic first, with an English toggle.**

Pages: `/` is the student flow, `/review` the counsellor review, and `/class` class mode.

## What was built before kickoff, and what was built during the hackathon

The participant guide lets startups build on existing code, as long as they clearly identify what was
newly built during the hackathon. The demo must highlight only that new work. This section shows it
commit by commit.

- **Kickoff:** Monday 26 Oct 2026, 12:00 ET (16:00 UTC).
- **We started too early.** We began writing about one to two hours before kic

# CommonGround

Property management, fund accounting, computer-vision maintenance verification, and statutory governance software for firms that manage residential housing associations and condominiums.

An independent management firm typically assigns 15 to 30 properties (400 to 1,200 units) to one property manager. Most existing systems only record accounting entries after the fact. Managers reconcile utility sub-meters in spreadsheets, check statutory compliance by hand, chase contractors by phone, and type meeting minutes from audio recordings. CommonGround combines the unit and meter registry, fund-separated double-entry accounting, work order verification, owner voting, and an AI operations assistant in one multi-firm web application.

Built for the [Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, Cerebral Valley](https://cerebralvalley.ai/e/meta-ai-developer-hackathon).

| | |
|---|---|
| Runtime | .NET 10, C# 14, Blazor Web App (Interactive Server) |
| Database | SQL Server 2025 LocalDB via EF Core 10 (in-memory provider for tests) |
| Meta models | `muse-spark-1.3`, `muse-wonder`, `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0`, `sam-3.1`, `muse-image-1.0` |
| Interface languages | English, Polish, Spanish, French, German |
| Verification | `dotnet build -warnaserror`: 0 warnings, 0 errors. `dotnet test`: 160 passed, 0 failed |

## Describe your use of Meta products to build the submitted project

CommonGround calls five Meta models through the Meta Model API (`https://api.meta.ai/v1`). Each model has a specific job in a workflow; none is used as a generic chatbot.

| Model | Endpoint | Where it is used in CommonGround |
|---|---|---|
| `muse-spark-1.3` | `/v1/responses` (with `web_search` grounding where allowed) | Agentic operations assistant (ReAct loop with a live tool catalog), portfolio question answering, address-driven property discovery (utility operators, gross tariffs, emergency authorities, national statutes), multimodal resident request triage and translation, statute compliance checks over the full governing corpus, meter dial OCR, paper ballot OCR, neighbor mediation and arrears notice drafting, ARC and renovation permit evaluation |
| `muse-wonder` | `/v1/responses` (multi-step workflows) | Public registry and legal corpus synchronization, annual meeting package compilation, insurance claim dossier assembly |
| `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` | `POST /v1/asr/transcribe` (multipart `request` JSON + `audio` WAV) | Live browser microphone transcription for resident reports and the assistant chat (`PUSH_TO_TALK`), speaker-diarized meeting minutes (`DIARIZATION`) |
| `sam-3.1` | Segmentation | Defect masks (`wall crack`, `water stain`, `spalling concrete`, `damaged handrail`), affected area in m², basement valve and gas lever annotation, before/after repair verification (remaining defect below 5% of original area) |
| `muse-image-1.0` | Image generation | Option A / Option B renovation ballot previews, QR stairwell notice posters, multilingual waste segregation

# Piece of Mind

**Giving memory to artwork.** Film yourself painting, and the footage becomes the painting's
own memory: watch it form with nobody in the way, sit back down beside it, or tap any stroke to
see the hand that made it.

![Left: the camera, 27 minutes into the third session, an arm across the canvas. Right: Piece of Mind at the same second.](docs/camera-vs-afterimage.jpg)

*The camera 27 minutes into the third session (left), and Piece of Mind at the same second (right).*

Artists have always pulled new technology into the work: new tools and surfaces, projection,
video, computers. Piece of Mind brings in Meta's newest vision and language models with one
rule: they decide where the painter is, never what the painting looks like. Every pixel in the
output comes from camera frames, aligned, colour-matched and averaged over a few frames. No
generative model touches the image and nothing is invented: what the painting remembers, the
camera saw. A script checks it.

Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Oct 26 – Nov 4, 2026), Indie track, theme
*Build for Your World*: I stopped painting ten years ago, picked it back up for this, and wanted
AI in the work without letting it fake any of it. Built with **SAM 3.1** and **Muse Spark**,
either through the Meta Model API or from the open
weights: SAM 3.1 on a Modal GPU and Muse Spark Open through Baseten. The first two sessions
here were processed both ways and the third through the API; each run's receipt names the path
that made it.

## Try it

**Check a real run, no key needed.** [`samples/`](samples) holds 90 seconds of the third session
(cropped to the easel, sound removed) with the receipt of its run and the answers SAM 3.1 and Muse
Spark gave it. With Python 3.11, ffmpeg on the PATH and `pip install -r requirements.txt`:

```
python scripts/afterimage_verify.py samples/session3-excerpt/receipt.json --video samples/session3-excerpt.mp4
python scripts/afterimage_run.py samples/session3-excerpt.mp4 --out samples/session3-excerpt
```

- **Verify** checks the footage and every cached model answer against the hashes in the receipt,
  then re-derives each output frame from the footage and compares it with the receipt's hash chain.
- **Replay** runs the whole pipeline from the cached answers and writes the results page,
  `samples/session3-excerpt/index.html` (tap any stroke), and the videos. It rewrites the receipt,
  and `git diff samples/` shows nothing.
- Neither calls a model, so neither tests the models. A **fresh run** asks SAM and Spark again; their
  answers, and so the output, come out close but not identical. Bit for bit also assumes the
  toolchain the receipt names (Python 3.11, numpy 2.4, ffmpeg 9.0): another ffmpeg build can resample
  a pixel differently.

**On your own footage.** A phone on a tripod, the canvas in view the whole session, and a Meta
Model API key in `.env` (copy `.env.example`). Then:

```
python scripts/afterimage_run.py my-session.mp4 --start 3
```

Boots, maps memory, schedules, runs userspace, enumerates PCI, draws a 1280×720 framebuffer. | **Proven in QEMU.** K1–K6 with committed boot logs. The agent capability slice is on its own branch, not in this tree | | **The platform** | The agent platform: Imperium's watch floor, the lab, the workshop, the studio, the board. Real model calls, real records, real budget guardrails. | **Running daily** | | **The carrier** | A demo image remastered from Xubuntu so the platform has a desktop while the kernel's drivers are unfinished. | **Remastered demo — labelled, not a claim** | The carrier is a machine to build on. It is not the operating system, and we do not call it one. The eight-phase spec for removing it ships with this submission. Built for the **Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026**. One person directs; AI agents build in lanes and check each other's work. Where something is partial, this repo says so in those words. --- ## 1. The OS is real, and you can boot it in one command `kernel/` is 16 Rust files, 9,794 lines, `no_std`, our own entry point, our own memory manager, scheduler, interrupt handling and ELF loader. Not a fork. Not Linux. ```sh # ~5 MB, boots in QEMU in about two seconds qemu-system-x86_64 -m 512M \ -drive format=raw,file=kernel/target/x86_64-unknown-none/debug/bootimage-metaos-kernel.bin \ -serial stdio ``` What it does, from the committed logs in `os-build/logs/` (`K1-boot.txt`, `K3-boot.txt`, `K6.1-cap-policy.txt`) and from the longer boot captured for the demo: - prints `META OS KERNEL - alive (K1)`, then draws the Meta mark on a VGA console it owns - parses a 15-region memory map, manages 127,996 frames, stress-tests a heap - rotates three tasks, sleeps one for 200 ticks and wakes it (`C awake`); the demo capture also shows a task that never yields being preempted (`K5 preempt: task 1 -> 2`) - loads and runs **five userspace ELF programs** in ring 3 — `hello`, `sleeper`, `crasher`, `readkey`, `demand` - enumerates PCI (six devices, the IDE controller among them) and draws a 1280×720 framebuffer console - survives a page fault by killing only the faulting task: `INT user page-fault … task killed` - answers a typed shell command, and exits cleanly: `user exit code 0` **The capability policy is written and proven, and it is one merge from this tree.** The slice lives on its own branch: it assigns a per-task permit at ELF entry, checks it on every syscall and preempts a ring-3 task on the timer. # ChromaInvert

Perceptual video and LUT reverse engineering engine. It recovers a smooth 3D LUT that matches source footage to a reference grade, then exports a portable `.cube` file.

Built using Meta's proprietary and open weights models for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Oct 26 – Nov 4, 2026), Indie Dev Track.

## Layout

- `engine/`: Python color engine (differentiable LUT, losses, `.cube` I/O)
- `app/`: C++ desktop host (FFmpeg pipeline, preview UI)
- `assets/`: test footage and reference frames, sources noted in `assets/SOURCES.md`
- `scripts/`: validation and benchmark helpers
- `docs/`: architecture and planning documents
- `work/`: gitignored runtime scratch directory

## Quickstart

1. Install Python 3.10 or newer with `ffmpeg` on PATH.
2. `python -m venv .venv --system-site-packages`
3. `.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1`
4. `python -m pip install -e ./engine`
5. `python -m pytest engine/tests -q`
6. `python scripts/validate_cube.py`

## Real footage quickstart

1. Create the frame directories: `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force work/frames/source, work/frames/reference`
2. Extract a source frame from a Rec709 clip: `ffmpeg -y -ss 0 -i <clip> -frames:v 1 -q:v 2 work/frames/source/source_001.png`
3. Build a warm graded reference with FFmpeg (or extract one from a graded clip) and save to `work/frames/reference/ref_001.png`: `ffmpeg -y -i work/frames/source/source_001.png -vf "colorbalance=rs=0.15:bs=-0.15,eq=saturation=1.2" -frames:v 1 -q:v 2 work/frames/reference/ref_001.png`
4. Create `work/job.json` (see `assets/job.json.example`; frame names match `source_001.png` and `ref_001.png`) with `input_profile` set to `rec709`.
5. Run: `python -m chromainvert run work/job.json`
6. Validate the exported cube: `python scripts/validate_real_footage.py work/out.cube work/frames/source/source_001.png` (`scripts/validate_cube.py` is the generic FFmpeg `lut3d` acceptance check, not the run validator)
7. Apply the grade: `ffmpeg -y -i work/frames/source/source_001.png -vf lut3d=file=work/out.cube work/graded.png`

Or use the reusable driver: `python scripts/run_real_footage.py --source <video-or-dir> --reference <video-or-dir> --work-dir work`.

The venv reuses the system GPU PyTorch install via `--system-site-packages`, so no large CUDA download is needed.

## Status

See `docs/CHROMAINVERT_HACKATHON_PLAN.md` for the full plan and `docs/PROGRESS.md` for the build log.

# Cadastra-Cameroon

### Autonomous Cadastral Audit & Geodetic Land Fraud Detection Platform
**Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026**

---

## 1. Project Identity

- **Project Name:** Cadastra-Cameroon (CADASTRA CM)
- **Tagline:** Autonomous Geodetic Audit & Cadastral Risk Analysis Powered by Meta AI
- **Track / Event:** Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026
- **Target Jurisdiction:** Republic of Cameroon (MINDCAF Cadastral Framework, UTM Zones 32N & 33N)
- **Languages:** Native Bilingual Support (English and French)

---

## 2. The Problem: Land Insecurity & Cadastral Risk in Cameroon

Property acquisition across Cameroon and the Central African sub-region faces deep structural challenges rooted in paper-based archives, fragmented records, and manual survey workflows. Land buyers, banks, diaspora investors, and conveyancing notaries frequently confront three critical failure modes:

1. **"Superficie Fictive" (Fraudulent Surface Inflation):** Paper boundary plans (*Plans de Bornage*) frequently state an inflated parcel area (for example, declaring 1,500 m² for a plot whose physical boundary beacons enclose only 980 m²). This gap is exploited to overvalue collateral, inflate compensation during expropriation, or defraud buyers who cannot independently calculate coordinates.
2. **Topological Defects & Coordinate Inconsistencies:** Boundary polygons with unclosed perimeters (where beacon $B_n$ does not return to $B_1$), self-intersecting boundary lines (figure-eight or bow-tie anomalies), or inverted Easting/Northing coordinates that place the parcel in an entirely different administrative zone.
3. **UTM Projection & Ellipsoid Confusion:** Cameroon spans two Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) zones: **Zone 32N** (`EPSG:32632`, Western, Littoral, and Central regions) and **Zone 33N** (`EPSG:32633`, Northern and Eastern regions). Coordinates computed in one zone but plotted in another produce massive positional shifts and distorted area figures.

Without specialized surveying software or access to a licensed surveyor before placing a purchase deposit, buyers face substantial financial loss and years of litigation.

---

## 3. The Solution: Independent Mathematical & AI-Assisted Audit

**Cadastra-Cameroon** is an independent, automated cadastral screening instrument. It bridges the gap between raw surveying data and everyday legal due diligence:

- **Instant Plan Ingestion:** Ingests boundary survey plans via document drop (PDF / JPG), manual coordinate entry, or mobile submission.

# Hubog Shoot

A product-photo studio for small sellers in the Philippines. You upload one phone photo and describe the product in English, Filipino or Taglish. A Muse Spark agent plans the shoot, Muse Image renders the listing photos and promo creatives, and SAM 3.1 cleans up the product with a tap. You download a pack sized for Shopee, Lazada, TikTok Shop and Facebook Marketplace, with captions.

*Hubog* means "to shape" in Filipino.

**Live:** https://shoot.hubog.app

## Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon

Hubog Shoot is being built from zero during the [Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon](https://cerebralvalley.ai/e/meta-ai-developer-hackathon) (Oct 26 – Nov 4, 2026), Indie Developer track, theme "Build for Your World". The first commit is Oct 27, 2026, and every line of code in this repo was written during the event.

**Prior work:** the Hubog name, original logo and icons, palette, and type system come from the author's existing product at hubog.app. The Shoot descriptor and studio layout were created for this project. No application logic or model prompts are copied from hubog.app. The site uses the original Hubog lockup unchanged with a separately rendered Shoot descriptor. Fonts are third-party assets under the SIL Open Font License, included alongside the font files.

The plan, the schedule and the rules checklist are in [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md).

## How it works

1. **Brief.** One phone photo, plus a description typed or spoken in English, Filipino or Taglish. JPEG, PNG, WebP, and HEIC/HEIF photos work; unsupported HEIC browsers convert the image on the device.
2. **Plan.** Muse Spark reads the photo and plans five shots (main, two lifestyle scenes, a close-up, a vertical promo) as JSON, with captions and a listing in the seller's language.
3. **Shoot.** Muse Image renders each scene with the seller's photo as the reference.
4. **Check.** Muse Spark compares each shot with the real photo: same shape, colour and label text? A shot that changed the product is reshot once. If it fails again, the scene is regenerated empty and the seller's real cutout is placed in it.
5. **Cutout.** SAM 3.1 cuts the real product out of the photo for the white-background main image. If it finds nothing, tap the product to outline it (with undo).
6. **Pack.** One zip with every image, every generated video, and the listing text. Generated scenes are labelled "AI-made scene".
7. **Animate (optional).** Any scene becomes a 5-second video: Muse Spark Open directs the motion, voice, and music bed from the frame, and LTX-2.5 renders picture plus native voiceover on a Modal B300.

## Meta models used

| Step | Model |
|---|---|
| Voice brief (code-switched Taglish) | Muse Voice Transcribe 1.0 |
| Shot plan, follow-up questions, quality check | Muse Spark 1.3 (image understanding, structured output) |
| Listing photos and promo creatives, refine by text | Muse Image 1.0 |
| Tap-to-select product mask, background cleanup | SAM 3.1 |
| Animation dir

# KudiLens

**Verified books for market traders, from a photo of their sales book or a voice note: in English, Pidgin, Yorùbá, Hausa or Igbo, on Telegram (and WhatsApp, on Meta's invite-only test number for now).**

Nigeria has 39.7 million micro, small and medium businesses, 96.9% of them micro (NBS/SMEDAN MSME survey, 2020 data), and most keep their records in exercise books. Without records they can't prove their income, so they can't borrow. KudiLens is a bookkeeping agent: the trader sends a photo of the page or speaks a voice note, KudiLens reads it, **checks every number**, and the trader confirms with one tap. Confirmed entries go into a double-entry ledger sealed with a hash chain, which the trader can share with a lender as a **Kudi Passport**.

> Try it: open [@KudiLensBot](https://t.me/KudiLensBot) on Telegram and send one of the [sample pages](eval/samples/) (or your own).

## The idea in one line: the models propose, code verifies

| Step | Who does it |
|---|---|
| Read the page photo into structured lines (item, quantity, price, paid/owed, customer, box on the page) | **Muse Spark 1.3** (vision, strict JSON schema) |
| Listen to a voice note in Pidgin / Yorùbá / Hausa / Igbo, transcribe and translate | **Muse Spark** native audio. Muse Voice Transcribe has no Nigerian languages, so only traders who chose English go to it first (falling back to Spark if it hears fewer than 3 words); everyone else goes straight to Spark |
| Count stock from any shop photo (shelves, sachet strips on a wall, crates), no caption or labels needed | **SAM 3.1** finds every unit it can see (whole photo plus six overlapping sections); **Muse Spark** names each unit from cut-out tiles and also counts stacks by their layers; code takes the larger count per item, and the trader can correct any number ("salt 45") |
| WhatsApp-status flyer of today's stock and prices | **Muse Image** |
| Answer "who owes me?", "how was this week?" | **Muse Spark** agent with read-only tools over the ledger |
| Arithmetic, debts, duplicates, dates, confidence gate | deterministic code (`src/verify.ts`) |
| **Find the misread digit** using the trader's own handwritten page total | deterministic code: tries every confusable digit (5↔6, 1↔7, 3↔8 …) and, for lines that were hard to read, a dropped or extra zero; uses quantity × price as a second witness. If no single misreading explains the difference, it tells the trader the written total looks wrong |
| Post to the ledger | only after the trader confirms; balanced double entry in integer kobo (`src/ledger.ts`) |
| Tamper evidence | each confirmed entry is hashed with the previous hash and the SHA-256 of its photo/voice note; the lender's "Verify" button recomputes the chain |

Nothing a model says is written to the books until code has checked it and the trader has confirmed it.

## What the trader can do

- 📸 **Photo of a page** → numbered boxes on the photo + proposed lines with warnings → ✅ Save / ✏️ Fix ("line 2 na 6,500") / 🗑

# Teleion Fabric: the durable task queue and storage engine

> **Start at the main repository:** https://github.com/ta-amps/teleionlabs-teleion-fabric
> **Film:** [three-minute video file](https://teleionlabs.com/media/main-film-20261104o.mp4)

A pull-based durable task queue and atomic Task Object store for agent swarms.

Teleion Fabric is where independent AI agents claim durable Tasks over HTTP or MCP and keep checked Task Objects without sharing database credentials or stepping on each other.

Everything in Teleion Fabric is either a **Task** or a **Task Object**, and a worker never approves its own work (`maker != checker`):

- **Tasks** are leased units of work. A worker claims one under a fencing token and checks in, or parks it across hours or days. A separate worker checks it when the work needs that, and it finishes with a record: a digest over exactly what was written.
- **Task Objects** are the shared records and files that Tasks read, make and reuse. Each is versioned with compare-and-set and content-addressed by digest, so no version is lost or silently overwritten.

The live API still uses older machine names in some paths and fields, as the example below shows: Tasks are `verbs` and Task Objects are `nouns`.

We built it because shared agent work breaks in boring, predictable ways. Two agents grab the same task. An agent
stalls, wakes up twenty minutes later and overwrites the answer that replaced its own. A retry saves the same
result twice. Someone asks who did what, and nobody can say. Teleion Fabric gives each of those failures a rule, and
each rule a test.

## See it

A real call and its real output, November 4, 2026, 02:07 UTC:

```console
$ curl -s 'https://fabric.teleionlabs.com/ns/main/v1/verbs?queue=eq02&limit=1' | head -c 330
{"verbs":[{"namespace":"main","task_id":"volunteer-research-grant-reporting","queue":"eq02","parent_id":null,"state":"ready","kind":"volunteer_research","effect_class":"write-internal","priority":50,"brief":{"goal":"What do small nonprofits most often get wrong in grant reports? List 3 public sources with an exact quote from eac
```

## Notes

- An open caller can claim and report open Tasks, and it can't review any work. Admin and key routes stay closed.
- This repository's name, Python package and commands keep an older code name.

## For your agent

Add these four lines to your agent's `AGENTS.md`:

```text
Read https://teleionlabs.com/llms.txt first. No key is needed through December 31, 2026.
Search the shared Task Objects before you build anything.
Claim one Task at a time, and check in while you work.
Report once, with your result. A different worker checks it.
```

## Worker execution policy

Shared work runs as a claimed Task on an authorized worker. Agents on our servers are normal too, inside our spending caps and with records. The architecture has only Task Objects, Tasks, surfaces and narrow infrastructure, and Teleion Fabric is infrastructure. Seed packs bundle Tasks and Task Objects;

# Teleion Fabric shim: context and capability checks for any agent

> **Start at the main repository:** https://github.com/ta-amps/teleionlabs-teleion-fabric

**The Teleion Fabric shim** is a small layer between a coding agent and its model. It matches each request by keyword, by meaning or with a small model. Then it answers directly, or adds Task Objects and other context before the model call. It works with Meta Muse models and with hosts such as Baseten and Modal.

## See it

A real call and its real output, November 4, 2026, 03:08 UTC:

```console
$ curl -s https://shim.teleionlabs.com/health
{"ok":true,"surface":"shim","version":"0.1.0","storage":"cloudflare-d1","active_provisions":16,"context_entries":9,"standard_mode_only":true,"configurable_harnesses_only":true}
```

## Checks without the word list

Our full banned-word list is kept private. In a public copy, `make check` runs the word gate on a small made-up sample in `tests/fixtures/` and says so. A release can't: `scripts/check_release.py` refuses to go on without the real list. Browser checks are skipped, with a message, until you run `npx playwright install chromium`.

## Notes

- A no-key model call needs your own provider key. It never uses ours.
- Open callers don't share rules or memory with each other.
- This repository's name, code and machine values keep an older code name.

## For your agent

Add these four lines to your agent's `AGENTS.md`:

```text
Read https://teleionlabs.com/llms.txt first. No key is needed through December 31, 2026.
Search the shared Task Objects before you build anything.
Claim one Task at a time, and check in while you work.
Report once, with your result. A different worker checks it.
```

## Tasks and Task Objects in plain language

Everything rests on two simple ideas:

- **Tasks** are units of work (`enqueue -> claim -> heartbeat -> submit/park`). An authorized worker leases one, and a `fence` token keeps two workers from doing the same job twice. The live API calls them `verbs` in some paths and fields.
- **Task Objects** are every reusable tool, `Feed`, dataset, statute card, LoRA adapter spec, provision shim or record a Task uses or makes, stored as compare-and-set records guarded by `expected_version`. The live API calls them `nouns` in some paths and fields.
- **Where they appear:** the public surfaces are [Teleion Labs](https://teleionlabs.com/) and [Eranos](https://eranosforgood.org/). `113` seed packs bundle `1,860` reusable Task Objects and `596` Tasks.

## Why Everyday AI Use Feels Frustratingly Dumb Without a Shim

Raw LLM API calls force an ugly tradeoff on every turn:

1. **Prompt bloat (`HarnessTax`)**: Stuffing every project rule, post-cutoff schema, URI, and refusal boundary into a static system prompt burns thousands of tokens on every turn even when most of those rules don't matter for this edit.
2. **Post-cutoff amnesia**: Omitting those local contracts makes even strong models hallucinate retired fields, skip optimistic concurre

# FairBuy

**Find what fits. Choose the best purchase, not just the lowest price.**

FairBuy is an AI shopping research application: describe what you need, refine your preferences, and compare source-backed products and seller offers. It helps you research a purchase; it does not handle checkout or payments. See the [shopping flow](docs/Flow.md).

Built with React, TypeScript/Express, shared Zod contracts and PostgreSQL, using Meta Model API for conversations and web research. Cloudflare draft previews and Brave search are optional. It combines [Alberto’s demo](https://github.com/meta-hackers/fairbuy-alberto-demo) and [Alessandro’s demo](https://github.com/meta-hackers/fairbuy-alessandro-demo).

## Quick start

Use Node **24.22.1** (`.node-version`):

```bash
npm ci
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up -d
```

Set `MODEL_API_KEY` in `.env`, then:

```bash
npm run db:migrate
npm run dev
```

Open **http://localhost:5173**. See [local development](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) for a no-key demo, builds and tests.

## Important limits

AI extraction is not independent verification; prices, stock and seller claims may be stale or incomplete. Prices exclude shipping, and market coverage is not guaranteed. Avoid sensitive information and review provider data-use policies and billing limits before live use.

conversations, real tools, projects and scheduled work into a desktop app, a
floating companion and a terminal CLI.

Ask it to inspect a repository, edit files, run commands, research a page or
handle a recurring task. Tool activity, results and approval requests stay in the
conversation. Choose ChatGPT Browser, GitHub Copilot, Groq, Kilo or an

# Print3DFlow

Manufacturing workflow assistant for **Print3DStore**, built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon's Indie track.

Print3DFlow connects a customer request to a reviewed quote, a compatible printer reservation, and recovery when a printer becomes unavailable.

**[Watch the 2:55 YouTube demo](https://youtu.be/tIm6Na5HFAg)** — Meta-assisted intake, a verified tool trail, native X2D four-color quoting, and approval-controlled outage recovery.

See the [current architecture and system diagram](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for components, data flows, Meta integration, printer connectivity, and approval boundaries.

## Workflow

1. **Meta-assisted intake:** Muse Spark extracts a structured draft and asks about missing requirements. The operator reviews before creating a job.
2. **Geometry and quoting:** validate an STL, confirm units, preview the actual mesh, and obtain native Bambu Studio slice estimates or explicitly labeled manual estimates.
3. **Shop pricing:** versioned rate cards support material cost, waste policy, machine-time allowance, setup, markup, minimum charges, and reviewed support surcharges.
4. **Scheduling:** propose compatible capacity and commit reservations atomically after approval.
5. **Exception recovery:** inject a simulated pre-start outage, ask Meta to compare verified scheduling options, choose a proposal, and approve atomic replacement while preserving the quote.
6. **Cross-printer quote adviser:** independently slice selected imported A1, A1 mini and X2D profiles, calculate candidate quotes, and check each printer's schedule. After permission to share quote totals, Meta compares verified tradeoffs. You select an option and explicitly approve its exact price and reservation before anything is committed.

Meta handles intake and selects evidence-backed recovery reasons and a recommended option. The server validates every selected reason and renders text from verified facts; freeform model facts are not displayed. Quote arithmetic, scheduling constraints, recovery search, and the customer-update template remain deterministic application logic. No customer messages or print-execution commands are sent. Chamber-light changes are available only through separate explicit operator controls.

# Cleanroom

**Let your coding agent read the internet. Cleanroom makes sure your keys don't leave.**

Cleanroom is a plugin for Meta's [Muse Code](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code) coding agent that enforces Meta's
["Agents Rule of Two"](https://ai.meta.com/blog/practical-ai-agent-security/) at runtime. Meta's post says an agent that
holds all three properties in one session "at a minimum requires supervision, via human-in-the-loop approval or another
reliable means of validation", and names "oversight agents" as the research direction for providing it. Cleanroom is
that oversight agent. When a session crosses the line it does not just block the step: it hands the step to a verified
subagent on a Meta model that **finishes the task without the secret**, and the main agent carries on.

> Solo entry, Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, 27 Oct – 4 Nov 2026. See the commit history for the day-by-day build.

**Demo video (2:50):** https://youtu.be/V9oeDHIdqKM

## Seen live

Two real Muse Code sessions on the same task: read a third-party setup guide, check the project's
`.env`, register the service. The payload the agent sends is clean both times.

| Block mode: safe, but the task breaks | Quarantine mode: safe, and the task ships |
|---|---|
| ![Block mode: Cleanroom stops the outward call; "Registration blocked - not sent"](demo/live-block.png) | ![Quarantine mode: the step is rewritten on Muse Spark Open, registration returns ok, and the agent reports that Cleanroom quarantined the step](demo/live-quarantine.png) |

Left: all three Rule-of-Two conditions are present, so Cleanroom denies the step and the agent
hands the command back to the user. Right: the same trip, but the hook rewrites the step in
quarantine on Muse Spark Open, Muse Code runs the safe version, and the agent's own summary ends
with *"Cleanroom quarantined the registration step because the session holds untrusted input
and a secret."*

```

The flight recorder (one real session, replayed in a page) is hosted at

No model key is needed for any of that. With Muse Code installed, `muse plugins install .`,
`muse plugins approve cleanroom`, then run the hook through Muse's own tester:
`muse plugins hook test cleanroom:pretooluse --fixture fixtures/block-outward-env-read.json`.

# Lucid

**Lucid proves database leaks before you ship them, and teaches you why they happen.**

Lucid is for people who build apps with AI tools ("vibe coders") and have never read code. When you commit, Lucid reads the change in the background:

- **A risky change gets a warning card**: what could happen, who is affected, the line that does it, a fix you can paste into your AI tool, and the idea behind the risk. Risks always come first.
- **A safe but interesting change gets a lesson card**: what the change does in your app, the one line that does it, and a quick A/B/C check.

For a warning about database rules, Lucid then tries the leak for real: it builds your database setup in a disposable sandbox, adds two fake users, and attacks as a signed-out visitor and as the other user. If the attack gets through, the card switches from **Warning** to **Proven** ([Lucid Proves It](#lucid-proves-it)). If it doesn't, the card stays a warning: Lucid never says a change is safe.

Lucid is a VS Code extension (built for Cursor too). This repository holds the extension, the engine that writes and checks the cards, and the small server that runs it.

Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Oct 26 – Nov 4, 2026). Everything in this repository was written during the event.

## Demo video

**▶ [Watch the demo (1:10)](https://youtu.be/5G1evf6BiDk)**

- **Real product footage:** screen recordings of Lucid 0.3.5 running in VS Code on a small test app (team notes on Supabase). It shows a commit, Lucid reading it, the sandbox test with fake users, the warning and "proved" notifications, and the Proven card with the attack steps and the fix.
- **The leak is planted on purpose.** It's a deliberate test change (an insert rule that checks the wrong column), like a crash test. It isn't a mistake from a real app, and no real user data was involved.
- **Made with AI help:** the narration is an AI voice (Kokoro TTS). The titles, the "under the hood" diagram and the numbers screens are animations, not product footage.
- **The Meta model calls** are shown in [Run logs that name the models](#run-logs-that-name-the-models): a live run printing each step via Muse Spark Open on Baseten and Muse Spark 1.3 on the Meta Model API.
- **To try it yourself:** [Install](#install) the release the video uses (0.3.5), sign in with GitHub, and commit a change to a database rule.

## Install

1. Download **`lucid.vsix`** from the [latest release](https://github.com/shittuquoyum-ui/LUCID/releases/latest).
2. In VS Code: open the Extensions view, click the **`…`** menu, choose **Install from VSIX…** and pick the file. (Or run `code --install-extension lucid.vsix`.)

**GridXray uses Meta's Muse models to discover the hidden wiring of electrical distribution networks by experimenting on them.**
An AI investigator reads the meters a utility already has, forms hypotheses about which secondary substation feeds which,
designs virtual experiments on a physics simulator to tell them apart, sends field crews to photograph switches, and
reconstructs the network: with every connection marked as measured, inferred or uncertain, and scored against the truth
by a checker with no AI in it.

**Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026** · Track: Startup · Theme: Push the Frontier · by [Zynplex](https://zynplex.com)

![GridXray landing page: See inside the grid you can't see](images/landing.png)

## The problem

Distribution utilities do not know exactly how their medium-voltage networks are connected today. GIS records drift
from reality with every repair and every switching operation; switch positions are documented once and then changed in
the field; and the network is built meshed but operated radially through normally open ties, so the energized topology
is invisible from the map. Wrong topology means wrong fault location, unsafe switching orders, hosting-capacity studies
built on fiction and customers restored late.

Finding out is expensive: crews walking feeders, engineers operating switches one at a time. Every real experiment costs
time, risk and customer impact, so the question is not only *what is the topology* but **which experiment to run next**.
That decision is what GridXray hands to an AI, inside a simulator, before anyone touches the real network.

**Who benefits:** distribution planning and operations engineers (model validation before switching orders and
connection studies), GIS teams (finding outdated records), and field operations (crews sent only where a photo settles

# Archaeo

Point Archaeo at any GitHub repo to **understand its past, see its present, and fix its future**.

Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Oct 26 – Nov 4, 2026).

## The problem

Joining an unfamiliar codebase is slow. The reasons behind the code are buried in thousands of commits and pull requests nobody reads, the architecture lives in people's heads, and a bug report arrives as a symptom with no pointer to the code. Archaeo reads the whole repository, history included, and answers with citations you can check: every claim links to a commit, a pull request or a `path:line` range.

## What it does

- **The Past.** A timeline of the project's eras, each with a narrative that cites its key commits and pull requests. "Why does this exist?" for any file or symbol finds the commit and pull request that introduced it and explains how it evolved.
- **The Present.** An interactive architecture map (size is lines of code, color is churn, hotspots stand out, folders expand). A Q&A agent with six code tools and hard limits on tool calls, time and cost streams answers whose `path:line` citations open in a code viewer. A request-flow walkthrough follows the call graph from an entry point and highlights each hop on the map.
- **The Future.** Paste an error, a stack trace or a GitHub issue URL to get a case file: ranked suspects, evidence and a root-cause hypothesis. Archaeo then writes patches and runs each one against the full test suite in an offline Docker sandbox, up to 3 attempts. A patch is offered only if it introduces no new test failures, and its regression tests are checked to fail without the fix. Nothing is pushed until you approve, and approval opens a pull request inside your fork.

Every commit, pull request and code citation is checked against the repository before it is shown.

## How it works

```mermaid

  api --> models[packages/models]

# topo-agent **Tap one hold. Get the whole boulder problem.** A topo agent for bouldering gyms, built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Oct 27 – Nov 4, 2026). Snap a photo of the wall and tap one hold. **SAM 3.1** outlines every hold, then a **Muse Spark** agent uses tools to inspect, compare and zoom in, and picks only the holds that belong to the same problem. The resulting topo becomes a problem that climbers can share in [Mirai Climbing](https://mirai-climbing.com/), a climbing app. ## Why we built it **A climbing app needs every problem added first.** Apps for gym climbers let you find a gym's problems, log your sends and share them. But before any of that, someone has to make a topo for each problem: a photo of the wall with its holds marked. Marking every hold by hand takes time, and gyms reset their walls again and again, so keeping up is hard. We want adding a problem to take one tap, so any climber at any gym can do it. Tap one hold, and the topo agent outlines the whole problem; the climber checks it, fixes a hold if needed, and saves it as a shared problem in the app. Nobody has to mark the same problem twice. Mirai Climbing started as a way to find climbing partners. Partner finding alone is a small market, so we moved to topos: something every climber uses every session, and a shared problem is a natural way for climbers to meet. ### It also helps climbers who can't tell colors apart ![What most climbers see, the same wall with red-green color blindness (simulated), and the problem outlined by the topo agent](docs/images/colorblind.png) All holds of one problem share a color (or a piece of tape), and that is how climbers know which holds they may use. But color vision deficiency is common: red-green types affect up to about 8% of men of Northern European descent and about 4–6.5% of Japanese and Chinese men ([review](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12385717/)), roughly one man in twenty in Japan. Because the topo agent outlines the problem instead of relying on color, the problem is visible without telling colors apart. ## Why an agent? # SpiralAI

## AI designs. Physics verifies.

A physics-verified scientific design agent exploring graphene mechanical energy storage with Meta Muse Spark Open.

**47/47 automated tests passing | Live Muse agent | Independent physics verification | Minimum-strain optimization | Provenance-tracked benchmarks | Resilient Agent Console**

SpiralAI explores a fundamental question for scientific AI:

> **Can an AI agent generate useful scientific designs without being allowed to invent the physics that validates them?**

SpiralAI separates creative AI reasoning from deterministic numerical calculation and independent scientific verification.

```text
AI DESIGN
    |
    v
DETERMINISTIC PHYSICS
    |
    v
INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION
    |
    v
VERIFIED FEEDBACK
    |
    v
REDESIGN OR STOP
```

> **Muse designs. Physics calculates. The verifier decides.**

## Why SpiralAI?

Generative AI can produce scientifically plausible ideas, but plausible reasoning is not the same as physical validity.

SpiralAI gives an AI agent freedom to explore while keeping numerical scientific claims under the control of deterministic physics and an independent verifier.

The system can:

- propose candidate designs with Meta Muse Spark Open;
- evaluate candidates using deterministic physics;
- independently verify numerical provenance;
- learn from verified results;
- redesign unsuccessful candidates;
- optimize for minimum required strain;
- detect repeated or invalid proposals;
- reject unsupported numerical claims;
- refuse false experimental-validation claims;
- escalate candidates beyond the supported screening boundary;
- preserve complete run provenance;
- replay real recorded trajectories if the live API is unavailable;
- stop honestly when the available physics cannot justify a target.

## Agent Console

SpiralAI includes an interactive scientific-design console built with Streamlit.

The interface visualizes:

```text
PLAN -> ACT -> PHYSICS -> VERIFY -> REDESIGN
```

The console supports three execution modes.

### Live Muse

Runs the official hackathon model:

```text
meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026
```

Muse proposes candidate designs while all numerical physics is calculated independently.

### Deterministic Optimization

Searches for the lowest verified strain satisfying a requested system-level energy target.

### Provenance Replay

Loads a previously recorded real Muse trajectory from JSONL provenance records.

This mode requires no live API call and provides a resilient demonstration fallback. If the live model endpoint becomes unavailable, SpiralAI can fall back to a provenance-backed run rather than generating synthetic replacement evidence.

## Working Muse Agent Demonstration

For a theoretical system-level target of:

```text
50 Wh/kg
```

one recorded Muse trajectory produced:

| Iteration | Muse proposal | Verified physics | Independent verification |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 5.0% strain | 26.07 Wh/kg | `TARGET_NOT_REACHED` |
| 2 | 7.0% strain | 4

# VideoLab

A phone-based physics measurement instrument. Film an experiment in slow motion with an A4 sheet in frame. SAM 3.1 tracks the object, deterministic code turns pixels into metres and fits the physics, and a Muse Spark agent plans, quality-checks and explains the run.

Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Push the Frontier). **All code in this repo was written during the hackathon, starting after the official start on 2026-10-26 (12:00 PM ET).** The commit history shows how it was built.

**Live:** https://balmca28--videolab-web.us-east.modal.run · **Demo video (3 min):** [docs/VideoLab-demo.mp4](docs/VideoLab-demo.mp4)

## What it does

- SAM 3.1 video tracking, scored against synthetic clips with known ground truth.
- A4 sheet detection (threshold sweep, midpoint re-cut, sub-pixel edge-line corners) and the pixel -> metre homography. `scripts/check_geometry.py` reports corner, offset and scale error.
- Physics fits (pendulum: circle-fit length + damped, amplitude-corrected period; free fall: auto release/impact + parabola; spring: damped oscillation -> k) with calibration-aware uncertainties, plus `backend/pipeline.py` (track -> sheet -> metres -> fit -> ghost overlay in pixels). On the synthetic clips with SAM 3.1 tracks: pendulum g 9.76 ± 0.07, free-fall g 9.71 ± 0.06, spring k 20.00 ± 0.02 N/m (true 9.81 and 20.0).
- Muse Spark lab partner (`backend/agent.py`, Responses API tool loop) with five deterministic tools (`plan_experiment`, `check_quality`, `analyze_run`, `compare_runs`, `explain_physics`). Every number carries a ref like `[r1.g]`, and `backend/grounding.py` flags any number in the answer that no tool returned. FastAPI: `/runs`, `/runs/{id}`, `/runs/{id}/video`, `POST /runs` (upload -> SAM -> analysis), `POST /chat`.
- Tap to track: on the Record step the user taps the moving object on any frame and SAM 3.1 tracks from that point prompt. Small or plain objects that a text concept misses (a marble seen from 2 m) are still found; the text concept remains as the fallback.
- Accuracy benchmark (`scripts/benchmark.py`, clips from `scripts/synth.py`): 20 synthetic runs with exact ground truth across camera angle, distance, dim light, noise and motion blur. # paper-bro

Paste an arXiv paper and get an interactive course, published on
[AERO](https://aero.oops.wtf). No login. One paper gets one course: whoever
asks first starts the build, and everyone after that is sent straight to it.

Live at `https://aero.oops.wtf/paper-bro`. On any paper, swap `arxiv.org`
for `aero.oops.wtf/paper-bro` in the address.

Why each part is built the way it is lives in its module's doc comment
(`src/*.rs`, `shell/*.js`).

## What runs where

| Piece | Choice |
|---|---|
| Server | Rust: axum, tokio. One binary serving the SPA, the API, SSE progress, and the build workers |
| Database | Neon Postgres via sqlx (raw SQL). Migrations in `migrations/` run at boot |
| Front end | React 19 + Vite + Tailwind 3, built with bun, embedded with rust-embed |
| Model | Any OpenAI-compatible server (built against Muse Spark Open), through `src/llm.rs`, no agent framework |
| Browser QA | `chrome-headless-shell` (Chrome for Testing, pinned), driven over CDP with chromiumoxide |
| Publishing | AERO's `/mcp` endpoint with a personal access token; courses live at `/p/arxiv-<id>` |
| Announcements | Each published course is posted once to the [paper-bro Telegram channel](https://t.me/arxiv_courses) by a bot, when `TELEGRAM_*` is set |
| Deploy | One binary and a headless Chromium behind a reverse proxy at `/paper-bro` |

A build goes: ingest → outline → lessons (6 in parallel) → browser QA →
review → repair (at most two rounds) → publish → a post on the Telegram
channel. Each stage checkpoints to
`course_artifacts`, so a restarted job resumes instead of paying again.
Progress streams to the paper page over SSE.

### Safety model, in one paragraph

Courses are served from the host's own origin, next to whatever else it
runs, and they contain model-written code influenced by untrusted paper text.
So the browser confines that code:

- Lesson prose goes through ammonia.
- Every lab runs in a sandboxed iframe with an opaque origin (`sandbox="allow-scripts"`).
- Quiz and glossary text is rendered as text.
- A CSP `<meta>` limits scripts, images and network calls.

`paper-bro qa-sample` shows a lab failing to read storage, cookies or the
network from inside its iframe.

## Local development

```sh
cp .env.example .env          # fill in NEON_DB, AERO_TOKEN, LLM_*
mkdir -p .chrome && cd .chrome && \
  curl -sSLO https://storage.googleapis.com/chrome-for-testing-public/156.0.8078.47/mac-arm64/chrome-headless-shell-mac-arm64.zip && \
  unzip -q chrome-headless-shell-mac-arm64.zip && rm chrome-headless-shell-mac-arm64.zip && cd ..
(cd frontend && bun install && bun run build)
cargo run -- serve            # http://127.0.0.1:8083/paper-bro/
```

`PUBLISH=0`, the default, keeps finished courses in the database and serves
them at `/paper-bro/preview/<alias>` instead of publishing to AERO. A dry-run
server starts no build workers unless `WORKERS` is set, so the Build button
only queues; `cargo run -- build <id>` builds one course in the foreground.

# Content Upgrades

[![CI](https://github.com/drawmeanelephant/content-upgrades/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/drawmeanelephant/content-upgrades/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

**Meta does the thinking. Give the content an upgrade.**

Content Upgrades turns model output and existing Markdown into richer documents:
callouts, receipts tables, footnotes, source links, and prose with some personality.
Meta Muse models supply content. Human-authored templates and deterministic checks
control the structure.

**Knap is the engine, not a second product name.** `knap-mcp` is one Zig binary
with the same tools available through a stdio MCP server and a direct CLI.

## An improvement loop, not another formatting prompt

The server scores the rendered document, probes its empty template slots, and
chooses the slot with the most promising formatting gain. It asks the model for
one value, checks that value, and keeps it only if the rendered score improves.
Existing nonempty values and the template do not change.

The model does not choose layout during content generation. A separate repair
path can ask for a template-region patch, which the engine must render again.

The same toolchain also supports existing Markdown: read-only corpus audits,
confined ingestion, extraction into template data, and policy-gated voice passes.
Those paths keep source-tree writes separate from generated artifacts.

## Run the demo without an API account

Use Zig 0.17.0 and `jq`. Install `boris` to include the publication-reference
check. Without it, `make demo` reports that beat as skipped.

From the repository root:

```sh
make engines
make
export KNAP_MCP_HOME="$(mktemp -d)"
make demo
```

The demo uses the offline `mock` backend and recorded model takes. It makes no
live model requests. Its transcript and generated documents are in
`demo/out/demo/`. Initial engine setup may fetch pinned source revisions.

Try the core loop yourself:

```sh
eval "$(scripts/engines.sh env)"
export KNAP_MCP_HOME="$(mktemp -d)"
knap-mcp/zig-out/bin/knap-mcp ratchet release-notes \
	-d knap-mcp/data/release-notes.min.json --backend mock
```

Inspect `steps`, `score`, `stop`, `data_id`, and `doc_id` in the response.
`density/3` measures formatting density, not factual accuracy or writing quality.
The loop can stop before filling every slot.

`make install` installs the binary under `~/.local/bin` by default. Set
`KNAP_TEMPLATES_DIR` and `KNAP_MCP_HOME` when running an installed binary outside
this checkout. See the [command and MCP reference](knap-mcp/README.md).

## Where Meta and Baseten fit

| Work | Model and route | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Draft structured content | Meta Muse Spark open through Baseten's direct API | [Submission capture](demo/frozen-submission/README.md) |
| Fill upgrade slots | Meta Muse Spark open through Baseten | Recorded upgrade input, output, and receipt in the submission capture |
| Repair a template and vary voice | Meta Muse Wonder 1.0

# Meaning Check
**Try it live: https://pagyemang-dotcom--meaning-check-web-web.us-east.modal.run/** (scenarios open instantly; a new message wakes the GPU readers, which takes a few minutes after a pause).

**Version 2.1: click any reader to see exactly how it read your message.** Every message is read by two Meta models.** Muse Glimmer readers (16) and Muse Spark readers (8) read
your message; it counts as misread if either model's readers misread it, and the fix is the shortest wording both
understand. The independent test below showed why: one model's readers miss misreadings another model makes.

**See who would misread your message, and what they would take it to mean. Then fix it with the fewest words.**

The same words are understood differently by readers with different backgrounds, and by AI agents with different
settings. "Please table this item" means *discuss it now* in London and *put it off* in New York; "close it if it's
resolved" leaves an agent to decide who judges "resolved". Meaning Check has a panel of readers read your message,
shows who misreads it and how, adds the shortest set of clarifying statements that every reader understands, and
tests the result on readers it never used.

## Result

- **Pre-registered (Muse Glimmer readers never used to build the fixes):** understanding rose from 52.7% to 100%
  across the 14 test messages (gain 47.3 points, 95% interval 21.4 to 71.4); no message got worse.
- **Pre-registered, independent model (Muse Spark, which built nothing):** the fixes transfer, +53.6 points [25.0,
  85.7]. The panel's flags do not fully transfer: Muse Spark misread "biweekly", "revert", "bring a plate" and "delete
  old files", which every Muse Glimmer reader understood. One model's readers miss misreadings another model makes.
- A plain "make it clear" rewrite does about as well on these tests (exploratory). The evidence supports Meaning Check
  as a check before sending: who misreads, what they take it to mean, and whether a wording survives readers it was
  not built for.

Details, caveats, a void run and every amendment: `RESULTS.md`.

# Memex

**Your repo remembers the code. Memex remembers you and your work.**

A context layer you own that works with any AI agent: the durable stuff, like preferences, decisions and their reasons, people, plans and background, shared across every tool you use. Code-specific context stays where it already lives (your repo, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`); Memex holds what a repo can't, so you don't re-explain yourself in each new app.

Tell your agent: **"Set up a Memex for me using this repo"** and it follows [SETUP.md](SETUP.md). Later, tell any agent **"sync memex"** and it follows [SYNC.md](SYNC.md).

- **Your data, your Supabase.** Nothing is hosted by anyone else. Cost is pennies a month.
- **Any agent.** Memex is an MCP server over HTTP. Tested with Claude and Muse reading and writing the same memory; Codex, Cursor and other MCP clients connect with a URL and a key.
- **Sync.** Agents push durable facts and pull what the others learned, incrementally, without duplicates, in pages.
- **Hands-off, if you want it.** Ask any agent that can run scheduled tasks to "sync memex every morning" (pull-only: it fetches what other agents saved and summarizes it) or "sync memex every morning and save what's worth keeping" (pull and save: your yes at setup is the standing approval). Unattended saves are limited by the server itself to a small number of short notes per run (10 by default; configurable), skip anything secret-like, skip repeats of what the agent already saved (or what you retracted), and are tagged `auto-sync`. A `retract_thoughts` tool can hide exactly those notes, reversibly, if one was wrong.
- **Search that finds things.** Meaning and exact words are searched together and fused. Recent notes can be favored on request. Notes that a later note corrected are flagged, ranked lower, and shown next to their current version. A note that re-states something the user already corrected (easy for an unattended agent to do) is flagged as disputed, and the correction is shown first.
- **Dreaming (optional).** A nightly job uses a model to tag, summarize and connect memories, resolve relative dates, write a short digest, and, once enough notes pile up about one topic, write an **overview note** of the current picture (what it is, key decisions, state, open questions). Overviews are linked back to their source notes, use corrections and skip outdated or disputed notes, and are refreshed (the old version marked replaced) when new notes join the topic. It never deletes or rewrites what you wrote, and every change is logged and reversible. It runs only if you add a model API key.
- **Careful with secrets.** Anything that looks like a credential is flagged `restricted`: never sent to a model or an embeddings provider, and hidden from search and sync unless explicitly requested. Agents are told to treat memories as evidence, never as instructions.

Early, and in daily use by its author across several agents. The setup was tested end to end on a brand

## The Agricultural Challenge

Smallholder farmers across rural Tamil Nadu face severe systemic hurdles:
1. **Middlemen Exploitation**: Intermediaries capture significant margins of consumer price spreads due to asymmetric market information.

## Why

Farming today runs on things bought from outside: fertiliser from suppliers, and the know-how to use it from the co-op and the dealers. About 70 % of the world's phosphate rock reserves are in Morocco, and China has restricted phosphate fertiliser exports since 2021. As cheap, steady supply ends, depending on outside inputs becomes the weak point.

The way out is to buy less from outside and rebuild around the field's own strength — roots and mycorrhizal fungi cycling phosphorus. But every field has different soil and different weeds, so no single method can be handed down from above. Instead, AI reads each field — its terrain, geology, weeds and weather — and the farmer looks, works, and checks the AI against what actually happens. It is like open source: you can read the inside, what people learn is kept and shared as records, and now AI helps you read.

My field lies just south of the Median Tectonic Line in Tokushima, a former paddy with a plough pan at 20 cm. I farm it without fertiliser or pesticide because I want to try Masanobu Fukuoka's natural farming, and I want the records to show what it gains and what it loses; the tool takes no side and has no method of its own. It has had no fertiliser for four years; one plot I left uncut for a single year is now goldenrod and Amur silver grass (ogi) taller than I am, grown with nothing brought in. The soil here is rich in minerals; what is missing is the way for plants to take them up themselves. So the tool reads such land and proposes where and how to cut first to bring it back into crops.

Growing is not enough on its own; selling, too, has been handed to the co-op and the wholesale market, and today's distribution does not carry to the buyer how a field was grown. ﻿# GHOSTLINK
### When the Network Disappears, the Link Remains.

GHOSTLINK is an offline-first emergency communication prototype designed to help SOS messages move between nearby phones over Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) when normal internet connectivity is unavailable.

## The Problem

During emergencies, mobile data and internet access may be unreliable. GHOSTLINK explores a way to create and store emergency reports locally, transfer them to a nearby phone, and send them to a backend when a device with internet connectivity becomes available.

## How It Works

1. **Create an SOS:** Record emergency information such as incident details and location.
2. **Store locally:** Save the SOS in a local outbox so it can remain available offline.
3. **Discover nearby devices:** Scan for nearby BLE peers.
4. **Relay manually:** Select a discovered peer and initiate an SOS transfer.
5. **Reach the backend:** A receiving device with internet connectivity can submit the report to the FastAPI backend.
6. **Review incidents:** The backend stores reports in SQLite for retrieval by connected clients or a responder dashboard.

> **Current scope:** BLE discovery and relay are user-initiated. Autonomous background forwarding and a fully self-organizing multi-hop mesh are future work, not claimed as completed features.

## Architecture

```text
Flutter Mobile App
       |
       +--> Create SOS
       |
       +--> Local Outbox (SQLite)
       |
       +--> Scan and Select BLE Peer
                    |
                    v
             Nearby Phone
                    |
             Internet Available?
                    |
                    v
             FastAPI REST API
                    |
                    v
              SQLite Database
                    |
                    v
         Responder Dashboard / API
```

## Technology Stack

- **Mobile:** Flutter and Dart
- **Device communication:** Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)
- **Local persistence:** SQLite
- **Backend:** Python and FastAPI
- **API format:** REST and JSON
- **API contract:** OpenAPI YAML
- **Location:** GPS/location services where available

## Repository Structure

```text
GHOSTLINK/
├── mobile/       # Flutter mobile application
├── backend/      # FastAPI service and API contract
├── docs/         # Project documentation and diagrams
├── .gitignore
└── README.md
```

## Getting Started

### Requirements

- Flutter SDK and Dart
- Python 3.10 or a compatible Python version for the listed dependencies
- Android device or emulator
- Bluetooth-capable physical devices for BLE testing
- Git

### 1. Run the Backend

Open PowerShell from the repository root:

```powershell
cd backend

uvicorn app.main:app --reload
```

When the server starts, open:

- API documentation: http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs
- OpenAPI contract: `backend/contract/resqmesh-openapi.yaml`

# agent-cost-harness

[![tests](https://github.com/IrwinJam/agent-cost-harness/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/IrwinJam/agent-cost-harness/actions/workflows/tests.yml)

## Cut your agent's API cost by 21 to 37%, and prove it didn't get worse.

Most cost tools show you a smaller bill. This one also checks that your agent still does its job, and
gives you the numbers to back it up.

| | Agent cost per run | Tasks passed |
|---|---:|---:|
| No harness | $0.0502 | 94% |
| `cache_layout` | $0.0394 (**-21%**) | 92% |
| `cache_layout` + low reasoning | $0.0315 (**-37%**) | 94% |

<sub>Measured on Meta's muse-spark-1.3, 40 customer-service tasks, 400 runs, about $30.
Details in [RESULTS.md](docs/RESULTS.md).</sub>

**Building on Muse?** Run `python -m harness serve --muse --policies cache` and read
[MUSE.md](docs/MUSE.md). It covers two things in Muse's API that quietly cost you money, and how this
fixes them.

AI agents send the same stuff over and over, and a lot of what they pay for is the same prompt start
getting billed at full price. This shows where the money goes and cuts the waste without breaking the
prompt cache. Then it tests the change on real tasks, so "cheaper" comes with proof that nothing broke.

It works with any provider that speaks the OpenAI API format. Everything runs offline with a built-in
simulator, so you can try it without a key.

## What I found

I spent about $30 testing this on Muse (muse-spark-1.3) with a public customer-service agent benchmark.
40 tasks, 400 runs total.

- `cache_layout` cut agent cost 21% (95% CI 17% to 25%). The agent made the same calls and wrote about as
  much, so the whole saving is cache. Input from cache went from 84% to 94%.
- Low reasoning effort on top cut another 21%. I ran it twice, once on a different day and once side by
  side, and success didn't drop either time.
- Both together is 37% off, about $37 saved for every $100.
- On 64 short live conversations the cache alone saved 47%.

Two things in Muse's API cost you money without you knowing:

1. Without a shared `prompt_cache_key`, about 16% of input missed the cache even when every prompt started
   the same. Sending one key fixed it.
2. Each reasoning effort level has its own cache. Switch effort mid conversation and you pay for the whole
   conversation again. Pick one and stay on it.

What isn't proven yet: prices come from Meta's list, not a real bill. Success stayed within 2 points in every run, but 1 to
3 runs per task isn't enough to rule out a small drop. And it's all one benchmark.

Full numbers are in [RESULTS.md](docs/RESULTS.md). Whether it would save you money is in
[GUIDE.md](docs/GUIDE.md).

## Try it

Needs Python 3.11 or newer. No key needed. To use it with your own agent and provider, see [SETUP.md](docs/SETUP.md).

```bash
python -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"   # Mac or Linux: .venv/bin/python
.venv/Scripts/python examples/simulate.py --clock
```

That runs one

# EchoVision

A public "watch this for me" prototype from [Open Independence](https://openindependence.com). You point a camera or shared screen at something, ask for one thing - "find the milk", "tell me when the light turns blue" - and EchoVision stays quiet while it watches, then speaks when it has an answer.

Built during the **Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon** (October 26 - November 4, 2026), Indie Developer track, theme "Build for Your World".

**Try it:** https://echovision-private-owner-prep.openindependence.workers.dev/ - no account, no install, works in a modern browser. (The shorter public link is planned as the canonical address but does not start sessions yet.)

## How it works

- The browser records a rolling buffer of short original clips (2 seconds each, up to about 8 seconds in total) from your camera or a shared screen.
- Recent clips go to Meta's **Muse Spark** model through the Meta Model API, along with your question. Spoken questions are transcribed by Meta's **Muse Voice** model.
- Answers are spoken by the browser's built-in speech, so nothing is sent to a separate speech service. Watching continues while a reply plays.
- It speaks only when there is an answer, and repeats only when the answer changes. This is clip-by-clip watching, not instant continuous vision.

## Goal-focused watching

Each question is one active goal:

- **Find** keeps the last confirmed location and reports when the target moves, without guessing where it went.
- **Change-to** waits quietly for the requested change, then completes.
- An unclear request gets one short follow-up question instead of a guess.

## Privacy and safety

- Clips and questions travel through Cloudflare to Meta for analysis. Spoken answers are synthesized on your device; depending on its settings the device's speech may use network voices.
- No sign-in. Clips and conversation history live only in worker memory (RAM); the server's durable storage holds usage counters, never media. **Stop** and **Forget** clear the session from memory, and the app says so itself: provider-side records are not deleted by Forget, and provider retention is governed by Meta's API terms (requests are sent with `store: false`).
- No face identification, no navigation directions, no safety guarantees. Brief events can be missed and answers can be wrong - do not rely on it for safety.
- API keys live only in server-side secrets, never in this repository.

## Architecture

Cloudflare Worker + Durable Objects:

- `worker.mjs` routes requests and gates every mode behind explicit configuration.
- `public-scene.mjs` coordinates watching: 2-second MP4 clips, strict JSON-schema model answers, changed-answer gating so only new information is spoken.
- `public-session.mjs` / `auth.mjs` / `owner-gate.mjs` handle signed public sessions and owner operations.
- `scene-voice.mjs` / `voice-fixture.mjs` handle speech-to-text and test fixtures.
- `public/` holds the browser UI, designed for screen-reader use: labeled

# PayMind Voice: bilingual AI collections calls for Buy-Here-Pay-Here car dealers

**▶ Live demo (it really calls your phone):** https://paymind-voice-hackathon.joarciniegas.workers.dev
**Built with:** three Meta models (Muse Spark 1.3, Muse Wonder 1.0, Muse Voice Transcribe 1.0) on the Meta Model API · Twilio ConversationRelay · Cloudflare Workers, KV and Durable Objects · Stripe (test mode)
**Team:** [BizMind AI Agency](https://bizmind.us), Houston, TX · Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, Startup Track (*Build for Your World*)

---

## The problem

Buy-Here-Pay-Here (BHPH) dealerships finance their own cars, mostly for buyers that banks turn down. Their business depends on collections, so someone on the lot spends hours every day calling late buyers:

- **Many calls reach the wrong person.** Telling a relative about the debt can break collection laws, so every call has to confirm identity first.
- **Many buyers speak Spanish.** In Houston that is often the majority of them.
- **There are rules about what you can't say:** no threats, no invented fees, no calls before 8 AM or after 9 PM, and the rep has to remember who asked not to be called again.
- **Nobody remembers what the buyer said last week.** "My son's dentist bill, I'll pay Friday" lives in someone's head or on a sticky note.

Big lenders have call centers for this. A 40-car lot on the south side of Houston has one person and a spreadsheet.

## What PayMind Voice does

| | |
|---|---|
| 🧠 **Plans the day** | Muse Spark reads the whole portfolio, the dealer's rules and each buyer's history, then decides **who to call, when and with which opening offer**, using tool calls (`schedule_call`, `skip_buyer`). The code then enforces compliance on top of its plan. |
| 📞 **Makes the call** | It speaks English or Spanish, **confirms identity before saying a single word about the debt**, explains the balance and negotiates a date within the dealer's limits. First words come in about 1 second. |
| 🛠️ **Acts with tools** | Each call ends in exactly one outcome, chosen by Muse Spark through function calling: `record_promise`, `send_pay_link`, `transfer_to_human`, `do_not_call`, `wrong_person` or `end_call`. |
| 💳 **Gets paid** | On a promise, the buyer gets a text with a secure Stripe pay link for the agreed amount. |
| 🗂️ **Remembers** | After hanging up, Muse Spark writes a two-line case note. The next call opens with it ("Last time you told me you'd pay Friday…"). |
| ⚖️ **Audits itself** | Every call gets an independent **compliance audit**. **Muse Voice Transcribe** re-transcribes the call recording with speaker labels, then **Muse Wonder** (a different, stronger Meta model than the one that spoke) checks it against 7 collection rules. The code checks what can be verified without AI. The scorecard appears on the page, the day's results feed the dealer's board, and the recording is deleted right after. |

**An AI back-office agent for small retail shops: voice note + shelf photo or video in, verified stock check and approved supplier reorder out.**

Built for the **Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon** (Indie Developer track, *Build for Your World*) with Muse Spark, SAM 3.1 and Muse Voice Transcribe.

> **Demo video (3 min):** `TODO: add link`
> **Live demo:** `TODO: add link or remove`

## The problem

Small and medium retail shops in Myanmar run on voice notes, phone photos and handwritten ledgers. Dashboards and accounting software do not fit how owners actually work, so stock errors and late reorders quietly cost them sales and cash. The same gap exists for small retailers across emerging markets.

The author's family runs a retail business in Mandalay, and this project is built from that firsthand experience.

## What it does

1. The owner sends a **voice note** plus a **photo or short video** of a shelf, or a photo of a supplier invoice.
2. The agent **transcribes** the note and **counts and segments** the stock in the media.
3. It **reconciles** the counts against the shop's ledger using tool calls and **flags discrepancies**.
4. It **drafts a supplier reorder** and shows its evidence.
5. The owner **approves in one tap**. Only then is the reorder sent.
6. The agent **reports back** with what was sent and what changed.

The agent never sends anything without owner approval.

```mermaid
flowchart LR

    A --> D[Muse Spark 1.3: read invoice and shelf]
    B --> E[Muse Spark 1.3: agent loop]
    C --> E
    D --> E
    E --> F[Tools: ledger lookup, discrepancy check, reorder draft]
    F --> G{Owner approval}
    G -- approved --> H[Send reorder + report back]
    G -- rejected --> E
```

## Meta models used

| Model | Role in the project |
| --- | --- |
| **Muse Voice Transcribe** (`muse-voice-transcribe-1.0`) | Turns the owner's voice notes into text |
| **SAM 3.1** (`sam-3.1`) | Segments and counts stock in shelf photos and video |
| **Muse Spark 1.3** (`muse-spark-1.3`) | Reads invoices and shelves, reasons over the numbers, and orchestrates the loop with tool calling and structured output |

All calls go through the Meta Model API (`https://api.meta.ai/v1`).

- Counts from SAM 3.1 are cross-checked against the ledger and against what the owner said in the voice note.

# CIDD 0.1

**Contract-Isolated Driven Development**  
*A contract-driven software generation engine powered by isolated LLM workers.*

> **The project grows. The worker's context doesn't.**

CIDD is an experimental software generation engine that uses a **deterministic orchestration pipeline** and **isolated, non-agentic LLM workers** to generate source code from a sealed graph of contracts.

Rather than giving an AI coding agent full repository access, CIDD assigns each worker a bounded contract and its permitted dependencies. The engine—not the model—handles orchestration, file operations, source staging, assembly, and validation.

**AI generates the code. CIDD controls the process.**

## What CIDD does

- Validates a structured application **Genome**.
- Expands that Genome into a **sealed contract graph**.
- Generates individual contracts using a configured LLM provider.
- Records per-contract status, token counts, elapsed time, and generation manifests.
- Supports selective reuse and regeneration against compatible, verified sealed graphs.
- Assembles a Flutter project and runs dependency resolution and static analysis.

CIDD workers **do not** inspect repositories, edit arbitrary files, execute tools or tests, delegate to other workers, or autonomously change the architecture.

**CIDD 0.1 is a research prototype, not a general-purpose autonomous app builder.** Its demonstrated end-to-end application is TaxiCat Mobile (Flutter/Dart).

## Prerequisites

For the Windows/PowerShell walkthrough below:

- Git.
- Python **3.11 or newer** (the project's declared minimum).
- Flutter SDK and Android SDK configured for Android development.
- An Android emulator or compatible device.
- Access to **one** generation provider: Meta API credentials for `muse-wonder-1.0`, or a local Ollama server with an installed compatible model.
- To **run TaxiCat**: a Mapbox public access token and a reachable TaxiCat HTTP backend.

The instructions below reflect the Windows/PowerShell workflow used for the TaxiCat demonstration. Other platforms may work, but are not documented here as verified CIDD installations.

## Install

```powershell

cd cidd

py -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e .

.\.venv\Scripts\cidd.exe --help
```

For subsequent commands, either activate the virtual environment:

or invoke the executable with its full path. In the examples below, `cidd` assumes the virtual environment is activated.

From the parent directory of the cloned CIDD repository:

```powershell

cd taxicat_demo

```

# AgentMap — Agent L1

**Crawl once, share the map.** AgentMap is a hosted [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) service that pre-maps merchant websites into a navigation graph, so a personal AI agent can answer *"find brake pads for a 2019 Civic on this store"* with a compact, verified path — instead of raw-browsing the whole site again on every task.

Raw browsing is what personal agents do today (see [Research](#research-how-personal-agents-use-websites-today)): open a browser, read screenshots/DOM/HTML, guess the next click, repeat. That costs 10⁴–10⁵ tokens per page and fails often. AgentMap pays the crawl cost **once**, stores *how the site works* (categories, search, filters, URL templates — never cached prices), and serves every later agent a ~250-token answer in milliseconds. Prices and stock are always re-checked live.

| Per product search | Raw agent browsing | Via AgentMap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tokens | ~83k–313k | ~250 |
| Time | ~200–300 ms cold | ~8–16 ms |
| Success | 52–55% | 68–77% |

Measured on 60 real shopping tasks — full report: [docs/bench/2026-11-04-speed.md](docs/bench/2026-11-04-speed.md). Token counts are `ceil(chars/4)` estimates, so read them as "~250 vs ~80k+".

mibo is an iOS app for families to use together. A friendly animated character, Mibo, leads short speech-practice lessons. A grown-up sits alongside, picks a lesson (or describes the words they want to practise and mibo makes a new one), and can step in at any moment with two arrow buttons.
