2. Press **Empezar la llamada de ejemplo**. A synthetic virtual-kidnapping call plays line by line, and the five script stages light up as they are heard.
3. Within a few seconds Ana's phone asks **"¿Estás bien?"** Press **Sí, estoy bien**. The house screen turns green: **"Ana ESTÁ A SALVO. CUELGA."**, with the seconds it took.

**The unhappy path:** press **Otra vez** and don't answer on Ana's phone. After 15 seconds Cuelga asks Lucía (the demo switches to her phone). If nobody answers, it tells you to hang up and shows **Llamar al 089**, Mexico's anonymous reporting line.

Virtual kidnapping is a common extortion script in Mexico. A caller plays a crying voice ("¡Abuelita, ayúdame!") and claims to be holding a relative. # It's the Medium

**Live site: [itsthemedium.com](https://www.itsthemedium.com)** · Demo video (3 min): [`its-the-medium-3min.mp4`](cancer-dependency-rsi/video/out/its-the-medium-3min.mp4) · Extended cut (5 min): [`its-the-medium.mp4`](cancer-dependency-rsi/video/out/its-the-medium.mp4)

An independent audit of two 2026 Nature studies that used organoids (tiny 3D copies of patients' tumours) to find genes cancers can't live without, as leads for new drugs.

## The problem, in one minute

Organoids differ from ordinary flat lab cells in two ways at once: their **3D shape**, and their **food**. Organoids are grown in a clean, lab-made liquid (the "medium") with almost no cholesterol. Flat cells usually get serum, the nutrient-rich part of blood.

So when a gene matters more in an organoid, is that because of the shape (the whole point of organoids), or just the diet?

The public DepMap database already held the control nobody had used: flat cells grown on the organoid medium. Same food, no 3D shape. We ran that check on all 17,525 genes.

**Result:** of the 456 genes that clearly behave differently in organoids, **387 (85%) change just as much in flat cells once they get the organoid food.** The effect follows the food, not the shape. The clearest case is cholesterol: with none in the food, cells must make their own, so cholesterol-making genes such as SQLE suddenly look essential. In a patient, tumours are fed by blood full of cholesterol, so those weaknesses may not exist there at all.

Of the other 69 genes, 68 are unresolved by the data and one (LSM7) leans weakly toward shape. Three Sanger headline genes (SCAP, DDX3X, ITGB1) are in the unresolved group: the more credible leads.

**The cheap test this points to:** put cholesterol back into the organoid medium and see whether these genes stop mattering. About two weeks, no new screen.

## How Meta's models are used

### 1. Muse ran the research loop

Muse Code, Meta's coding agent, was the host agent for the whole audit, under human direction. It ran the orchestration loop: it planned each step, wrote and ran the local analysis code, dispatched candidate generation and reviews, applied fixes, and kept the append-only record of every generation and decision.

- Loop specification and goal: [`cancer_rsi_handoff.txt`](cancer_rsi_handoff.txt), [`GOAL.md`](GOAL.md), [`PLAN.md`](PLAN.md)
- Every research generation, including failures and retractions: [`cancer-dependency-rsi/GENERATIONS.md`](cancer-dependency-rsi/GENERATIONS.md) and [`cancer-dependency-rsi/generations/`](cancer-dependency-rsi/generations/)

Candidate generation and adversarial reviews were sent to a separate model (`gpt-6.1-sol` through the Codex CLI, recorded in [`config/host.json`](cancer-dependency-rsi/config/host.json)), so the reviewer was never the model that wrote the work. Reviews ran over five roun

# Tap Me Volleyball

Tap yourself once in a phone-recorded amateur volleyball match, and get vertical (9:16) highlights of your rallies — the frame follows you, everyone else's face is blurred, and optional live-style commentary subtitles come in Korean, Japanese and English.

Built for the [Meta AI Developer Hackathon](https://cerebralvalley.ai/e/meta-ai-developer-hackathon) (Oct 26 – Nov 4, 2026) as a feature for Baegugu, a Korean amateur volleyball community. It runs as a mobile web app for Baegugu members; judges get access through the link in the submission form.

**Demo video (1:50):** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2Sbqm1EUjTg

## What the user does

1. Open the app from the Baegugu banner and pick a match video. "Do it all for me" works 10 minutes at a time; for a longer match the user picks where to start, then taps "do the next 10 min too" on the results screen (the video is not uploaded again). "Pick one by one" scans up to 30 minutes.
2. Pause on a frame where they look big (on the near side of the court) and tap themselves. A quick check stops a tap on someone too small or on nobody. Optionally add a hint ("green jersey #10") and the team name.
3. Close the screen. If other people are ahead in line, the app shows how many and roughly when it starts. A push notification arrives when the highlights are ready: a list of small previews, a combined reel, and one-tap "save all to Photos".

## How Meta AI is used

Everything goes through the **Meta Model API**. Only face-blurred clips and stills are sent, uploaded files are deleted right after each answer, and the contributor (training) mode is never used.

| Step | Model | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Find rallies | **Muse Spark** (`muse-spark-1.3`) | Watches the blurred match in 60-second chunks (2 fps) and returns when each rally starts and when the point is decided |
| Player cards | **SAM 3.1** (`sam-3.1`) | Detects every player at three moments of each rally |
| Find "me" in every rally | **Muse Spark** | Compares labeled player cards with a reference crop of the tapped user, one question per moment, and keeps the surest answer |
| Follow "me" | **SAM 3.1** | Video tracking of the chosen player across the whole rally, from just before the serve to just after the point (10 fps, up to 60 s); the vertical crop follows this track |
| Other players | **SAM 3.1** | Tracks everyone else, so face pixelation is never drawn on bodies and one team can be left unpixelated (with consent) |
| Team sorting (optional) | **Muse Spark** | Sorts players into the user's team and the opponents from two separate moments; a team is unpixelated only when both answers agree |
| Who won the point | **Muse Spark** | Asks which side serves the next rally (the rally winner serves next) and combines it with the side the user is on in that set |
| Commentary subtitles (optional) | **Muse Spark** | Writes 2–4 timed lines of broadcast-style commentary in ko/ja/en that match which team won the point |

# Meta Glass Academics

A demo academic platform for school & college students, designed around the
flow in `working plan.png`:

```
Meta Glasses Record ─┐
                     ├─→ Phone for Processing ─→ Database record ─→ Website ─→ Student / Teacher / Parent panels
Ask Meta AI (stuck) ─┘
```

**No glasses? No problem.** The external/laptop webcam acts as the glasses
camera (Glass Studio in the student portal). The Django server is the "phone"
processing layer, the JSON folder is the database, and Ask Meta AI runs on the
Meta Llama API with an offline study fallback.

## Quick start (Windows)

1. Start the server — double-click or run:
   ```
   backend\run-server.bat
   ```
   Everything serves from one URL (project venv lives in `backend\.venv`).
2. Open `http://127.0.0.1:8000/` in Chrome/Edge and sign in:
   - `student1` / `pass123` → student portal
   - `parent1` / `pass123` → parent portal
   - `teacher1` / `pass123` → teacher portal
3. In the student portal, open **Glass Studio → Start recording** (allow camera),
   then ask something in **Ask Meta AI**.

macOS/Linux: `bash backend/run-server.sh`.

## Project layout

```
website/
  main/      landing (Default.png) + aesthetic login (Login.png) — index/main/login files
  student/   student portal — stats, calendar, previous, diary, ASK, glass studio, profile
  parent/    parent portal — child, record, teacher consult, settings
  teacher/   teacher portal — students, marks, progress, calendar, announcements, parents
  shared/    api.js (client+session) · glass.js (camera module) · theme.css
backend/
  config/    Django settings/urls/wsgi
  core/      jsondb.py · meta_client.py · vision.py · views.py · urls.py
  database/  JSON tables + main_record.json index + SCHEMA.md
```

Each website folder has its own HTML/CSS/JS; `shared/` holds the two extra
modules (API client, Glass camera). Every sidebar label from the mockups is a
working icon button wired to a real endpoint.

## Enabling live Meta AI answers

```bat
set META_API_KEY=your_llama_api_key
backend\run-server.bat
```

Optional: `META_API_URL` (default `https://api.llama.com/v1/chat/completions`),
`META_MODEL` (default `Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8`).
Without a key, ASK answers from the built-in study guide and labels itself
`offline-fallback` so you always know which provider served you.

## Notes & limits (demo)

- Passwords are plain text in `users.json` — demo only, never ship this.
- Camera frames are analysed for brightness/sharpness/focus; only the metadata
  is stored (`glass_captures.json`), no video is retained.
- Camera needs Chrome/Edge on `localhost`/HTTPS; `file://` pages can use the
  camera in Chrome but the Django server must still be running for data.

# Hearth

Hearth is a control room for coding agents. It shows which agent windows really work. It shows which ones are stuck. It shows which ones wait for you.

Built with Muse (Meta) for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon.

![Hearth hero: a phone with a calm amber ring on dark glass](docs/images/hero.png)

## What it is

Hearth is one board for work and life. It lists coding agents across computers and projects. It holds tasks, reminders, and notes too.

## Why

One developer now runs many agents at once. They work on many projects and many computers. They fix bugs and add features at the same time. No one can track all that in memory. Agents give no board unless you read files or code. Hearth gives the board.

## Features

- Live list of agent windows across computers and projects.
- Truth check: working now, stuck, or waiting for you.
- Stuck reasons name billing and API errors.
- Needs-you list for approvals and questions.
- Approve or stop from the phone.
- Preview plus one-use code plus audit on every send.
- Voice commands from the phone, read-only by default.
- Tasks, reminders, and notes in the same place.

![Dev flow: agent lanes as a calm constellation](docs/images/dev-flow.png)

## How it works

The bridge reads terminal panes on each computer. It derives state from output signs. It never pastes screen text. The server merges panes into one feed. The phone app renders the board. Voice reads the board aloud. Writes need preview plus code. Details live in [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

![Architecture: phone, private server, bridge, model endpoint](docs/images/architecture.png)

## Run it

Prereqs: Rust stable, Node 22. No keys needed for the demo.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sanmayp/hearth.git
cd hearth
scripts/demo.sh
```

Full stack next: `make test`, then `cargo run -p hearth-server`. Then run `make ui-dev` for the phone UI.

## Built with Muse

Muse windows wrote the code. Claude reviewed it. Limits stay plain:

- Glasses speech is unverified on real hardware.
- Remote-host send stays OFF by default.
- AI batch runs in mock mode. No live calls ship in this repo.

## Safety

This repo holds no secrets. Voice is read-only by default. Writes need preview plus a one-use code. Every send lands in the audit log. Read [docs/SECURITY.md](docs/SECURITY.md) first.

## Status

Done: board, truth check, Needs-you list, approve and stop from the phone, voice commands, tasks and reminders.
Planned: Meta glasses audio on real hardware, live AI batch runs.

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

Haq (हक़, "what is rightfully yours") is an AI agent that takes an Indian consumer from "they refused my refund" to an escalation the company has to answer. leadui/hoist-decisions.readme_excerpt:
# Hoist

You've got an idea and an agent to build it. Whatever you build, the agent will ask you things: option one, option two, option three. Some of those answers take weeks to undo. Hoist stops the agent at those questions, answers the questions you'd have before you ask them, lets you decide, and writes the decision down so the next agent (or future you) knows why.

- **Try the demo** (sample data, runs in the browser): pick an idea (cake pre-orders, dog-walk bookings or a paid newsletter) and decide its hard questions: https://leadui.github.io/hoist-decisions/
- **Read the pitch:** https://leadui.github.io/hoist-decisions/landing.html
- **Built on [Bento MADR](https://github.com/leadui/bento-madr)**, the decision-canvas library that started here.

Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon with **Muse Code** (the agent Hoist guards) and, optionally, **Muse Spark** (an independent drafter and critic). No API key is needed: your agent can draft the decisions and Hoist checks them. With a key, Muse Spark drafts them in seconds.

What Hoist stands for:

- **It's okay to pause.** A pause costs a minute; a wrong call can cost weeks.
- **It's okay to ask dumb questions.** Every option comes with an everyday analogy, what living with it is like, and the terms explained.
- **It's okay to take your time.** Decide later, send it back to chat, or pick for now. The record says why, so changing it later is a plan, not a regret.
- **It's not okay to say yes to everything.** When speed matters, autopilot lets the agent decide, and Hoist writes every call down for you to review.

## How it works

Hoist steps in at two moments.

**When the agent is about to ask you something hard to undo**, Hoist's skill has it ask one question first: *"These are hard to change later. How do you want to decide?"* with **Answer here** or **Decide with Hoist instead**. If you pick Hoist:

1. Your agent drafts the decisions for the page through `hoist brief` and `hoist submit`, Hoist checks every draft against its rules (plain words, fair options, an honest downside for each) and sends problems back to fix. With a Muse Spark key, Muse Spark drafts instead, in about 20 seconds.
2. Your browser opens the decision page. Each decision is one canvas: the options in plain words, your answers as a matrix that shows what would flip the pick, the risks, the agent's own lean, and a critic.
3. You pick and commit. Hoist writes one [MADR](https://adr.github.io/madr/) record per decision to `docs/decisions/`.
4. The agent, waiting on `hoist wait`, gets your decisions and carries on. The page tells you it's okay to go back to the terminal.

**When the agent is about to add a database package** (for example `npm install mongoose`), the hook pauses it before the install runs and opens a single decision page for that choice.

Records bind afterwards: if the agent later tries something that conflicts with a recorded decision, Hoist blocks it and cites the record.

## Install

Requires macOS

# Fieldwise

**Crop-protection advice that works without signal.** An offline-first assistant for smallholder farmers and the extension workers who support them, built on Meta's Muse Glimmer, Muse Spark and SAM 3.1.

A farmer asks a question or photographs a leaf from any phone with a browser. The phone connects over local Wi-Fi to a **village hub**, one shared machine at the co-op or extension office, where **Muse Glimmer** answers from FAO extension guides with no internet, citing the guide page and showing how confident it is. Only when Glimmer is unsure does the hub remove personal details and send the case to **Muse Spark** in the cloud; with no signal, it waits in a queue. **SAM 3.1** outlines the leaf in a photo so the damaged tissue can be marked.

On 87 held-out questions, routing answered **46% on the hub** and scored **82.8%**, against 83.9% for Glimmer alone and 79.3% for Spark alone, at **about half the cloud cost** per question.

## The problem

Smallholder farmers often find a pest or disease when no extension officer is nearby, and mobile signal on farms comes and goes. A cloud-only assistant needs a good connection for every question, sends the farmer's words and photos (with names, phone numbers and GPS tags) off the phone, and a general-purpose model can state pesticide doses with no source.

Fieldwise is designed the other way round:
- **The hub answers first, offline.** Phones need only a browser and the hub's Wi-Fi, so no mobile data.
- **The cloud is a second opinion, not a dependency.** Only low-confidence cases go to Spark, and only after redaction. Offline, they're queued and the farmer gets the hub's answer marked as tentative.
- **Advice comes from the guides, with the page cited.** Doses must appear in a cited passage, chemical advice always carries a safety reminder, and anything the guides don't cover becomes a referral to the local extension officer.

## How it works

![FieldWise Flowchart](FieldWise.jpg)

| Model | Runs | Job |
|---|---|---|
| **Muse Glimmer 30B** (open weights, Meta's Q4_K_M GGUF via llama.cpp) | Village hub, offline | First answer to every question and photo. Confidence comes from its own token probabilities. |
| **Muse Spark** (`muse-spark-1.3`, Meta Model API, Standard mode) | Cloud | Second opinion when Glimmer's confidence is below the threshold. Receives redacted text and a GPS-free photo, plus the same guide passages. |
| **SAM 3.1** (`sam-3.1`, Meta Model API) | Cloud, on request | Outlines the leaf in a photo; the hub then marks the parts that aren't healthy green. |

**Why a hub and not the phone:** Glimmer is a dense 30B model (Meta's Q4 build is about 17 GB plus a 1.4 GB vision projector). No low-end phone can hold it, but one machine with about 24 GB of memory can serve a whole village's phones.

aeroxy/ainance.readme_excerpt: # Ainance A daily market briefing written by an AI analyst that grades its own calls. **Read today's:** https://aeroxy.github.io/ainance/ · **Every briefing:** https://aeroxy.github.io/ainance/archive/ · **Each morning on Telegram:** https://t.me/ainance_daily Every day at 05:00 Singapore time, just after the US close, finance-bro reads about 200 headlines from the last 24 hours, checks prices across markets, and publishes a briefing: - **Markets**: indices, rates, FX, commodities, crypto and US sectors, with each one's last move. - **Today's calls**: ten bullish and ten bearish, each scored 1x to 9x for conviction, with a thesis, the risk to it, and its sources. - **What happened**: a plain-English recap of the last 24 hours across stocks, crypto and commodities, every story linked to its sources. - **Watch next**: data releases, earnings and deadlines coming up. - **Scorecard**: how the earlier calls did. ## How calls are graded A call is about one asset's next trading session (the next 24 hours for crypto), and that is exactly how it is graded the next morning. - A hit is a move in the called direction, from the price shown with the call to the price once the asset has traded again. A weekend call on a stock waits for Monday's session. - Each graded call sits next to its market (the S&P 500 or the local index for stocks, bitcoin for crypto), so a call that rode the market reads differently from one that beat it. - A futures call whose front-month contract rolls over is voided rather than graded, since the jump between contracts isn't a move. A call that doesn't trade again within a week expires. - Hit rates by direction and by score band (1x–3x, 4x–6x, 7x–9x) go back to the analyst every morning, so its scores get calibrated against what actually happened. ## How it learns After grading, finance-bro writes down why each call worked or didn't, then revises a notebook of lessons: rules that have held up, mistakes to avoid, how its scores are calibrated, and what the market is like right now. # The Sentence Book — Muse

**Your life becomes your textbook.**

The Sentence Book turns the context a learner shares with their personal AI into a daily English lesson, then helps them practise it and build a printable book, page by page.

It is a language-learning app and a working example of a broader idea: a personal AI agent can bring context into a focused application without making the user explain their life again every day.

Built for the **2026 Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon**.

- **Live app:** https://sentence-book-muse.pages.dev
- **3-minute demo:** https://youtu.be/P3pbuOrL3ZQ
- **English connection/settings screen:** https://sentence-book-muse.pages.dev/settings?lang=en
- **Implementation and verification history:** [PROJECT_STATUS.md](PROJECT_STATUS.md)

## The problem

Generic lessons teach useful situations, but not necessarily the things you want to say about your own life. Free conversation asks you to produce those expressions before you have practised them. Writing a diary or choosing a new prompt every day adds another task.

The Sentence Book connects these experiences: your own Muse prepares a lesson from the context available to it, delivers it on a schedule, and the app provides structured practice before you return to conversation.

## Why Meta: two distinct roles

**The learner's own Muse supplies personal context and lessons.** With the learner's permission, it can use their conversations and social posts that it can access, read a shared learning-state summary, and deliver a lesson draft to their inbox. The schedule runs in Muse, not in a background timer inside this web app.

**Meta Model API supplies focused help during practice.** The app calls `muse-spark-1.3` through server-side routes for contextual expression meanings and English reconstruction feedback. The provider key stays on the server.

This separation is the point of the project: the personal agent knows the learner's context; the application provides a specific learning experience. Social posting is optional. The app does not independently collect a learner's social-media accounts or automatically publish posts.

A possible longer-term loop is life and posts → personal lessons → expressions the learner can use → new conversations or posts. This is a product hypothesis, not a measured engagement or learning result.

## Try it

1. Open the live **Desk** and try the built-in sample page.
2. To receive personal lessons, open **Settings**, sign in, create an inbox, and choose what to share with Muse.
3. Follow the connection instructions: review the shared summary and permissions, ask Muse to connect, create a connection key, and enter it into Muse's secure input.
4. Ask Muse to deliver lessons at your preferred time. Settings include lesson material, level, explanation language, delivery days and time; the schedule request must be conveyed to Muse.
5. Open **Inbox**, preview an arriving draft, and decide whether to file it in an existing or new binder

Zambia's early-childhood syllabi ask for play-based, adult-guided activities that the teacher observes rather than marks.

Teachers are expected to prepare this material themselves. For one lesson, a teacher has to:

# Genebark

![Genebark](public/brand/genebark-lockup-white.png)

**An agent harness for evidence-grounded genetics research.**

[Live demo](https://evidence-workbench-xi.vercel.app) · [Architecture](docs/architecture/00-overview.md) · [Evaluation evidence](evals/genetics/) · [Security](SECURITY.md)

Genebark turns an open-ended genetics question into a concise, traceable answer and an appropriate scientific visualization. It retrieves literature, reads the relevant sections, extracts atomic findings, checks those findings against verbatim source text, compares experimental context and progressively renders the result while research continues.

It is designed for researchers, laboratory teams and technically trained students who need to understand what the evidence actually supports without manually reconciling dozens of papers. Genebark is a research tool—not a clinical decision system and not medical advice.

## Why it is different

A conventional chatbot usually retrieves passages and writes an answer. Genebark provides a controlled execution environment around the model:

- **Progressive research:** an immediate contextual acknowledgement is followed by an explicitly provisional abstract-grounded overview, then an immutable synthesis grounded in verified findings.
- **Evidence verification:** claims retain their source, locator and verbatim quote; deterministic checks validate existence, quotation, numbers, retraction signals and scope before verification.
- **Context-aware comparison:** agreement or contradiction is assessed only after considering organism, model, intervention, assay and experimental conditions.
- **Intent-driven visuals:** the same evidence can become an evidence map, comparison matrix, mechanism diagram or decision algorithm instead of a wall of text.
- **Transparent ranking:** every source receives an explainable score based on deterministic relevance, evidence level, explicit quality signals, currency and applicability.
- **Temporary conversational memory:** follow-up questions can refer to earlier genes, studies and findings inside the active anonymous chat without permanent conversation storage.

## How Meta powers Genebark

Genebark uses **Muse Spark 1.3 through the Meta Model API** for the semantic work that deterministic code cannot reliably perform:

- structuring complex genetics questions;
- reformulating thin or ambiguous literature searches;
- extracting atomic findings from scientific passages;
- judging semantic support and experimental scope;
- synthesizing provisional and verified overviews;
- labelling cross-study concordance and contradiction;
- transforming verified evidence into mechanism and algorithm structures.

# Bonisa

**Bonisa** ("show" in isiZulu) turns a phone video of a physics experiment into a
verified scientific measurement. Film a pendulum, and Bonisa measures *g* with an
honest uncertainty, or refuses to give a number and tells you how to fix your setup.

Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Oct–Nov 2026). All code in this
repository was written during the hackathon.

## How it works

1. **SAM 3.1** (Meta Model API) tracks the pendulum bob through every frame from a
   plain-language description such as "orange ball", and finds an A4 sheet on the
   wall to convert pixels to metres.
2. **Physics fit**: Bonisa fits a damped oscillation to the motion to get the period,
   fits the arc to locate the pivot and measure the string length from the video,
   corrects for swing angle, and computes g = 4π²L/T² with propagated uncertainty.
3. **Verification**: eight physics checks (tracking coverage, time resolution,
   number of swings, model fit, swing angle, camera tilt via the A4 sheet's aspect
   ratio, video-vs-tape length, precision). Any failure means no number is reported.

## Run it

```bash
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate          # Windows  (macOS/Linux: source .venv/bin/activate)
pip install -r requirements.txt
copy .env.example .env          # then paste your Meta Model API key into .env
python scripts/measure.py path\to\pendulum.mp4 --object "orange ball" --length 0.80
```

Results land in `runs/<video name>/`: `result.json`, `plot.png` and the cached SAM tracks.

## Tests (no API key needed)

```bash
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
pytest
python tests/make_video.py data/fake_pendulum.mp4
BONISA_FAKE_SAM=1 python scripts/measure.py data/fake_pendulum.mp4 --length 0.70
```

## Results so far

- **Simulated pendulum** (L = 0.70 m, 12° release, true g = 9.81 m/s²): Bonisa measured
  **g = 9.824 ± 0.042 m/s²**, found the pivot, and measured the string length from the
  video as 69.9 cm (true 70 cm). It also correctly **rejected** a video that was too
  short and one filmed with a tilted camera (`tests/test_physics.py`).
- **Live SAM 3.1 check**: on a real lab video frame, SAM 3.1 detected the object
  "mug" from a text prompt with 0.93 confidence, so the Meta Model API pipeline
  (upload, segmentation, parsing) is working end to end.
- **Real chalkboard video**: in *Pendelgesetz (mit Rechnung)* the pendulum weight is a
  ~10-pixel dark object on a dark board. SAM 3.1 found it in 0 frames, so Bonisa
  stopped and reported no value instead of guessing. This is why Bonisa asks for a
  bright, contrasting bob and an A4 sheet in view.

`bonisa/track.py` reads both SAM box and mask records and writes `runs/sam_debug.txt`
with what SAM returned, to diagnose empty results.

## Next steps

- Film our own pendulum runs with a bright bob and an A4 sheet.
- Muse explanations and re-filming advice in English, isiZulu and isiXhosa.
- More experiments with the same pipeline: springs, falling objects, projectiles.

## Credits

# RoboRally: The Factory Rescue

**An AI-agent-powered 3D maze game built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon.**

Demo Video: [Watch here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fdWfV4etr14)

Guide a robot through a factory maze by giving natural-language missions to an AI agent. The agent plans a sequence of moves with Meta's Muse Spark model, the game engine validates every move against walls, lasers, doors, and patrolling enemies, and the robot executes valid plans step by step in a 3D factory environment. There are no manual controls: the AI agent is the sole driver of the robot.

## The agentic loop

1. **Mission** - the player types a goal ("Reach the exit without touching lasers").
2. **Plan** - Muse Spark returns structured moves in bounded segments (<=12 per call).
3. **Validate** - the backend simulates each move against the authoritative level layout.
4. **Execute** - approved moves play out through the real game engine, one step at a time.
5. **Observe and replan** - execution stops honestly on death, victory, or state changes; the player requests a fresh plan from the new state.

The game engine is authoritative: victory requires the robot to actually reach the exit tile. The AI never declares success and can never bypass collision, hazards, doors, or enemy detection.

## Tech stack

- Frontend: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js via React Three Fiber + Drei.
- Backend: FastAPI (Python) with Pydantic validation.
- Database: MongoDB Atlas (`roborally`: `users`, `levels` collections).
- AI: Muse Spark 1.3 through the Meta Model API (`https://api.meta.ai/v1`, OpenAI-SDK compatible) with constrained JSON structured output.

## Project structure

```text
backend/
  main.py                 # FastAPI app (routers, CORS)
  ai_engine/              # Meta client, planner, rules mirror, agent API
  game_logic/levels.py    # GET /api/levels/{id}
  authentication/         # Session-cookie register/login/logout/me
  users/                  # Profile, completed_levels, prompt_history API
  community/              # Player-made levels, attempts, rankings
  leaderboard/            # Story run submissions and rankings
  tests/                  # pytest suite (no live services required)
  requirements.txt
frontend/my-app/
  src/app/                # Routes: landing, auth, start, game/level/[id],
                          # profile, learn/*, community/*
  src/lib/                # Game engine (maze, movement, enemies, validation)
  components/maze/        # 3D scene, robot, mission panel, executor
  data/levels.ts          # Level definitions (seed source)
  scripts/                # 17 check-*.ts guards (see Checks), seed-levels
```

## Setup

Prerequisites: Python 3.10+, Node.js 20+, plus:

- A MongoDB database: a free [MongoDB Atlas](https://www.mongodb.com/atlas) cluster (create a cluster -> add a database user -> allow your IP under Network Access -> copy the connection string), or a local MongoDB (`mongodb://localhost:27017`)

# Pyosi

**Pyosi identifies the part of a screenshot you are talking about, and marks it.** Write or paste the message you would send with the screenshot ("the delivery date on the second line looks wrong", "the card and the button are too close"), and Pyosi works out which parts you mean, marks them with numbered boxes, highlights the distance when you talk about the space between two things, and says "not found" when it cannot find a part and "ambiguous" when several parts could be meant, instead of guessing. Each mark has a short explanation you can edit, and the marked image can be exported as a PNG. Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Indie Developer Track, "Build for Your World"), with Meta's Muse Spark model through the Meta Model API.

It is not an image analyzer: it does not describe what is in a picture. It starts from what the person says and answers one question, "which part is that?", with positions that are checked against the pixels and an evaluation harness that measures how often the marks are right.

## What it does

1. **Identifies the part you refer to, and marks it.** It finds things by what they are (a date, a price, "the message where she confirms the price") and not only by name, from a rough note or a full message. The model answers with boxes on a 0-1000 grid; Pyosi converts and validates them. A note about an element Pyosi cannot find (for example because it is not on the screen) is reported as "not found", and a note that fits several elements as "ambiguous"; neither gets an invented box.
2. **Highlights the distance for spacing notes.** The model finds every item of a row or column once. The code works out the distance between neighboring items, and the line is then snapped to the real edges in the original image's pixels (when the background is plain enough to be sure).
3. **Lets you edit the result:** move, resize and delete boxes, edit labels and descriptions.
4. **Exports a PNG** at the original image size (annotated, which adds the description list below the image; boxes only; or the original), as a download or to the clipboard.
5. **Keeps the notes' language and tone** (a question stays a question; the answer is written in the language of the notes).

# TokenPilot

TokenPilot measures the cost of *successfully completed* engineering work.

Token counters tell you how many tokens left the building. Provider bills tell you what you paid. Neither tells you whether that spend fixed a bug, shipped a feature, or burned retries into a dead end. TokenPilot sits between your coding agent and the model API, records every request with project/session/task labels, finds waste with deterministic rules, asks Meta Muse to explain the evidence, then runs a paired benchmark that only labels **Verified savings** when the alternative still passes your acceptance tests.

The product loop:

1. **Observe:** agent traffic through a local OpenAI-compatible gateway
2. **Attribute:** cost to projects, sessions, and tasks
3. **Detect:** seven rule-based inefficiency detectors
4. **Explain:** Muse investigation with citations into recorded events
5. **Experiment:** same repo revision, baseline vs alternative, same tests
6. **Verify:** compare cost, runtime, retries, and correctness
7. **Report:** methodology and evidence in a project report

Local-first by default: SQLite on your machine, secrets stay on the API process, content storage and content-bearing investigation off unless you flip the flags.

## What you can do

### Capture usage through a gateway

Point Codex, Muse, or any OpenAI-shaped client at TokenPilot instead of Meta directly:

| Setting | Value |
|--------|--------|
| Base URL | `http://127.0.0.1:8787/gateway/v1` |
| API key | your `TOKENPILOT_LOCAL_TOKEN` (Bearer) |
| Upstream secret | `MODEL_API_KEY` stays on the TokenPilot server |

Supported surfaces: Chat Completions, Responses, model list relays, Muse `/muse-code/models`. Project-scoped base for tooling that wants a fixed project: `http://127.0.0.1:8787/gateway/p/<project-slug>/v1`.

Optional headers bind spend to your work:

- `X-TokenPilot-Project`
- `X-TokenPilot-Session`
- `X-TokenPilot-Task`
- `X-TokenPilot-Retry-Of`

Each completed call writes a ledger event (`usage_events` + `cost_records`) and returns `X-TokenPilot-Event-Id`. Costs come from a versioned pricing catalogue with an explicit basis badge in the UI (**Estimated**, **Simulated**, or **Unavailable** when usage never arrived).

### See where money goes

# Attest — proof-of-fix for AI pull requests

[![verify](https://github.com/Master07/attest/actions/workflows/verify.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Master07/attest/actions/workflows/verify.yml) <sub>Every push re-checks the types, the tests and all 220 committed receipts on Windows, macOS and Linux, with no keys and no model calls.</sub>

A verifier that never sees the code reproduces the bug, confirms the fix in the running app, shows it would reject a wrong fix, and seals it all into a receipt anyone can check.

UI bugs are worse: a test without a browser can check the code, not what the user sees, so in CI a fix that works and a fix that doesn't look the same.

From the repository root in PowerShell:

```powershell

python -m pytest
cd frontend
npm install
npm run typecheck

npm run build

Open `http://127.0.0.1:3000`, allow microphone access, and use the button and simulated transcript field. To run browser tests, stop the development server and run:

$env:PYTHONPATH = "backend"

```

The API provides `POST /tasks`, `GET /tasks`, `PATCH /tasks/{id}`, `DELETE /tasks/{id}`, `POST /tasks/{id}/complete`, `POST /reminders`, and `GET /reminders/{id}`. The scheduler persists claims before delivery; an interrupted attempt remains attempted and is not automatically repeated. The worker uses the test phone provider when configured as described below; otherwise it reports failure. `POST /safety/assess` accepts `text` and `language` (`en` or `es`). Local heuristics check every report. # Veritas

**CI/CD for multimodal AI.** Veritas is a declarative verification engine: it
generates with Meta's models, then cross-checks every artifact against a
*policy* — a hot-swappable contract of tiered checks — in a closed loop until it
provably passes, refusing to ship anything it cannot verify. Each run ends in a
cryptographic receipt.

Built for the **Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon** on the Meta Model API
(Muse Spark, Muse Image, SAM 3.1).

![Veritas verifying a robotics synthetic-data scene with SAM 3.1 box overlays](docs/ui-robotics.jpg)

## For hackathon judges

Everything below is implemented and tested (30 tests, CI-green) — no slideware.

| Capability | Meta / partner tech | Where in the repo |
|---|---|---|
| Copy, brand, consistency, legibility, plausibility critics | **Muse Spark** (muse-spark-1.3, text + vision) | `veritas/critics.py` |
| Image generation + **surgical in-place edits** | **Muse Image** (`/images/generations`, `/images/edits`) | `veritas/meta_client.py`, `veritas/generators.py` |
| Grounding + object counting (masks, boxes) | **SAM 3.1** (sam-3.1) | `veritas/meta_client.py`, `veritas/critics.py`, `veritas/sam.py` |
| Tier-3 deep-reasoning escalation arbitrator | **Muse Wonder** (muse-wonder-1.0) | `veritas/fixer.py` → `arbitrate` |
| Meta Model API client + live spend ledger | Meta Model API (`api.meta.ai/v1`) | `veritas/meta_client.py` |
| Hybrid routing of text critics to open weights | **Baseten** (OpenAI-compatible) | `veritas/providers.py`, `veritas/config.py` |
| Formal numeric verification | **Z3** SMT solver | `veritas/checks.py` → `_z3_constraint` |
| Receipt bound into the image | **C2PA** content credentials | `veritas/c2pa_export.py` |
| Self-improving preference dataset | **DPO** export | `veritas/dpo.py` |
| Tiered DAG · short-circuit · content cache | — | `veritas/engine.py` |
| Cryptographic audit receipt | — | `veritas/receipt.py` |
| Declarative policy packs (5 domains) | — | `policies/*.yaml` |

```bash
pytest -q
python cli.py policies/commercial_brand_guard.yaml --partner --surgical --arbiter --c2pa

Generative models are powerful but confidently wrong. Veritas treats every
output as a *claim to be disproven*. The same engine runs any **Policy Pack**, so
a whole domain is just a YAML file — five ship today:

| Policy Pack | Theme | Gates against | Grounded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Commercial Brand Guard | Build for Your World | false ad claims, product misrepresentation | FTC advertising substantiation |
| Accessibility Gate | Build for Your World | unreadable copy, illegible / mismatched creative | WCAG 2.2 (SC 1.1.1, 1.4.3), CDC plain-language |
| Health Claim Safety | Build for Your World | dangerous / unsupported medical claims | FTC 2022 Health Products Guidance |
| Synthetic Data Gate | Push the Frontier | bad robot-perception training data | object presence / count / plausibility |
| Trust & Safety Gate | Push the Frontier | AI misinformation — out-of-context image↔

# LandProof

**Proof-carrying emergency landing for drones.** When a drone must land *now*, LandProof
lands it only where every safety claim has survived pixel evidence, and it keeps
checking all the way down.

> To a drone, a flooded street looks like the perfect runway.

![LandProof HUD: hold on predicted intrusion, abort, divert](docs/media/hero.gif)

*Simulation shown above, with oracle evidence (no API key). The real stack swaps in
SAM 3.1 evidence, Muse Spark planning, a SAM-distilled student and Muse Glimmer.*

---

## The problem

Battery critical, motor fault or GPS loss: a drone that cannot fly home has to come
down within seconds. Today's `LAND` failsafe descends straight down onto whatever is
below it. Research systems choose a site first, but they recognise a **fixed list of
classes** (SafeLand [TUM 2026] uses 20). They have no word for:

- **floodwater**: in a Chennai monsoon the flattest, smoothest open patch is often water;
- **a power line**: a fixed model sees an open, dry field;
- **a cow, a tarpaulin, a vendor's umbrella, a child lying on the grass.**

Asking an LLM "is this safe?" is not the answer either. It is slow (tens of seconds),
it can be wrong, and nobody can audit it.

## What LandProof does

| Layer | When | What | Meta model |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Contingency atlas** | healthy flight, in the background | Spark looks at the scene, chooses the hazards that matter *here* (from a vetted vocabulary), proposes zones and makes **falsifiable claims** ("no standing water within 5.4 m of Z2"). | **Muse Spark 1.3** (vision, tool calling, structured output) |
| **Proof** | per claim | SAM 3.1 segments each claimed-absent hazard. A deterministic verifier refutes any claim with an instance inside radius + class buffer. Mandatory classes are always checked. A zone is certified only if **every** claim survives. | **SAM 3.1** (Meta Model API) |
| **Descent watch** | every frame, onboard | A student model trained only on SAM 3.1 pseudo-labels, plus ego-motion compensation and ground-frame tracking. It predicts when a person will walk into the zone, then **holds**, **aborts** and **diverts** to the next certified zone, skipping any zone on the intruder's path. | student distilled from **SAM 3.1** |
| **Edge mode** | cloud link lost | Muse Glimmer re-checks the zone crop with a structured yes/no. It can **veto**, never approve. | **Muse Glimmer** (open weights, vLLM) |
| **Human override** | any time | The operator's spoken "stop", in English, Tamil or Hindi, aborts immediately. The human outranks every model. | **Muse Voice Transcribe** |
| **HazardForge** | offline | Muse Image inserts traps into real frames. SAM 3.1 must confirm every trap before it counts. Spark designs the next round from what fooled the system. | **Muse Image**, **SAM 3.1**, **Muse Spark** |

**Authority order:** human > deterministic verifier > student > LLM.
**The LLM never flies the drone.** Every decision is written to a hash-chained,
tamper-evident ledger.

## Why it matters

Millions of Indian small businesses — tailors, kirana stores, repair shops — have no website. Their owners are more comfortable speaking than typing, often in a mix of Hindi and English, and existing site builders assume English typing and design skill. BolSite removes both barriers.

## The one rule: never invent a fact

Everything on a published site comes from the owner's own words, a photo, or an answer they gave. This is enforced in code, not just in prompts:

- Every extracted fact must cite the exact words from the transcript that support it, matched as a verbatim substring (not loose word overlap). If the quote is not in the transcript, the fact is capped below the publish threshold.
- The proposed value must be bound to its own cited evidence: a business name must appear verbatim in its quote, and a phone's digits (including digits spoken as words, in English, Hindi, or Devanagari) must match the cited span. Interpreted fields like category and hours still require a real transcript quote.
- A regression suite (`npm run test:gate`) encodes four exploits reviewers found — a value citing unrelated evidence, a mismatched phone, an unspoken price, and word-overlap-only evidence — as tests that must stay red-before / green-after.
- Business name, category, and phone must each reach 0.75 confidence or the site does not publish.
- Any weak fact gets at most one clarification question (tap, type, or skip). Still weak afterwards, it is left off the page. Never guessed.
- Prices are returned as a number plus the exact spoken words, and a deterministic parser cross-checks them (so "ढाई सौ" must equal 250).
- The generated copy is scanned: any number not in the owner's facts, or any marketing claim the owner did not make, is rejected.
- A pre-publish verification pass checks phone format, price sanity, that every link and image resolves, that every number on the page traces back to the owner, that there is no placeholder text, and that the page renders cleanly at 360px. Any failure blocks publishing.

# oral_biofilm_sim

**Hackathon workspace:** see [Cube Lab setup and scope](docs/HACKATHON_BUILD.md)
for the interactive diffusion experiment and bounded Meta research agent.

**The mechanistic core (Layer 1) of the Oral Microbiome Node Schema.**

Turns the 8-layer schema substrate from a static ontology into a running dynamical system —
the engine that the GNN bridge-asymmetry test (Layer 4), the SCM intervention engine (Layer 5),
and the criticality/early-warning detectors (Layer 6) sit on top of.

## Architectural contract: 1D now, 4D-ready

Spatial dimensionality is abstracted behind `sim.grid.base.SpatialGrid`. Agents and the chemistry
solver address the grid by `position` tuples — `(depth,)` for v1, `(x, y, depth)` for v2/v3.
Going from a depth column to a 3D voxel field is two class swaps (`SpatialGrid1D` →
`SpatialGrid3D`, `Diffusion1D` → `Diffusion3D`). Agent logic, chemistry, observables, model
orchestration: all unchanged.

Time is the ABM step counter — that's the 4th axis (xyz, time) requirement, satisfied for free.

## What the simulator solves

For each tick `t`:

1. **Chemistry update** (reaction-diffusion) — O₂, pH (via H⁺ and buffers), fermentable sugar,
   heme, lactate, NO, H₂S, NH₃ evolve under ∂c/∂t = D∇²c + sources/sinks.
2. **Boundary conditions** — saliva at the top (O₂ ≈ 8%, pH ≈ 6.8, sugar pulses per Stephan
   curve), gingival sulcus at the bottom (heme flux from bleed loop, IgG/IgA, serum proteins).
3. **Agent step** — each bacterium reads local chemistry, checks viability against its 4-field
   Layer-3 constraints, computes growth from chemistry + crossfeed neighbors, divides or dies,
   emits byproducts and (stochastically) OMVs.
4. **Observables update** — composition vector per depth, OMV cargo flux at top boundary,
   coherence indices (NO/H₂S/pH variance), dynamic topology (betweenness over the realized
   coaggregation graph at this tick).

## Falsification targets for v1 (week 2)

The simulator must qualitatively reproduce:

1. **Succession** — pioneers (Sa, Sm, An, Hp, Rm) establish first; anaerobes (Vp, Fn, Pg, Td, Tf)
   colonize as O₂ depletes with depth. Order matches Kolenbrander.
2. **Dynamic bridge emergence** — *F. nucleatum* becomes the highest-betweenness node from its
   aerotolerance + universal coaggregation properties, not as a hard-coded fact.
3. **Stephan curve** — sugar pulse → *S. mutans* bloom + local pH crash → recovery as buffering
   restores pH 6.8.
4. **OVN ignition** — heme flux at the bottom boundary (simulated bleed) → *P. gingivalis*
   bloom + OMV-flux spike at the top boundary (the systemic input).

Most AI analysis setups paste a sample's strings and decompiled code straight into the model that decides. Built with Muse Spark Open.

## What is included

- `src/prototype.mjs` - language detection, relative-date slot matching, booking guardrails, deterministic dummy booking persistence and owner handoff.

Availability language and fake-inventory use are verified through the recorded integrated calls. Booking persistence is verified offline and deterministically; no live booking-confirmation model call is part of this demo.

# ✂️ SayCut: edit Reels by saying what you want

> “Blur every face except mine.” “Make the dog glow pink.” “Put me on a beach at sunset.”
> SayCut turns a sentence (typed or spoken) into a frame-accurate video edit.

**Live demo: [saycut.softmelody.dev](https://saycut.softmelody.dev)**

Built for the **Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon** with four Meta models working together:

| Model | What it does in SayCut |
|---|---|
| **Muse Spark 1.3** | Watches the uploaded clip (video understanding) and suggests edits for that clip. Turns each command into a structured edit plan (JSON schema). Looks at tracked objects to work out *which* person you mean (“the girl in the green shirt”, “everyone except me”). |
| **SAM 3.1** | Segments and **tracks** the target through the whole video from a text prompt (“face”, “dog”, “person”), giving pixel masks with stable object IDs across frames. |
| **Muse Image** | **Restyles the whole video** (“make me an anime girl on a beach”, claymation, cyberpunk) one keyframe at a time, paints new backgrounds (“put me on the moon”) and designs a scroll-stopping Reels cover from any frame. |
| **Muse Voice Transcribe** | Takes push-to-talk voice commands and burns in captions from the clip's own speech. |

## How it works

```
 "make the girl in green glow pink"  (voice → Muse Voice Transcribe, or typed)
        │
        ▼
 Muse Spark ── plan ──►  { effect: glow, target: "girl", selection: described,
        │                  description: "girl in green shirt", color: "#FF69B4" }
        ▼
 SAM 3.1  ── tracks every "girl" across all frames (stable ids #0, #1, #2)

In Taiwan, the student on duty is the last one out: they stay after class to clean the room and lock the door.

# MediClear — Understand any medical bill, in your language

Snap a photo of a medical bill, EOB, or insurance letter → plain-language explanation in your language (text + voice) → suspicious charges flagged → concrete next steps to lower the bill → a ready-to-send dispute/appeal letter draft → follow-up Q&A by text or voice, per case.

Built for the **Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon** (with Cerebral Valley).

**Live demo:** https://kend150212.github.io/mediclear/ (PWA — installable, works offline for the app shell)

## Why

Medical billing confusion is one of the top US consumer pain points. Immigrants, the elderly, and non-English speakers are hit hardest. MediClear is elderly-first: white, ultra-simple UI, minimum 18px text, 48px touch targets, max 3 steps per flow.

## Features

- **📷 Scan tab** — take a photo (or try a sample bill), pick from 13 languages, get a full analysis
- **Plain-language results** — summary, every line item explained, flagged charges (duplicates, upcoding, balance billing…), next steps (EOB check, itemized bill, prompt-pay discounts, financial assistance, appeals), dispute-letter draft with copy button
- **🔊 Voice** — hear the results read aloud in your language (Web Speech API — Meta has no TTS API)
- **🗂️ History tab** — every case saved on-device (IndexedDB): re-read analyses, replay voice re-synthesized from saved text
- **💬 Follow-up Q&A** — ask more about any case by text or voice mic
- **⚙️ Settings** — BYOK API key field (stored in localStorage, never leaves your device), mock mode for keyless testing, UI language, privacy info

## AI — 100% Meta Model API

Base URL `https://api.meta.ai/v1` (OpenAI-compatible). Bring your own key — paste it in Settings.

| Model | Used for |
|---|---|
| `muse-spark-1.3` | One structured-JSON call per bill: vision extraction + analysis + flags + next steps + dispute letter, in the user's language |
| `muse-spark-1.3` | Follow-up Q&A per case (bill JSON sent as context) |
| `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` | Streaming speech-to-text for voice questions (70+ languages) |
| Web Speech API (browser) | Voice *output* — Meta offers no TTS |

No backend. No analytics. Bill photos are sent to the API for analysis only and are never stored server-side. History lives in IndexedDB on the device.

**Mock mode** (on by default): realistic fixtures + a mock-bill generator so QA, design, and the demo flow work with no API key. Flip it off in Settings and add your key for live AI.

## Run it locally

```bash

No build step — vanilla HTML/CSS/JS.

# Asih

An agent for older adults' needs and quality of life. It is not a chatbot: it has no open-ended chat mode. The demo shows three fixed flows that end with an action the person chooses:

## Persona: Asih

Asih is a plain-spoken AI helper. Asih is honest about being an AI, not a person or doctor. The person decides every step. Use short, plain sentences, with care and patience. Do not use pet names or exclamation marks. In Spanish, use formal “usted.”

The Asih mark (`public/asih-avatar.svg`, also the watch launcher icon) is hand-drawn and abstract: a calm ring with a small spark that signals AI, with no face. TODO: a Muse Image (`muse-image-1.0`) version could replace it later, once the app has a Meta API key.

- **Appointment help:** read an example letter, confirm each extracted item, then save the visit or download a calendar file.
- **Find a group:** review an example community event, confirm when and where it meets, plan transportation, and edit an invitation.
- **Check an ad:** review quoted warning cues, learn how to inspect ad settings and find the advertiser in Meta's Ad Library, then choose whether to share a note.
- **Voice note:** record or upload audio, read the transcript, then edit a reply before opening WhatsApp or asking Asih about it.
- **My activity notes:** save a private participation note on this phone and optionally edit a caption to share.

All offline example content is synthetic and labeled **EXAMPLE (synthetic data)**.

## Safety design

- No medical advice. A red-flag pre-screen redirects urgent phrases to the Get help screen before an agent runs. The app never calls emergency services by itself.
- Scam wording is fixed in code. The agent can list cues with exact ad text evidence but cannot give an ad a safe/scam verdict.
- Dates, times, places, and names must be confirmed one at a time before they can be saved, exported, or used in a draft.
- Before the first photo, voice note, or message is sent, the app displays and reads aloud this notice and requires acknowledgment:

  > Your saved items stay on this phone. To read a photo or voice note, it is sent to Meta's AI service. Meta says it does not use it to train its AI. This app tells Meta not to store its answers. Meta may still keep what is sent as needed to run the service, follow the law, and check for misuse and safety; it does not say for how many days. Delete everything removes what is saved on this phone. It cannot remove what Meta may have kept.

- An output guard checks content before it is shown. Live calls have a $10/day spend guard.

## Models and tools

The live agent loop uses `muse-spark-1.3` through the Responses API for tool use, vision, and an output-guard check. `muse-wonder-1.0` gets one retry for unreadable images only. Voice transcription uses `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` at `/v1/asr/transcribe`.

# Rosetta

**Record a legacy application. Generate a replacement. Verify behavioral parity with evidence.**

Rosetta turns a screen recording of a legacy desktop application into an evidence-backed AppSpec, a generated React application, a real Playwright replay, a weighted parity report, and a ZIP export.

- Windows 10/11 or a recent Linux/macOS environment.
- Python 3.11.
- Node.js 20 LTS or newer, with npm.
- FFmpeg available on `PATH`.
- A configured Muse-compatible API endpoint and API key for observation, AppSpec generation, visual judging, and repair.
- Internet access on first use if `faster-whisper` must download its speech model or npm must install dependencies.

The Muse adapter currently assumes an OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint, Bearer authentication, image input, and strict JSON Schema response formatting. Those provider-specific assumptions must be verified against the actual API account before running a real job.

Run these commands from the repository root.

1. **Install prerequisites.** Install Python 3.11, Node.js 20 LTS, and FFmpeg. Confirm that `py -3.11 --version`, `node --version`, `npm --version`, and `ffmpeg -version` work in a new PowerShell window.

   ```powershell

   ```

   If PowerShell blocks virtual-environment activation, run `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass` in that PowerShell session, then activate again.

   Set `META_API_BASE`, `META_API_KEY`, and `MUSE_MODEL`. Keep the key private. # AdistributionSystem

Mid-roll ads are mostly watched to the end. What they cost is goodwill: they cut a video at an arbitrary second, and people resent the interruption. AdistributionSystem watches the video, finds a moment where a break already feels natural, and writes a short motion-design bridge from what is on screen to what the ad says. The ad then arrives as part of the video instead of breaking it.

We showed the idea to 10 people: 9 found an ad that arrives this way more pleasant than a regular mid-roll, and said they would stay on it longer. A small informal check, not a study.

Choosing a better moment is not new on its own: platforms already avoid cutting people mid-sentence. The bridge is: the frozen picture itself carries the viewer into the ad, with a line written for that video and that ad. A brand with one ad gets a different way in for each of its ten thousand videos, and nobody has to check them one by one: the system watches its own work.

Built solo with Meta's models during the [Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon](https://cerebralvalley.ai/e/meta-ai-developer-hackathon) (Indie Developer track, Oct 27 to Nov 4, 2026). Everything in this repository was written during the hackathon; the commit history shows it step by step.

# Road to 5K

A PT-to-5K run coach for Meta Ray-Ban Display: a plain-web (HTML/CSS + JS) lens-style app, built solo for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon ("Build for Your World" track). It reads today's physical-therapy exercise plan, walks the user through the session on the glasses display, answers questions about the session, and — new in this event — sees the world through a SAM vision layer that can estimate the distance to a runner ahead and count the people around the wearer.

On the glasses the camera is the runner, so the count is reported from the wearer's point of view — the people around them. In this build the count comes from a still frame; a still provides no passed-you / you-passed split, so those fields return null rather than an invented number. Photos attached in Ask pass a content gate first: the coach model classifies each one at temperature 0, and only an appropriate run-scene photo reaches SAM — anything else is refused before the vision model runs. **Live demo:** https://bridgevoice.us

## What it is

BridgeVoice is a real-time multilingual co-pilot for Pashto/Dari community
interpreters and the families they serve. Community interpreters and families
who speak Pashto or Dari often face essential information — medical
instructions, school letters, official forms — written in difficult English.
A mistranslated word or number can change what someone does. BridgeVoice
helps them understand that language while keeping the human in control of
the final meaning. It does not replace the human interpreter.

## Who it serves

- Community interpreters working in Pashto and Dari (with English and
  Spanish also supported in the app).
- The families they serve: people who need to understand difficult wording
  in simple language before they act on it.

## Headline feature: live voice

One tap on "Start listening" on the live voice screen (`/agent`) and the app
keeps listening, answers out loud, and can be interrupted by speaking — with
typed chat as a fallback. The voice screen is the centerpiece of this
release, together with a private access gate (see below).

## What else it does

- Chats in English, Pashto, Dari, and Spanish, and explains difficult
  wording in simple language.
- Checks critical details such as numbers and negations before they are
  acted on (meaning checks — the human judges the meaning).
- Answers questions about uploaded documents with exact quoted excerpts.
- Keeps history local and off by default; the voice-screen transcript is
  memory-only.
- A 120-entry interpreter glossary is wired into agent requests (see
  Honest limits below).

# wayfinder

An open model, post trained using Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B, that searches code at frontier quality.

**Built with Muse Spark Open.**

Submission to the Meta hackathon, "Build for Your World", startup track, from Voyage AI.

## What it is

- **wayfinder-qwen**: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, post trained with LoRA SFT on 1,383 successful search trajectories written by Muse Spark Open. Open weights: [hweller1/wayfinder-qwen-35b-a3b](https://huggingface.co/hweller1/wayfinder-qwen-35b-a3b). Model card: [docs/MODEL_CARD_QWEN.md](docs/MODEL_CARD_QWEN.md).
- **Scout**: a plugin for Muse Code that hands search to Wayfinder. A hybrid search plus rerank step refines its list on every call.
- **The index**: `voyage-code-4` vectors in turbopuffer. No code is stored.

## How it works

![Scout architecture](docs/figures/architecture.png)

Wayfinder searches with grep and file reads and reports files. One cascade then refines the list: hybrid search (`voyage-code-4` vectors plus BM25 on hashed identifiers, top 100 chunks rolled up to files) is merged with the model's list by reciprocal rank fusion, and Voyage rerank-3 reorders positions 6 to 40 with the instruction "Rank source files a developer must edit or test for this change".

## Results

Intervals are 95% bootstrap intervals over tasks.

**The cascade.** 200 held-out tasks, 47 repositories, 2 seeds. Recall@12 is the share of the right files in the top 12.

| List | recall@12 |
|---|---|
| Model's own list | 0.414 |
| After the merge | 0.493 |
| After the rerank | 0.531 |

The rerank adds +0.038 [+0.023, +0.054]; the whole cascade adds +0.117 [+0.095, +0.139]. Recall@5 moves from 0.336 to 0.345, which is not significant. The cascade adds about 0.4 s per search. It shows the cascade finds more of the right files in the top 12; it does not show a gain at the very top of the list.

**Coding pass rate.** 34 tasks that fail without search, 2 seeds, Opus 5.5 as the coder, network blocked, coder sees only the files the searcher returned.

| Searcher | Pass rate |
|---|---|
| No search | 0.074 |
| wayfinder-qwen with the cascade | 0.824 [0.71, 0.93] |
| Right files given | 0.971 |
| Sonnet 5.5 high, run without the cascade | 0.868 |
| GPT-6.1 Sol, run without the cascade | 0.853 |
| Agents-A1-35B, run without the cascade | 0.853 |

Search lifts the pass rate by about 0.8 over no search. The differences between searchers are not resolved. The other searchers were run on 2026-11-02 without the cascade. Earlier write-up: [docs/results/e2e_final_results.md](docs/results/e2e_final_results.md).

**Search benchmark.** Same 200 tasks, grep arm. Reported recall is the share of right files in the model's final report. Cost is per search task.

| Model | Reported recall | Cost per task |
|---|---|---|
| wayfinder-qwen, own list | 0.415 | about $0.045 (open-price equivalent) |
| Agents-A1-35B | 0.313 | $0.113 |
| Sonnet 5.5 high | 0.529 | $0.120 |
| GPT-6.1 Sol | 0.580 | $0.062 (rate unconfirmed) |

# Blindspot

**Blindspot is a stress-testing harness for AI scientific verifiers.**

Before trusting an AI reviewer’s PASS, test it against physics claims whose truth

unavailable answers and cost.

verdicts with checkpoints**. These findings concern the fixed testbed.

```powershell

measurements. The included physics suites are implemented; a new scientific
domain requires code plus an independent correctness oracle.

## The three-minute path

1. **The claim.** The exact middle splitting is 1/104. The proposed 101/10400 is
   exactly 1% too large. Spark-low rejects it in the diagonal representation.
2. **Change basis.** Exact validation confirms unchanged levels, gap and false
   claim. In the general rational basis, Spark-low passes this claim eleven times
   in twenty attempts. Inspect the saved explanation.
3. **Density control.** A fully dense Hadamard representation remains easy.
4. **Trusted checkpoints.** Add only the exact lowest and highest levels; inspect
   the recovery and the optional algebra explaining the short exact route.
5. **Choose a verifier.** Compare wrong PASSes, rejected correct controls,
   unavailable verdicts and measured cost for the three tested configurations.

Spectrum 005 was selected after collection for illustration. Aggregate estimates
retain every frozen case. Full tables and exact evidence remain under Study
records. The current build is a research demonstrator and reusable evaluation
harness, with one completed physics case study.

A developer planning to use an AI scientific reviewer needs evidence about the
reviewer’s approvals. Exact physics cases act as calibration weights: an
independent oracle already supplies their answers. For this 4×4 calculation,
exact linear algebra is the appropriate checker; its role is to test the AI.

# SpatialScout

**A co-scientist for kidney research, powered by Meta models.** A scientist who sees an unexpected signal in kidney tissue has to check whether the analysis is dependable, whether other evidence agrees and what the papers say before choosing the next experiment. Everything the product shows comes from a computed artifact ([ADR-0001](docs/adr/0001-computed-results-only.md)).

The first investigation module asks whether a signal survives stricter counting of which RNA molecules belong to which cell: in crowded tissue a molecule from one cell is easily counted toward its neighbour.

[![Meta Global AI Hackathon](https://img.shields.io/badge/Meta%20Global%20AI%20Hackathon-Push%20the%20Frontier-7928CA?style=for-the-badge&logo=meta&logoColor=white)](https://cerebralvalley.ai)

---

## Overview

- **Core Mission:** Transforming massive astronomical sky surveys into an autonomous, explainable queue of high-value scientific discoveries without human inspection bottlenecks or AI hallucinations.
- **Problem Statement:** Accelerating deep-sky scientific discovery and physical systems modeling from optical surveys (SDSS, DESI, Rubin LSST).
- **Demo Walkthrough:** A complete 3-minute video demonstration script is available in [`voice.md`](voice.md).
- **Key Capabilities:**
  - Specialized 5-layer autonomous agent fleet coordinating multi-step astrophysical workflows.
  - Morphological decomposition via SAM 3.1 and zero-hallucination non-parametric CAS analysis.
  - Forward gravitational collision physics solver (+500 Myr) paired with multimodal visual specifications.
  - Hybrid support for Meta Model API cloud and open-weight model deployments.

---

## 🔭 The Scientific Problem & Our Solution

Every night, wide-field optical surveys like the **Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS)**, **DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys**, and the upcoming **Vera C. Rubin Observatory (LSST)** capture petabytes of deep space data containing billions of celestial bodies. Within these vast datasets lie the rarest keys to understanding cosmic evolution: **collisional ring galaxies, prograde galactic mergers, gravitational lenses, and tidal disruption events**.

### The Bottleneck
- **Manual inspection is impossible:** Astronomers cannot eyeball hundreds of millions of cutouts.
- **Generic classifiers fail:** Supervised classifiers only identify predefined categories (e.g., "spiral vs. elliptical") and ignore unknown anomalies.
- **Standard LLMs hallucinate:** Generic

# Testigos del Bólido

**Colombia has no fireball camera network. Its phones can be one.**

When a fireball crosses the sky, people film it with phones, dashcams and security cameras. Testigos del Bólido ("fireball
witnesses") is an agent that turns those witness videos into a trajectory with error bars, a speed and a verdict: a
natural meteor, a re-entering satellite, or not enough evidence to tell. Each camera must first be oriented against
landmarks on a map, which today is an offline step (see How it works). It was checked against the published solutions
for the Chelyabinsk fireball of 2013 and pointed at a green fireball seen over Colombia on 30 July 2025, which has no
published trajectory. Today it needs cameras that stood still (a dashcam, a security camera, a phone resting on
something), and its orientation and trajectory steps have only been tested by day.

# cocoverse

**A little universe for you and your pet.** Live at [cocoverse.app](https://www.cocoverse.app) · [3-minute demo](https://youtu.be/628PXRkQE8c).

Your pet will never tell you who they are. So cocoverse builds your pet's AI twin the only honest way: from what they actually do. Every photo you share becomes a collectible card, a **Memory Print**; the twin grows only from those cards, answers in your pet's voice, names the cards each answer rests on, and says plainly when it has no memory of something. It never makes a memory up.

Built for the **Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon** (Indie track, *Build for Your World*), Oct 26 – Nov 4, 2026. Everything in this repository was written during the hackathon; the commit history is the log. First user: Coco, a black Labrador. Biscuit (a corgi) and Mochi (a tabby cat) are demo pets whose photos were made with Muse Image.

*co-* means together, as in *companion*, the one you share your bread with: coco is the two of you. *verse*, as in universe, is everything you share, and a little one: only the two of you are in it.

---

## What happens in a cocoverse

**Start with one photo.** You answer three easy questions (name, kind of animal, girl or boy), then pick one photo. Muse Spark says what it sees (breed guesses, coat, marks, size); you correct anything and confirm. People's faces are blurred in your browser before the photo is uploaded.

**Starter Kit: ten moments you already have.** Each slot asks for a kind of photo that is probably in your album (sleeping, eating, playing, with you, out on a walk, its strangest habit…). Animals don't pose on request, so you pick what you have and skip the rest. Each photo turns a card over right away. Finishing the kit unlocks the **soul portrait**: the pet reads back through all its cards, says who it is, and gets a legendary card that steps out of its frame.

**Every card is one real moment.** Muse Spark reads the photo into short notes (traces), a card name and a line in the pet's voice. Muse Image paints a *new* picture of your pet in that moment, in one of nine blind-box styles (three rarity tiers). On rare cards, SAM 3.1 cuts the pet out of the painting, so it moves in front of the scene when you tilt the card. Then you can tell the story the photo can't show; your words are kept as evidence marked as yours, and they outrank anything the model guessed.

**Memory Points and packs.** Sharing a moment earns M pt (three free a day, plus today's tasks). Three M pt open a Daily Booster: your shared memories, already painted in the background, turn over one by one, and sometimes a **move card** falls out (a new way the character moves). Cards fill **series** that follow who your pet is: favourite things, food, games, friends, places, the seasons, the hours of a day.

# BREAKSHIFT

**Your AI says "fixed." BREAKSHIFT says: prove it.**

A simulated robotic-workcell repair workbench. Inspect a component, replay a
recorded Meta-model proposal, challenge it against changed conditions, and export
or independently replay the resulting evidence. Passing a simulation does not
establish a real machine's condition or authorize a physical repair.

## Live Demo & Hosted Bay

[Open the workbench](https://breakshift-maintenance-bay.dreamnet-intel.workers.dev/)

**Inspect. Challenge. Replay.** Change the modeled conditions and see whether a
repair plan still holds up. Changed assumptions withdraw stale green verdicts;
a fluent proposal is not proof that a physical machine is repaired.

Team DreamNet #217, Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon. The existing entry's
demo link was updated and reloaded on November 4, 2026. This is not a judging,
eligibility, organizer endorsement or prize claim.

The corrected 2:13 recording replays retained Meta-model outputs. Its fictional
presenter and synthetic voice were produced with Google Vids; the script was
Muse Wonder-assisted. Meta Voice and Muse Code use are not claimed. The
recording's closing source identifiers and test counts describe its historical
capture, not every subsequent app revision.

Try the existing Cloudflare Worker deployment directly in any desktop or mobile browser:
**https://breakshift-maintenance-bay.dreamnet-intel.workers.dev/**

The hosted workbench opens without credentials or account sign-in. Its current
published build is identified by `/release.json`; a source checkout may include
newer, unpublished changes. Fresh paid model analysis remains operator-restricted.

## Offline Quick Start

Use Node.js 22.12 or newer. No packages, API keys or account access are required:

```sh
npm run build
npm test
npm start
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:5193. Set PORT to change the local port. The local preview
is read-only server-side; repair experiments run in your browser. Paid scans are
disabled. Historical Muse Spark and SAM/Wonder examples are labeled recorded,
not presented as new model execution. Tests block real network transports.

Optional browser checks use an already installed Playwright module, without
installing or bundling a browser dependency:

```sh
node verify-user-facing.mjs /absolute/path/to/playwright/index.mjs
```

That verifier starts and closes its own loopback server and checks phone, tablet
and desktop journeys, including nonblank WebGL pixels. Its fake camera is a

# TERRATERM

> See the oil market and the oil itself, in one place.

TERRATERM follows crude oil two ways at once. It tracks prices and market news, and it watches the big storage yard at Cushing, Oklahoma from satellite photos, spotting each tank and measuring the area it covers. # GTM Shortlist

Open-source company discovery and research for B2B sellers. Confirm your offer and targeting criteria, discover candidates, inspect dated source passages, and review/export a shortlist. Human acceptance never means buying intent.

Created by Eygentic. Every seller uses the same workflow; Eygentic profiles are optional examples and test inputs, not product defaults.

This is an early local implementation. Hosted accounts, external signup, deployment, real provider benchmarks and observed user testing remain release gates in [the checklist](docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md). [Progress](docs/PROGRESS.md) records what has actually passed.

## Try it with sample data

No provider keys are needed. Install from source below, open the local app, and choose **Try it with sample data** on the setup card. Confirm the sample target, inspect the three invented companies and their evidence, accept or reject a result, and export CSV, JSON or Excel. Every screen and export labels the sample data. Sample source links are plain text because the invented pages do not exist online.

## Install from source today

Install Git, Python 3.11 or newer, and Node.js 22.12 or newer with npm. Run these commands in a terminal:

```sh
git clone --branch claude/signal-landing https://github.com/adkbbx/GTM_Shortlist.git
cd GTM_Shortlist
```

Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
py -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.lock.txt
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pip install -e . --no-deps
npm ci
npm run build
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m shortlist.cli serve --port 8014 --open
```

macOS or Linux:

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.lock.txt
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -e . --no-deps
npm ci
npm run build
.venv/bin/python -m shortlist.cli serve --port 8014 --open
```

Keep the terminal open. The app opens at http://127.0.0.1:8014 and starts its API and research worker together. If the browser does not open, visit that address manually. Stop with Ctrl+C. Source installs save research in `data/shortlist.sqlite3` inside the checkout. No environment activation or `.env` file is needed for the sample path. On Linux, your distribution may require its Python venv package before creating the environment.

The install commands download dependencies. They do not make research-provider requests. The source path includes the UI build; installing only the editable Python package does not build the UI.

## Install a published package

The PyPI release is still a release gate. Use the source instructions above today. After the maintainer publishes `gtm-shortlist`, Python 3.11 or newer plus [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) can run it without Node or a UI build:

```sh
uvx gtm-shortlist
```

Alternatively, with [pipx](https://pipx.pypa.io/stable/installation/) installed:

```sh
pipx run gtm-shortlist
```

The package starts the API and worker, opens http://127.0.0.1:8014, and stores research in you
