---

## 1. What is NOVA?

NOVA // Ygdrassil is an evolving multi-model AI ecosystem designed to connect specialised models, agents, shared project context and human participants in one collaborative environment. Its intended operating model combines Multi-Agent Bus Chat for cross-model collaboration, a Workflow Manager for coordinated task execution, and Human Authority for accountable decisions. The goal is to move from an unclear problem to a reasoned plan, a coordinated implementation and a reviewable result.

The META Edition is the current Hackathon implementation. It combines:

- a browser-based V6 workspace;
- a local Node.js bridge exposing a small HTTP API;
- parallel, memory-aware requests to six model providers;
- a content-based project-memory index;
- a sequential workflow manager for CLI and interactive-session agents;
- an approval queue and a separate Human Authority portal;
- a Muse Spark connector prototype using the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

The central engineering question is not simply *“Which model gives the best answer?”* It is:

**How can different AI capabilities work together on a real task, share relevant context, expose their limits, and produce changes that remain inspectable and under human control?**

NOVA is built as a practical system rather than a claim of autonomous general intelligence. Its current implementation focuses on orchestration, context continuity, bounded tool execution and human approval.

# AVO

**Say what you want done. AVO handles the clicks—and asks when your meaning is unclear.**

[Watch the 3-minute demo on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u7045Y1N5V0) · [Website](https://bowenx307.github.io/AVO/) · [Install on Mac](https://bowenx307.github.io/AVO/docs.html#install) · [Evaluation](docs/eval.md) · [Try without an API key](docs/reviewer-trial.md#public-reviewer-invitation)

I broke my hand while climbing during a summer software engineering internship at Lenovo. I still needed to use my computer. AVO began with that experience: a Mac app for people who can speak clearly but find precise mouse or trackpad use difficult.

## The interaction

Say “Reply to Professor Smith, say I’ll be ten minutes late.” If two Smiths fit, AVO rings both and asks. Say “the physics one,” and it continues. Before a detected send or other irreversible action, it shows a preview and asks for explicit approval.

**“Which person do you mean?” and “Can I send this?” are different questions. AVO is designed to ask both.**

AVO Remote brings this exchange to a paired phone on the same Wi-Fi. Send a task to your Mac, receive a question with a cropped, numbered view of the relevant screen area, and answer without returning to the desk. Remote is off by default; Control–Option–R opens pairing. Losing the phone connection pauses the task.

## Review in three minutes

1. Watch the [submitted demo on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u7045Y1N5V0).
2. Inspect the [27 E3 run records](eval/e3/results.json) and [methodology](docs/eval.md). To run the actual agent, use the setup guide below.

## How it is built

| Component | Role |
| --- | --- |
| Muse Spark 1.3 | Plans tasks and proposes computer-use actions; a separate structured-output call reviews proposed pointer batches for ambiguity and target location. |
| SAM 3.1 | Segments targets from points or rough boxes and supplies screen regions for highlights. |
| macOS accessibility | Reads control names and bounds, checks locations, and snaps near-miss clicks when the nearest target is unambiguous. |
| Muse Wonder 1.0 | Replans after repeated actions fail to change the screen. |
| Muse Voice Transcribe 1.0 | Realtime speech recognition, biased with visible names and the current answer choices. |
| Python + Electron | Local execution, visual questions, interruption handling, and the paired phone interface. |

All runtime AI calls use Meta models. Spark, Wonder and SAM use Meta’s Responses API; speech uses its realtime ASR endpoint. The OpenAI Python package is the API-compatible client, not an OpenAI model dependency. [Architecture and design decisions](docs/architecture.md).

## Evidence, with limits

E3 tested three deliberately ambiguous tasks, three times per setup. A silent error means a wrong result reported as completed without a clarification or target-check question. A yes/no send or booking confirmation is not counted as clarification.

| Setup | Silent errors | Correct outcomes |

# Byline

**Think it. Write it.**

Byline is a writer-controlled editor. It does not write your draft for you. It offers the next words, a phrase, or a question, as options you can accept or ignore.

## Manifesto

AI writing is usually sold as completion: give a prompt, receive a paragraph. That model replaces the writer's judgment with a model's average.

Byline challenges that assumption. Writing is not a single completion event. It is a sequence of small decisions: the next word, the next clause, the next transition, the next question. Byline keeps those decisions small and visible:

- It suggests **bits**, not blocks: cues, fragments, sentences, and questions.
- It offers **options**, not answers: several alternatives at each level.
- It waits for **approval**: nothing enters the draft until you accept it.
- It stays **grounded**: source cards must carry a verbatim passage; citations are deterministic APA from metadata, not free text.

The writer remains the author. The model is a fast, opinionated margin note.

## Main features

- **Suggest with assist levels**: cues, phrases, sentences, and questions at the cursor.
- **Review feedback**: Reader notes anchored to exact passages.
- **Paraphrasing**: synonym and rewrite options for selected text.
- **Phrase connecting**: connectors and drafted bridges between sentences.
- **Library from provided sources**: grounded cards and APA/MLA/Chicago citations from URLs, PDFs, and documents.

## What Byline is

- A Tiptap-based rich-text editor that runs in the browser.
- Ghost text at the cursor with four levels: cue, phrase, sentence, and question.
- A Reader rail that anchors critiques to exact passages.
- Local grammar checks via Harper.js (WebAssembly, offline-capable).
- Connect seams that join sentences with contrast, cause, elaboration, or example.
- A Library of source cards with verbatim passages and APA citations.
- Provenance tracing that matches draft sentences to saved source text.
- A per-IP budget and model allowlist that keep usage bounded and Meta-only.

## What Byline is not

- It is not a chatbot that writes your draft.
- It does not auto-apply rewrites except small grammar fixes.
- It does not store your document on a server by default.
- It is not a general-purpose LLM gateway: the backend allowlists Meta-authored models only.

## Core features

### Ghost text levels

When you pause, Byline offers a small set of options at the cursor:

- **Cue**: 2-4 word nudge.
- **Phrase**: finish the current clause.
- **Sentence**: finish the sentence with one new idea.
- **Question**: three questions that prompt the writer.

You can switch levels, cycle alternatives, reroll, and accept with Tab or a number key.

### Reader review

The Reader persona reads the draft and leaves notes anchored to exact spans. Each note can include replacement options. Notes are grouped by explanation, can be reprompted for fresh alternatives, and can be dismissed. Grammar findings are a separate persona, so mechan

# Sofía × Muse Spark: call intelligence for immigration law firms

Sofía is a bilingual (Spanish/English) AI voice receptionist for U.S. immigration law firms. She answers 24/7, routes callers, books free pre-evaluations and transfers urgent calls to the team.

This repository holds the part that runs after every call. When a call ends, the server sends the transcript to **Muse Spark** through the Meta Model API. Muse Spark returns 18 structured fields, a summary in Spanish, an urgency level and a next action for the team. Each call becomes one row in Google Sheets.

```
Retell (voice)  ──call_ended webhook──▶  Server (Render)  ──transcript + JSON schema──▶  Muse Spark 1.3
                                               │                                            │
                                               ◀──────── validated JSON (18 + 3 fields) ─────┘
                                               │
                                               └──▶  Google Sheets (one row per call)
```

## How Muse Spark is used

- **Structured output.** The JSON schema in `schema.py` forces every answer to contain all 18 fields, with the right types and only the allowed values (enums). The server validates the answer before saving it.
- **Deterministic facts win.** Facts Retell knows for certain, such as office hours from the flow's HORARIO node and whether a transfer happened, override the model's reading of the transcript.
- **Priority rules.** Detention outranks every other outcome. Callers who mention a live show are tagged as `live`. Relative dates ("tomorrow", "next Tuesday") are resolved against the call's start time in U.S. Central Time.
- **Bilingual by design.** Calls can be in Spanish, English or a mix. Summaries and next actions are written in Spanish for the team.

## The 18 fields

`name`, `language`, `immigration_call`, `subagent`, `initial_request`, `source`, `detention`, `detention_details`, `contact_preference`, `appointment_date`, `email`, `message`, `caller_type`, `call_outcome`, `transferred`, `transfer_destination`, `after_hours`, `high_priority`

Enrichment fields: `summary_es`, `urgency`, `next_action`. Each row also stores the call ID, duration, the last four digits of the caller's number, model latency, token usage and a link to the recording.

# Orbit-X

**Orbit-X is a health-information intelligence and interoperability platform.** It helps a person keep their own health information in one place, understand it with evidence-linked explanations, exchange it using a limited FHIR R4 subset, and (optionally) have family or caregivers alerted if they need help.

Orbit-X **does not give medical advice and is not a medical device.** Plain code finds patterns in the person's own logged data; the AI only rewords facts, and its output is checked so it cannot suggest medicine, doses or diagnoses. Emergencies are decided by fixed code, never by an AI. Built solo for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Startups track, theme: Build for Your World). Use **synthetic (pretend) data only**.

**Status: pilot-ready MVP.** Ready for a small, supervised pilot with consenting testers (a patient, their caregivers and, optionally, a clinician). It is **not** cleared for unsupervised clinical use, for emergencies on its own, or for use with real patient data at scale. See "Pilot-ready MVP: what that means" below and "Security: what is in place, and what is not".

# Lantern Keep

A 1–4 player co-op castle defense game on Roblox. An **AI director** reads how your team played and designs the next wave. **NPC companions** remember your last match and bring it up when the next one starts.

Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (indie developer track). Everything in this repository was made during the build period (see [docs/ORIGINS.md](docs/ORIGINS.md)).

You defend the **Lantern** at the center of a keep. Enemies come through four gates (north, south, east, west).

- **The run:**
  - Each match is one **Day**: 3 waves on Day 1, growing to 10 waves with a boss from Day 5.
  - If you win, the next Day starts. If you lose, you retry the same Day.
- **Classes:** guardian (tank), ranger (ranged), cleric (healing and revives), arcanist (area magic).
- **Enemies:** Grunt, Runner, Brute, Archer, Shaman, plus the boss "Shadow Warlord".
- **Support squad:** Short on players? Vote in the lobby for rule-based bots to fill the empty slots. They either spread out to hold separate gates or group up and heal each other.

All runtime AI calls go to Meta models. They happen only **between waves**, never during combat.

When a wave ends, the server builds a match summary. It contains:
- lantern health and the gate where the most enemies broke through
- each player's class, damage dealt and deaths
- revives
- the previous wave's plan

During the 20-second intermission, the director turns this into the next wave as strict JSON. The plan has four parts:

# RecoverFlow AI

**Chase only the money that is actually owed.**

RecoverFlow AI is an accounts receivable and dispute-resolution platform engineered for Indian MSME distributors, wholesalers, and retailers selling on credit. When a buyer partly pays an invoice and disputes a line item, staff need to reconcile evidence before deciding what amount to request. RecoverFlow AI mathematically isolates disputed amounts from undisputed amounts, verifies claims against physical and digital evidence, drafts collection notices asking exclusively for the undisputed balance, enforces exact-version human staff approval, and updates ledger statuses only upon verified payment settlement.

- **Live Staging Demonstration:** [https://recoverflaw.duckdns.org/](https://recoverflaw.duckdns.org/)
- **Interactive API Documentation:** Available at `/docs` (when running locally or on staging)
- **Public source repository:** [lakshya14-ds/RecoverFlow-AI](https://github.com/lakshya14-ds/RecoverFlow-AI)
- **Hackathon Track:** Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon | Track: Indie Developer | Theme: Build for Your World
- **Status:** Live deployment with verified Meta Model API integrations, deterministic accounting rules, and interactive demonstration environment.

---

## 1. The Problem and the Solution

### The Friction in Indian B2B Credit Trade
In Indian wholesale and distribution sectors, credit terms of 15 to 45 days are standard. However, invoice settlements rarely match the invoice total. Deliveries frequently involve missing cartons, transit damage, price variances, or return schemes. A buyer typically pays what they believe they received, leaving a residual balance unpaid while disputing specific line items.

A full-balance reminder can include money that is genuinely disputed. The target workflow involves manual document hunting across delivery receipts, customer audio messages, and bank statements; RecoverFlow aims to make that review traceable.

### The RecoverFlow AI Approach
RecoverFlow AI operates on a single principle: **never demand payment for an item under active dispute**.

The system ingests commercial tax invoices, purchase orders, delivery challans, and customer communications. It reconciles line items and bank deposits to compute an exact mathematical split:

```
Gross Invoiced Amount
  - Payments Received to Date
  = Total Outstanding Balance
  - Disputed Line Items (Frozen on Hold)
  = Actionable Undisputed Balance (Eligible for Recovery)
```

### For example (The Synthetic Hero invoice Case)

The system's core mechanics are demonstrated through a realistic synthetic benchmark case (`INV-2026-HERO`):

| Financial Dimension | Synthetic Value | Evidence and Explanation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Gross Invoiced Amount** | INR 2,40,000 | 80 Units Precision Valve Sets at INR 3,000 each (`INV-2026-HERO.pdf`). |
| **Payments Received** | INR 1,50,000 | Verified bank transfer deposit via UTR ledger match on 2026-09-25. |
| **Total Outstanding** | INR 90,000 |

**You missed the moment. You don't have to miss the story.**

*Bedtime, in the language your family speaks at home.*

A PWA bedtime handoff for families. A parent adds a memo and an optional photo or voice recording, reviews source passages, and chooses which confirmed details to use. From those selected details, the app prepares:

1. A short briefing for the parent who missed the day.
2. A contextual recall question that the parent can edit.

# MetaFabricAI

### A Data Discovery Revolution for the AI Era

**From a mission to the right data. From fragmented data sources to actionable Data Recipes.**

For decades, finding public data has meant typing keywords into dozens of separate government portals and hoping your words match the agency's terminology. The data exists, but people (and the AI systems that depend on it) can't find it.
Keyword search leaves users with seven problems:
1. It depends on perfect metadata, yet standards vary and fields are often incomplete.
2. It matches strings, not the meaning of titles, descriptions, or data dictionaries.
3. It can't turn a real-world mission into the data needed to address it.
4. Users must guess which keywords agencies use.
5. Natural-language questions don't work.
6. Nothing explains how datasets relate or how to combine them for analysis.
7. Data gaps stay invisible until deep into an analysis.
   
MetaFabric AI is a metadata-first, AI-assisted application that changes the starting point from *keywords* to *missions*. Users describe what they want to accomplish (for example, analyzing traffic safety near schools). Powered by Meta's **Muse Spark** model, MetaFabric interprets the mission, reasons over **every record** in a unified catalog of public metadata retrieved through an MCP service, recommends sources with explanations and caveats, supports conversational refinement, and proposes a **Data Recipe**: a structured plan for combining the selected datasets, including its own data gaps and limitations.

The same mission, tested on Washington, DC's official open-data portal and in MetaFabric AI:

| Approach | Result |
| --- | --- |
| **opendata.dc.gov**, full sentence typed in | **No results found** |

# Agent Gate

A QA agent for enterprise AI agents. Give it an agent's spec and it generates test cases, proves its own checks can fail, runs the cases, triages failures, and returns a release verdict: **SHIP**, **BLOCK** or **CONDITIONAL**.

Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Oct 26 to Nov 4, 2026), Indie track.

**Demo video (2:47):** https://youtu.be/B2FvLE6puwU

**Status:** working harness with two sample domains (support-ticket triage, refund desk), a rule-based reference agent with seeded defects for each, and an LLM-driven refund agent that runs on Muse Spark or any OpenAI-style endpoint. The Meta Model API path (`MetaProvider`, `LLMRefundAgent`) has been run live on `muse-spark-1.3`: see [Live run on Muse Spark](#live-run-on-muse-spark).

## Why

Enterprises will not ship agents they cannot test. In a 2026 VentureBeat (VB Pulse) survey of 157 enterprises, about half reported an agent or LLM feature that passed internal evaluations and then failed in front of a customer (self-reported, so directional). Agent Gate generates the tests and refuses to trust a check until it has shown that the check can tell a good answer from a bad one.

## The six loops

| # | Loop | Code | What it does today |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Discover | `agent_gate/spec.py` | Reads the spec, lists requirements and tools, reports tools that no requirement covers |
| 2 | Generate and validate | `agent_gate/generate.py` + a domain module | Builds cases per requirement kind (permission, leak, rule, injection, tool failure, boundary, role gate). Each case proposes several checks. A check is kept only if it passes a known-good trace and fails a known-bad trace |
| 3 | Execute | `agent_gate/runner.py` | Fresh data for every run, tool-failure injection, k repeats per case (default 5), per-run seeds. API, network and malformed-response errors are scored `env_error`, never as agent failures; transient 429/5xx/timeouts are retried |
| 4 | Triage | `agent_gate/runner.py` | Re-runs anything that did not pass cleanly, then labels it `agent_bug` (fails every run), `flaky` (fails some), `test_bug` (a trusted reference agent also fails it) or `env_error` |
| 5 | Expand | `agent_gate/generate.py` | Creates new variants of failing cases through the same builders, so every new check is validated again |
| 6 | Gate | `agent_gate/runner.py` | P0 failure or any regression against a baseline gives BLOCK. Only lower-priority failures give CONDITIONAL. Otherwise SHIP. `--changed-tool` re-runs only the cases for requirements touching that tool |

Plate photo + plain request → colony count you can audit.

![Demo — AGAR 14684.jpg: 55 true, 56 predicted](docs/img/demo.png)
![Landing — Colony counts you can audit.](docs/img/landing.png)

## Built during the hackathon

Everything in this repository was built **Oct 27 – Nov 5 2026** (submission deadline Nov 4, 21:00 ET = Nov 5, 03:00 in Barcelona) as a solo entry in the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Indie track). See the dated [BUILD_LOG.md](BUILD_LOG.md) for what was built and when. How it was built: [docs/process/](docs/process/) — plan, per-session instruction files, and design mockups.

## What it does

- **Count colonies / cells** with SAM 3.1 from a short noun phrase (e.g. `round spot`).
- **Measure in Python** — counts, areas, equivalent diameters come from `labvision/measure.py`; numbers never come from the model. Pixel size → mm via plate diameter detected in Python with OpenCV HoughCircles (90 mm plate, otherwise px with a note).
- **Quality checks** — blur (Laplacian variance), glare (saturated pixels), empty, crowded.
- **Size filters** — “larger than X mm” and “smaller than X mm” (or both) are applied in Python by the `measure` tool; colonies excluded by the filter are drawn dashed and the header says “N of M detected”. The report states which filter was applied — or that a requested one was not.
- **TNTC** — counts >300 → “Too numerous to count (>300 CFU): dilute and re-plate”.
- **Self-check retry** — if SAM returns 0 but the image is sharp, retry once with the alternate prompt `colonies`.
- **Descriptive colony-type table** — Python features (Lab colour minus agar background, circularity, log diameter, texture) are clustered in Python (fixed global scales, average linkage); Muse Spark Open writes a short description per group from a constrained vocabulary (colours, shapes, margins, elevations, surfaces). The table is descriptive only.
- **Voice input** — click the mic, say “count colonies larger than 2 mm” hands-free (gloves, biosafety cabinet); Muse Voice Transcribe fills the request box.
- **Human in the loop** — draw a box around a missed colony (SAM box/point prompt) in the Result tab; accepted only if it contrasts with the surrounding agar (“No colony visible here” otherwise). Removing a false detection and every edit is logged separately from model output.
- **Sanity guards** — duplicates (IoU), plate size check (40–98% of image), implausible sizes (0.1–15 mm flagged), dense-plate undercount flag. A flagged plate gets status **Review**, never OK.
- **Batch / folder upload** — pick many photos or a whole folder (in `/app` or the queue); non-images are ignored, the browser sends them in requests of 50, and one background worker analyses them in order. Progress shows in the queue (“N plates waiting”).
- **Stop** — cancel a running analysis; the agent stops before its next model call.
- **Light / dark / system theme** toggle on

# Scope — Autonomous Pentesting Agent

An autonomous penetration-testing agent that **thinks like an ethical hacker but only
acts inside an authorized range**. It is driven by a Meta model (`muse-spark-1.3`) through
the Meta Model API, and it follows one strict rule:

> **A finding only counts if the exploit actually succeeds** — a reproducible
> request/response that proves the vulnerability, never a guess or a "possible" issue.

Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Indie Dev track).

---

## Why this is different

Most "AI security" demos either (a) describe vulnerabilities without proving them, or
(b) run offensive tooling with no guardrails. This agent does neither:

- **It proves what it reports.** The model forms a hypothesis, tests it with real HTTP
  requests, and only records a finding once it can show the exact request and the response
  that proves it. Unproven guesses are discarded.
- **It cannot go out of bounds.** A deny-by-default allowlist is enforced *in code* before
  every single action. Anything outside the authorized scope is refused and logged — the
  model has no way to override it.

---

```

                 │          Meta model (muse-spark-1.3)         │
                 │   recon → hypothesize → verify → record      │
                 └───────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘

                 │                 Agent loop                   │

                 └───┬───────────────┬───────────────┬──────────┘
                     │               │               │
         ┌───────────▼──┐   ┌────────▼───────┐  ┌────▼──────────┐
         │  Scope Guard │   │     Tools      │  │  Cost Guard   │
         │ (allowlist,  │◄──┤ http_request   │  │ (token/$      │
         │  deny by     │   │ run_python     │  │  accounting,  │
         │  default)    │   │ port_scan …    │  │  hard stop)   │
         └──────────────┘   └────────────────┘  └───────────────┘
                     │
         ┌───────────▼──────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  Report (Markdown findings) + Transcript (full trace) │
         └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

1. **Recon** — probe the target to understand the application.
2. **Hypothesize** — name a specific, testable weakness.

   reproducible request/response that proves it.
4. **Record** — save the exact evidence and a remediation.

HCI and social-science labs run on students who rotate every year or two. What they know lives in chat threads, Drive folders, consent forms and their heads. # Antinoise

Feedforward noise cancellation for road traffic — not in your earbuds, but across an open roadside zone.
Sensor towers hear the rumble first; an optical-fiber relay (analysis faster than sound) hands the noise
profile to a downstream controller before the sound arrives, turning geometry into **anticipation time**.

Built for the **Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon** (Oct 27 – Nov 4, 2026) — 100% of this repository
was built during the building period (first commit is the scaffold below).

## What's in the sim

- **Physics core** (`src/core/`): seeded traffic-rumble source (60–160 Hz harmonic stacks + low-passed
  broadband), propagation paths (delay + attenuation), an NLMS-based **FXLMS adaptive controller** with
  divergence guards, and the two-tower fiber scenario with the emission scheduler.
- **Honest physics:** lead time = distance ÷ 343 m/s; the quiet zone is **wavelength-capped** — deep rumble
  cancels across a region, short waves only in a narrow spot. The page says so, not just the README.
- **The commissioning agent** (`src/brain/`): Meta's open-weights **Muse Spark Open**
  (`meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026`) on Baseten reads the live field state and proposes physical
  parameter changes (tower distance, array nodes, standoff, adaptation rate) — every proposal is validated
  against feasibility physics before it is applied and re-measured on screen. It has two selectable goals —
  **deepest dB** or **widest quiet band** (the area objective trades a little depth for width, by its own
  admission in the note) — and an **agent memory**: every accepted, re-measured turn is filed locally and
  fed to later turns as measured precedents (a memory protocol, not weight tuning). **SAM 3.1** (Meta Model
  API) proposes placement from a street photo.
- **Audio + field UI** (`src/audio/`, `src/ui/`): audible A/B (traffic vs. quiet zone), interactive field map
  with drag markers, per-frequency wave view with cross-section, live dB readouts. Sources: seeded synthetic
  test bed, three real CC0 recordings, or **your site's own baseline recording** (upload) — the sim,
  measurements and agent all run on whichever is active.

## Security posture

## Overview

ModelMuse is a static single-page application for viewing and creating 3D and 2D educational models directly in the browser. It needs no backend and no build step to run: the only release artifact is a single self-contained HTML file:

- `dist-standalone/modelmuse-standalone.html` (approx. 430 KB, single file, zero local references)

Publish this file via GitHub Pages or any other static web server, open it in a browser, and you are ready. The application requires an internet connection at startup: it loads five CDN libraries (Three.js 0.186.1 pinned, Vue 3 unpinned via `vue@3`, OrbitControls from the Three.js 0.186.1 package, Tailwind CSS Play CDN unpinned, and Inter from Google Fonts). It is therefore a single file, but not offline-capable.

Runtime generation and revision run in the browser against one of three providers — Meta Muse, Baseten, or OpenRouter (see [Features](#features)). You provide your own API key where required (bring your own key); keys are kept only in memory or `sessionStorage` and are never written to the repository. A local proxy (`scripts/proxy.mjs`, localhost only) exists solely as a fallback for network/CORS problems on the Baseten path; OpenRouter is direct-call only.

India has tens of millions of small shops: sweet shops, salons, tailors, tuition centres. Their customers are on WhatsApp and Instagram, but Ads Manager asks for objectives, bid strategies and audiences in English jargon. Most shopkeepers never run an ad, or pay an agency they cannot judge.

# MOAT Guard

![MOAT Guard's intro animation: with MOAT off a messenger carries "pouch cell 272 Wh/kg" out to the web and the spy reads it; with MOAT on the guard stops the same search, rewrites it to "high energy density", and the spy gets nothing](docs/demo.gif)

**A fail-closed privacy guard at the trust boundary between a deep-research agent's internal documents and its web searches.** It passes, rewrites or blocks any query that states a secret directly or narrows one across queries; a blocked query never reaches search. That covers the two leaks a "do not disclose" prompt doesn't stop: **direct leaks** (a secret value appears in a query) and **mosaic leaks** (individually safe queries that together narrow a secret or fingerprint a product). Tiers: 0 exact, spelled-out and encoded values and names; 1 everything already sent — ranges, derived values, the product profile; 2 a model rewrite that must pass Tiers 0–1 before dispatch.

## Run in 60s

```
make demo    # → http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

No API key needed. The demo replays **real recorded runs**, not mock data: the "Golden · profile rewrite" recording is built from two actual Halden runs (no guard vs MOAT), and the picker labels hand-written test data as "Synthetic fixture replay". It opens on the intro page — **Watch it work** plays the golden recording. **Demo video:** _link before submission_.

On **Windows** without `make`, run the steps by hand (WSL users can just run `make demo`):

```
uv sync
cd web && npm ci && npm run build && cd ..
uv run uvicorn api.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
```

All numbers: Halden dev company, 5 docs, 5 tasks, seed 0. Agent, Tier 2 rewrite and observer run on `muse-spark-1.3`. Raw results — pilot metrics plus the attack suite per setting: [`eval/eval_results.json`](eval/eval_results.json) (labeled), `eval/eval_results.unlabeled.json`, `eval/eval_results.internal.json`.

### Attack suite — deliberate leaks

150 attack queries across 10 leak types, each trying to get one secret past the guard, plus 150 benign queries a researcher might send. Hand-written by us for this dataset: a development suite and a first check of the guard, not a benchmark. It calls `guard.check` only (Tier 2 off, no model calls), so the same numbers appear in every label setting.

| | Before Tier 0 update (#70) | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Attacks caught | 104/150 | **145/150** |

Both false positives sit within `bound_tol` (3%) of a secret. E.g. "68 Wh cell weighing 250 g" never states the secret but works out to 272 Wh/kg; Tier 0 now catches it.

# Headroom

**An AI operator that fits more EV chargers on the grid connection a building already has: no grid upgrade, every driver charged, never over the limit.**

Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026 · Indie track · *Push the Frontier* (energy: controlling a physical system)

**[See how it works](https://headroom-meta.vercel.app/demo/)** · **[Watch the demo video](https://youtu.be/1-Ch1mL8464)** · [Project page](https://headroom-meta.vercel.app/) · [Run it yourself](#run-the-demo-no-key-no-account) · [All results](#results)

## The problem
Offices, malls, campuses and fleet depots all want more EV chargers, and the chargers plug into the same grid connection as the building.
- **The bill.** US utilities bill a business for its highest 15 minutes of power each month. Under Palo Alto's E-4 tariff, one 50 kW charging spike at 6 pm on a summer weekday adds **$2,572** to the bill, for about $3 of electricity.
- **The limit.** Owners size chargers for the worst case: the building's peak plus every charger at full power. So they install fewer chargers, or cap them and waste capacity they already pay for.
- **The upgrade.** More connection capacity means a utility study, a new transformer and a long wait.

## What Headroom does
Headroom sits between the building's meter and its chargers.
- **It watches the building** and charges the cars in the room the building leaves.
- **It never lets the site go over its connection.** A safety layer guarantees the limit.
- **The site manager just asks it questions** in plain language: *"Can I add 12 more chargers? What would it cost me?"* The operator, built on Meta's **Muse Spark**, answers from simulation, with every number checked against the math.
- **If the internet drops,** Meta's open-weight **Muse Glimmer** takes over on site.

# Then & There

**Race Nellie Bly around the world in real time, 137 years later.**

On November 14, 1889, Nellie Bly left Hoboken to beat Phileas Fogg's 80 days. From **November 14, 2026 to January 25, 2027**, Then & There replays her trip one day at a time, using only what American newspapers printed that morning. Each day you read a real clipping, on the original scan, and make the call: *will she make it?*

**How it works, on one real page:** https://then-and-there-flame.vercel.app/how

Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (indie track) by Tarik Moody.

---

## The problem

The Library of Congress has digitized 23.8 million pages of historic American newspapers. Almost nobody reads them. The stories aren't hidden by bad scans; they're hidden because you have to know a name before you can search for it. A Milwaukee barber praised in a Black weekly in 1898 is findable today only if you already know to type "Ellmore."

Then & There uses Meta's models to do an editor's job at archive scale: cut each page into stories, repair the text where the machine-read text (OCR) is garbled, find the human stories, and check every claim against the scan before a reader sees it. The daily race is the first way in.

## What a day looks like

1. **The dispatch.** A clipping from that date in 1889, shown on the original scan with a blue-pencil ring, plus a clean transcription and its Library of Congress citation.
2. **The Morgue.** Free background clippings from the files: what other papers had printed by then. Never anything from later.
3. **The call.** A "will she make it?" question. A wrong call costs 3 days; each question to the City Editor costs 1. You start with Fogg's 80. Finish with more than 8 left and you beat Nellie.
4. **The reveal.** What the papers printed next, on the scan, with an explanation.
5. **Meanwhile, back home.** A story from your own Midwest state's papers that same day.
6. **Share.** A spoiler-free result card.

The finale on January 25 is a ballot for her exact time, modeled on The Evening World's real 1889 contest ("A FREE TRIP TO EUROPE for the NEAREST GUESS as to the Exact Time of NELLIE BLY'S TOUR").

# HOLD — prêt-à-porter habilitation for autonomous agents

[![Tests](https://github.com/skiredj-prog/hold/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/skiredj-prog/hold/actions/workflows/tests.yml)

**HOLD separates intelligence, authority and evidence.** The agent proposes. The architecture governs execution. Evidence establishes what was accomplished. An agent may be right; its conviction alone does not make it the authority.

No Ollama, Meta credentials, tunnel, or live WhatsApp access is required.

    E --> J["Journal + replay\ncloses mission"]

**Observe:** one booking, one lost response, no duplicate dispatch, one bounded human decision, one correlated receipt.



We don't need infallible AI agents to entrust them with missions. We need an architecture in which their capabilities are not confused with their powers. # IncidentLab

IncidentLab investigates why a Docker app on Linux has stopped working, explains the cause with evidence that code checks, and verifies that an approved fix actually restored what the user was trying to do.

Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Indie developer track) with Muse Spark on Meta Model API, and with Muse Code.

**Demo video:** https://youtu.be/-jymOnRLxes

## The problem

When someone reports that uploads have stopped working, the usual signals can mislead. A health check can pass while every upload fails. A database container can report healthy while the app can't reach it. And after a fix, a running container doesn't show that uploads work again.

IncidentLab is a focused prototype for this situation: one self-hosted app (a file-upload service with a Postgres database) in a test VM, and three kinds of failure: a full volume, a directory the app can't write to, and an unavailable database.

## What it does

1. **Investigates.** Given the complaint, Muse Spark chooses from seven read-only checks: the lab's containers, a container's details, its logs, disk and inode usage, directory permissions, Docker events and the app's health endpoint. It often runs several at once, up to 12 per investigation.
2. **Records evidence.** Each check result gets an ID (E1, E2, …).
3. **Reports.** The model writes a structured report: the cause, its findings and the causes it ruled out, each citing an evidence ID, a field and the exact value, plus any open questions. "Healthy" and "insufficient evidence" are valid answers.
4. **Checks every citation.** Code compares each citation with the raw evidence and marks it supported or unsupported. The schema guarantees the report's format, not that its claims are true.
5. **Answers follow-up questions** using the same evidence. On the demo page, answers cite evidence in the same format and are checked by the same code.
6. **Repairs only with approval.** Each diagnosis maps to one predefined repair in code, and nothing changes until a person approves it.
7. **Verifies recovery the way a user would.** It uploads a random 1 MB file, downloads it, compares SHA-256 hashes and deletes the test file. Recovery counts only if that round trip works.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Complaint: uploads have stopped working"] --> B["Muse Spark chooses read-only checks"]
    B --> C["investigate.py runs them and records evidence E1, E2, ..."]
    C --> B
    B --> D["Structured report: cause, findings and ruled-out causes, each with a citation"]
    D --> E["Code checks every citation against the raw evidence"]
    E --> F{"Person approves the mapped repair?"}
    F -- yes --> G["repair.py runs one predefined repair"]
    G --> H["Verifier: upload, download, compare SHA-256"]
    F -- no --> I["Nothing changes"]
```

Build and animate an editable low-poly scene, then use it to direct AI video.

Built for the **Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon** by Zhening Zhu, Qingxuan Yan and Xiang Chang. Powered by Muse.

## Why

AI video models are powerful, but describing actions, camera movement and the relationships between objects through long prompts is hard. LittleTake lets everyday creators show those intentions with an editable 3D scene and a rough performance.

![LittleTake creator flow](docs/assets/creator-flow.png)

## What you can do

- **Describe a scene.** Muse builds characters, a set, cameras and shots from a sentence. Every edit is a preview you can compare and apply.
- **Start from a reference.** Turn a clip, storyboard or sketch into an editable proxy scene.
- **Perform the shot.** Edit keyframes, or record objects and cameras live with Pilot. Muse can refine a take.
- **Direct the look.** Attach appearance references and generate storyboards with Muse Image.
- **Hand it off.** Export PNG frames, WebM previs and a video brief for an AI video model, then import the finished video.
- **Step inside.** Experimental [WebXR](docs/webxr.md) for working in the scene in VR.

## How it uses Meta models

| Model | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| Muse Spark | Scene design, the tool-calling director, the asset expert, visual review and video briefs |
| Muse Image | Scene concepts and AI storyboards |
| SAM | Segmenting objects in reference frames |

Requires Node.js 24 or newer.

```sh
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local   # then set MODEL_API_KEY
npm run dev
```

On Windows, run `setup.bat` once, set `MODEL_API_KEY` in `.env.local`, then run `run.bat`.

```sh
npm test                     # run the tests
npm run build && npm start   # run the production server
```

| `src/` | The editor |

# DebugCode: LeetCode for Codebase Navigation & Debugging

**Built for the Meta Global AI Hackathon**

---

## 💡 The Problem & Philosophy

Technical interviews are undergoing a massive industry shift:
> Traditional interviews test: *"Write an algorithm from scratch in a single empty function."*  
> Modern engineering loops test: *"Here is an existing, realistic multi-file repository. Find the bug, fix it without breaking other features, and defend your architectural rationale."*

Platforms like LeetCode, HackerRank, and CodeChef only train the old style. **DebugCode** is built from the ground up to train the modern debugging and code comprehension loop.

### 🚫 Strict Anti-Cheat: No AI in the Coding Experience
- Zero AI code assistants, zero chat copilot sidebars, zero AI autocomplete, and zero AI hints during problem solving.
- Hints are curated, static text written by problem authors in `meta.json`.
- Test files are marked **read-only** in the Monaco editor to guarantee integrity.

### 🧠 The AI Feature: "Understanding Check" (Meta Llama 3 via Groq)
- Brute-forcing test cases or guessing lines is discouraged.
- When you click **Submit** and pass all visible + hidden test suites, a dedicated 4th tab unlocks: **The Understanding Check**.
- Powered by **Llama 3.3 70B** on Groq, the model inspects your git diff and conducts a structured **3-question Socratic viva**:
  1. **Root Cause Identification**: Why did the bug occur in the original architecture?
  2. **Mechanism of the Fix**: How does your patch resolve it without regressions?
  3. **Architectural Prevention**: What tests, typing, or design patterns prevent this class of bug systemically?
- Scores your comprehension on a 0–100% rubric and awards a **"Verified Comprehension"** badge!

---

## 🚀 Quick Start

### Prerequisites
- **Node.js**: v18+ (v20+ recommended)
- **Python**: 3.11+

### 1. Launch Everything in One Click (Windows)
Double-click `start_all.bat` or run:
```bash
./start_all.bat
```
Then open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) in your browser.

---

```bash

pip install -r requirements.txt

# (Optional) Add your Groq API key to backend/.env:
# GROQ_API_KEY=gsk_...
# If omitted, the platform uses an intelligent local evaluator fallback.

python -m uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --reload
```

#### Frontend (Next.js)
```bash
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```
Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000).

# FollowAlong

**Instructions that see your work: real-time visual guidance for hands-on work.**

People learn and do hands-on work from how-to videos and manuals, and the instructions never know whether you got the
step right: you find out when it doesn't work. FollowAlong turns any video, manual or set of photos into a live, step-by-step guide that
follows along through your camera, checks every step before the next one starts, and tells you the moment something's
off, by voice, hands-free. Muse Spark writes the steps and judges what geometry can't; SAM 3.1 measures what's there.

**Who it's for:** anyone doing hands-on work from instructions: makers and students with electronics and robotics kits,
people doing repairs and installs at home, assembly and workforce training (new hires checked step by step, with a log
of every check), and the teams and creators who want to see exactly where people get stuck.

## Meta Global AI Hackathon 2026 — submission overview

- **Track · problem statement:** Indie Developer · Build for Your World
- **Provenance:** built from scratch during the hackathon window (Oct 26 – Nov 4, 2026) by Samruddhi Kakade and Unnati Shah.
- **Meta models at runtime:**
  - **Muse Spark** (Meta Model API): turns a video or an instruction manual into a step plan, runs the live coach
    (a look every 2–3 s with short-term memory), judges the checks code can't measure, answers spoken questions.
  - **SAM 3.1**: outlines the hand and each step's parts so plain code decides measured checks (present, count, inside).
  - **Muse Voice Transcribe**: hands-free voice commands, questions and barge-in.
- **Not a chatbot, not a one-prompt wrapper:** instructions → step plan → a camera that watches the work → SAM-measured
  checks plus Muse Spark judgements, rule-based safety gates, scored on CF-Bench (303 labelled frames from CC BY
  tutorials). Best case, the breadboard guide: 93% of frames right and no unfinished step let through.
- **Bonus prize targeted:** Best Agentic Use-Case (the coach watches, decides, interrupts and advances on its own,
  with the learner able to overrule it).
- **Quickstart, no key:** `docker compose up` → **Watch a replay**. Live mode: `cp .env.example .env`, set `MODEL_API_KEY`.

Start from a video, a kit manual, or snapped pages. FollowAlong plays one step at a time and watches your work through
the camera: done → the next step plays; wrong → it tells you what's different and loops the three seconds you need to
see again; not sure → it asks you. The same engine works for any hands-on task (a knot, a cable, a thermostat, a robot
arm), and the bundled lessons show that range.

# Centurion

Centurion is an AI commerce analyst for Shopify brands. It shows which sales came from AI assistants (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot, Meta AI) with the evidence for every order, finds what AI tells shoppers about the products that contradicts the catalog, fixes it in the store in one click, and tests whether an AI shopping agent can reach checkout. **Ask Centurion**, an analyst on Meta's Muse Spark model, answers questions from the store's own data with charts and takes those actions inside the chat.

Built for the Meta Global AI Hackathon, Indie Dev track, "Build Your World" (Oct 26 to Nov 4, 2026).

## Design rules

- **Attribution is deterministic.** No language model decides which orders count or how much revenue AI sent. Every number traces back to an order ID and the signal that matched.
- **No overclaiming.** A direct visit to a product page is reported as "worth watching", never as AI revenue.
- **Official APIs only.** AI answers are read through model provider APIs, never by scraping chat interfaces.

## Repository layout

```
apps/
  shopify/        Embedded Shopify admin app (Polaris)
  web/            Standalone app on a fictional mid-market store, no Shopify account needed
  gateway/        MCP server that answers outside AI agents with a brand's verified facts
packages/
  attribution/    Order classifier, AI source signatures, sample store generator, reports and CLI
  checkout-test/  Agent Checkout worker (Playwright) and its local test store
  core/           Shared logic for both apps: view builder, Answer Check, fixes, Ask Centurion, Postgres store
supabase/
  migrations/     Postgres schema
```

| Package | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/web` | Three tabs on the fictional Northpine store (60 products, 237 SKUs, 12,000 orders): **AI Revenue** (click-to-filter explorer), **Fix AI Answers** (wrong answers ranked by AI revenue at stake, with the fix and Apply), **Agent Checkout** (animated replay of a recorded agent run). **Ask Centurion** in a corner chat: Muse Spark answers with metrics, charts and tables, runs actions, keeps history, takes voice input, and nudges when something needs attention. Command palette (Ctrl/⌘ K) and keyboard shortcuts. |

Answer Check, Checkout Test and Weekly Fix as before, plus an **Ask Centurion** page with the same structured answers and actions, including applying and undoing the fix on the live store. Shows labeled sample data until the store has AI orders of its own. |

# MindTrace — Agentic Cognitive Diagnostic Engine

> **Trace the thinking, not just the answer.**

MindTrace is a production-grade diagnostic engine for mathematics education, built for the **Meta Global AI Hackathon 2026**. It moves beyond simple answer-checking by analyzing a student's *workflow trace*—every committed step, transformation, and final answer—to produce a structured **Cognitive Diagnostic Report** with error classifications, conceptual breakdowns, and the next optimal transition.

The system combines a deterministic math referee (to prevent LLM hallucination) with Meta's `muse` models, a Firebase-backed cognitive profile, and a secure serverless proxy that keeps API keys out of the client.

---

## ✨ Features

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| **Workflow Trace Analysis** | Students commit step-by-step transformations; the engine diagnoses the *process*, not just the result. |
| **Deterministic Math Referee** | A JavaScript equivalence checker (`checkMathEquivalence`) compares the student's final answer numerically before the LLM is invoked, injecting ground truth to prevent false "correct" verdicts. |
| **Adaptive Probe Generation** | Generates targeted practice questions based on the student's identified gaps and mastery level. |
| **Cognitive Profile & Skill Graph** | Persistent, Firebase-backed profile tracking validated competencies and skill gaps, synced after every diagnostic pass. |
| **Handwritten Derivation Upload** | Accepts image uploads (max 600KB) via a secure proxy for multimodal analysis. |
| **Secure Serverless Proxy** | All model calls route through `/api/proxy` (Vercel/Netlify function); the API key never reaches the browser. |
| **Anonymous, Session-Isolated Auth** | Firebase anonymous authentication—no email required, session-isolated by default. |
| **Mobile-Responsive UI** | Dark-mode design with 44px minimum touch targets, safe-area insets, and responsive breakpoints. |

# FourthMatch

**Companies pay for goods nobody verified. FourthMatch makes the delivery itself the fourth match.**

Procurement runs on a three-way match: the purchase order (PO), the goods receipt note (GRN) and the
vendor invoice must agree before payment. All three are documents, and a signed GRN is only as good
as the storekeeper's count. FourthMatch adds a fourth source that is not a document: the receiving-dock
video. When what the camera shows contradicts what the paperwork says, the agent holds or reduces the
payment and cites the clause of the company's own receiving policy that justifies it.

Meta Global AI Hackathon entry, built solo between Oct 30 and Nov 4, 2026. All data is synthetic.

| | |
|---|---|
| Demo video | [Watch the 3-minute demo](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hjwKrbPxWAvOUrlRANbDsHdovghxMpQw/view?usp=sharing) |
| Docs | [Deploy](DEPLOY.md) |

![FourthMatch landing page](docs/screenshots/landing.png)

## The problem

Take purchase order `FM/PO/26-27/002` from the seeded data (scenario `scn2_short`). Shree Ganesh
Packaging Industries is to deliver **14** corrugated cartons (SKU `CTN-5PLY-24`) at ₹550 each, so the
line is worth **₹7,700** before GST. The storekeeper signs the GRN for 14. The vendor invoices 14,
₹9,086 with 18% GST. Every document agrees, so a three-way match passes and the invoice is paid.

The dock video shows **12** cartons. Two never arrived, and the company pays ₹1,100 for them. No
document in the chain can reveal that, because all three were written by people who were not
counting against an independent record.

At one carton line this is small. The same seed set has a steel-coil purchase (`FM/PO/26-27/010`,
Bharat Steel Rolling Mills, 20 coils ordered) where a short shipment beyond tolerance puts
₹12,20,000 on the line, and the 12 seeded cases carry ₹18,42,370 in total at risk. Receiving fraud and
honest miscounts both land in the gap between "signed" and "seen", and nobody audits that gap at
invoice volume.

## How it works

A receiving-dock video is uploaded against a PO. Muse Spark reads the footage and chooses what to look
for, SAM 3.1 segments and tracks every object, and plain Python merges the tracks into a count and
decides whether the evidence is good enough to trust. Python then reconciles that count with the PO,
GRN and invoice under rules compiled from the company's receiving policy, a tool-calling decision agent
explains the outcome with cited clauses and track IDs, and the result is sealed into a
SHA-256-hashed, re-verifiable evidence pack.

For `scn2_short` the served verdict is `partial_pay`: SAM counts 12 tracks, the PO, GRN and invoice
say 14, clause 4.2 (tolerance on cartons is 0.0%) fires, ₹1,100 is held, and the undisputed portion
is released.

# Wildlife Road Alert

Wildlife Road Alert watches dashcam video for deer, moose, elk, bear and
bison near the road and warns the driver before the vehicle reaches the
animal. SAM 3.1 finds and tracks each animal and segments the road surface
from a 960 px analysis copy (boxes and masks are scaled up to the
full-resolution display copy); plain geometry — on the road, in the
roadside band, moving toward the road, box growth as time-to-reach, and
distance from box height and a per-species standing height — drives three
warning levels (green, amber, red), with a group count, a "MORE MAY
FOLLOW" hold, severity by species and an assurance level. Every red alert
is checked by Muse Spark, which can confirm the species (its species
then renames the track and sets severity and distance, with SAM's word
kept in `detected_as`), write the road-sign text, or mark the alert
rejected. Confirmed alerts become sightings on a small network map;
vehicles behind the sighting are warned, an operator can approve a
sighting into a Waze-ready feed (`output/waze_feed.json`), drivers can
file voice reports that Muse Voice Transcribe turns into sightings, and
Muse Wonder writes a text briefing from the day's sightings and
hotspots. Built for the Meta Global AI Hackathon 2026.

## Setup

1. Install Python 3.10+ and ffmpeg (Mac: `brew install python ffmpeg`).
2. In this folder:

   ```bash
   python3 -m venv .venv
   source .venv/bin/activate        # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
   pip install -r requirements.txt
   ```

3. Set your Meta Model API key (never commit it):

   ```bash
   export MODEL_API_KEY=your-key    # Windows: set MODEL_API_KEY=your-key
   ```

## Getting the data

The clips and datasets are not in this repository (see `.gitignore`).

- **Night dashcam clip:** Pond5 item **141272328** (commercial licence),

  clip. Clip naming and expected results: `test_videos/CLIP_LIST.md`.

  Universe, CC BY 4.0 — https://universe.roboflow.com/scalersai/deers-on-roads
  Export in COCO format into `Deers on roads.v4i.coco/`.

  there into `thermal_samples/`.
- **Voice samples:** short driver recordings (`.mp3`) in a local
  `voice_samples/` folder; they are not shared.

# Meta dev skills

**Meta dev skills** is a public, reusable pack of AI-optimized, modular instructions
(open-standard agent skills) for building on Meta's AI developer stack. It grounds
coding agents — Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Muse Code, and Hermes — with the
workflows, constraints, and gotchas that come up when you build with Meta's models,
Meta's open weights, the Muse Code coding agent, and Ray-Ban Meta / Wearables glasses.

Each skill is one `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter and a `## When to Use` section,
following the open-standard agent skills format (<https://agentskills.io/home>).
Skills are picked up automatically when a task matches their triggers.

Part of the Zoth / NullAI skills collection. MIT licensed.

- **Meta Model API models** — Muse Spark series, Muse Wonder, Muse Image,

- **Ray-Ban Meta / Wearables** — apps built with the Wearables Device Access
  Toolkit (DAT).

| Slug | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `meta-model-api-quickstart` | First API call: account, credits, auth, model IDs, spend limits |
| `muse-spark-multimodal-agents` | Multimodal, tool-calling agents on the Muse Spark series |

user-level equivalent). Cursor also reads a root `AGENTS.md`; referencing the

# SWARM EVOLVE-X

A small, reproducible design loop for the Meta Global AI hackathon.

You give it a gripper objective, bounds, a seed, and a simulator budget. A planner proposes where to search. A deterministic surrogate scores every design. An adversary looks for valid stress cases inside a declared envelope. Evolution spends the same budget three ways: random search, evolution alone, and evolution plus the adversary. Finalists are frozen before they see the holdout set.

The optional second domain is a 24-hour energy balance with the same runner. It is a teaching model, not a grid study.

## What is novel here

The model does not invent the physics and it does not run code. It can only return a hypothesis, a region inside the bounds, and an action from an allowlist. The simulator is the measurement. Every result stores the evaluator version, the assumptions hash, the seeds, and the holdout fingerprint.

## Layout

```
backend/app/sim/gripper.py     analytic gripper score
backend/app/sim/energy.py      optional daily energy balance
backend/app/search/            random, evolutionary, and adversarial search
backend/app/agents/            Meta client, mock planner, rule planner
backend/app/orchestration/     plan → search → frozen holdout
frontend/                      run form, gripper figure, charts, provenance
docs/                          contract, assumptions, holdout numbers
experiments/                   example config, manual check, recorded run
```

## Run it locally

Python 3.10+ and Node 20+ are enough. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and leave `ENABLE_META=false` until you have a key. Do not commit `.env`.

```powershell
cd swarm-evolve-x
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r backend\requirements.txt -r backend\requirements-dev.txt
cd backend
python -m pytest
python -m uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

In a second terminal:

```powershell
cd swarm-evolve-x\frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:3000`. The API docs are at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs`.

If the API is down, use **Replay recorded gripper run**. That file is `frontend/public/demo/hero.json`, generated by:

```powershell
cd backend
python scripts\export_hero.py
python scripts\evaluate.py
```

`evaluate.py` rewrites `docs/evaluation.md` from a fresh three-seed holdout. Do not paste numbers into that file by hand.

## Model use

Set `ENABLE_META=true` and `MODEL_API_KEY` only on the server. The client posts to `META_BASE_URL` (`https://api.meta.ai/v1` by default) at `/responses`, with timeout, retry, and a six-call cap. The dashboard provider switch cannot reveal the key. If the flag is off, or the call fails, the run continues with the mock or rule planner and says so in the provenance log.

## Metrics

Search calls are split equally across random, evolutionary, and adversarial search. Adversarial trials count against that method's own budget. Holdout evaluations are extra and are not used to pick the win

# REWIND - AI Forensic Reconstruction

> **Upload a photo of damage. Watch AI reverse-engineer exactly what happened.**

REWIND analyzes photos of physical damage and reconstructs the event that caused it using Meta AI's multimodal models and real-time physics simulation. See cracked glass, a toppled shelf, or water damage -- and REWIND shows you the force, angle, speed, and sequence of events, animated over the original photo.

Built for the **Meta Global AI Hackathon 2026** by Team Parallax.

---

## How It Works

REWIND runs a 5-stage AI pipeline, streaming results in real time:

| Stage | Model | What It Does |
|-------|-------|-------------|
| 1. Segment | **SAM 3.1** | Identifies and isolates damage regions in the photo |
| 2. Analyze | **Muse Spark 1.3** | Multimodal physics analysis -- estimates forces, velocities, materials |
| 3. Reason | **Muse Wonder** | Deep causal chain reasoning -- why did this happen? |
| 4. Simulate | Physics Engine | Generates frame-by-frame reconstruction animation |
| 5. Visualize | **Muse Image** | Creates AI-generated "before the damage" reconstruction |

Every stage streams progress via SSE, so you watch the analysis unfold live.

## Demo

**No API key needed to try it.** REWIND ships with a full demo mode that returns realistic pre-built analysis with simulated delays, so you can experience the complete flow immediately.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/KMaruthi2002/REWIND.git
cd REWIND
pip3 install -r requirements.txt
python3 app.py
# Open http://localhost:8000
```

Upload any damage photo and hit RECONSTRUCT. The app auto-detects your missing API key and runs the full pipeline with simulated Meta AI responses.

## What Makes This Different

**Forensic reconstruction from a single photo is novel.** Existing damage analysis tools classify damage type or estimate severity. REWIND goes further -- it reverse-engineers the entire event:

- **Impact analysis**: A cracked windshield becomes "28g steel projectile at 30 m/s, 35-degree angle, Hertzian contact fracture with 11 radial cracks"
- **Collapse reconstruction**: A fallen bookshelf becomes "seismic P-wave at 0.3g triggered cascading failure, 2.1s from initial displacement to ground contact"
- **Fluid trace analysis**: Water damage becomes "4.2 L/min flow rate from 1.8m elevation, capillary front advanced 34cm over 45 minutes"

The physics simulation plays back as a canvas overlay on top of your original photo -- force vectors, trajectories, and deformation in real time.

The model drafts the lesson. The server checks its structure, curriculum quality, learning quality, and safety. The teacher makes the final decision.

The current release covers Grade 4 equivalent fractions (Common Core `4.NF.A.1`). English is the product language, and teachers can also generate lessons in Arabic that render right to left. Everything runs on synthetic data.

![Scholé landing page showing the hero, a sample equivalent-fractions activity, and the target preparation-time metric](docs/assets/readme-hero.png)

![Scholé lesson-results dashboard showing learners grouped by who needs attention and the stored next step for each run](docs/assets/readme-dashboard.png)

## Run Scholé locally

You need Node.js 26 or newer, pnpm 10.17.1, Docker, and a Meta API key.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/abodacs/edu-canvas.git
cd edu-canvas
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
docker compose up -d postgres
cp .env.example .env
# In .env, uncomment META_API_KEY and set it to a server-side key.
set -a; source .env; set +a
pnpm db:setup
pnpm dev
```

Open `http://localhost:3000`. In development, sign in as the teacher `amira.north@example.test` with the password `synthetic-pass-1`.

The app needs PostgreSQL and a server-side provider key. It has no in-memory fallback. The [foundation runbook](docs/foundation-runbook.md) covers configuration, readiness checks, and safe redeploys.

## Safety boundaries

Three rules apply in every environment:

- Answer keys, mastery, and permissions stay on the server. They never appear in a client bundle or an A2UI message.
- The server sends no student images or identifying data to the model.
- The foundation blocks real student data until a data-processing agreement, EU data residency, a security review, and consent are all in place. Until then, deployments use synthetic data only.

## Contribute a change

Before you open an issue or a pull request, read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). It lists the checks for each kind of change. Run `pnpm check` before you push.

[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) maps the code. [docs/README.md](docs/README.md) indexes the rest of the documentation.

## Report a vulnerability

Report vulnerabilities privately through [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/abodacs/edu-canvas/security/advisories/new). Do not open a public issue for a suspected vulnerability.

# RatesCheck

Checks a 2026/27 English business rates bill against the published rules and
reports possible errors in £/year.

Submitted to the Meta AI Developer Hackathon (27 Oct – 4 Nov 2026). Not legal or
tax advice.

## What it does

1. **Read.** The owner photographs a 2026/27 English business rates bill (or
   presses "Try the DEMO bill"). Muse Spark 1.3 extracts the fields as JSON that
   is checked against a strict schema. A field it cannot read is `null`, never a
   guess, and values that look implausible are flagged for the owner.
2. **Confirm and answer.** The owner sees what was read (read-only in this
   build, see Known limits) and answers five questions: occupied, retail /
   hospitality / leisure use, number of properties in England, on the rating
   list before 1 Apr 2026, City of London.
3. **Recompute.** A deterministic rules engine (TypeScript, integer arithmetic;
   code, not AI) recomputes the 2026/27 England multiplier and the expected
   charge and compares them with the bill. The finding is in £/year.
4. **Explain and draft.** Muse Wonder 1.0, using tool calling, explains the
   finding and drafts a letter to the council using only figures from the
   engine's output (or the text of a rule it looked up). Code verifies every £
   and pence-in-the-£ figure in both texts, and an independent Muse Spark 1.3
   call reviews the claims. **Nothing is ever sent**: the letter is a draft the
   owner copies and sends themselves.
5. **Open-weight path.** For extraction only, the owner can choose Muse Spark
   Open (`meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026`, Meta's open-weight model) served by
   Baseten, under "Model:" on the Extract screen. It is implemented and covered
   by offline tests; whether the hosted demo has the Baseten key set is not
   verified. The explanation, the letter and the review always use the Meta
   Model API.

## Meta models used at runtime

| Model id                           | Host                             | Where it is called                                                                                   | Used for                                             |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `muse-spark-1.3`                   | `api.meta.ai` (Meta Model API)   | `supabase/functions/_shared/extract/prompt.ts` and `_shared/extract/extract.ts`, from `extract`      | Reading the bill                                     |
| `muse-spark-1.3`                   | `api.meta.ai`                    | `supabase/functions/_shared/agent/review.ts`, from `agent`                                           | Independent review of the explanation and the letter |
| `muse-wonder-1.0`                  | `api.meta.ai`                    | `supabase/functions/_shared/agent/prompt.ts` and `_shared/agent/run.ts`, from `agent`

# ServeDoctor

**An on-call agent for LLM serving, and ServeIncidents, a benchmark of real GPU incidents with sealed answers.**

A local Muse Glimmer model watches a live vLLM server every 30 seconds. On an anomaly it escalates to Muse Spark or
Muse Wonder, which names the root cause and proposes at most two fixes from a fixed whitelist. In live runs the fix is
applied, recovery is measured on real requests, and the change is rolled back if the service has not recovered.

Built during the Meta AI Developer Hackathon (Push the Frontier), October 29 – November 3, 2026. See the dated
[build record](BUILT_DURING_HACKATHON.md).

**Results page with live-repair replays:** https://rajoza8.github.io/servetune/ (built from the committed results by
`scripts/build_site.py`; it makes no API calls).

## Try it in five minutes (no GPU)

Needs Python 3.11 or later; there is nothing to install.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Rajoza8/servetune && cd servetune
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q
```

**A live Meta model call, with your own Meta Model API key:**

```sh
cp .env.example .env            # put your key after MODEL_API_KEY=
set -a; . ./.env; set +a        # load it into this shell (nothing reads .env automatically)
python3 -m servedoctor demo
```

The demo loads a real incident recorded on the GPU (a traffic surge, with a harmless decoy job running on the same
GPU), prints what the agent sees, sends that snapshot to **Muse Spark** (`muse-spark-1.3`) on the Meta Model API, and
prints the diagnosis, its evidence and the proposed fix. It then grades the reply against the sealed answer key, which
the model never sees, and shows what the threshold rules did on the same incident. One call uses about 3,000 input and
1,000 output tokens, roughly $0.01. The prompt hash, reply, token usage and cost are saved under `runs/demo/`; the key
never is. Options: `--model wonder` for Muse Wonder (`muse-wonder-1.0`), `--incident`, `--study-dir`, `--at` and
`--recorded`.

**The whole Hard set, live:** `python3 -m servedoctor demo --suite` sends all 15 recorded Hard-set incidents to Muse
Spark, four calls at a time (`--workers`), and prints each diagnosis as it arrives next to the sealed answer and what the
threshold rules did, then a tally scored by the benchmark's own scoring code. One call per incident, about $0.11 in all
for Spark (about $0.40 with `--model wonder`); the replies and costs are saved under `runs/demo/`. The two live suite
runs made while recording the demo video each scored 10 of 12 with zero harmful actions (the rules: 7 of 12, five
harmful); their records and a verifier are in [results/live-demo-20261104](results/live-demo-20261104/README.md).

**No key?** The same commands run in recorded mode and say so: they show the replies the model gave when the study was
evaluated (`--suite` then reproduces the published Spark and rules scoreboard rows). Every recorded reply, its token usage and cost are in `results/*/decisions/`. `.env` is git-ignored;

AI-assisted social campaigns for small businesses with no marketing history: product
in → Facebook and Instagram campaigns out → owner approves → publish/export → measure →

# DecideOnce

An MCP server that finds the decision and categorisation steps inside agent
workflows, records every decision the agent makes there (inputs, choice,
outcome), and then lets confident decisions skip the LLM call: hosted Jev
first, a private model only when the evidence demands it.

Decisions route through the **hosted Jev** tier (System One over OpenRouter or
TypeSafe) once a point reaches `shadow` (register with `remote_ok:
["hosted_jev"]` and `confirm: true`: points default to private): no training
step, just a temperature and threshold fitted automatically from the first
200 labelled shadow calls. The API
key arrives via `envsave` (`hosted_jev.key_ref`), lives only in server memory,
and every call counts against `hosted_jev.monthly_budget_usd`. `do_train` stays
locked until `do_report` says `train_recommended` (low coverage, a missed
margin, repeated drift, or heavy teacher-only options) — that is the point at
which a private LoRA earns its keep. Training runs on Fireworks: `do_train`
launches a smoke job first, then the paid full job once confirmed. There is
no local model path. The calling agent still does all the LLM
work (it analyses workflows and acts as the teacher). The hosted path above
is the default (`[decider] backend = "tiered"`, plus the key and a budget):
"promote to shadow" needs no training step.

## Built during the Meta AI Developer Hackathon

Everything in this repository was written during the hackathon (event 26 Oct – 4 Nov 2026; all code
written 1–4 Nov 2026), by one person (solo, Indie Developer track), with Meta's Muse Code coding agent. The
development history is 100+ commits from 1 to 4 Nov 2026; this public repository is a code-only export
of it, so it shows one commit per export.

**Built by us during the event**

- The DecideOnce MCP server (`decideonce/`):
  - decision core and store (`do_decide`, `do_record`, `do_outcome`)
  - discovery (`do_analyze`, `do_register`): rubric, text hints, agent-proposed candidates, a trace detector, and
    (built 3 Nov) a Python static detector, a check that the next step uses each answer, and evidence
    levels where 2 of 3 signals (text, code, traces) must agree (`decideonce/discovery/`)
  - shadow and serve gates: error bound, margin over random escalation, audits, drift detection, demotion (`do_promote`, `do_report`)
  - the hosted-Jev tier with automatic temperature and threshold fitting
  - the zero-edit gateway, one-turn runs and the autopilot (`autopilot.py`)
  - the training export for Fireworks (`fireworks_export.py`), the live Fireworks trainer
    (`fireworks_trainer.py`) with a test fake (`trainer.py`), and the scoring worker
    (`fireworks_worker.py`)
- The Muse plugin (`plugin/`) with two skills: `decideonce-workflow` for existing workflows and
  `decideonce-design` for new, decision-first workflows.
- For the demo video (kept in the private development repository):
  - the synthetic refund-ticket generator and its written policy
  - the live MCP demo

# Postor AI Bid Team

A multi-agent AI system that takes a small business from a public procurement
opportunity to an honest, evidence-backed answer: **bid here, bid with
conditions, don't bid, or let a human decide** — plus a first draft of the
technical proposal when bidding makes sense.

Built for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon (Startup track, _Build for Your
World_) with **five Meta models**, each with one job: **Muse Spark** reads,
judges and drafts, **Muse Wonder** audits the draft, **SAM 3.1** localizes
official marks on scanned pages, **Muse Voice Transcribe** lets the bid manager
answer open `[PENDING]` items by voice, and **Llama Prompt Guard 2 (86M)** —
Meta's open-weights prompt-injection classifier, self-hosted on **Modal** and
called by URL — screens every tender page before the agents read it, with Muse
Spark confirming what it flags.

### What Postor does

1. **Finds and reads the tender** — real Dominican public tenders (DGCP
   portal): pliego, amendments and official forms, never modified.
2. **Checks it against the company** — every requirement against the
   company's private _Company Brain_ (certifications with expiry dates,
   projects, finances, team), citing document + page.
3. **Decides honestly** — _GO / GO WITH CONDITIONS / NO GO / NEEDS REVIEW_,
   with financial ratios, revenue concentration and conditions with owner and
   deadline.
4. **Prepares the bid** — a technical proposal draft audited by a second
   model, the SNCC forms and the tender's own **F.033 economic offer with
   prices** (store and rate-card costs, ITBIS, total in words).
5. **Leaves the human in charge** — anything unproven stays `[PENDING]`; the
   bid manager can answer by voice. Postor never submits, signs or sends.

### Postor is a live product — Meta completes the flow

Postor is not a hackathon concept: it is a live, paid SaaS for Dominican
public procurement at **[postor.do](https://postor.do)**, already used by a
small number of paying customers (7-day trial, then US$49.99/month or
US$479.90/year, up to 5 users per company).

|                     | Postor before the hackathon ([postor.do](https://postor.do))                                  | Postor with Meta AI (this repository)                                                                                                                |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Find**            | Tenders from DGCP open data, filtered by the company's categories, institution and modality   | Same, plus the tender's own pliego, amendments and official forms read end to end                                                                    |
| **Understand**      | Pliego analysis: an overview of what the tender requires, with citations to document and page

# 🎲 GameSchooling **Homeschool, played as quests.** A Parent writes what each Child should learn. The Child proves it. Two Meta models check the proof. [**▶ Try the live demo**](https://gameschooling.web.id) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Meta models](#meta-models) · [Run it locally](#run-it-locally) ![TanStack Start](https://img.shields.io/badge/TanStack_Start-on_Cloudflare_Workers-F38020?logo=cloudflare&logoColor=white) ![D1 + R2](https://img.shields.io/badge/Storage-D1_%2B_R2-F38020?logo=cloudflare&logoColor=white) ![Meta Muse](https://img.shields.io/badge/Models-Muse_%C2%B7_SAM_3.1-0866FF?logo=meta&logoColor=white) ![shadcn/ui](https://img.shields.io/badge/UI-shadcn%2Fui_%2B_Tailwind-000000?logo=shadcnui&logoColor=white)
--- ## Why Homeschooling Parents know what their Children should learn. What they lack is time: turning a goal into daily tasks, checking every answer, and keeping a six-year-old and a ten-year-old motivated at once. GameSchooling takes the Parent's plain-language Plan and runs the loop for them, while the Parent stays the final judge. ## How it works ``` Parent writes a Plan ──▶ Make quests ──▶ Child plays a Quest ──▶ Child sends a Proof ▲ │ │ ▼ Parent Accepts / Rejects ◀── unsure or disagree ◀── Two judges reach a Verdict │ both pass ≥ 0.7 ──▶ Points ──▶ Rewards ``` 1. **Plan.** One free-text note per Child: what to learn, in which language, what to avoid, and which Rewards cost how many Points. Start from one of 47 **Starter Plans** (curriculum, faith, method and subject) for ages up to 18, then edit freely. 2. **Make quests.** One press turns the Plan into about five Quests, each with a cover, read aloud, a fixed Points value and one Proof kind. Progress streams to the screen as it happens. 3. **Guardian check.** Every Quest's text and cover prompt is checked for child safety before a Child sees it.
