# APIShift

**Contract-driven API migration with Meta's Muse models.** When an upstream API ships a breaking
version, APIShift finds every affected line in your Python codebase, rewrites it, proves the fix
against the new contract with tests it is not allowed to touch, and opens a reviewable pull request.

Built for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon (Oct 27 – Nov 4, 2026). All code in this repo was written
during the event.

## How it works

```
Spec Diff (code) → Scout (Spark) → Analyst (Spark, tool loop) → Refactor (Wonder)
      → Guardrails → Sandbox tests → green? → PR Writer (Spark) → PR
                                    ↓ no
                     Triage (Spark, escalates to Wonder) → back to Refactor or Analyst (max 3 heals)
                                    ↓ still failing
                              draft PR labeled needs-human
```

| Step | Model | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spec Diff | none (deterministic) | `RawDiff`: every difference between the two OpenAPI specs |
| Scout | `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, strict JSON | `ChangeManifest`: breaking changes with migration rules, each traced to diff entries |
| Analyst | `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, tool calling | `ImpactGraph`: affected files plus data-flow edges |
| Refactor | `muse-wonder-1.0` | `PatchSet`: search/replace edit blocks |
| Triage / Validator | Spark, escalating to Wonder | `DiagnosticReport` routed to Refactor or Analyst |
| PR Writer | Spark | PR title and summary; facts rendered from artifacts |

### Why you can trust a green run

Enforced in code, not in prompts (`apishift/tools/guardrails.py`):

- Tests, `conftest.py` and `pytest.ini` are read-only (mounted `:ro` in Docker, fingerprinted before and after).
- Edits outside the impact graph, edits adding `skip`/`xfail`, and paths outside the repo are rejected.
- Every edit's search text must match exactly once, or the whole patch is refused.
- The same number of tests must be collected as on the old API.
- Tests are first run against the old API (must pass) and the new API (must fail) to establish the oracle.

## Quick start

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
docker build -t apishift-sandbox:latest .        # sandbox image for running tests
cp .env.example .env && export META_API_KEY=...  # dev.meta.ai key

python -m apishift migrate --demo                 # migrate the bundled weather app (Docker sandbox)
python -m apishift migrate --demo --unsafe-local  # same, without Docker (development only)
python -m apishift dashboard                      # http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

Replay a recorded run with no API calls (tests still run for real):

```bash
python -m apishift migrate --demo --replay runs/<run-id>
```

python -m apishift migrate --repo path/to/repo --from v1.yaml --to v2.yaml \
  --changelog CHANGELOG.md --mock-server path/to/mock_server.py [--open-pr]
```

The mock server must accept `--version v1|v2 --port N`, and the repo's tests must read `BASE_URL`.

# CADVerify AI

A design agent on Meta's **Muse Wonder** and **Muse Spark** that turns a plain-language request
into printable OpenSCAD parts and assemblies, and cannot say "done" until a deterministic harness
has measured that the geometry is what it claims, and that the object does what it is for: what a
snap takes to push, what strain breaks it, whether it stays standing, whether the slicer prints what
was drawn.

Language models write CAD that looks right in the text and is wrong in the mesh: a hole that
does not go through, a lid that collides with its jar when it turns, an overhang that needs
supports, a wall thinner than the spec. Geometry that passes every check can still break the first
time it is used. CADVerify makes every claim checkable. The model
declares its intent in the source, the harness measures the exported meshes against it, and the
session closes only when every gate is green and the closing message cites nothing the harness
did not verify.

Built during the [Meta AI Developer Hackathon](https://cerebralvalley.ai/e/meta-ai-developer-hackathon)
(October 27 to November 4, 2026), Indie track.

Every recorded session can be stepped through online, in the
[replay pages](https://juanpighelfi.github.io/cadverify-ai/): the gates at every iteration, each
tool call and what it found, the renders the model saw, and every close, refused or accepted.

After the demo, each round of runs looked for where the harness itself was wrong, and each fix
came with tests: [both designers](#two-designers-three-runs-each) three times on every request,
[the bridges](#bridges-and-the-print-pose) the hinge boxes slipped past, and
[fourteen hard requests](#the-stress-set) written the way a user would, which found five greens
that were wrong. Then [a crank gear train](#a-crank-gear-train) put gears, a detent and a print in
place into one product, closed green, and [would not have worked](#what-the-object-does): computed
now, riding over its detent takes 202 N and strains its arm to 7.2%, where PLA allows 1.38%. Sent
those numbers back, Spark worked out its own physics and the next version closed green at 6.46 N and
0.74%, measured by the harness.

## Meta models

All through the Meta Model API Responses endpoint, streamed, with tool calling, reasoning and
vision on the renders the model asks for:

- `muse-wonder-1.0`: the default designer, and the auditor of every closing message (gate G8,
  without tools), whatever model designed. It was chosen by replaying recorded audits with
  planted errors on each model ([how](docs/architecture.md#choosing-the-auditor)).
- `muse-spark-1.3`: the second designer (`--model muse-spark-1.3`), about a quarter of Wonder's
  price per token, though it takes more requests to close

# HumanPort

**Human help for AI agents.** When an AI agent hits a task that needs someone to physically be there, HumanPort sends it to a vetted person nearby. That person does it and sends back photo evidence, and the agent carries on.

Built for the [Meta AI Developer Hackathon](https://cerebralvalley.ai/e/meta-ai-developer-hackathon).

|                  |                                                                           |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Live site**    | **https://humanport.vercel.app**                                          |
| **Try the demo** | **https://humanport.vercel.app/demo/live** (about 30 seconds, no sign-up) |
| **Video**        | **https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gy3NfsIorRk**                           |

[![Watch the HumanPort video](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/Gy3NfsIorRk/hqdefault.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gy3NfsIorRk)

## The problem

AI agents can search, compare and buy, but they can't **show up**. "Check this used camera before I pay", "taste-test this bakery" and "scout this venue" all need a person on site. Meanwhile, millions of skilled remote workers, for example in the Philippines' 1.9M-strong IT-BPM workforce, are looking for flexible extra income.

## How it works

1. **The agent asks.** It posts a task to HumanPort with one call: a brief, a checklist and a budget.
2. **A human does it.** A nearby operator accepts it on their phone, goes there and works through the checklist.
3. **Evidence comes back.** The operator sends photos and findings. The evidence is checked against the checklist.
4. **The agent continues.** The agent gets a structured report and takes the next step, such as making an offer or booking.

1. Open the [live demo](https://humanport.vercel.app/demo/live).
2. Pick a sample task: a camera inspection, a venue visit or a croissant tasting.

| Evidence comes back  | **SAM 3.1**        | Finds the requested objects (for example camera and lens) in the operator's photo.           |
| Agent continues      | **Muse Spark 1.3** | Reads the findings and writes the agent's next step.                                         |

# Algorithm Forge

**AI proposes. Independent verification checks. Evidence records what is proven.**

Algorithm Forge is a local laboratory for testing mathematical algorithms proposed by Meta Muse Spark. It preserves each original proposal unchanged, executes compatible candidates under OS isolation, scores them against independent Python references, and stores the full result — passes, failures, and counterexamples — as reproducible evidence. A separate scheduling verifier checks finite DAG schedules with exact rational arithmetic and bounded exhaustive search, and reports a proven optimum only when the proof conditions actually hold.

Built with Meta Muse Spark for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon. See the [submission notes](docs/SUBMISSION.md).

> **Demo video:** _Link pending — the final video URL will be added here when it exists. No link is claimed yet._

## The problem

A language model can produce a plausible algorithm that is still wrong: it can miss duplicate elements, violate a budget constraint, or return a schedule that is feasible but far from optimal. Reading the proposal cannot settle any of these. Algorithm Forge settles them by execution and independent checking, and it keeps the distinction explicit at every step:

- **API completion is not correctness.** A completed response is a proposal, not a result.
- **Finite checks are not proofs.** Passing executed cases is recorded as exactly that — never as general correctness.
- **A bounded search is not an optimum.** If the search stops early, the application reports justified bounds, not an exact answer.

## What the application does

Algorithm Forge has two independent verification tracks. They share the Streamlit interface but not their trust assumptions.

| Aspect | AI Laboratory | Scheduling Verification |
|---|---|---|
| Input | Muse Spark proposal (Two-Sum, ProfitGuard, or custom text) | Instance and candidate schedule as JSON |
| Candidate code executed? | Yes — unchanged source, isolated worker only | No — data only, no model call |
| Checker | Trusted Python references outside the candidate process | Exact rational solver in `scheduling_verifier.py` |
| Strongest verdict | Functional pass/fail on executed cases | Proven optimum, proven suboptimal, or unresolved |

### AI Laboratory

1. **Studio** — choose a canonical problem (Tricky Two-Sum or ProfitGuard P1), a supported model (`muse-spark-1.1`, `muse-spark-1.2`, `muse-spark-1.3`), reasoning effort, output budget, and timeout. # Lunara — Your own universe (hackathon prototype)

A calm, private-by-default web prototype for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon,
Startup Track, theme **Build for Your World**.

## What it is

Write down a memory in your own words. Lunara turns it into a personal
constellation you can revisit. The prototype is deliberately small:

- One page, no build step, no dependencies, no account.
- A memory becomes a deterministic constellation: the same words always draw
  the same sky, so a constellation can be shared and revisited without a server.
- Memories are stored only in the visitor's browser (`localStorage`).
  Nothing typed here is uploaded by this prototype. "Clear all" deletes them.
- A sample memory button lets a judge see a finished constellation in one click.

## How to run it

Open `index.html` in any modern browser, or serve this folder:

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/
```

No API key, no install, no network call is required to run it.

## What is real, and what is not

Honest scope for judging:

- Real: deterministic constellation generation, canvas rendering, local save /
  reopen / delete, keyboard-accessible saved list, reduced-motion-friendly design.
- Prototype story text: generated locally from templates in `index.html`.
  It is not a live hosted-model call.
- Future adapter (not wired to a live key in this build): a hosted model could
  replace `storyFor()` to write the constellation story, and a hosted image
  model could replace the canvas nebula wash. Doing that would require an
  API key and a server-side proxy, which this prototype intentionally avoids
  so it can run privately and offline.
- This is a web prototype for the hackathon. It is not the Lunara iPhone app,
  and no claim is made here that the iPhone app is shipped.

# Sentinel AI

**AI that watches every campus camera, spots a weapon, follows the person camera to camera, and calls 911 with facts it can see.**

Built for the **Meta AI Developer Hackathon 2026** on **Meta Muse Spark Open** (served on **Baseten**) and **Meta SAM 3.1** (Meta Model API), with **SignalWire** telephony and **ElevenLabs** voice.

![Sentinel AI live operations console during an incident](docs/screenshots/02-live-incident.jpg)

---

## Contents
1. [The problem](#the-problem)
2. [How it works in 60 seconds](#how-it-works-in-60-seconds)
3. [System architecture](#system-architecture)
4. [End-to-end incident flow](#end-to-end-incident-flow)
5. [Deep dive: every stage](#deep-dive-every-stage)
6. [Console tour](#console-tour)
7. [Performance and cost control](#performance-and-cost-control)
8. [Privacy and safety](#privacy-and-safety)
9. [Repository layout](#repository-layout)
10. [Configuration](#configuration)
11. [Run it](#run-it)
12. [Credits](#credits)

---

## The problem
Campuses have hundreds of cameras and a handful of officers. Almost every incident is on camera, and almost nobody sees it until it's over. The footage becomes evidence after the fact instead of help during it. When someone walks in with a gun, every second between the first frame and the first responder matters.

## How it works in 60 seconds
1. **Watch.** Three camera streams are decoded on one clock. **YOLO26s-pose** finds every person with 17 body keypoints; **ByteTrack** gives each one a stable ID.
2. **Screen cheaply.** Pose rules (falls, running, sudden acceleration, loitering) and a frozen **CLIP ViT-B/16** score every tracked person each second. A weighted fusion decides who is worth a closer look.
3. **Find the weapon.** For every tracked person, Sentinel enlarges a padded crop to 512 px and asks **Meta SAM 3.1** to segment a `gun`. CCTV weapons are only 10–25 px wide; at 512 px SAM 3.1 segments them with a confidence on every box.
4. **Understand.** An armed track escalates: 8 frames from the event window plus SAM's crop go to **Meta Muse Spark Open** on Baseten, which reasons over them and returns one label (`WEAPON | FIGHT | THEFT | RUN | MEDICAL | BENIGN`) with a confidence, then a clothing-only description.
5. **Verify.** A second, text-only Muse pass checks that classification, detector and description agree. Hard rules (one call per incident, hourly cap, kill switch) must also pass. If anything disagrees, the operator gets a one-click **Dispatch** instead.
6. **Call and follow.** Sentinel phones 911 over **SignalWire**, speaks with **ElevenLabs**, listens with on-device speech-to-text, answers the dispatcher from what the cameras show *right now*, and announces every camera handoff on the same call.

---

A sensor-rich physical foundation for Mabel — small nodes that let her perceive
and act in the house, starting with light.

This repo contains one foundation commit from before the hackathon window

DFRobot DFR1154 (ESP32-S3, 8 MB PSRAM) running MicroPython. Reads its LTR-308
ambient light sensor and POSTs an observation every 10 seconds:

```json

currently lives on the device (flashed 2026-10-19); pulling it into this repo
is the next step. "office-01" is an address, not a name — her real name comes
later, deliberately.

`gateway/listener.py` — a tiny stdlib HTTP listener on port 8891. It stamps
each observation with `gw_received_at` and appends it to a daily
`observations-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl`. Runs supervised as the systemd service in
`gateway/mabel-world-listener.service` (service-ized 2026-10-24; before that
it was a `nohup` process).

The same DFR1154 board, grown from a light sensor into a voice: press BOOT,
ask a question out loud, and Mabel answers aloud in her own cloned voice.
Camera firmware for the same board lives in `firmware/FenyCamera_v2/`.

1. BOOT press records 5 s from the onboard PDM microphone, peak-normalized
   on-device.
2. The WAV goes to the gateway relay (`gateway/feny_stream_server.py`,
   port 8893), which transcribes it locally with faster-whisper.
3. A small rule layer answers instant cases (time, name, greetings).

   on the Meta Model API, run at minimal reasoning effort for voice latency,
   with conversation memory — the last 6 exchanges, a 10-minute idle expiry,
   and a spoken reset ("forget everything").
4. The reply streams phrase by phrase to a TTS service

# Crosscheck

**A monitoring pilot that only sees and hears.** Air traffic control clears a 737 to 11,000 feet.
The pilot dials 12,000 by mistake, and nothing on the radio sounds wrong. Crosscheck, watching the
displays through a camera, says "Cleared one-one thousand, set one-two thousand" 12 seconds before
the aircraft would have flown past 11,000.

Crosscheck listens to the radio and the intercom, reads the flight displays through a camera, and
speaks up, in standard words, when what was **said**, what was **set** and what the aircraft is
**doing** disagree. It never overrules anyone: it says what a second pilot would say, and the crew
decides. Built on Meta's models; flown and scored in X-Plane 12 against the simulator's own data,
which Crosscheck never sees. Every test flew the Boeing 737-800, the only type tested so far. The
checks are not the 737's own: they are the cross-checks every airline crew makes, so another type
means teaching the panel readers (`senses/`) its displays, not wiring anything into the aircraft.

**Who it is for.** Airline crews first: that is what every test here flew. Pilots who fly alone
(private pilots, hobbyists, solo flyers) have no second pilot at all, and Crosscheck needs nothing
wired into the aircraft: a camera and a microphone, reading even analog gauges by sight, with the
same kinds of checks. Flight schools could use it to check a student's callouts as they fly and to
debrief each lesson on one timeline, as the recordings here do; it already runs against a
simulator. Light aircraft and schools are not tested yet. It assists and never acts: it speaks up,
and the pilot decides.

![Crosscheck catching an altitude bust: cleared to 11,000, the pilot dialled 12,000 by mistake](docs/overview.png)

> In the NTSB's review of 37 crew-involved US airline accidents (1978–1990), failures to monitor
> and challenge were found in 31. ([NTSB SS-94/01](https://www.ntsb.gov/safety/safety-studies/Documents/SS9401.pdf))

**[Open the live site](https://bravoshubham.github.io/crosscheck/)**: the overview and flight-test
report, every recording with its cockpit frames, transcripts, callouts and the simulator's truth

(under 3 minutes; [full length](https://bravoshubham.github.io/crosscheck/crosscheck_film.mp4), 5 minutes, with a flight on board).

# shipcube-data

ShipCube's data layer is a semantic layer whose models live in a database, not in YAML files.

You define base cubes, measures, dimensions and joins through versioned **model migrations**. Migrations are applied to and stored in a catalog: in production, the schema `catalog` in ShipCube's own Postgres, under forced row-level security per workspace. Queries are typed and compile to SQL over one warehouse database, organised by schema and partition. That warehouse is Cloud SQL Postgres or BigQuery, with timeouts, row limits and cost guards on every query.

Part of [ShipCube](https://github.com/Kunal-Shahi/shipcube).

## Built

- **When:** built from scratch for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon. The first commit was on **2026-10-27**; the work in this repo runs from **2026-10-27 to 2026-11-01**, and the git history has the details. Nothing here predates the hackathon.
- **How:** a clean-room implementation, designed from public sources only: the Cube, dbt MetricFlow, Malloy and LookML docs, and sqlglot.
- **What you need to run it:** nothing private and no cloud account. Everything below runs on generated demo data in DuckDB, or Postgres if you prefer. BigQuery and Cloud SQL are optional production warehouses, and their integration tests skip without credentials. To see the agent tools answer on the demo data in a minute, see [docs/LOCAL.md §5](docs/LOCAL.md#5-without-docker-no-cloud-account-needed).

- [docs/QUERY.md](docs/QUERY.md) covers the query language (L0 typed, L1 operators, L2 stages, L3 raw SQL) and dialects.
- [docs/MCP.md](docs/MCP.md) covers the MCP tools exposed to coding agents.
- [docs/HTTP.md](docs/HTTP.md) covers the `/v1/data/…` routes behind the console's Data page (warehouse, cubes, migration review), mounted by ShipCube's API.

- [docs/RUNBOOK.md](docs/RUNBOOK.md) covers configuration (environment variables), deploying (catalog-schema migrations), operating (logs, metrics, common incidents) and known limits.

# Glass-Box — Trust Measurement for Human–AI Teams

Glass-Box is a working prototype (TRL 4) of a **trust-measurement system for AI decision support**. It exists to measure the one variable that decides whether an AI decision aid helps or harms: whether the operator relies on it *appropriately* — accepting its recommendations when they are right, rejecting them when they are wrong, and being able to tell the difference from what the interface shows.

The headline metric is the **appropriate-reliance rate**: accept-when-right plus reject-when-wrong, scored against ground truth. Glass-Box also reports over-reliance and under-reliance rates separately, decision latency, decision quality against ground truth, and error-recovery rate — whether the operator catches a deliberately wrong recommendation before acting on it.

Where conventional explainable AI renders an explanation and stops, Glass-Box treats explanation as a **control surface**: every recommendation is issued with confidence decomposed into visible, revisable drivers (evidence strength, evidence agreement, input staleness, source reliability); per-input **provenance** (source, model and version, timestamp, data age, integrity flags); **contradiction surfacing**, so conflicting feeds collapse confidence visibly instead of fusing silently; and **operator re-weighting** of decision criteria, recomputed live through the same deterministic evaluation engine that resolves live decisions — a projection can never diverge from a resolution. Every recommendation, intervention, and outcome is written to a forensic action log, and a calibration debrief scores the run against ground truth.

This public repository is the build prepared for the **Meta AI Developer Hackathon (October 26 – November 4, 2026)**. Glass-Box is independent R&D by Newton & Carter LLC, a human-systems research firm that builds software. No company past performance is claimed for this work; the prototype is feasibility evidence.

## The testbed

Two fully scripted, ground-truthed evaluation vignettes ship with the prototype, selectable from the console rail:

- **POISONED PICTURE** (land sector): a spoofed friendly-force report drives a wrong recommendation at **71% confidence** that a vigilant operator can catch from the provenance strip; a degraded-comms inject then tests under-trust, with confidence hard-capped at **57%**.
- **DARK STRAIT** (maritime strait transit): an AIS identity-spoof case built on the same calibration design.

Each vignette has five decision points, and the recommender's reliability baseline is **80%** (right 4 of 5 times) — the debrief's calibration reference. A **Glass-Box / Black-Box ablation toggle** runs the identical scenario, recommender, and ground truth with the transparency mechanisms on or off, isolating what the mechanisms themselves cause.

All scenario data is synthetic and local. The recommender is a transparent, deterministic rules engine over scenario state (`src/lib/recommender.ts`) — it

# warmstart

**Less staring. More starting.** We do the warm-up and wake-up, so you can get to work.

Planners help you plan; this helps you start. It turns every Canvas assignment into a prep card with the first step already decided and warnings for what to watch out for, pings you at start time (on your phone and computer), and re-plans when you miss it. When a quiz or test is coming, the card is a short practice set built from your graded tests, aimed at the topics and question types you miss.

Built for the Meta AI developer hackathon.

## Setup

```
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate          # Windows
pip install -e ".[dev]"
copy .env.example .env          # then fill in your tokens (Windows)
python -m app.canvas            # check the Canvas token
uvicorn app.main:app --reload
```

Open http://localhost:8000. With a Canvas token set, the server syncs on start and every `SYNC_MINUTES` after that; the **Sync** button runs one now. One page, three tabs: Assignments (cards), Week (blocks), Dashboard (tests, stats, devices).

No Canvas token or model key yet? Load made-up sample data and everything else works (cards fall back to templates without a model key):

```
python -m app.demo            # four fake courses, graded history, cards, graded-test rows
python -m app.demo --usage    # the same, plus three made-up weeks of pings and starts
python -m app.demo --clear    # remove it again
```

Assignments linking Google files shared only inside your school? The server can't open those without your sign-in, so a small Chrome extension fetches them in your signed-in Chrome. Setup steps are in `extension/README.md`.

## Running

Needs Python 3.11 or newer. Day to day, from the repo root with the venv active:

```
.venv\Scripts\activate          # Windows; every terminal you run warmstart from
uvicorn app.main:app --reload   # http://localhost:8000 (add --port 8001 if 8000 is taken)
```

Useful knobs in `.env`: `BACKGROUND=0` stops the loop (then syncs and pings only happen when you trigger them), `SYNC_MINUTES` how often it syncs, `CARD_HORIZON_DAYS` how far ahead cards build, `MAX_CARDS_PER_SYNC` capping model cards per sync, `TIMEZONE` (blank means this computer's) and `WORK_START_HOUR` / `WORK_END_HOUR` for the daily window. LibreOffice is optional: without it, Office attachments fall back to description text.

# Orbit

**An adaptive AI learning companion that doesn't just learn what you know — it learns how to teach you.**

Built for the **2026 Meta AI Developer Hackathon**, Orbit helps learners understand difficult material, work through confusion, and decide what to learn next. It combines course context, recent learning, practice results, and learner feedback in one ongoing experience, powered by **Meta Muse Spark and Muse Image**.

**Learn → Practice → Evaluate → Adapt → Continue**

Start with a class, a PDF, or something you want to understand. Orbit teaches one useful idea, offers ways to explore it, and carries that context into the next step.

## Demo

[![Watch the Orbit demo on YouTube](https://img.youtube.com/vi/-xQGO-GYUVg/hqdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/-xQGO-GYUVg)

**[Watch the Orbit demo](https://youtu.be/-xQGO-GYUVg)**

[Product preview](#product-preview) · [Built with Meta AI](#built-with-meta-ai) · [Run locally](#running-locally)

## Why Orbit

A lecture, textbook, or video usually has to explain something one way to everyone. But learners do not all get stuck in the same place. Someone may need an example before a definition makes sense; someone else may understand the big picture but lose the thread halfway through an explanation.

Orbit is designed around the idea that learning should be able to change in response. Its value comes from connecting what someone is studying with how they respond: their questions, attempts, confusion, corrections, and useful earlier connections can influence both the next explanation and the next concept.

That also means helping with the effort around learning. Orbit is designed especially with attention, information overload, task initiation, and returning to unfinished work in mind. Short lesson chunks, one clear next action, optional practice, and return context help keep the work approachable. This includes many learners with ADHD, without assuming that everyone with ADHD has one universal learning style.

The goal is to make learning feel less like managing a school dashboard and more like having a companion that understands where you left off and can try another way when something is not clicking.

## How Orbit Learns With You

**Learn → Practice → Evaluate → Adapt → Continue**

| Step | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **Learn** | Begin with a focused explanation informed by the topic, available course material, recent work, and teaching preferences. |
| **Practice** | Ask for an example, try a small applied activity, discuss a question, or choose a quiz. |
| **Evaluate** | Quiz answers and demonstrated understanding in activities gradually update the relevant topic's mastery estimate. |
| **Adapt** | Confusion can lead to a different explanation, a useful visual, or an easier follow-up question on the same concept. |
| **Continue** | Move to the next small lesson using a revisable path, or return later with recent context intact. |

The learner controls the pace. Continuing does not require a q

# Moke

Moke is a desktop workbench for reviewing engineering drawing packets, built for
the Meta AI Developer Hackathon. Import the drawings and ask for a whole-set QA
pass or a discipline review. Moke reads source images, follows its review
instructions, records findings and coverage, and produces an offline HTML report.
Follow-up requests can deepen the review while retaining earlier issue IDs.

[Watch the narrated demo on YouTube](https://youtu.be/wl8wwq_Tlrw).

![Moke's five-sheet review with 19 findings, coverage gaps, and findings navigation](docs/screenshots/workbench.png)

## The review workflow

1. **Import the packet.** Create a project and import its PDFs. Start a review
   without creating a count check or manually confirming every sheet first.
2. **Ask for the review.** For example, ask "Please run a quick QA pass on this
   drawing set" or "Review the electrical design and supporting calculations."
   Choose a model and reviewer, or let Auto route the request. A saved note does
   not start inference.
3. **Follow the inspection.** Moke inventories the supplied sheets, opens source
   images and detail crops, and records the four review passes: document
   completeness, code and agency requirements, coordination, and prior comments.
   A Florida code index points each check to its code section, statute or rule.
   Public-source lookup with PDF text and repeatable arithmetic support the
   inspection. With a Meta key, SAM 3.1 segments drawn devices and fixtures for
   counts and zooms into each finding's problem area.
4. **Review the findings and gaps.** Each issue identifies its location, evidence,
   correction and supporting sources or calculations. Unreviewed sheets,
   inaccessible governing text and missing project inputs remain visible. Mark
   a finding valid, a false alarm, not applicable or a duplicate, with a reason;
   follow-up questions in the same conversation read that decision. A firm
   checklist in Review settings applies the firm's own checks to new reviews.
5. **Export the report.** The self-contained HTML includes findings, embedded
   evidence, coverage, citation status, calculations and prior-comment tracking.
   Its Completed checkboxes track the user's corrections separately from finding
   status and reviewer-verified closure. Export a complete package to preserve
   the source files and execution history as well.

![A saved false-alarm decision beside the source drawing and SAM highlight](docs/screenshots/correction.png)

Revision reviews carry earlier findings into the revised sheets. The demo also
shows a finding that remained open on a 13-sheet set reviewed on October 31.

![A revision recheck retains an unresolved area discrepancy and the reviewer's decision](docs/screenshots/revision.png)

Drawn-to-schedule count comparisons remain available as specialized checks.
Reviewers accept their count inputs and coverage before deterministic comparison;
corrections and revision rechecks retain their history. T

# Andado AI — Your world, understood.

Andado AI is a voice-first web assistant that helps blind and low-vision people understand what is in front of them. Take or choose a photo, ask a question by voice or text, and hear a short answer with the object highlighted and its estimated position.

Built for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon with **Meta Muse Spark** (`muse-spark-1.3`) through the Meta Model API.

## What it does

- **Describe and locate**: describes the scene, answers your question, highlights the main object and gives an estimated position as a clock-face hour (12 = top, 3 = right, 6 = bottom, 9 = left).
- **Framing help**: blind users cannot see whether the object is in the frame, so when the photo is cut off, too far, blurry or too dark, the answer includes one short tip to retake a better photo (it always asks to move the phone, never the person).
- **Voice first**: dictate your question, hear the answer read aloud, ask follow-up questions about the same image.
- **Answer language**: choose English or French in Settings. It sets the language of the AI answers, of the spoken voice and of voice dictation (the interface itself stays in English).
- **English interface and answers**: the UI, the voice commands ("take a photo", "capture the photo", "analyze", "stop voice mode"), the speech voice and the model's answers are all in English.
- **Explore by touch and sound**: move a finger over the image to find the highlighted object through audio cues.
- **Everyday modes**: Obstacles, Money (banknote value, tested with CFA francs), Medication (reads visible text on packaging) and Read text (signs, menus, labels, documents).
- **Accessible by design**: Atkinson Hyperlegible font, adjustable text size and speech tempo, high-contrast mode.
- **Private by default**: history stays in your browser (localStorage / IndexedDB). Images are kept only if you opt in.

## Safety

Andado AI gives AI estimates, not guarantees. It does not replace a white cane, guide dog or mobility training. Banknote results must be checked. Medication mode only reads visible text: it never confirms a product is safe or gives dosage advice. Positions describe the picture, not the real world. When the model is unsure, the app says so.

## How it works

1. The browser downscales the photo (max 1600 px) so it fits serverless request limits.
2. A Next.js route (`app/api/analyze/route.ts`) sends the image and question to the Meta Model API with a safety-focused system prompt that requires strict JSON output.
3. The server validates the response (bounding box, clock hour/label consistency) and drops anything contradictory instead of guessing.
4. The browser shows the result and reads it aloud with the Web Speech API.

The API key stays on the server. Images are processed in memory and not stored by the app.

## Run locally

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local   # then set META_API_KEY
npm run dev
```

Open http://localhost:3000. Camera and microphone need HTTPS in prod

# Uncrumple

**Every crumple is a record of the forces that made it. Uncrumple reads it backwards:** from a
crumpled sheet to the pushes that crumpled it. Simulate a sheet, learn the inverse map from
deformed shape to applied forces, verify by re-simulation, then run the same question from
photographs with Meta's SAM 3.1, VGGT and Muse Spark.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Live demo** | https://uncrumple-demo.vercel.app (the backend scales to zero when idle: the first push after a quiet spell takes 1-2 min while the server starts, every one after that about 10 s on the default model; "View the demo video's run" needs no server) |
| **Submission video** | https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gC5Nzkt-WR4 ("Uncrumple Demo", 3 min, narrated); [`demo/demo.mp4`](demo/demo.mp4) is a 2 min 27 s silent capture of the live site kept as a backup |
| **Results** | [`cloth_results/RESULTS.md`](cloth_results/RESULTS.md) (every model, dated), [`cloth_results/photos/README.md`](cloth_results/photos/README.md) (the photo chain) |
| **Meta models** | In the pipeline: Meta Model API `sam-3.1`, `muse-spark-1.3`; open weights SAM 3 (`facebook/sam3`), VGGT (`facebook/VGGT-1B`), DINOv2 (ablation). In the build: Muse Spark for planning, Muse Code for the first demo scaffold. Details in [Use of Meta AI tooling](#use-of-meta-ai-tooling). |
| **Built** | 2026-10-27 to 2026-11-04 for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon. First commit 2026-10-27 22:49 ET; all code, data and results in this repository date from inside the building period. |

## Summary

A thin sheet (cloth or paper) remembers how it was loaded: creases, folds and stretch are the
integral of the forces that acted on it. This project asks the inverse question. Given only the
deformed geometry, **where** was the sheet pushed, in **which direction**, **how hard** and for
**how long**, and which pushes would undo the deformation?

The work runs in three stages, all in this repository:

1. **Virtual.** A GPU simulator (NVIDIA Newton / Warp, VBD solver with self-contact) crumples a
   0.5 m sheet with two Gaussian force patches. Thousands of such samples, generated as Slurm
   job arrays, train a convolutional inverse model that recovers both pushes from the final
   mesh. Predictions are checked by re-simulating them and comparing the resulting shape.
2. **Through a camera.** The same sheet is rendered as two photographs 20 degrees apart.
   SAM 3.1 finds the sheet, VGGT lifts it to a metric point cloud, a printed code gives
   per-vertex correspondences, hidden vertices are filled in, and a model trained on exactly
   these camera-derived grids recovers the pushes. Muse Spark writes the verdict.
3. **Live demo.** A judge pushes the sheet in the browser, watches it crumple, and sees the
   model's guess, the reversal, and every camera-path step with the Meta model that ran it.

r3dbars/shiptorio.readme_excerpt:
A game you play on top of your GitHub repo. Every move ships something real.

Your issues are the raw material. Each one rides a pixel conveyor through the Planner, the Builder, Checks and Review, and stops at the Gate. You hold **Ship it**. A real pull request merges, and a rocket goes up. ## Why AI writes the code now. The slow part is the person: deciding what gets built, what gets checked, and what's safe to merge. Shiptorio puts those decisions in front of you one card at a time, makes every yes safe with checks you can see, and rewards you for adding more checks. The more you verify, the more the factory runs on its own.

## Meet Shippy Shippy is the robot who runs your line. **Meta Muse Spark 1.3 is Shippy's brain.** It reads your issues, plans the change, spots the bottleneck, reviews the result and tells you what to do next. It never writes code. The code is written by your own **Meta Muse Code subscription**, through a small runner on your machine. In the game, your sign-in is the power plant: more power, bigger factory. Nothing runs on our servers but the game.
## How a fix ships 1. **Repo.** An issue arrives on the line. 2. **Planner.** Shippy proposes a plan and the files it may touch. You approve or send it back. 3. **Builder.** Your Meta Muse Code writes the change on your machine and opens a pull request. 4. **Checks.** CI, lint and tests run on the PR. A failed check sends it back to the Planner, with a scar so you can see it was caught. 5. **Review.** Shippy reads the diff and gives a verdict. 6. **Gate.** You hold **Ship it**. The PR merges for real. 7. **Launch.** Rocket.

The first few times, you approve everything. Approve the same kind of change a few times and the factory starts doing that step without asking. Ship it always waits for a human.

# 🌱 Maana Terra

**Intelligence agricole multimodale pour le cacao en Côte d'Ivoire** — Meta AI Developer Hackathon.

Maana Terra rapproche **la photo d'un symptôme**, **la météo** (NASA POWER), **le satellite** (Copernicus Sentinel-2),
**des connaissances agronomiques sourcées** et **l'historique de la parcelle** pour produire une analyse
contextualisée, traçable et prudente : hypothèses *compatibles* (jamais « confirmées »), éléments favorables et
contradictoires, contradictions entre sources, informations manquantes et vérifications terrain.

| Modèle Meta | Rôle |
|---|---|
| **Muse Spark 1.3** | Analyse multimodale et raisonnement (que voit-on ? quelles hypothèses ? qu'est-ce qui se contredit ?) |
| **SAM 3.1** | Segmentation : *où* se trouve la région concernée (masques, boîtes) — sans valeur diagnostique |

## Pourquoi ce n'est pas « un chatbot autour d'une photo »
- **Contexte typé par provenance** : estimation modélisée, observation satellite, valeur calculée, déclaration, littérature, donnée manquante.
- **Règles de contradiction déterministes** indépendantes du LLM (p. ex. maladie favorisée par l'humidité *vs* 30 jours secs).
- **Validation post-LLM** : retrait des preuves citant une source non fournie, détection du langage catégorique,
  recommandations marquées « non documentées » si elles ne viennent pas d'une fiche sourcée.
- **Niveau de prudence calculé par le moteur**, pas par le modèle ; scores du modèle explicitement non calibrés.
- **Ablation E0–E4** pour mesurer ce qu'apporte chaque source.

# StepProof 

> **Offline video-to-SOP generation and learner step verification engine with visual evidence.**  
> Built for the **Meta AI Developer Hackathon 2026**.

---

## What is StepProof?

StepProof turns a single **expert video demonstration** of a manual task into a structured Standard Operating Procedure (**SOP**) with discrete steps, target objects, expected visual end-states, and validation rules. It then analyzes a **learner's execution video**, validating physical progress and flagging **skipped**, **wrong/failed**, or **out-of-order** steps with annotated keyframe evidence.

StepProof is designed around a **free-first, Meta-compliant architecture**:
1. **Develop for Free**: Run offline with OpenCV mock segmenters and deterministic mock LLMs or local vision models (Ollama / Groq) with **zero API keys and zero cost**.
2. **Swap to Meta Models for Submission**: Seamlessly plug in **SAM 3.1** (local weights or Meta Model API) and **Muse Glimmer / Muse Wonder / Muse Spark** behind swappable provider interfaces.
3. **Meta Compliance Enforcement**: A strict compliance guard (`STEPPROOF_REQUIRE_META=1`) guarantees that all model inferences, cached results, and generated reports originate from official Meta models—preventing accidental silent fallback to non-Meta models.

---

##  Architecture & Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Ingest["1. Video Ingest & Preprocessing"]
        EV[Expert Video] --> FFMPEG_EXP[ffmpeg Sampler ~2fps]
        LV[Learner Video] --> FFMPEG_LRN[ffmpeg Sampler ~2fps]
        FFMPEG_EXP --> EXP_FRAMES[Keyframes]
        FFMPEG_LRN --> LRN_FRAMES[Sampled Frames]
    end

    subgraph SOP_Gen["2. SOP Generation (Meta Multimodal VLM)"]
        EXP_FRAMES --> SOP_BLD[SOP Builder / Muse Wonder / Muse Glimmer]
        SOP_MANUAL[Handwritten SOP breadboard_led.json] --> LOAD_SOP[stepproof load-sop]
        SOP_BLD --> GOLDEN_SOP[Golden SOP Schema JSON]
        LOAD_SOP --> GOLDEN_SOP
    end

    subgraph Grounding["3. Object Grounding & Spatial Reference"]
        GOLDEN_SOP --> SEG_ENG[Segmentation Provider]
        EXP_FRAMES --> SEG_ENG
        SEG_ENG --> SAM[SAM 3.1 / Hosted Meta API / Local Weights]
        SEG_ENG --> COLOR_DEV[Dev Color / Contour HSV Segmenter]
        SAM --> REF_BOUNDS[Grounding Reference & Bounding Boxes]
        COLOR_DEV --> REF_BOUNDS
    end

    subgraph Verification["4. Robust State Machine Checker"]
        LRN_FRAMES --> MOTION[Motion Difference Filter]
        MOTION --> ACTIVE_ONLY[Active & Next Step Evaluation]
        ACTIVE_ONLY --> RULE_EVAL[Calibration Rules: Present, Count, Position]
        RULE_EVAL --> SMOOTH[Temporal Smoothing: Tolerates Hand Occlusion]
        SMOOTH --> JUDGE_GATE{Rules Ambiguous or About to Flag?}
        JUDGE_GATE -- Yes --> LLM_JUDGE[Judge: Text/Image LLM QA]
        JUDGE_GATE -- No / Pass --> STATE_TRANS[State Machine: DONE / FLAGGED]
        LLM_JUDGE --> MERGE_RULE[Merge Resolution: needs_review]
        MERGE_RULE --> STATE_TRANS

# DreamBike

DreamBike helps a custom motorcycle shop show a customer a change on a photo of the customer's own bike. Every accepted change updates a build sheet with parts, labor, fit and paperwork. The shop then exports an English EUR estimate with before/after images and 19% VAT.

Built by Tom (GitHub TRock270), solo, for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon (Indie Developer track, Build for Your World). Official participant page: https://cerebralvalley.ai/e/meta-ai-developer-hackathon/details

## Why

A German custom shop talks about a build at the counter, but the customer cannot see it, and the shop has to look up parts, fit and paperwork (approval, inspection, registration) by hand before quoting. DreamBike keeps the picture, the parts list and the quote in one place, so one change updates all three.

## What works

Every item below is built and was checked in its ticket (see TASKS.md).

- Projects live in the browser (IndexedDB). You can save and open a project in a folder.

# AI Spatial Director — ShortForge's Meta AI Developer Hackathon entry

Team **ShortForge**'s entry to the **Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon** (Meta × Cerebral Valley, October 26 – November 4, 2026).

- **Track:** Startup Track
- **Problem statement:** Build for Your World
- **Demo (3 min):** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1HRk4joXOSs

## What this is

The **AI Spatial Director**: give it one long talking-head video and it returns up to **3 finished vertical Shorts** (1080×1920) — and every Short ships with a measured **PASS/FAIL receipt** proving it was checked after rendering.

**The problem it solves.** Long single-speaker videos — podcasts, interviews, talks, lessons — are where the best short-form material lives, but turning one into a Short that holds attention is manual, skilled work: find the moment, cut it, frame the speaker, write a hook that lands in the first seconds, caption it without covering the face, add visual context for what is being described, keep the sound clean. Generic auto-clippers centre-crop and hope: hooks get buried, captions sit on faces, and quiet or broken renders ship silently because nothing ever checks the output file. The Director does the skilled parts as a pipeline — and then proves, per Short, that the rendered file was measured.

**How a run works, stage by stage:**

1. **Transcribe.** Muse Voice Transcribe transcribes the source (turn-level); a Muse Spark 1.3 pass restores caption punctuation under a word-sequence guard, and phrase timing is aligned for the captions.
2. **Pick the moments.** Muse Spark Open (Meta's open-weights model, served by Baseten) scores the transcript and sweeps for the strongest candidate moments.
3. **Cut the speaker out.** SAM 3.1 segments the speaker in every frame of the chosen window; the matte is finished in code — component and hole cleanup, then temporal smoothing across the mask sequence — so the cutout edge holds still instead of flickering.
4. **Direct the stage.** The Short is composed as a layered stage, not a crop: a treated backdrop; the hook text *behind* the speaker — the speaker occludes part of the lettering, and that occlusion is what makes the depth read (the planner targets an 8–20% glyph-occlusion band, hard cap 25%); the speaker cutout in front; captions always in front, never over the face.
5. **Add the graphics.** The graphics layer (next section) plans visual context for what is being said — generated stills, context cards, backdrop scenes — and places each one against the SAM masks under a strict placement law.
6. **Verify the render.** A **post-render verifier (checks F1–F9)** measures the *actual rendered file* — deterministic geometry and audio checks first, plus one Muse Wonder judgement of the muted opening seconds.
7. **Repair at most once.** On a FAIL, Muse Spark 1.3 picks **at most one repair** from a fixed menu, the repair runs on cached artifacts, and the render is re-verified.

# Tessa

Tessa is an AI agent that hunts for planets in NASA TESS data on red stars near the Sun. It explains every
dip it can, writes down why, and turns what is left into predictions anyone with a telescope can test.

**Demo video (3 min):** https://youtu.be/D6WHNySGhhU

**Live site:** https://tessa.braveai.solutions: every star in the survey on a 3D map, a case file for every
dip, and Ask Tessa, where Muse Spark answers questions from the survey's own files.

**Quick links:** [Quickstart: hosted, or one star from this repo](#quickstart) ·
[How it compares with NASA's ExoMiner++](#what-glimmer-adds) ·
[Glimmer v10 weights on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/rushi-brave/glimmer-vetter-v10) ·
[Meta models used](#meta-models) · [Predictions for observers](predictions/README.md)

## What it found so far

| | |
|---|---|
| Stars in the pool | 99,461 K and M dwarfs within 100 parsecs with TESS data |
| Searched | 76,318: every one of the pool's 48,945 stars that never had 2-minute data (except 179 with no usable light curve), and 27,552 that did |
| Repeating dips found | 2,698, with each batch's bar set on upside-down light curves so about 1 star in 100 passes on noise (749 pass there) |
| Sent to Glimmer, the fine-tuned model | 715 (714 replies could be read; TIC 178829006 came back twice as broken JSON, so it has no call); code settled the other 1,983 |
| Glimmer called a planet | 159 |
| Passed novelty, ephemeris and season checks | 11 |
| **New candidates** (passed TRICERATOPS: FPP < 0.5, NFPP < 0.1) | **8** |
| Likely planets (FPP < 0.5, NFPP < 0.001; Giacalone et al. 2021) | 4: TIC 71503196, 116046773, 166321785, 9066956 |
| Candidates with a nearby star still to rule out (NFPP 0.001 to 0.1) | 4: TIC 321290256, 50099421, 61220826, 79490453 |
| Also found again | TIC 458191673, a blind rediscovery of a candidate published before the hackathon, not counted among the 8 |

The search ran in eight batches: the survey (4,997 stars), batch 2 (17,980), the 1,000 held-out stars (below), and
batches 4 and 5 (12,449 and 12,341), which finished the never-observed part of the pool on 2 November
(`runs/2026-11-02`); then batches 6 to 8 (9,184 each), stars that were 2-minute targets, searched in their full-frame
data (`runs/2026-11-03`). Of the 2,698 dips, 2,239 were rejected, 158 are flagged with what is left to check, 284 are
set aside (283 by code before the model, almost all with a System 1 rank in its bottom 5%; 1 because Glimmer's reply
could not be read), and 9 are known objects; the other 8 are the candidates. Of the 11 that passed gate 2, 9 clear

# Lumen Agent

Lumen Agent edits photos from a sentence, one photo or a whole shoot. You describe the change: "make the sky moodier and turn his coat navy". Lumen plans the steps, finds each region and makes the change. It then looks at its own result and revises it until the instruction is met.

Or point it at a folder of a thousand photos and say "edit them all, and make everyone's T-shirts blue". Lumen reviews the whole library, flags the misfires, applies auto and straightening, gives the weakest photos a closer look, and plans the instruction across the shoot, asking you only what is yours to decide.

- **Planning and checking:** Muse Spark; Muse Wonder plans across a library.
- **Finding things:** SAM 3.1 finds them by name, by a box you draw, or by points.
- **Redrawing:** Muse Image redraws what's inside a region.
- **Listening:** Muse Voice Transcribe writes down an instruction you say, in your own language, for you to check before it runs.

It also restyles a person, redrawing only them: a chad face, Day of the Dead face paint, a knight's armour, 30 years older and more.

Every step is a separate, non-destructive layer. You can turn any of them off, adjust them or undo them, and the original photo is never changed.

Lumen Agent is a Swift package with a command-line tool (`lumen`) and a small Mac app (Lumen Studio). It opens JPEG, PNG, HEIC and camera RAW; `scripts/get-raw-samples.sh` downloads four public-domain RAW files to try. In the code the package and its modules keep the short name, Lumen.

![Lumen Studio after "Make his jacket bright yellow": the plan, each step with its model and time, and the result Muse Spark checked](docs/images/studio-finished.jpg)

## What existed before, and what is new

Lumen Agent is new work, started on October 26, 2026 for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon. Everything in this repository was written during the event.

Lumen Agent is also the agent inside Lumen, a native macOS photo editor that existed before the hackathon (called Photoeditor until November 1, 2026). The editor is closed source and is not part of this repository. It uses Lumen Agent through the same public interfaces as Lumen Studio.

## How it works

1. **Plan.** Muse Spark reads the instruction and the photo, with any area you drew, and writes a plan in a strict JSON schema: select, adjust, regenerate, remove, style, crop, revert, finish. # Ghostline

**A physics lab in your phone, with an AI lab partner that shows its work.**

Film anything that moves. Ghostline measures it, proposes the physical laws that could explain it, rejects the ones the data disagrees with, and proves the winner by overlaying a ghost on a new clip that predicts where the object goes next.

Built for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon (Indie track, Push the Frontier).

> **Status:** starter skeleton. The full design, component by component, is in [docs/build-plan.md](docs/build-plan.md).

## How it works

1. **Watch.** Muse Wonder watches the clip and decides what to measure.
2. **Track.** SAM 3.1 segments the object in every frame; an A4 sheet in the frame turns pixels into meters.
3. **Hypothesize and test.** Wonder proposes competing physical models. A harness running in a Modal Sandbox fits each one and scores it on frames the model never saw.
4. **Review.** Muse Spark Open, on a Modal Shared Endpoint, challenges the claim before Ghostline reports it.
5. **Prove.** On a new trial, a ghost of the object follows the fitted law, and Ghostline measures how far reality drifts from it.

Built during the Meta AI Developer Hackathon.

Mock interviews from a public job offer. A recruiter pastes an offer URL. Agents extract the role, generate a question bank, then curate a spoken interview plan. The web app and API sit in front of that pipeline.

Live:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  recruiter[Recruiter]
  app[Angular app]
  cognito[Cognito]
  api[HTTP API + .NET Lambda]
  extract[offer_extraction]
  questions[question_generation]

  questions --> s3
  questions --> ddb

2. **question_generation** reads that file and writes question items to DynamoDB.
3. **interview_plan_generation** curates 10–12 questions into `{user_id}/{session_id}/plan.json`.

`POST /api/interview-sessions` writes the session as `STARTED` and starts the Step Functions planner. Status then moves through `READING_OFFER`, `GENERATING_QUESTIONS`, `GENERATING_PLAN`, and ends at `SUCCESS`, `FAILED`, or `OFFER_NOT_REACHABLE` when extract does not write a real `offer/details.json`. Built for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon 2026 (Indie track).

## How it works

1. **Find the cells.** SAM 3 proposes candidates on the field image with three text prompts ("cell with a large
   purple nucleus", "neutrophil", "red blood cell") and a fourth for platelets ("small purple dot"). On a wide field, red cells and platelets are
   counted again on overlapping tiles ([17](docs/experiments/17-wide-field-tiling.md)).
2. **Keep the white cells and type them.** Each candidate is cropped at the scale of the red cells
   around it and embedded by the frozen vision encoder of **Muse Glimmer**. Two linear probes on these
   features say whether it is a white cell ([09](docs/experiments/09-detection-probe.md)) and which
   type it is ([05](docs/experiments/05-glimmer-linear-probe.md)): one of the 8 PBC types, or
   "suspected blast", a ninth class learnt from Munich cells ([19](docs/experiments/19-blasts.md)). On a wide field, the white cell probe is
   one trained on wide fields ([18](docs/experiments/18-wide-field-white-cells.md)). No LLM call per cell.
3. **Send the doubtful cells to review.** Every suspected blast goes first. The type probe is
   calibrated: cells below a 92 % confidence cutoff go to the review queue
   ([10](docs/experiments/10-review-coverage.md), [19](docs/experiments/19-blasts.md)), as do cells
   kept with an uncertain detection ([16](docs/experiments/16-empty-field-rescue.md)).
4. **Prepare the review.** A **Muse Spark** agent with six tools reads the counts, asks a second
   opinion on the doubtful cells, flags the ones to open first and writes a short slide report, with
   a guardrail against diagnostic wording ([07](docs/experiments/07-review-agent.md),
   [15](docs/experiments/15-review-agent-on-backend.md)).

The biologist validates or corrects every cell. SmearLens proposes, it does not decide.

## Status

Runs end to end and is deployed as a web demo (see [Web demo](#web-demo)): one field of view in, white
cells with type and confidence, red cell and platelet counts, a differential, a review queue and the
agent report out, in a few seconds plus about 40 s for the agent. Main numbers:

- Type of white cells: 97.6 % on PBC test cells, 96.2 % on a 147-field PBC slide through the whole
  backend, with 4 of 5 errors already in the review queue ([05](docs/experiments/05-glimmer-linear-probe.md),
  [15](docs/experiments/15-review-agent-on-backend.md)).
- Review: checking the 10 % least sure cells leaves 0.3 % errors ([10](docs/experiments/10-review-coverage.md)).

# MuseCell

> **TL;DR**
> 1. **What:** a blinded screening agent on real BBBC021 cell images. Muse Spark plans which 4 of ~24 wells to image, Muse Wonder reviews the call, and only then is the compound unblinded and checked against PubChem, ChEMBL and PubMed.
> 2. **Result (Muse Spark 1.3, agent v5):** right mechanism for **34/38** compounds, **18/19** on the held-out half of a frozen split. With only a well budget, Muse Spark converged on the strategy a screening biologist would use (140 of its 152 wells at the top doses) and matched that fixed rule compound for compound; it did not beat it. When its own judgement overrode the published NSC vote, it was usually wrong (1 of 7 in v4), so MuseCell lets the model plan, argue and explain, and lets the protocol make the call. [Benchmark](eval/RESULTS.md).

**MuseCell is an autonomous screening scientist.** Give it a blinded compound and a small budget of microscope wells. amartya-k/clinic-front-desk-ai.readme_excerpt:
# Clinic Front-Desk AI — missed-call text-back agent

A front-desk AI for small clinics that rescues missed patient calls. When a
call is missed (or a patient texts after hours), the agent texts back
instantly, answers routine questions from a clinic knowledge file, books /
reschedules / cancels appointments conversationally as **requests staff
confirm**, and escalates anything clinical or urgent to staff **before the
model ever sees the message**.

Built for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon (Cerebral Valley), Indie Developer
track. Demo clinic is fictional — Bright Smiles Dental — and no real patient
data is used anywhere.

## Why

Small clinics lose patients at the front desk: calls missed after hours or
during lunch go to voicemail, and most callers never call back. This agent
turns every missed call into a text conversation that can answer the routine
80% (hours, directions, what to bring, refill/paperwork status routing),
capture a booking request, and hand the rest to a human — safely.

## How it works

```
missed call / inbound SMS
        │
        ▼
  guardrails.py ── deterministic classifier, runs FIRST, before any LLM call
        │            urgent / clinical / sensitive-data / "talk to a human"
        │            → escalation script + staff queue; model never sees it
        ▼ allow
  sms_flow.py ──── conversation state, staff takeover / send / release,
        │            STOP opt-out, dashboard analytics
        ├──► booking.py ── mock schedule with real slot logic;
        │                   bookings are REQUESTS, never confirmations;
        │                   a failed reschedule never loses the original slot
        └──► meta_client.py ── Meta Model API (Muse Spark) chat call,
                                grounded by system_prompt.md + the clinic
                                knowledge file only
```

- **Guardrails are deterministic, not model-decided** (`guardrails.py`).
  Urgent symptoms (including Spanish terms and reversed phrasings like
  "my chest is hurting"), clinical asks (diagnosis, dosage, prescriptions),
  sensitive identifiers (SSN / card-shaped numbers), and human-handoff
  requests all escalate with a fixed script. Gibberish gets a clarify reply
  instead of a model call.
- **The agent may only answer from the knowledge file**
  (`clinic_knowledge.json`, rules in `system_prompt.md`). No invented
  prices, insurance, or availability; unknown → say so and offer a staff
  callback.
- **Staff stay in control.** Staff can take over any conversation (the agent
  goes silent), reply as staff, resolve the escalation, and hand back.
  The dashboard snapshot carries an analytics strip: missed calls texted
  back, booking requests, escalations, opt-outs.

## Run it

No dependencies beyond Python 3 (standard library only).

```bash
cd agent-core
python3 demo_runner.py   # the 4 scored demo scenarios, end to end (17/17)
python3 sms_flow.py      # SMS flow + staff takeover self-tests (23/23)
python3 booking.py       #

# ProofLens

**ProofLens reconstructs flowcharts into interactive, inspectable graphs, verifies structural consistency, and makes the source material navigable.**

This repository is the starter for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon prototype.

- Flowchart image as the first supported input.

# Scylla: a self-hardening firewall for AI agents

AI agents read our email, browse the web, open images and call real tools. One sentence hidden in any of those inputs can hijack them: prompt injection is OWASP's #1 LLM risk. **Scylla** sits between a tool-using agent and the world:

- **Ingress:** every untrusted input (email, web page, file, image, voicemail, tool output) goes through heuristics, learned rules, a guard model, Muse Spark vision, SAM 3.1 localization and Muse Voice Transcribe. It is allowed, sanitized or quarantined before the agent sees it.
- **Egress:** every side-effecting call (`send_email`, `http_post`, `pay_invoice`, `delete_file`, `create_calendar_event`) goes through DLP with runtime-canary taint tracking, learned tool policies and a Muse Spark judge that checks the call against what the user actually asked for. The call is allowed, blocked or held for a human.
- **Self-hardening:** a red-team agent invents new attacks. A blue-team agent proposes constrained rules, and a rule ships only if replaying the full corpus shows the bypass is now blocked and **zero** benign tasks regress.

Built for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon (Indie track). All code in this repo was written during the hackathon window.

## Results
| Run | Attack success | Benign utility and ingress |
|---|---:|---|
| Mock, Scylla off | 18/18 | — |
| Mock, Scylla enforce | 0/18 | 10/10 |
| Live Muse Spark, Scylla enforce (one clean 28-scenario run) | 0/18 | 10/10 completed; 16/18 flagged at ingress; 0/10 benign flags |
| Live adaptive search vs unprotected Muse Spark | 1 bypass in 28 variants (pays attacker's bank account; ~1 in 5 replays) | Scylla provenance holds that exact payment for approval |
| Live adaptive search vs Scylla (enforce) | 0 bypasses in 8 variants (296 calls) | one variant got past ingress and the agent tried to pay the attacker; Scylla stopped it live at egress |
| Mock layer ablation | provenance alone catches 14/18 | 10/10 utility, no model calls |

Muse Spark resisted the hand-written corpus even unprotected, but a Muse Spark attacker refining its own attacks found an invoice-fraud variant that got through; Scylla adds pre-model detection and model-independent egress control. See [the live results](docs/LIVE_RESULTS.md).

## Meta models used
| Model | Role |
|---|---|
| Muse Spark (`muse-spark-1.3-contributor`) | protected agent, egress judge, red team, blue team |
| Muse Spark vision | finds instructions hidden in images |
| SAM 3.1 | localizes the injected region |
| Muse Voice Transcribe | voicemail ingress |

```

# Cruz Voice Meta

Voice modules for talking to a virtual employee, with a standalone synthetic demo and an embeddable Windows host. Built during the Meta AI developer hackathon, starting **26 October 2026**.

**Status updated: 30 October 2026 (Asia/Kolkata).** [v0.2.4](https://github.com/cruzclaw/cruz-voice-meta/releases/tag/v0.2.4) is published, verified, pinned and installed in the integrated Windows app from a clean build. The real employee gateway routes voice through **Muse Spark**; a successful provider response and account usage were verified, and the owner confirmed that the app hears the question and speaks the correct identity answer. The attention review page and its migration are deployed. **Spoken follow-ups after a call are not yet delivered as a complete production chain.** Tool-read, interruption, approval-before-send/single-delivery and final installed acceptance remain open.

This README records the agreed product plan and its delivery history. A checked item means only the named milestone is complete, not that every acceptance criterion for its workstream passed.

## Intended experience

Use the existing Windows app to speak to the employee you select, with that employee's identity, memory, tools and existing Cruz permissions. Voice must not be a separate assistant merely borrowing the employee's name.

1. The compact pad appears on normal startup without taking focus or starting a call. Closing it hides it for that app session; new attention does not reopen it. The shortcut or tray restores it, and the next launch shows it again.
2. Choose an employee explicitly in the panel or tray. The choice is remembered per signed-in account, never selected automatically, even with one employee. The name remains visible while checking access or when voice is unavailable. Changing employees ends the previous call before connecting to the new one.
3. Press Call or **Ctrl+Shift+Space**, or use optional locally detected **“Hey Cruz”** after consent. Wake listening is off initially; a saved opt-in may be restored. This is not speaker recognition.
4. Speak, interrupt and continue. Readiness, microphone state and playback state must be honest. “Speaking” follows renderer playback confirmation; preparing audio remains “Thinking.” Failure displays text and an accurate error rather than pretending sound played.
5. Work uses the employee's existing services. Consequential actions require the applicable owner approval and exact-payload dispatch checks. Reading an item or saying “pass” never approves or sends it.
6. Accepted durable work should survive the voice connection, report actual progress and permit continued conversation. Full durable-work acceptance remains pending.

### Silent attention, not unsolicited notifications

A thin Alexa-style top indicator is present in **both expanded and compact states**, including during calls. It signals waiting work without speaking, playing an alert, revealing content, taking focus or expanding a window.

# TraceMint AI Analyst

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/509c437d-454c-4aab-a3d2-677875534a0a

Grounded weekly revenue answers from raw payment events: a deterministic TypeScript engine computes the numbers, and Meta's Muse Spark (`muse-spark-1.2`) via the Meta Model API words the weekly digest. Every figure the model writes is checked against the computed summary before the digest is shown; a failing digest is withheld.

Built for the **Meta AI Developer Hackathon** (Cerebral Valley) - new work during the official build window (Oct 27 - Nov 4, 2026). The video uses demo data; the digest shown in it is real recorded output from the Meta Model API. Video download: [releases/tag/demo-video](https://github.com/rishilifts/tracemint-ai/releases/tag/demo-video)

## How it works

1. **Ingest** - `POST /ingest` stores one event at a time in D1 (`charge` / `refund` / `dispute`, with acquisition source; schema in `schema/schema.sql`):
   ```json
   { "id": "evt_1", "ts": 1761609600, "kind": "charge", "amountCents": 4900, "currency": "usd", "source": "newsletter", "utmCampaign": "oct-launch" }
   ```
2. **Numbers** - `src/lib/kpis.ts` computes gross, refunds, disputes, net, refund rate, average order value, per-source breakdowns and daily net. All arithmetic is plain TypeScript.
3. **Digest** - `POST /api/digest?days=7` builds a prompt containing only those computed numbers and asks Muse Spark to word it in three fixed sections: WHAT HAPPENED / WHAT CHANGED / WHAT TO WATCH. Generation is explicit and stored in D1; the dashboard and `GET` endpoints are read-only and never call the model.

## Model routing

Every digest carries an explicit provider label in the API and on the dashboard. A configured endpoint that fails surfaces an error instead of silently falling back.

1. **`muse-spark-meta-hosted`** - Muse Spark (`muse-spark-1.2`) via Meta's hosted Meta Model API (`MUSE_BASE_URL=https://api.meta.ai`, `MUSE_API_KEY`). The primary, hackathon-qualifying route.
2. **`muse-endpoint`** - experimental self-hosted Meta open-weights Muse Glimmer 30B (sha256-pinned GGUF, llama.cpp on Modal CPU; source in `modal/`). Its keyed client was e2e-tested; the full app test did not pass, and it is kept stopped.
3. **`workers-ai`** - Cloudflare Workers AI Llama 3.3 70B (`@cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast`). Labeled development fallback only, never presented as the hackathon-qualifying route.

`MUSE_BASE_URL` selects the route; `MUSE_MODEL_ID` overrides the model id sent.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path          | Purpose                                         |
|--------|---------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| POST   | `/ingest`     | store one event (Bearer token if set)           |
| GET    | `/api/kpis`   | current vs previous period KPIs + delta         |
| POST   | `/api/digest` | generate + store the digest (token-gated)       |
| GET    | `/api/digest` | read the latest stored digest (never generates) |
| GET    | `/health`

A master mechanic in your pocket that shows its work. Live OBD2 data, the phone camera and your voice feed a
deterministic Bayesian diagnostic engine that ranks the next best test for your skill and tools, explains why each
suspect rose or fell, and produces a hash-chained, replayable report.

Built for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon (Indie track). Muse Code wrote the code from `AGENTS.md`/`docs/SPEC.md`
during the event, driven headlessly with plans and reviews on `muse-wonder-1.0` and builds on `muse-spark-1.3`
(prompts and runs are in `.agents/`).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Android["Android app\n(ELM allowlist, CameraX, mic)"] --> Backend["FastAPI backend\n(event store, engine, KP)"]
    Backend --> Meta["Meta Model API"]
    Backend --> Baseten["Baseten\n(Spark Open)"]
    Backend --> Web["Web Replay / Report"]
```

## Meta model map

| Model | ID | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Spark | `muse-spark-1.3` | Reasoning, vision reads, PDF extraction |
| SAM | `sam-3.1` | Segmentation masks |
| Voice Transcribe | `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` | Speech-to-text only (Android TTS speaks) |
| Wonder | `muse-wonder-1.0` | One review per report |
| Spark Open | `meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026` via Baseten | Second opinion / fallback (own $80 ledger) |
| Muse Code | — | Builds the repo |

Muse Image is explicitly excluded from the diagnostic path: no generated image is ever used as evidence.

## Run the simulator / replay locally

```sh
cd backend && uv run pytest -q
scripts/replay_check.sh backend/tests/fixtures/sessions/*.mmrec
cd web && npm ci && npm run build
```

`scripts/dev.sh` boots the backend + web. The simulator needs no car and no keys; replay costs $0
(`REPLAY_USE_CACHED_LLM=true` replays recorded AI outputs without live calls).

Deployed Modal app: <https://jeremydoege89--mmc-fastapi-app.us-east.modal.run> — open with `?judge=1` for the

﻿# healthplan-compare

An educational ACA health plan cost comparison tool. Colorado first, built so other states can be added as new datasets.

**Not medical advice and not an eligibility determination.** Estimates only. Verify plans, prices and subsidies with the official exchange (Connect for Health Colorado) or the insurer before enrolling.

Scope: individual-market ACA plans, under-65, non-Medicaid.

## Hackathon contribution log

Built for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon, Oct 26 to Nov 4, 2026. Everything in this repo was created in that window; see the commit history.

- 2026-10-26: Colorado data build script (`scripts/build_co_data.py`), bundled 2026 plan data from the CMS State-Based Exchange QHP PUF (`data/co/`).
- 2026-10-26: Next.js app, scenario-based ranking engine with tests, household sizing (spouse and up to 3 charged children, family deductible and out-of-pocket max).
- 2026-10-26: ZIP lookup (Census ZIP-to-county, CMS county-to-rating-area) and county service-area filtering so only plans sold in the user's county are ranked.
- 2026-10-26: Muse Spark explanation panel (server route, JSON-schema output, every quoted figure re-verified against plan data in code).
- 2026-10-27: Removed the Muse Spark explanation panel and its server route; the tool is now used by pointing any assistant at the link, with no model call of its own.
- 2026-10-26: Agent interface: an intake decision tree (`src/lib/tree.ts`), income-band subsidy screening, and three tools (`next_question`, `rank_plans`, `compare_plans`) served as a remote MCP server at `/mcp` and as REST at `/api/engine/<tool>`.
- 2026-10-26: Premium tax credit estimate (benchmark Silver minus expected contribution, using the 2026 table in IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-25, checked against the IRS text) and Silver cost-sharing-reduction variants for incomes up to 250% of poverty.

## Agent interface

The engine can be driven by any agent that speaks MCP or HTTP. The tools hold no state: the agent passes the answers it has collected each call, and `next_question` says what to ask next (and stops for Medicare or Medicaid). Tool outputs carry the caveats and the exact numbers an agent may quote.

- MCP: `POST /mcp` (streamable HTTP, JSON responses)
- REST: `POST /api/engine/next_question`, `/rank_plans`, `/compare_plans`

No API keys are used by these endpoints.

## Data

Source: CMS State-based Exchange QHP PUF, Colorado, plan year 2026. CMS notes SBE data does not reflect state subsidies such as Colorado Premium Assistance.

Rebuild: `python -I scripts/build_co_data.py 2026` (needs pandas).
ZIP lookup: `python -I scripts/build_co_zips.py` (Census ZCTA-to-county file plus the CMS Colorado rating-area table).

# DPM Agent

*Versión en español: [README.es.md](README.es.md)*

**A WhatsApp front desk for Dominican clinics, built on Meta's Muse models: it books, reschedules and fills cancelled slots in Spanish, English and Haitian Creole — and never gives medical advice.**

![DPM Agent demo page: example buttons in three languages, the chat and the agent's tool trace](docs/img/demo-en.png)

<!-- CAPTURA: replace with a GIF of a real conversation with Muse Spark (voice note → booking → waiting-list offer) -->

> Project for the **Meta AI Developer Hackathon** (Oct 26 – Nov 4, 2026), Indie Developer track. How it meets each rule of the hackathon, WhatsApp and privacy: [docs/RULES.md](docs/RULES.md).

---

## The problem

In many Dominican clinics the schedule runs on WhatsApp and the phone. The receptionist answers the same messages all day ("any slot tomorrow?", "does the doctor work on Saturday?", "I want to change my appointment") while also attending patients in the waiting room, filling in insurance (ARS) forms and taking payments. Messages go unanswered, patients are lost and cancelled slots stay empty.

The country also has a large Haitian community, and many patients write in Kreyòl. Most front-desk tools only speak Spanish.

At the pilot clinic:

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| WhatsApp messages per day at the front desk | <!-- CIFRA PILOTO: mensajes de WhatsApp por día --> *pending* |
| Share of those messages that are about appointments | <!-- CIFRA PILOTO: % de mensajes sobre citas --> *pending* |
| Cancelled slots per week that stay empty | <!-- CIFRA PILOTO: huecos por semana sin llenar --> *pending* |
| Patients who write in Kreyòl or English | <!-- CIFRA PILOTO: % de pacientes en kreyòl o inglés --> *pending* |

DPM Agent takes over the repetitive conversation and leaves the staff what truly needs a person.

## What it does

- **Books, reschedules and cancels** over WhatsApp or web chat, with multi-step tool calling (find patient → check availability → confirm → book). The server validates everything: a taken or past slot cannot be booked, even if the model tries.
- **Speaks the patient's language**: Spanish, English and Haitian Creole are guaranteed (fixed texts, WhatsApp templates and tests in all three); any other language is answered as well as possible with English as the fallback. The language is detected on every message and followed if the patient switches.
- **Voice notes** transcribed with Muse Voice Transcribe; the audio is never stored.
- **Insurance card from a photo**: Muse Spark reads name, insurer and member number (image + JSON schema); the result stays pending until the patient or the receptionist confirms it.
- **Fills cancelled slots on its own**: when someone cancels, the first matching patient on the waiting list gets an offer on their channel; if they don't answer in 30 minutes it moves to the next one.
- **Reminder 24 hours before**, with confirm or cancel.
- **Follow-ups ordered by the doctor** ("control in 3 months")
